Although all-in-one models integrate multiple restoration tasks, they face a trade-off between generalization and task-specific accuracy. To address this issue, we propose a SR-Agent (Seismic Restoration Agent) containing three sequential stages: classification, restoration, and evaluation. For the first two stages, we design an intelligent classifier based on ResNet to identify the degradation types presented in low-quality seismic data, and the classification results are used as task instructions to activate the corresponding restoration models in a pool, which contains dedicated networks for different restoration tasks. For the last stage, SR-Agent can dynamically schedule the activated models and explore an optimal restoration path, rather than relying on a predefined processing pipeline. Specifically, we first develop a no-reference restoration-performance evaluation measurement by combining four parameters: seismic trace coherence, energy distribution in F-K domain, spectral smoothness, and high-frequency energy ratio. Second, the evaluation measurement is applied to quantify the restoration performance of different candidate restoration paths. Finally, the path with the highest evaluation score is automatically selected and then applied to input seismic data. The results show that, when multiple degradation mechanisms coexist, SR-Agent can effectively plan an optimal restoration path, achieving accurate and intelligent restoration of degraded seismic data.

authors.name: Songmin Wang, Xintong Dong, Zilong Wang, Xinyang Wang, Zhengyi Yuan, Wenshuo Yu

papers.title: Multi-Illumination Spectral Reflectance Reconstruction: A method for hyperspectral imaging using digital photography
papers.summary: Quantitative measurement of complex coloration patterns is essential for many biological studies and practical applications. Although color perception depends on the observer's visual system, an objective characterization is possible by measuring the spectral reflectance across the sample surface. Traditional methods for measuring spectral reflectance are either limited in spatial resolution, as with spectrometer probes, or limited in spectral detail, as with digital cameras. We present a method for reconstructing spatially resolved spectral reflectance of samples from multiple images taken under different illuminants with known spectral irradiance. Using an optimization scheme that minimizes pixel-value error while regularizing for the smoothness of the reflectance spectrum, our method generates high-resolution hyperspectral images. We tested our method using both existing spectral reflectance datasets and original multi-illumination images taken in a custom photo-box, demonstrating high accuracy and simple implementation of the method, as well as the ability to infer how samples are perceived by different visual systems. Our method can be a useful tool for objective quantification of complex visual patterns in color-related biological research and imaging applications.

authors.name: Robert Heyck, Vincent Gillaspy, Stephen J. Hagen, BingKan Xue

papers.title: High-fidelity six-dimensional optical data storage
papers.summary: Multi-dimensional optical data storage, wherein each voxel encodes multiple bits of information within a three-dimensional isotropic medium, presents a revolutionary approach to dense data storage. This approach exploits multiple degrees of freedom of light, such as intensity, polarization and wavelength, to selectively control distinct optical responses in the medium. However, increasing dimensionality exacerbates crosstalk between different encoding dimensions, thereby compromising recording fidelity. In this study, we introduce a novel six-dimensional (6D) multiplexing approach that exploits ultrafast interactions of polarized light with a three-dimensional medium. By manipulating three light parameters within a Poincar\'e-like semi-sphere, we systematically induce three distinct material responses in laser-induced nanostructures, each corresponding to a unique physical quantity: fluorescence, phase retardance, and slow axis orientation. Thanks to such multiple one-to-one correspondence between light parameters and material responses, we achieve unprecedented high fidelity, attaining a raw accuracy of 99.45%. Furthermore, this independently controlled 6D multiplexing technique maximizes the effective user capacity to 0.38 petabits per disc. The versatility of laser-induced nanostructures across multiple physical dimensions enables diverse applications, ranging from high-capacity data storage to microfluidics, optical elements, integrated photonics, micromechanics, and quantum technologies.

authors.name: Jichao Gao, Tong Jin, Chenqi Yi, Yihui Fu, Zhi Yan, Xiya Xie, Rokas Drevinskas, Zhexiang Xiao, Lei Wang, Guangda Niu, Jingyu Zhang, Hong-Bo Sun

papers.title: Direct measurement of the on-shot focal-spot size of a kilojoule-class petawatt laser
papers.summary: We report a direct, on-shot determination of the focal-spot size of a kilojoule-class, four-beam petawatt laser. Encircled-energy curves were inferred from the energy transmitted around aluminum-coated spheres of varying diameters placed at the focal plane. The 50% encircled-energy diameter D50 of each beam was obtained by fitting a two-component Gaussian mixture with Bayesian inference. With all deformable mirrors optimized in closed loop, the best-corrected alignment beam reached D50 = 34 (+4/-5) um, three times the diffraction limit of 10 um. Under full-power conditions, the thermal distortion of the main amplifier broadened this beam to D50 = 102 (+9/-8) um and reduced its peak intensity ninefold, to 2.2 (+0.6/-0.9) x 10^18 W/cm^2 at 250 J and 1.3 ps. The energy fraction of the narrow component decreased from 68% to 38%. These reference values serve facility users, and a deformable mirror upstream of the pulse compressor, now on one beam only, doubles the on-shot peak intensity.

authors.name: Ryunosuke Takizawa, Keisuke Takahashi, Yuhei Kawakami, Hiroki Matsubara, Yuga Karaki, Rinya Akematsu, Ryou Oomura, Kai Kimura, Yuki Tamaru, Yasunobu Arikawa, Koji Tsubakimoto, Shinsuke Fujioka

papers.title: A Heterogeneous CPU-GPU Framework for Finite Element Micromagnetic Simulations on Tetrahedral Meshes
papers.summary: The design of magnetic storage materials relies on repeated micromagnetic simulations. Within each simulation, the demagnetization field evaluation and the sparse linear solve are executed at every time step and together dominate the computational cost. To address these bottlenecks, we develop a heterogeneous CPU-GPU framework that exploits the complementary computational capabilities of the two processors. In the existing AFEMAG solver, developed by Yang et al [J. Comput. Phys. 431 (2021) 110142], computationally intensive boundary integral evaluations and sparse linear solves limit performance. We offload these operations to the GPU while retaining assembly and iteration control on the CPU. We validate the framework using cases from all five $\mu$Mag standard problems, covering quasistatic hysteresis, equilibrium configurations, field-driven dynamics, and spin-transfer-torque dynamics. This approach accelerates simulations across the benchmark suite; notably, for Standard Problem 3 on a mesh of 137,313 nodes, augmenting the CPU with one NVIDIA A100 GPU yields a $17.1\times$ speedup over the CPU-only configuration. The heterogeneous AFEMAG framework thus provides an efficient and practical platform for micromagnetic simulations in the design of magnetic storage materials.

authors.name: Zekai Zheng, Zixuan Cui, Guanghui Hu

papers.title: How zonal states beat-driven by Alfven eigenmodes stabilize micro-turbulence in tokamak plasmas
papers.summary: The effects of zonal states (ZS) beat-driven by Alfven eigenmodes (AEs) on micro-turbulence stability are investigated; taking toroidal Alfven eigenmode (TAE) and ion temperature gradient mode (ITG) as an example. The analysis is carried out by deriving the nonlinear gyrokinetic equation describing particle response to ITG, in the presence of TAE beat-driven ZS. It is found that, the phase space zonal structure generated by AEs could lead to a significant reduction in the local nonuniformity drive and, thereby, stabilize the local ITG instabilities. The zonal flow induced shearing, on the other hand, contributes only to a real frequency shift and, typically, negligibly small additional stabilization.

authors.name: Liu Chen, Zhiyong Qiu, Tiancheng Liu, Fulvio Zonca, Qian Fang

papers.title: Seamless Gradient Pixels for Multidimensional Optical Information Interrogation
papers.summary: Information from light interaction with its environment can be extracted from its numerous properties. Yet capturing and interpreting this information within a single and compact platform remains challenging because conventional systems rely on discrete components and detection channels. Here we introduce the concept of "gradient pixels" that provides a universal metasurface platform to interrogate optical field information in the infrared (IR) spectrum. By continuously varying a design parameter across two dimensions, we encode multidimensional optical information into measurable spatial patterns, e.g., both spectral and polarization information are acquired from a single snapshot image. A free-form gradient pixel further enables prescribed wavelength-selective spatial patterns within a single metasurface through tailored gradient profiles. Unlike isolated filter arrays, seamless gradient-pixels multiplex neighbouring meta-atoms, increasing channel spatial density and relaxing Q-factor constraints. A 250-$\mu$m footprint of these meta-atoms achieves spectral resolution better than 100-pm over a 100-nm spectral span based on a serpentine configuration. Snapshot wavelength-polarization reconstruction yields polarization angular accuracy at 0.3$^\circ$. We extend this concept to perform near-field refractive index sensing at video rates using the same explicit parameter-space mapping. By linking far-field detection and near-field sensing, it enables spatially resolved analysis of optical fields and local dielectric environments through a common image-based readout. It offers prospects for multidimensional optical sensing, computational imaging and intelligent information processing.

authors.name: Zhenchao Liu, Bochang Wu, Houxin Fan, Tingbiao Guo, Hongtao Wang, Lei Chen, Cheng-Feng Pan, Shutao Zhang, Md Abdur Rahman, Wen Siang Lew, Hongyoon Kim, Heechang Yun, Junsuk Rho, Joel K. W. Yang

papers.title: Exceptional unidirectional radiation modes
papers.summary: Singularities such as exceptional points (EPs) and bound states in the continuum (BICs) fundamentally reshape the spectral response of non-Hermitian open systems, unlocking exotic physical phenomena and unprecedented ways of wave manipulation. Nevertheless, the radiation behaviors of modes evolving around these singularities lack a unified picture. Here we show that a mode originating from a BIC can radiate unidirectionally, exhibiting a quality factor that continuously varies in parameter space from a near-infinite value (near the BIC) to a finite lower bound as it coalesces with the other (leaky) mode at an EP. The crossing of the unidirectional radiation mode and the EP in parameter space results in not only merged poles (resonant EP) but also merged zeros (absorbing EP) of the scattering matrix, along with a counterintuitive reversal of radiation direction decoupled from the coalesced eigenmodes under near-field excitation. These phenomena are experimentally observed in an acoustic waveguide system featuring two side-branch resonant cavities with deliberate frequency detuning and asymmetric dissipation. Our findings reveal the intrinsic connection between eigenmode topology and radiation behavior in open systems, offering a viable route for tailoring scattering and radiation responses via non-Hermitian modulations.

authors.name: Shuowei An, Tuo Liu, Jie Zhu, Li Cheng

papers.title: Onset of three dimensionality in transonic shock boundary layer interaction over a natural laminar flow airfoil
papers.summary: The development of three-dimensionality in transonic shock--boundary-layer interactions (SBLI) can significantly influence the aerodynamic response of natural laminar flow (NLF) airfoils, yet the associated vorticity dynamics remain insufficiently understood. The present study investigates the short-time evolution of transonic SBLI over the SHM1 NLF airfoil using high-fidelity three-dimensional (3D) simulations at three operating conditions reported by Fujino et al., Natural-laminar-flow airfoil development for a lightweight business jet, J. Aircraft 40, 609-615 (2003). The selected cases represent three distinct operating regimes: the initial development of a normal shock, drag divergence, and shock-induced separation. Comparisons with previously reported two-dimensional (2D) simulations establish the temporal interval over which the spanwise-averaged 3D flow remains close to the corresponding 2D evolution, while departures in surface pressure and skin-friction responses identify the subsequent development of 3D effects within the SBLI region. The temporal evolution of volume-integrated streamwise and wall-normal enstrophies further characterizes the development of the associated 3D vortical field. The compressible enstrophy transport equation (CETE) is subsequently employed to examine the mechanisms governing the evolution of the 3D vortical field. Viscous and compressibility-related terms dominate the normalized enstrophy budget during the early evolution, while vortex stretching remains a minor contribution in the normal-shock and drag-divergence regimes but becomes appreciable, albeit intermittently, with the development of shock-induced separation. Across the three operating regimes, the same principal enstrophy-transport mechanisms remain active, but their relative contributions to the normalized budget are redistributed with the SBLI topology.

authors.name: Abhijeet Guha, Aditi Sengupta

papers.title: A branch-free three-dimensional ghost-cell immersed boundary method with direction-averaged extrapolation kernels
papers.summary: Ghost-cell immersed boundary methods impose the wall boundary condition on a Cartesian grid by assigning values to the grid points just inside the body, the ghost points. A common approach reconstructs the ghost value from an image point, which requires a wall normal for every ghost point. Special treatments are also often required where the interpolation stencil leaves the fluid region, e.g., near thin, concave or highly curved parts of complex bodies. We present a ghost-cell method that needs neither wall normals nor image points. Instead of a single extrapolation direction, the method uses all fluid nodes within 2.5 grid spacings of a ghost point that satisfy a simple geometric condition. The ghost value is obtained as the average of one-dimensional linear extrapolations from these nodes through the wall crossings of the connecting segments. The weights depend only on the geometry and are computed offline as one kernel on a $5 \times 5 \times 5$ stencil per ghost point. The boundary treatment at run time is thus an explicit, branch-free weighted sum. For the flows around a sphere and the Stanford Bunny, a self-convergence study shows approximately second-order convergence of the velocity in the $L_1$ and $L_2$ norms. The maximum difference also decreases at second order for the sphere but more slowly for the Stanford Bunny, where it is observed at a few nodes next to the wall. The drag coefficient of the sphere at Reynolds numbers of 25--200 agrees with a previous study within 2.4% for 32 grid cells per diameter and 0.4% for 64. For the Stanford Bunny at a Reynolds number of 100, the force coefficients agree with a body-fitted solution within 1% for 64 grid cells per reference length, without any geometry-specific treatment. Although no pressure condition is imposed on the wall, the pressure field is smooth and consistent with the body-fitted solution.

authors.name: Itsuki Takarabe, Ryuto Saeki, Koji Fukagata

papers.title: Effective-dimension estimation of a minimal turbulent channel flow via IRMAE-WD
papers.summary: The implicit rank-minimizing autoencoder with weight decay (IRMAE-WD) (Zeng et al. 2024) aims to estimate the dimension of the low-dimensional manifold underlying high-dimensional data from a sharp drop in the latent singular values of a single trained model. We apply IRMAE-WD with a three-dimensional convolutional autoencoder to velocity fields of a minimal turbulent channel flow at ${\rm Re}_{\tau}=110$ and examine whether the drop represents the intrinsic degrees of freedom. We also compare the number of coordinates IRMAE-WD needs for a given reconstruction accuracy or smallest reproduced scale with that of proper orthogonal decomposition (POD). We find that a clear drop appears and that the reconstruction rate decreases by at most 0.01 percentage points with truncation at the drop. The drop thus marks the effective dimension of the trained representation. However, the drop position moves to the lower-dimension side as linear layers are added. In addition, the reconstruction error decreases only gradually with the number of coordinates in all but the smallest wavelength band. These results suggest that the drop position is set by the implicit regularization of the linear layers and cannot be regarded as the intrinsic degrees of freedom. In contrast, with transfer learning, the smallest number of coordinates needed for a given accuracy hardly depends on the number of linear layers and is smaller than that of POD up to a reconstruction rate of about 97%. IRMAE-WD also reproduces a given scale with fewer coordinates than POD. Above about 97%, however, POD requires fewer coordinates, mainly because IRMAE-WD reconstructs large-scale structures less precisely. Hence, when the error decreases continuously, as in the minimal channel flow, the number of coordinates needed to represent wall turbulence should be stated with the required accuracy or scale, not as a single number.

authors.name: Ryuto Saeki, Keita Nakamura, Koji Fukagata

papers.title: Solving the puzzle of tropical cyclone track bifurcation
papers.summary: Tropical cyclones whose predicted tracks bifurcate are among the most dreaded storms in disaster planning. Understanding when and why these bifurcations occur has been a long-standing puzzle in track forecasting. We address this issue by introducing the concept of "fate boundaries" hidden in the steering flow. Storms located on opposite sides of these boundaries follow dramatically different tracks. By analyzing 1,179 Northern Hemisphere storms over 2011-2025, we identified 61 with a strong signature of bifurcation. In every instance, fate boundaries explained why the ensemble tracks split. Additionally, they can reveal bifurcations days before they appear in any operational ensemble. Because fate boundaries often separate devastating from nearby benign tracks, they mark when and where minimal interventions could, in principle, redirect a storm.

authors.name: Wei Zou, Jizhou Li, Xurui He, Lei Liu, Pinaki Chakraborty, Lin Li

papers.title: Energy transfers in decaying three-dimensional Hall-magnetohydrodynamics turbulence: Dependence on the Ion-Inertial Length and the Magnetic Prandtl Number
papers.summary: We present a systematic study of energy transfers in three-dimensional (3D) decaying Hall-magnetohydrodynamics (HMHD) turbulence. Our study has been designed to investigate the dependence of these transfers on initial energy spectra, the ion-inertial length $d_{i}$, and the magnetic Prandtl number $Pr_{m}$. Using shell-to-shell decomposition, we compute the energy transfer rates for (a) kinetic-to-kinetic, (b) magnetic-to-magnetic, (c) kinetic-to-magnetic, and (d) magnetic-to-kinetic interactions by carrying out extensive pseudospectral direct numerical simulations (DNSs) of 3D HMHD and its MHD counterpart. Furthermore, we examine the magnetic-to-magnetic and current-density-to-magnetic energy transfers arising from the Hall term in this framework. Energy transfers between like fields -- namely, kinetic-to-kinetic and magnetic-to-magnetic -- are predominantly local and forward in direction, cascading energy from large to small length scales. This behavior is consistent with a self-similar flow structure in the inertial range. Cross-field transfers, between kinetic and magnetic energy, are found to be forward but non-local in character. At low and high $Pr_{m}$, the transfers become local, and the nonlinear energy transfer is significantly suppressed. Moreover, we observe that the Hall term drives both inverse and forward transfers of magnetic energy, associated with local and non-local transfer, respectively.

authors.name: Pratik Patel, Sharad K. Yadav, Akanksha Gupta, Hideaki Miura, Rahul Pandit

papers.title: Controlling the mixing efficiency in a rotating arc-wall mixer
papers.summary: In the rotating arc-wall mixer, the flow through a plane channel is stirred by three segments of its walls, which rotate back and forth periodically, two in phase and the third in anti-phase. Using two-dimensional simulations of a Newtonian fluid, I study how the Strouhal number $St$ (0.25-8), the forcing ratio $\Lambda$ of the wall speed to the mean flow velocity (6.75-54), the Reynolds number $Re$ (0.1-20) and the Peclet number $Pe$ ($10^2$ up to the grid-limited regime) set the mixing efficiency and the chaotic transport that produces it. Throughout this range the fluid crosses a chaotic saddle without regular islands, so that mixing is limited not by a lack of chaos but by the fluid that crosses the mixer without being stretched much. The contrast of the stretching field, i.e., how unevenly the stretching is distributed, correlates with the efficiency better than the properties of the saddle ($r=-0.90$). The efficient periods lie in a window bounded by two kinematic conditions: every fluid parcel must see at least one reversal of the walls, and the fluid at mid-channel must be displaced by about one channel width per half period. Below the window, fluid escapes in pulses through the cells of an almost steady flow; above it, fluid is held near the arcs without being folded. The window closes below $\Lambda\approx7$ and moves to faster forcing as $\Lambda$ increases. Inertia strengthens the stretching but opens a weakly stirred wake, so that the efficiency is highest at moderate inertia ($Re\approx8$) and decreases beyond. The efficiency decreases only slowly with $Pe$, and a lamellar model based on the measured stretching extends the results to the Peclet numbers of applications. The energy cost grows as $\Lambda^2$ and does not depend on the period, which should therefore always be chosen inside the window.

authors.name: Teodor Burghelea

papers.title: Real-Time Single-Pixel Imaging via Exploiting Temporal Mixing: A Unified Calibration and Composite Readout Framework
papers.summary: In high-speed optical measurements and computational imaging such as in single-pixel imaging temporal mixing arising from the mismatch between modulation and the electro-optical acquisition chain is conventionally treated as an unmitigated distortion that corrupts measurement orthogonality, breaks compressive sensing priors, fundamentally limits imaging speed, and induces catastrophic reconstruction failure. Here, we establish a transferable, unified calibration and composite-readout framework for single-pixel imaging that systematically repurposes temporal memory from a readout limitation into a powerful measurement resource. Beyond achieving robust high-fidelity recovery, this engineered approach enables cost effective, lower bandwidth configurations to consistently deliver superior image quality compared to higher bandwidth reference setups across diverse operating conditions turning a historical hardware bottleneck into an active imaging advantage. Specifically, target scenes are reconstructed directly from mixed observations without the need to recover individual pattern projections, thereby significantly advancing high-speed and video-rate single-pixel imaging capabilities. Crucially, the transferability of our framework allows calibration routines established on one hardware platform (such as digital micromirror device-based setups) to be readily transferred across different optical systems (such as rotating coding disks), paving the way for calibrated temporal memory as a versatile and generalized measurement paradigm for broader computational imaging.

authors.name: Jing-Sen Li, En-Rui Zhang, Kan-Xu Jia, Yi-Zhu Zhang, Qian-Qian Bao, Shao-Ying Meng, Xi-Hao Chen

papers.title: Probing thin films and their interfaces via angle-resolved second-harmonic generation
papers.summary: Increasing demands on the performance and reliability of optical thin films stimulate the development of more sensitive characterisation methods capable of investigating thin-film interfaces or local mechanical stress. Second-harmonic generation (SHG) is a phenomenon that can serve as a non-destructive probe, tracing local symmetry changes in the film surface, bulk, and buried interfaces. Here, we investigate the decomposition of the SHG response from these three regions by combining angle- and polarisation-resolved measurements. We utilised a theoretical model of SHG accounting for multiple reflections and optical interference in a thin layer. The theory was first experimentally evaluated using Ta2O5 films deposited on different glass substrates. The fitting procedure accurately reproduced the measured SHG responses, revealing pronounced substrate-dependent variations in the buried-interface contribution, while the surface and effective-bulk responses remained similar. As the next step, we studied the reliability of the SHG signal decomposition into the surface, bulk and buried-interface components. The decomposition was evaluated by generating synthetic datasets and testing whether their retrieval was unique and accurate. The influence of film thickness, measurement noise, uncertainties in linear-optical parameters, and the polarisation channels used on the retrieval of nonlinear susceptibilities was also examined. Our results demonstrate that reliable separation of SHG contributions requires accurate linear optical parameters, global fitting of multiple polarisation channels, and sufficiently pronounced interference features, outlining the capabilities and practical limitations of SHG-based region-specific characterisation of optical thin films.

authors.name: J. Lukes, D. S. Gaur, V. Kanclir, K. Zidek

papers.title: Scattering by Small Ice Crystals in Turbulence: From Orientation Statistics to Retrieval Biases
papers.summary: Ice-cloud retrievals from polarimetric radar, lidar and submillimeter radiometry commonly assume random orientation, horizontal alignment or a prescribed flutter angle. We link the orientation dynamics of ice crystals to their scattering. Fluid-inertial torque turns small settling crystals broadside on, and turbulent velocity gradients turn them away, so their orientation depends on the dissipation rate. We combine a closed-form orientation distribution for overdamped spheroids, including rotational diffusion and turbulence intermittency, with orientation-averaged Rayleigh, Rayleigh--Gans, T-matrix and specular scattering. Turbulence enters the scattering only through the Legendre moments of the orientation distribution. In the Rayleigh regime the specific differential phase follows crystal alignment, so assuming perfectly horizontal crystals biases ice-water-content retrievals low. Combining the specific differential phase with differential reflectivity limits this bias to $25\%$ for a single size of the shapes studied. For size distributions that span the alignment transition the bound can fail, because the two observables weight sizes differently. Depolarization adds sensitivity to higher-order moments and to intermittency. At finite size the second orientation moment mainly controls the scattering cross sections and the asymmetry parameter, and for optically soft crystals its contribution vanishes $54.7^\circ$ from the vertical. Specular returns from partly aligned plates should persist for lidars pointed $3^\circ$ from nadir. An exploratory analysis of EarthCARE lidar data finds a weakly depolarizing, low-lidar-ratio signature most frequent near $-11^\circ$C, where plates grow. Degree-scale tilt widths inferred from glints and lidar require larger crystals, near or beyond the validity range of the model.

authors.name: Himanshu Mishra, Mohd. Meraj Khan, T. Narayana Rao, Anubhab Roy

papers.title: Sign-Controlled BIC Merging and Flatband Formation in C2-symmetric Photonic Lattices
papers.summary: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) on flatbands promise long-lived, weakly dispersive photons, yet their interplay remains elusive. Here, we develop a four-mode non-Hermitian Hamiltonian for $C_2$-symmetric photonic-crystal slabs. We show that the sign of the interpair coupling determines whether two Friedrich-Wintgen (FW) BICs and a symmetry-protected (SP) BIC occupy the same photonic band, a necessary condition for merging. In rectangular lattices, merging eliminates the quadratic radiative-loss term in a perfect-square form and strongly suppresses the quartic contribution, giving an effective $Q \sim k^{-6}$ scaling. Deviations from rectangular geometry induce noncollinear radiation polarizations, converting FW-BICs into quasi-BICs with $Q_{\mathrm{qBIC}} \sim (90^\circ-\theta)^{-2}$ and restoring the asymptotic $Q \sim k^{-2}$ scaling. Unlike BIC band selection, quadratic band flattening is insensitive to the coupling sign and can occur without BIC merging, even in oblique lattices. Our results reveal distinct conditions governing BIC merging, higher-order radiation suppression, and band flattening.

authors.name: Jiayao Liu, Zhuoyang Li, Zimeng Zeng, Jinpeng Wang, Zelong He, Zhaona Wang

papers.title: Particle physics science communication with grass-roots Instagram: a success story
papers.summary: Communicating science to the public is an integral part of the work of a research collaboration, not an afterthought. Institutional and collaboration-level social media accounts are often run by professional communicators rather than by practising scientists, and single-scientist ``influencer'' accounts are demanding to sustain. We describe {\em CMSatDESY}, a crowd-sourced Instagram account on which the CMS group at DESY tells its own stories, each member in their own voice. In the first half of 2026, the science communication activities through this reached 140k+ unique accounts and received 250k+ views, with an engagement rate of 7\%. We discuss experiences and best practices that can be used by other groups, and describe how the account doubles as a science communication playground for outreach training for a large particle physics group.

authors.name: Freya Blekman, Lucia Coll Saravia

papers.title: Multi-scale dynamics of deep convective self-aggregation. Part I: physical-space structures and energy variance budget
papers.summary: Vertically resolved budget analyses of frozen moist static energy (FMSE) variance within a cloud-resolving model provide a rigorous perspective on the equilibrium state of deep convective self-aggregation. The analysis reveals that the variance budget is governed by a leading-order balance between vertical variance advection and the gradient term, which quantifies the coupling between vertical covariance FMSE fluxes and the mean vertical stratification. Because vertical FMSE covariance fluxes are strictly positive throughout the atmospheric column, the sign of the gradient term is entirely dictated by the vertical gradient of mean FMSE. The primary peak of variance production occurs at the boundary layer top, driven by the interplay between sharp FMSE gradients, intensified in dry regions where the moist boundary layer decouples from the dry free troposphere, and robust vertical covariance fluxes. The persistent positivity of these fluxes implies that moist (dry), high-energy (low-energy) anomalies are systematically tied to updrafts (downdrafts), regardless of the mean gradient sign. This breakdown of classical down-gradient mixing indicates that vertical transports are governed by non-local, long-distance interactions driven by large-scale overturning circulation. The large variance produced near the boundary layer top is subsequently transported upward and dissipated in the upper troposphere, where the gradient term turns into a sink. While radiation does not directly force local variance, it indirectly shapes the budget by establishing the mean stratification. Overall, local thermodynamic forcings are translated by the overturning circulation into the spatial redistribution of variance across multiple scales.

authors.name: Lorenzo Silvestri, Paolina Bongioannini Cerlini, Andrea Cimarelli

papers.title: Moir\'e-Enabled Recursive Phase Unwrapping for Differential Atom Interferometry
papers.summary: Weak equivalence principle tests comparing different elements may be more sensitive to violations than those comparing isotopes. However, differences in effective wave vector complicate common-mode rejection of vibration noise. We propose a Moir\'e-enabled recursive phase unwrapping (MRPU) method for differential measurements with dual-species atom interferometers. The method exploits the moir\'e structure of the joint phase likelihood and temporal acceleration correlations to unwrap both phases and determine the relative acceleration. We implemented an $^{85}$Rb $\mathrm{D_1/D_2}$ line dual-scale-factor interferometer with an identical normalized transfer function and a large effective wave-vector difference to emulate different atomic species. Under $40\,\mathrm{rad}$ equivalent vibrational noise, this method achieved phase unwrapping over 5000 consecutive measurements, with a relative-acceleration Allan deviation of $1.47\times10^{-8}g$ at 997 shots. Numerical simulations under random vibrations and slow drifts show a $9.76 - 26.03\,\mathrm{dB}$ increase in the tolerable narrowband vibration amplitude. This method is promising for weak equivalence principle tests based on different atomic species, dark matter and dark energy detection, and high-dynamic-range atomic gravimetry.

authors.name: Junjie Jiang, Sitong Yan, Jiaming Wei, Chuan He, Xi Chen, Lin Zhou, Jin Wang, Ming-Sheng Zhan

papers.title: Multi-scale dynamics of deep convective self-aggregation. Part II: scale-by-scale budget and mesoscale self-similarity
papers.summary: This work investigates deep convective self-aggregation in the space of scales, extending the physical-space analysis of Part I. We introduce a novel theoretical framework by examining and deriving a generalized Yaglom equation for the second-order structure function $\langle \delta h_f^{\prime 2} \rangle$, the scale-dependent variance of Frozen Moist Static Energy (FMSE). Self-aggregation is found to be sustained by an inverse energy cascade driven by boundary-layer production and mediated by mesoscale circulations with horizontal scales $r \sim$(100-250 km). The inverse cascade of energy is found to be realized through a series of shallow and mid-level mesoscale circulations which behave in a self-similar way. Accordingly, the scale-energy variance exhibits an extraordinary collapse across all atmospheric layers onto a robust self-similar power law, $\langle \delta h_f^{\prime 2} \rangle \sim r^{6/5}$. In contrast, horizontal velocity increments show a degree of self-similarity ($\langle \delta u_r^{\prime 2} \rangle \sim r^{2/5}$) that retains a residual height dependence. Interestingly, the FMSE scaling breaks down at elevations lower than 750 m and at small local scales below 100 km, allowing us to identify the boundary layer top as a scale-dependent dividing layer where the strong stratification filters the interactions between the surface and free-troposphere, so that small scale dynamics of the low and high atmospheric layers are decoupled while those at large mesoscale are coupled. The derived scaling laws are also used to quantify the moisture-convection feedback via scale-dependent correlation coefficients that show that vertical transport strengthens with scale ($\rho_{mc\perp} \sim r^{2/5}$), while horizontal convergence weakens at the exact inverse rate ($\rho_{mc\parallel} \sim r^{-2/5}$).

authors.name: Lorenzo Silvestri, Paolina Bongioannini Cerlini, Andrea Cimarelli

papers.title: Witnessing Molecular Conformation via Optical Cycling Centers
papers.summary: Molecular conformation plays a central role in determining molecular properties and dynamics. Here, we report the production and conformer-resolved spectroscopy of cold calcium 3-hydroxyphenoxide radical (CaOC$_6$H$_4$-3-OH) in a cryogenic buffer-gas cell. Internal rotation of the hydroxyl group gives rise to distinct $anti$- and $syn$-conformers. The CaO moiety acts as an optical cycling center (OCC), enabling the $\widetilde A - \widetilde X$ and $\widetilde B - \widetilde X$ transitions of both conformers to be resolved by laser-induced fluorescence spectroscopy. Dispersed fluorescence measurements reveal diagonal vibrational branching fractions of 0.91-0.93, indicating favorable optical cycling characteristics. Following excitation of off-diagonal vibronic transitions near the calculated torsional barrier in the $\widetilde A$ state, the emission remains predominantly conformer specific, indicating that conformational identity is largely preserved over the excited-state fluorescence lifetime. These results demonstrate that a metal-centered OCC can serve as an intrinsic, site-specific optical reporter of molecular conformation, providing a foundation for repetitive optical readout and studies of conformational dynamics at the single-molecule level.

authors.name: Guo-Zhu Zhu, Taras Khvorost, Haowen Zhou, Guanming Lao, Claire E. Dickerson, Cecilia Chang, Ryan Choi, Wesley C. Campbell, Anastassia N. Alexandrova, Eric R. Hudson

papers.title: Partitioned iterative FD-SPH for fluid-rigid-body interaction: Stability and validation for lightweight floating bodies
papers.summary: This study assesses partitioned iterative fictitious-domain smoothed particle hydrodynamics (FD-SPH) for free-surface fluid-rigid-body interaction. Extending a strong-coupling framework for deformable structures, it combines volume-based hydrodynamic loads with Newton-Euler rigid-body updates. Within each time step, the mismatch between pressure-projected fictitious-fluid and rigid-body velocities is fed back iteratively. A fractional-step interpretation identifies conditions under which Passively Moving Solid (PMS) projection and Newton-Euler updates yield identical rigid-body velocities. Single-pass and iterative FD-SPH are compared under matched conditions. A two-dimensional settling-disk benchmark agrees with published results. In three-dimensional buoyancy-driven cube tests, single-pass coupling becomes unstable at specific gravities of 0.1 and 0.2. At 0.1, reducing the time-step size by a factor of 500 does not suppress the instability. Iterative strong coupling remains stable across the tested range of 0.1-1.0. Equilibrium heights and orientations agree with hydrostatic expectations and published stable configurations, respectively. Two- and three-dimensional wet-bed dam-break simulations reproduce experimental trends in wave elevation and floating-body heave and pitch. Two star-shaped rigid bodies demonstrate applicability to complex geometries without explicit interface reconstruction or surface-normal evaluation. All production strong-coupling simulations satisfy the prescribed relative-residual criterion at every time step before reaching the maximum coupling-iteration count. These results support iterative FD-SPH for lightweight and complex floating bodies in transient free-surface flows.

authors.name: Kumpei Tsuji, Ciara Galvin, Hiroyuki Omura, Naoto Mitsume, Mitsuteru Asai

papers.title: A Quantum Genetic Algorithm for Optimization of Benchmark Test Functions using Entangled Qutrits
papers.summary: Typically, quantum genetic algorithms are based on qubits, a two-level quantum system. This work investigates the optimization of Rastrigin, Rosen-Brock and Table Holder Function in comparison with Classical Genetic Algorithm (CGA), using two quantum approaches: Quantum Genetic Algorithm (QGA), and Higher-Order Quantum Genetic Algorithm (HO-QGA) based on qutrits, a three-level system. HO-QGA uses higher-dimensional quantum representations, such as entangled qutrits, to test its capability of enhanced optimization. We show that the QGA convergence rate is higher than the CGA, and the solution quality is considerably improved. Based on this study, a three-state quantum object novelly provides more capabilities than qubits in terms of computational and information resources.

authors.name: Muhammad Farooq, Mehrosh Talat

papers.title: The final stages of a Chapman-Jouguet detonation: support by its own products
papers.summary: A planar Chapman-Jouguet detonation that runs out of fuel must become a shock. We show that, when the chemical energy decreases in the direction of propagation, the wave does not pass through the local Chapman-Jouguet states. The products of the richer mixture are at a higher pressure than the local Chapman-Jouguet state, so the wave is overdriven, it loses its sonic point, and forward characteristics carry the state of the rich products to the shock. The rarefaction behind the wave removes this support only if the distance travelled since initiation is small compared with the thickness of the fuel gradient, which is rarely the case. The wave speed instead approaches an envelope given by a Riemann problem between the rich products and the local mixture, ending at the Mach number of the shock transmitted into inert gas. For strong detonations this Mach number tends to a fraction $C$ of the Chapman-Jouguet value, with $0.621<C<0.625$ for every ratio of specific heats. The mechanism is purely gas-dynamic. Shock-fitted computations with a two-step chain-branching mechanism, for gradients 1 to 1000 induction lengths thick, confirm that no sonic point forms and that the induction zone never decouples.

authors.name: Prabakaran Rajamanickam, Adam D. Weiss

papers.title: Dephasing-free plasma acceleration with millijoule picosecond lasers
papers.summary: Laser-plasma accelerators reach gradients a thousand times above radio-frequency cavities, but need joule-class femtosecond lasers firing about once per second, and electrons outrun the wave. A comb of laser lines spaced by the plasma frequency, each in its own mode of a matched channel, drives a wake moving at the speed of light. In particle-in-cell simulations a 175\,mJ, 0.5\,ps drive holds 21\,GV/m over 10\,mm with a 0.15\,rad phase drift; a test electron gains 208\,MeV, 2.6 times more than in one mode. Because the wave builds up resonantly, the required energy falls steeply with density: a 29\,mJ drive sustains 20\,GV/m, and a 10\,mJ drive, within reach of kilohertz industrial lasers, gives a test electron 170\,MeV over 30\,mm. A simulated stage transfers 5\,\% of the laser energy to the wake; the Manley--Rowe limit is about 18\,\% for five lines.

authors.name: Alexander Pukhov

papers.title: Bifurcation analysis of particulate Rayleigh-Benard convection
papers.summary: Particles carried through a convecting fluid layer exchange momentum and heat with the fluid, and so change not only where convection starts but also how it saturates. We study this coupling in the particulate Rayleigh-Benard system, in which a dilute stream of thermally inertial particles is injected at one wall and removed at the other. An Eulerian two-fluid model retaining drag, pressure-gradient, added-mass, and buoyancy forces and interphase heat exchange describes heavy particles and bubbles through a single density parameter beta. After reproducing the linear stability results of Raza et al. (2025a), we use a multiple-scale expansion and a Fredholm solvability condition to compute the first Landau coefficient a1 near onset. At low and moderate particle loading, the bifurcation is supercritical for every density ratio considered, extending the conclusion of Srinivas and Tomar (2025) for very heavy particles. At higher flux, however, Re(a1) changes sign, and the onset becomes subcritical over a broad band of density ratios, from moderately heavy particles injected below their terminal speed to most light particles. In the plane of density ratio and injection velocity, this band is bounded by lines of tricritical points. Splitting a1 by the balance equation shows that its sign is set almost entirely by the fluid energy equation, while the direct nonlinear terms of the particle equations are five to six orders of magnitude smaller. The particles thus change the nature of the bifurcation indirectly, through the base state and the linear mode they help to shape, rather than through their own nonlinear dynamics.

authors.name: Thota Srinivas

papers.title: Swimming formula in a linearly viscous fluid with anisotropic and odd viscosity tensors at low Reynolds number
papers.summary: We theoretically investigate the low-Reynolds-number hydrodynamics of a microswimmer in a linearly viscous fluid. The fluid is characterized by a viscosity tensor containing both even and odd components, and can therefore exhibit anisotropic and chiral properties absent in an isotropic Newtonian fluid. By employing the generalized Lorentz reciprocal theorem, we establish the Onsager-Casimir reciprocity for the resistance tensors of an arbitrarily shaped rigid body. We then derive a swimming formula that linearly relates the swimming velocities to the prescribed surface velocity of a microswimmer and imposed background flows. As a showcase application of the derived swimming formula, we prove that the scallop theorem holds in this class of linearly viscous fluids. Furthermore, we investigate the equations of motion for a spherical swimmer in a fluid with odd viscosity, as a representative example of the generalized linear constitutive framework. In particular, we reveal that sufficiently strong shear flows destabilize the bimodal chirotactic alignment of a microswimmer. Our results highlight how intrinsic fluid chirality and anisotropy fundamentally alter the orientational dynamics and transport phenomena of microswimmers.

authors.name: Yuto Hosaka, Kenta Ishimoto

papers.title: Influence of an oxide cap on the combustion of aluminum particles using boundary-layer resolved simulations
papers.summary: A distinctive feature of burning aluminum particles is the condensation of the primary combustion product, alumina, forming an oxide cap that covers part of the aluminum particle and alters the local combustion characteristics. This study systematically investigates the effects of an oxide cap on the combustion characteristics and interfacial processes of aluminum particles, using boundary-layer resolved simulations, considering variations in cap size, cap position relative to the flow direction, and the particle Reynolds number, $\mathrm{Re_p}$. The oxide cap modifies both the interfacial transfer and the surrounding combustion characteristics. Front caps enhance local evaporation near the junction between the cap and the aluminum body, whereas heat absorption by rear caps contributes to lower reaction temperatures. Variations in integrated heat release generally follow those in the evaporation rate. Based on the simulation results, the Lagrangian modeling framework was first revised for spherical particles. The film state is approximated using a 0.55-rule applied to temperature, species mass fractions, and pressure, from which the remaining thermophysical properties are derived. A simplified composition scheme enables film-state viscosity and fuel diffusivity to be pre-calculated as functions of temperature. Optimized Whitaker and Schiller-Naumann correlations were developed for the mass evaporation rate and drag force coefficient, respectively, showing good agreement with the simulation results. The framework was further extended to doublet particles with oxide caps. Accounting for the exposed aluminum area provides good evaporation predictions for rear caps, while front caps require a correction to the surface-averaged evaporation mass flux, particularly at high $\mathrm{Re_p}$.

authors.name: Hesheng Bao, Hongchao Chu, Shibam Bose, Heinz Pitsch

papers.title: Photonic processors that carry their own unclonable fingerprint
papers.summary: Physically unclonable functions (PUFs) derive cryptographic keys from uncontrollable fabrication disorder, removing the need to store secrets in vulnerable non-volatile memory. Programmable photonic processors are natural candidates for PUFs, because each of their many tunable interferometers carries its own fabrication imperfections. However, we show that the mesh topology itself funnels light along short paths, so that most of this disorder contributes little to the response. Here we introduce an isotropic ring routing scheme that steers light to the core of a hexagonal mesh and redistributes it uniformly towards the perimeter, suppressing a distance-dependent power decay of 14.7 dB and raising the mean Shannon entropy of the response from 1.95 to 3.48 bits by reprogramming alone. Experiments on two independently fabricated 72-unit silicon processors show that a nominally identical device cannot reproduce the target's responses even after its passive phase profile is fully compensated. Combining isotropic routing with spectral readout yields 1107 bits per challenge, exceeding previous results by two orders of magnitude, with 49.8% inter-challenge and 50.0% inter-chip Hamming distances and a 4.9% intra-chip distance. These results establish general-purpose programmable photonic processors as reconfigurable, high-capacity hardware roots of trust.

authors.name: Oxel Arnal Mart\'inez, Pablo Mart\'inez-Carrasco Romero, David \'Alvarez Outerelo, Francisco Javier Fraile-Pel\'aez, Jos\'e Capmany Francoy

papers.title: High-Speed Widefield Hyperspectral Imaging
papers.summary: Fourier-transform hyperspectral imaging is an emerging technology that combines widefield acquisition with flexible spectral resolution. Yet, it typically requires the acquisition of dense sequences of full-field interferograms during optical-path scanning, which ultimately reduces the final throughput. To circumvent this limitation, this manuscript introduces an event-based Fourier-transform hyperspectral microscopy technique that exploits the coupling of a neuromorphic event camera with a common-path birefringent interferometer operated under continuous scanning. Specifically, two complementary acquisition strategies are investigated, one with steady broadband illumination where the event stream corresponds to a derivative-like interferogram, and another with a temporal modulation of a broadband LED, which produces an intensity-like event response. Both approaches are able to retrieve the principal spectral profiles of photographic filters, showing a good qualitative match with both frame-based and spectrometer references. Compared against the typical 15-minute acquisition time for step-scan reference configuration, both methods represent a speedup larger than 3 orders of magnitude, entering real-time acquisition speeds: the derivative-based method acquires the useful interferometric range in approximately 200 ms, corresponding to an effective rate of approximately 5 hyperspectral cubes per second, whereas the modulation-assisted method achieves an experimentally measured spectral resolution of 17.9 nm at an effective acquisition rate of 2.5 datacubes per second. Finally, reflection-mode imaging and motion-compensated reconstruction of moving particles further demonstrate spatially resolved spectral recovery beyond static transmission measurements, establishing the solution as a promising technology for continuous, wide-field hyperspectral imaging.

authors.name: Joana M. Teixeira, Tom\'as Lopes, Tiago D. Ferreira, Catarina S. Monteiro, Pedro A. S. Jorge, Nuno A. Silva

papers.title: Dual Action of Electrolyte Additives in High-Voltage Li-Ion Cells
papers.summary: Electrolyte additives have outsized effects on cell performance, but determining their mechanism of action can be difficult. Here, we evaluate whether simple electrochemical tests can reveal which electrode (cathode, anode or both) is targeted by specific additives. Our experiments quantified the rates of reductive and oxidative side-reactions in NMC532 vs. graphite cells containing 12 different electrolyte formulations. We found that gains in interphasial stability were highly correlated, with successful additives decreasing both types of side-reactions by similar magnitude. This dual action could be indicative of the role of crosstalk on cell degradation, as soluble species formed on one electrode can decompose at the other end of the cell. Although electrochemical tests are insufficient for understanding mechanisms of improvement, they can reveal interesting effects that complement other characterization tools.

authors.name: Aidin I. OBrien, Bingning Wang, Stephen E. Trask, Adam Tornheim, Chen Liao, Marco-Tulio F. Rodrigues

papers.title: DUV (257 nm) LIDT of Anti-Reflective Coatings
papers.summary: Laser-induced damage threshold in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) was used to perform tests on AR coated windows intended for industrial processes. The 257 nm wavelength was generated from Yb:YAG fundamental (1030 nm) and the long-term LIDT stability (up to 100000 shots) was selected as representative for minimal industrial qualification. Selected setup for the fourth harmonics generation consists of two stages, generation of second harmonic and subsequently the fourth harmonic with 13,4% conversation efficiency. In both 1-on-1 and S-on-1 experiments, the optics coated with Al2O3/SiO2 by ion beam sputtering technique demonstrated the highest LIDT value of 0.73 and 0.5 J/cm2 respectively. Various damage morphologies, color centers, ballistic damage, delamination, and blistering were observed across the samples with respect to the 1-on-1 and S-on-1.

authors.name: Martin Mydlar (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Hana Turcicova (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Priyadarshani Narayanasamy (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Mihai George Muresan (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Ondrej Novak (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Jan Vanda (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Tomas Tolenis (ELI Beamlines Facility, The Extreme Light Infrastructure ERIC, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Jan Brajer (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia), Tomas Mocek (HiLASE Centre, Institute of Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Dolni Brezany, Czechia)

papers.title: Theory of magneto-electrokinetics in unidirectional electrolyte flow: Hydrodynamic potential and Hall effect
papers.summary: We develop a theoretical framework for magneto-electrokinetic transport in dilute electrolytes under unidirectional flow and streaming current conditions. Unlike standard magnetohydrodynamics in liquid metals, where charge carriers are electrons and conductivity is typically uniform, electrolytes exhibit spatially varying ion densities and additional forces such as osmotic pressure. In steady state, the coupled Navier--Stokes, Nernst--Planck, and Poisson equations become analytically tractable. We derive a Boltzmann-like expression for ion distributions that incorporates both the electrostatic potential and a novel hydrodynamic potential arising from the magnetic field. This potential depends explicitly on the flow profile and is not screened close to the bounding walls. Applying the theory to Poiseuille flow, we derive expressions for the induced Hall potential and demonstrate its near-linear dependence on flow velocity and magnetic field strength, while remaining largely independent of salt concentration. To validate this one-dimensional framework, we analyze the two-dimensional spatial transients near the channel entrance. We demonstrate a separation of length scales: the Hall electric field and space charge adjust to the magnetic field almost instantaneously, whereas the macroscopic salt concentration wake develops over a much longer Graetz length dictated by the P\'eclet number. We also examine a similar flow with counterions only and no added salt, determining the resulting potential and ion distributions. This work offers new theoretical tools for understanding ion transport in microfluidic and electrochemical systems.

authors.name: Yoav Tsori

papers.title: Resonant filling for long-pulse operation of EuXFEL using iterative learning based feed forward
papers.summary: A future operation scenario of the European XFEL (EuXFEL) is long-pulse (LP) mode, where the 800 superconducting radio frequency (SRF) cavities of the linac are energized with RF pulse lengths of up to 500ms. Compared to the current, short-pulse (SP) mode with less than 2ms, the dominant mechanical eigenmodes of the cavities at a few hundred Hertz pose a significant control challenge, as the RF pulse extends beyond a multiple of their periods. To improve energy efficiency of LP operation, cavities are operated at bandwidths in the range of tens of Hertz, a factor of 10 narrower than in SP. Due to peak power limitation of the proposed high power amplifiers, even the fill time surpasses mechanical mode periods. This paper presents experimental evaluation of two feed forward adaptation approaches to facilitate resonant-filling despite mechanical mode transients: In a single-cavity regulation setup, the RF drive phase is adjusted to match the Lorentz force detuning induced cavity phase shift. In vector-sum RF regulation systems, the incident phase cannot be adjusted to each cavity individually, so the concept is inverted by adapting mechanical cavity tuner drives to match each individual cavity resonance trajectory with a fixed common RF drive phase.

authors.name: Bozo Richter, Julien Branlard, Joshua Einstein-Curtis

papers.title: Triplet adiabatic potential energy surfaces for the O($^3$P) + C$_2$(X$^1\Sigma_g^+$, a$^3\Pi_u$) reaction and quasiclassical trajectory dynamics
papers.summary: We present three global adiabatic potential energy surfaces (PESs) for the O($^3$P) + C$_2$(X $^1\Sigma_g^+$, a $^3\Pi_u$) to CO(X$^1\Sigma^+$) + C($^3$P) reaction, computed at the icMRCI+Q/aug-cc-pVTZ level. This reaction is relevant to combustion chemistry, atmospheric processes, and astrochemistry. Since the energy difference between the $^1\Sigma_g^+$ and $^3\Pi_u$ states of C$_2$ is smaller than the zero-point energy, both states mix upon interaction with the approaching O atom. Consequently, the PESs exhibit a double-well topography in the reactant valley. Beyond this feature, the three PESs display markedly different topographies. The 1 $^3A''$ PES features a deep minimum 7.16 eV below the O + C$_2$ entrance channel. In contrast, the 2 $^3A''$ and 1 $^3A'$ surfaces possess shallower collinear wells ($\approx$ 5.7 eV) and strong angular anisotropy arising from avoided crossings with higher-lying triplet states. The analytical fits reproduce the \textit{ab initio} data with root-mean-square (RMS) deviations of 0.022--0.028 eV over an energy interval exceeding 13 eV. Quasiclassical trajectory (QCT) calculations reveal higher reactivity on the barrierless $1\,^3A''$ surface compared to the $2\,^3A''$ PES, where an angle-dependent entrance barrier reduces the cross sections. Furthermore, cross sections for reactions initiated from C$_2$(X $^1\Sigma_g^+$) and C$_2$(a $^3\Pi_u$) are remarkably similar for the three PESs, regardless of the initial rovibrational state.

authors.name: A. Veselinova-Marinova, S. G\'omez-Carrasco, L. Gonz\'alez-S\'anchez, A. Zanchet, P. G. Jambrina, C. Sanz-Sanz

papers.title: Flux-induced condensation in a radial geometry
papers.summary: Stirring and shear usually suppress phase separation, but transport through a boundary can induce it. We study a binary mixture that is stable everywhere at rest and fills a two-dimensional annulus. The inner boundary is semipermeable and exchanges material with a permeate held at a fixed chemical potential, so that a steady flux of one component crosses the annulus. Although this driven system carries a steady current and produces entropy, within Model B dynamics its steady state is an equilibrium profile in an effective external field that is logarithmic in the distance from the center. Its strength is not imposed from outside but set by the permeate and the permeability of the boundary. Above a threshold driving flux, a condensed annulus forms around the inner boundary. It is bounded by a stationary front whose radius depends exponentially on the ratio of the bulk driving force to the flux. The front is pinned by the effective field and does not coarsen, and the threshold flux decreases only as the inverse logarithm of the system size. The driving flux shifts the phase lines but leaves the critical temperature unchanged. Interfacial tension gives rise to a critical nucleus and to a fold, at which the condensed state ceases to exist, with a threshold that we obtain in closed form. Numerical solutions confirm these predictions and reveal a hysteresis loop bounded by two saddle-node bifurcations. By symmetry, the theory also describes cavitation around a sink.

authors.name: Yoav Tsori

papers.title: Compact GridPix Tracking: Test Beam Performance and Detector Response Modelling
papers.summary: We characterise a Timepix-based GridPix detector with a 21 mm drift length using 2.6 GeV electrons at ELSA. Tracks entering through the window at several angles are reconstructed as compact $\mu$TPC tracklets, providing position and local direction from one layer. Measured angular widths are approximately 5--10 mrad. An empirical response model calibrated to these data augments Geant4 ionisation information with gas-transport and readout effects, reproducing ten of twelve angular widths within approximately 20% and all spatial-residual widths within approximately 12%. Application without re-tuning to an independent 5 mm-drift measurement shows larger angular discrepancies. Our response model therefore provides input to feasibility studies of future compact tracking detectors.

authors.name: Dhruv Chouhan, Jochen Kaminski, Konstantinos Spyrou, Matthias Schott

papers.title: Hybrid Plasmon-Phonon Eigenmodes and Vortex States in a Graphene Ring on a Silica Substrate
papers.summary: We investigate hybrid plasmon-phonon eigenmodes and localized electromagnetic vortex states in a graphene ring supported by a dispersive silica substrate. The interaction between graphene plasmons and infrared-active optical phonons of the substrate gives rise to distinct spectral branches of surface polaritons, whose dispersion characteristics are established analytically and validated by full-wave numerical simulations. Geometric confinement of these hybrid surface excitations produces spectrally separated families of localized multipolar eigenmodes with corresponding azimuthal symmetries. Particular attention is devoted to quadrupolar eigenstates, which exhibit nearly identical normalized spatial field distributions despite their substantial spectral separation and different attenuation characteristics. We demonstrate that coherent superposition of orthogonal quadrupolar field patterns gives rise to localized vortex states with opposite azimuthal phase winding. The preservation of the spatial eigenmode structure across distinct spectral branches is consistent with a quasistatic description in which the resonator geometry governs the modal symmetry, whereas the dispersive material response determines the spectral properties. These findings reveal a route toward controlling structured electromagnetic near fields through plasmon--phonon hybridization and establish a physical basis for multiband vortex states in deeply subwavelength graphene resonators.

authors.name: Yanxu Guo, Oleh Demianyk, Vladimir R. Tuz

papers.title: How Should Candidates Be Weighted under Open-List Proportional Representation? Harmonic Weights and Dirichlet Order Statistics
papers.summary: Candidates in open-list proportional representation systems are not equally prominent, and measurements that involve aggregation over candidates therefore require some form of weighting. We address the question of how those weights should be chosen. Since weights based on realized preference votes are unavailable in advance and endogenous to the electoral outcome, we seek a priori weights that depend on list position alone, and derive them as expected ordered vote shares under a probabilistic model of the division of the list vote among candidates. The natural starting point -- the uniform distribution on the simplex -- is unrealistic, as it prescribes the same degree of concentration of the vote for every list, and under it the leading candidates become more alike as lists lengthen. The other members of the symmetric Dirichlet family require a concentration parameter, which is unknown and which there is no reason to expect to be constant across countries, parties, and elections. Accordingly, we treat that parameter as random. We prove that under a scale-invariant prior restricted to lists with at least two effective candidates, the expected share of the $k$-th candidate decays as $1/k$, and we show that over the leading positions of a long list, up to one hundred of them, the resulting weights are within 1.4 to 3.4 percent, in total variation, of the harmonic weights $(k H_n)^{-1}$, where $H_n$ is the $n$-th harmonic number. No fixed value of the parameter yields similar weights. Moreover, under the uniform distribution itself, harmonic weights are exactly the normalized expected margins between consecutive candidates.

authors.name: Daria Boratyn, Dariusz Stolicki

papers.title: High-Power Short-Wavelength Frequency Comb from Coherent Radiation of Uncompressed Electron Beams
papers.summary: High-power frequency combs at short wavelengths would open new opportunities for precision measurements and high-resolution spectroscopy. Here, we propose a frequency comb based on coherent undulator radiation from uncompressed electron bunches. An optical frequency comb serves as the seed, establishing a common phase reference for microbunching in successive electron bunches and transferring its phase coherence to short-wavelength harmonic radiation. By exploiting interference between distinct laser-induced microbunching pathways, we reduce the sensitivity of the harmonic bunching phase to electron-beam energy fluctuations, a major challenge for maintaining interpulse coherence. Start-to-end simulations demonstrate frequency comb generation in the vacuum-ultraviolet (148 nm) and soft X-ray regimes, yielding average radiation powers of approximately 1 W and 100 mW, respectively, with approximately 6 $\mu$W and 100 nW concentrated in individual comb teeth. These results establish a promising route toward high-power, phase-coherent short-wavelength frequency combs for precision spectroscopy, including searches for the nuclear transition in trapped $^{229}$Th ions.

authors.name: Chenzhi Xu, Bingyang Yan, Hanxiang Yang, Jiawei Yan, Kai Li, Haixiao Deng

papers.title: A photon-number-conserving multimode framework for pulse propagation dynamics across zero nonlinearity: Kerr-Raman cooperation and competition
papers.summary: Raman scattering in multimode fibers shifts pulse spectra to lower frequencies and transfers photons between spatial modes. When the nonlinear coefficient changes sign within the pulse spectrum, the ordinary generalized nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (GNLSE) can give unphysical predictions. Existing photon-number-conserving formulations either treat a single mode or exclude Raman scattering. We develop a time-domain multimode GNLSE that conserves photon number, includes the full Raman response and remains well defined at the zero-nonlinearity frequency. For narrowband pulses with a constant positive nonlinear coefficient, the framework reduces to the standard multimode GNLSE with instantaneous Kerr and delayed Raman terms. We then apply the framework to three coherently excited modes whose spectra shift across the zero-nonlinearity frequency. The Kerr and Raman processes first cooperate and then compete. In the first stage, both processes transfer photons into the fundamental mode, contributing about 2\% and 43\% of the initial total photon number. In the second stage, Kerr transfer drives photons out of the fundamental mode, while Raman transfer drives photons back, contributing about $-27\%$ and $+15\%$, respectively. Consequently, the fundamental-mode photon fraction rises from 20\% to 65\% and then falls to 53\%. Kerr terms that leave the modal photon populations unchanged still reshape the fields and thereby enhance Raman transfer. Moreover, changing only the relative input phases can reverse the initial Raman-driven flow into the fundamental mode, even for identical modal spectra. Taken together, the results show how instantaneous and delayed nonlinear responses, together with intermodal phase, govern photon redistribution across zero nonlinearity.

authors.name: Chao Mei, Weiye Huang, Junhong Yang, Tao Sun, Qian Gao, Jintao Fan, Peilong Yang, Xinzhu Sang, Jinhui Yuan

papers.title: Aggregating soft-photon recoil with a positive finite-step sampler
papers.summary: We model stochastic radiation reaction by aggregating soft photons into one positive recoil, retaining the local no-emission probability and two loss moments of the crossed-field QED kernel. Unlike Gaussian diffusion, the sampler preserves one-sided energy loss. Analytical synchrotron moments expose a finite-step cooling bias, which state feedback reduces. Laser and ion-channel tests probe excessive-loss risk and directed radiation spectra, providing a practical route to stochastic particle simulations without resolving individual soft emissions.

authors.name: Nina Elkina, Alexander Pukhov

papers.title: Lagrangian transport driven by travelling waves in a radially deforming circular cavity
papers.summary: A travelling deformation of a circular cavity wall can carry particles with the wave or against it. For two counter-propagating waves of azimuthal order $m$ and amplitudes $a$ and $b$, the leading axisymmetric component of the total (Lagrangian) drift scales with the intensity difference $S_3=|a|^2-|b|^2$. We obtain the radial profile of the azimuthal drift in closed form in the viscous limit, where the Womersley number $\mathrm{Wo}$ tends to zero, and by quadrature for any finite $\mathrm{Wo}>0$. The total drift is the sum of the Eulerian mean velocity and the Stokes drift. For radial wall motion with $m\ge2$ and unequal wave intensities, the total drift follows the stronger of the two waves throughout the interior in the viscous limit, although the Stokes drift changes sign with radius for all $\mathrm{Wo}$. For $m=2$ and large $\mathrm{Wo}$, the predicted total drift just inside a radially moving wall opposes the wave to leading order in wall amplitude. For the same travelling shape, the total drift there follows the wave when the wall material also moves tangentially to preserve local arc length to first order. For the radial wall at large $\mathrm{Wo}$, the near-wall profile consists of the planar Longuet-Higgins result and a closed-form curvature correction. At large $m$ the core rotation approaches Tuck's finite-Reynolds-number waving-sheet result. At $m=2$ and $\mathrm{Wo}^2=10$, moving-domain simulations recover the leading-order drift coefficients for both wall motions.

authors.name: Zijian Liu, Julian Olszewski, Jie Xu

papers.title: Fast electrons and high energy photons produced in strong-field ionization of atoms as diagnostics of multi-petawatt laser beams
papers.summary: We calculate numerically energy spectra and angular distributions of photoelectrons and X-ray photons emitted in the process of tunnel photoionization of argon by a focused laser beam of multi-petawatt power. By scanning the beam power and varying the degree of focusing and the field polarization, we show these distributions to be sensitive both to the peak laser intensity and to the field configuration in the focal spot. Investigated parameters of the laser beam correspond to those of several recently commissioned lasers of multi-petawatt power. These findings, in line with the earlier reported proposals, provide a basis for the development of a reliable ionization diagnostics of extremely intense laser fields.

authors.name: A. V. Khudov, N. V. Makarenko, A. A. Mironov, S. V. Popruzhenko

papers.title: Hydrodynamic modeling of liquid metal field emitter deformation under combined RF and DC magnetic fields
papers.summary: Radio-frequency (RF) breakdowns, also known as vacuum (or electrical) arcs and breakdowns, or electrical discharges, have been studied for over decades, but the mechanisms of the RF breakdown are still questionable. This phenomenon reduces the stability of the beam, damages the RF cavities, and thus limits the achievable accelerating field in the particle accelerator. In the case of Muon Collider, the RF cavities have to withstand an electric field of the order of multi tens of MV/m and a DC magnetic field of a few tens of teslas, with a minimum rate of RF breakdown. Different models have been proposed, and some important factors that could lead to the RF breakdown have been identified, such as the field emission current, irregularity of the surface , presence of hot particles on the surface and the role of the DC magnetic field. In this paper, we give insights to the mechanism of RF breakdowns using a hydrodynamic and a magnetohydrodynamic approach, focusing on understanding the forces that deform the liquid copper emitter. We found that if the local RF electric field is sufficiently high, it could provoke the emission of hot copper droplets into the cavity. Our simulations use the computational fluid dynamics module, the magnetic and electric field module, and the level set method in the COMSOL software to simulate the behavior of a copper liquid emitter with the Navier-Stokes equation under the influence of the pressure radiation, and the surface tension force.

authors.name: Yuan-Zhi Lim, Juliette Plouin, Guillaume Ferrand

papers.title: Full Kummer Beams: Skyrmionic textures in bichromatic light
papers.summary: In this work, we introduce full Kummer beams, the bichromatic analog of full Poincar\'e beams. To this end, we define three parameters that characterize bichromatic states of polarization and span the Kummer shape, the bichromatic counterpart of the Poincar\'e sphere. We find that, under certain conditions, full Kummer beams can exhibit skyrmionic textures with a Skyrme number that depends not only on the topological charges but also on the frequencies. These beams can also exhibit emergent behavior upon propagation, including robust, higher-order-like structures and a propagation-invariant Skyrme number over a wide range of beam-waist selections.

authors.name: Jefferson Delgado-Quesada, Miguel A. Alonso, Eileen Otte

papers.title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias alone
papers.summary: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits. We demonstrate a generic, fabrication-free alternative in which a standard commercial photodiode becomes a spectrometer through its electrical drive alone, requiring no modification of the device, no optical filter and no modulation of the light. The mechanism is bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion (OED): light of different wavelengths is absorbed at different depths, and a sinusoidal bias changes how carriers generated at each depth are collected, so that every spectrum is encoded in the shape of the photocurrent waveform over one bias period. Applied to an unmodified InGaAs PIN photodiode at room temperature, a 10 us waveform decoded by a neural network reconstructs spectra of one to three laser lines across the 80 nm of the telecom C+L band, locating the lines to 0.3-0.4 nm, counting them in about 99% of measurements and identifying their power levels, with line shifts tracked to tens of picometres. Because OED relies on universal semiconductor transport physics, the approach is material-agnostic and applies in principle to any off-the-shelf photodiode, turning detectors already deployed as power monitors into low-cost spectral sensors.

authors.name: Roi Yozevitch, Shmuel Sternklar, Ziv Glasser

papers.title: A Liquid Film Can Survive without Being Bulk-Like: Rupture and Mechanical Isotropy Set Different Thickness Limits in Lennard-Jones Films
papers.summary: How thick must a liquid film be before its middle behaves like ordinary bulk liquid? Free-standing films are the standard geometry for computing surface properties by molecular simulation and the simplest model of soap and foam films, coatings and polymer layers, yet the question is seldom answered quantitatively. We answer it for Lennard-Jones films by comparing two criteria: whether the film survives without rupturing, and whether the lateral pressure at its center has relaxed to the bulk value. Covering three interaction ranges (cutoffs rc = 3.5-7.5 times sigma), three temperatures and lateral system sizes from 20 to 100 times sigma, we find that the two criteria give different thicknesses and respond to different parameters. Films thinner than 6-7 times sigma (about 2 nm for argon) rupture within 105 tau (~0.2 microseconds); this kinetic limit hardly depends on the interaction range but grows with the lateral size of the system, and close to it rupture is an activated event. The center becomes mechanically bulk-like only at a larger thickness h*, where the tangential anisotropy computed with the Irving-Kirkwood definition falls below 0.003 epsilon x sigma^3; h* grows from ~11 times sigma (3.8 nm) to ~15 times sigma (5 nm) as the cutoff increases from 3.5 to 7.5 times sigma, but it is nearly independent of temperature and of lateral size. Between the two limits films are long-lived yet perturbed throughout. Neither the surface tension, which shows no thickness dependence, nor the central density, whose relative deficit is about 16 times smaller than the relative anisotropy, reveals this perturbation: the stress detects confinement before the structure does.

authors.name: Jose Luis Altamirano-Corona, Alfonso Lemus-Solorio, Francisco Villanueva-Mejia, Mariana Ramos-Estrada, Jose L. Rivera

papers.title: The BSM Rollercoaster, 1980-2000
papers.summary: This contribution is a personal historical retrospective on beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) physics from 1978 to the early 2000s, organized around its emotional rollercoaster.
