I trace two waves of optimism separated by a multiyear contraction of confidence, both ultimately ending in disappointment when decisive experimental confirmation failed to arrive. The story begins in 1978, when the Standard Model emerged as the front-runner. It then moves from the first wave of excitement over naturalness and Technicolor, rumored proton-decay events, and the construction of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, to the contraction of confidence in the late 1980s. A dramatic revival came in 1991, when the LEP and SLC precision data pointed toward supersymmetric unification, but it eventually gave way to renewed disappointment over the absence of superpartners and the sharpening of the LEP paradox. I also describe how the realization that Newtonian gravity had been tested only down to distances of order centimeters opened the door to large extra dimensions. Finally, I discuss how Weinberg's 1987 anthropic argument for the cosmological constant, the 1998 discovery of cosmic acceleration, and the emergence of the string landscape changed the intellectual status of naturalness itself and led to Split Supersymmetry. I have tried to describe not only what was proposed, but why these ideas felt compelling at the time, why confidence rose and fell, and how later evidence changed our sense of what could count as an explanation.

authors.name: Savas Dimopoulos

papers.title: Chiral Phonons Protected by Symmetry in a Strongly Anharmonic Helical Material
papers.summary: How chiral phonons survive anharmonic phonon-phonon interactions, which underpin lattice dynamics at finite temperature, remains poorly understood. Using an ab initio many-body approach, we study crystalline tellurium (Te), a strongly anharmonic helical crystal. We show that rotational symmetries in Te impose pseudoangular momentum selection rules on phonon-phonon interactions, restricting mode mixing and scattering at rotationally invariant symmetry points in the Brillouin zone. These symmetries protect the circular polarization of vibrational modes at finite temperature but not their lifetimes such that the dynamic chirality of handed vibrational modes persists to 600 K, even as lifetimes drop sharply. We find that the temperature-dependence of angular momentum generated by a thermal gradient is governed by lifetimes rather than chirality, decreasing by two orders of magnitude between 10 and 600 K.

authors.name: Supriyo Ghosh, Dipti Jasrasaria

papers.title: A plane-wave auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo study of silicon point defects
papers.summary: Accurately predicting the energetics of point defects remains a formidable challenge in computational materials science. For the tetrahedral silicon self-interstitial, for example, previous periodic coupled-cluster [CCSD(T)] and diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) calculations disagree by about 1.2 eV. Here, we present formation energies of silicon self-interstitials and vacancies using auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) in a plane-wave basis formulated within the projector-augmented wave framework, and compare them with the random-phase approximation (RPA) and CCSD(T). Using 16- and 64-atom cells, we demonstrate that an RPA-based correction effectively removes the two-body finite-size errors that remain after twist averaging in AFQMC for bulk silicon and for the dumbbell and hexagonal self-interstitials. With this correction, we obtain formation energies of 4.4 eV and 4.6 eV for these two self-interstitials in 16-atom cells, in good agreement with DMC and transcorrelated coupled-cluster results. For the tetrahedral interstitial and the Jahn--Teller-distorted vacancy, 16-atom cells are too small to obtain realistic formation energies; in 64-atom cells, we obtain 5.7 eV and 5.2 eV, respectively. With identical setups in 16-atom cells, CCSD(T) yields systematically lower formation energies than AFQMC, with the largest difference, 250 meV, for the tetrahedral interstitial. Our results indicate that the earlier overestimation of CCSD(T) for the tetrahedral interstitial stems from the finite-size treatment in the coupled-cluster workflow rather than from multi-configurational character of the defect.

authors.name: Moritz Humer, Faruk Salihbegovic, Martin Schlipf, Zoran Sukurma, Georg Kresse

papers.title: A Symmetry-Stratified Framework for Phase Transitions: Thermodynamic States, Critical Dynamics, and Spectral Mechanical Signatures
papers.summary: Structural symmetry, thermodynamic phase stability, and elastic-wave response provide related but distinct descriptions of a transforming solid. We formulate a symmetry-stratified framework that connects these descriptions through a finite-dimensional internal state and a parent-invariant free energy. Stabilizers classify structural states, whereas free-energy comparisons and stability conditions determine equilibrium branches and dissipative evolution. Equivariance ensures that the frozen elastic tangent inherits the structural stabilizer. Equality requires additional identifiability conditions. Little-group representations and degenerate perturbation theory then determine whether an acoustic doublet splits and the first nonzero splitting order $p$. On a selected continuous branch with order-parameter exponent $\beta$, a regular, observable acoustic gap scales as $|t|^{p\beta}$, provided critical self-energies and structural relaxation do not dominate the measurement. Explicit tensorial and cubic-to-tetragonal realizations yield linear and quadratic splitting channels, together with directionally protected degeneracies. Separate numerical benchmarks examine free-energy reconstruction, coexistence, elastic compatibility, finite-temperature spectra, and controlled critical readouts. Reanalysis of NiTi measurements illustrates effective elastic degeneracy, thermal-history dependence, and the predictive value of independently measured phase fractions. Most importantly, the framework identifies the constitutive and measurement assumptions required to infer structural changes from mechanical spectra.

authors.name: Pengfei Zhu, Leiming Du

papers.title: Distributed Fiber Monitoring on a Coherent DSP ASIC: Implementation of Longitudinal Power Monitoring
papers.summary: Coherent DSP ASICs and transceivers to date report a rich set of optical link metrics, yet these remain cumulative over the link and provide no spatial localization. This paper presents the implementation design of fiber-longitudinal power monitoring (LPM), which recovers spatially resolved power profiles from received traffic, on a coherent DSP ASIC chip. We first identify the challenges specific to DSP implementation, and describe the enabling algorithm and architecture. We then present the key design considerations for retaining the estimation fidelity of the on-chip LPM during in-service operation. On this basis, we implement LPM on a coherent DSP, a 3-nm 800G low-power DSP ASIC housed in an OSFP pluggable module, which constitutes, to our knowledge, the first coherent DSP ASIC and transceiver to perform distributed fiber monitoring and data communication simultaneously. The on-chip LPM is experimentally validated over links of up to 1005 km using 400ZR+ and 800ZR+ traffic, with no measurable impact on Q factor or module power consumption. Multi-vendor interoperability is also demonstrated, where the on-chip LPM operates on signals transmitted by third-party transceivers. These results extend coherent DSPs from cumulative to spatially resolved monitoring, allowing pluggable transceivers, deployable from DCI to long-haul, to act not only as cost-efficient transmission elements but also as distributed monitoring points across diverse optical network infrastructure.

authors.name: Takeo Sasai, Yukinobu Nakajima, Minami Takahashi, Runa Kaneko, Masanori Nakamura, Asuka Matsushita, Fukutaro Hamaoka, Etsushi Yamazaki

papers.title: Interfacing Silicon Nitride Nanophotonics with Cuprous Oxide Rydberg Excitons
papers.summary: Rydberg excitons in cuprous oxide (Cu$_2$O), the solid-state counterpart of Rydberg atoms, are hydrogen-like electron--hole quasi-particles with micron-sized wavefunctions and strong long-range interactions that promise optical nonlinearities at the few-photon level. Exploiting them in a waveguide quantum electrodynamics (WQED) setting can enable what atomic Rydberg platforms achieve only with ultrahigh vacuum and laser cooling/trapping---a guided optical mode interfaced with the Rydberg medium---while adding the scalability and advanced fabrication of integrated photonics. Here we demonstrate a monolithic, CMOS-compatible interface of Cu$_2$O Rydberg excitons with a SiN$_x$ nanophotonic waveguide. Under non-resonant excitation, excitonic emission from the Cu$_2$O microcrystal is coupled to the guided mode, routed along the waveguide, and collected from an output grating. The spectrum shows the phonon-assisted 1$s$ orthoexciton emission together with the low-lying 2$p$ and 3$p$ lines of the yellow Rydberg series. Spatially selective excitation excludes substrate background and direct scatter, and the enhanced linear polarization of the grating-collected signal identifies the TE-like guided mode as the collection channel. These results establish the complete material--device--measurement stack for a novel platform of nonlinear quantum nanophotonics based on Rydberg excitons.

authors.name: Artem Kryvobok, Hamza Ather, Julio Herreros Garc\'ia, Ziqi Niu, Abhishek Bharatbhai Solanki, Vahagn Mkhitaryan, Benjamin Cerjan, Alexandra Boltasseva, Vladimir M. Shalaev, Hadiseh Alaeian

papers.title: Topological trapping of active tracers in branched ring polymer matrices
papers.summary: Branched macromolecular architectures are ubiquitous in living systems and synthetic polymeric systems, create topologically complex media that strongly influence tracer dynamics beyond simple packing fraction-driven crowding effects. Motivated by biological systems such as amoebae, astrocytes, cytoskeletal assemblies, and cyclic bottlebrushes, we investigate active and passive tracer transport in polymeric environments of topologically distinct architectures. Here, using Langevin dynamics simulations, we focus on how polymer topology alters diffusion behavior in a branched-ring polymeric (BRP) environment. To isolate the role of intramolecular topology from monomer density, we specifically benchmark the BRP dynamics against an unlinked linear-ring polymer mixture (LRM). In general, we find that while passive tracers are largely unaffected by the polymer connectivity and bending rigidity, the self-propelled active tracers strongly distinguish between the two architectures. Increasing chain rigidity facilitates active diffusion in the unlinked LRM but strongly restricts mobility in the BRP matrix, driving a transition to pronounced long-time subdiffusion that becomes more prominent with propulsion strength. Different physical observables reveal that interconnected topological cages are formed in the stiff limit, leading to transient weak ergodicity breaking and leptokurtic displacement statistics. Further, the self-intermediate scattering function confirms that the short-range dynamics remain unaltered by the matrix connectivity, while relaxation at large spatial length scales is governed by the topological caging. Finally, varying the branch length and number, we identified an optimal branch architecture that maximizes active trapping. Our results establish that macromolecular connectivity and stiffness dominate the active transport even in the system of identical packing fraction.

authors.name: Rahul Bag, Baburao Simma, Vrinda Garg, Surya K. Ghosh

papers.title: Geometry-induced orientational trapping dictates escape of active rods in corrugated channels
papers.summary: The non-equilibrium transport of anisotropic active matter through geometrically confined environments is fundamentally governed by the interplay between self-propulsion and geometry-induced entropic barriers. Using overdamped Langevin dynamics, we reveal contrasting escape mechanisms of self-driven rods in narrow corrugated channels by comparing smoothly varying sinusoidal (SC) geometries to circular (CC) cavities with localized, uniform curvature. We observe a strictly non-monotonic dependence of the mean first escape time (MFET) with increasing Peclet number (Pe) in the CC channel, contrary to the monotonic dependence in the SC channel. This non-monotonicity emerges from a competition between activity-enhanced escape at low-to-intermediate propulsion and persistent, geometry-induced orientational trapping along the circular boundary at high propulsion, which inhibits reorientation toward the exit neck. This regime crossover is further corroborated by trajectory-to-trajectory escape fluctuations and bimodal radial probability distributions reflecting persistent wall-collision and wall-aligned sliding transport. The self part of van-Hove correlation function exhibits distinct anisotropic non-Gaussian displacements in the SC channel, in contrast to symmetric profiles with extended active-trapping plateaus in the CC cavities. These results establish local channel topology as a critical determinant of confined active transport, with direct implications for microfluidic sorting, biological navigation, and targeted drug delivery in corrugated environments.

authors.name: Baburao Simma, Rahul Bag, Hari K. Reddy, Radha Ramana, Vrinda Garg, Surya K. Ghosh

papers.title: TWIN-2: Timing Solar Radio Bursts between 180-350 MHz Against GOES and Aditya-L1 X-ray Detections
papers.summary: We have conducted continuous solar observations for approximately two and half years using the Two-Element Interferometer (TWIN) at Gauribidanur Radio Observatory (RRI). During which several solar events have been detected. Our observational period coincides with the maximum events phase of the Solar Cycle 25, providing us opportunity to analyse the evolution of the solar activity. Our analysis of two and half years data show a clear increase in the occurrences of solar events, which is consistent with the expected rise in the solar activity towards the peak phase of the Solar Cycle 25. We further investigate the detected solar radio events using X-ray observations from the space based Aditya-L1 and the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES) satellites. For the automated detection of SRBs, a machine learning suite has been trained. This also serves as an instrument for space weather monitoring. On the 7th of November 2025, a solar storm was detected by our pipeline in realtime. A brief overview of the data-processing pipeline, along with the RFI mitigation techniques employed to identify and characterize the solar events, is also presented. Observation data of two and a half years of TWIN is available for public access. The data has been used in student training programmes on solar radio data analysis, with students carrying out the analysis and contributing to the initial analysis of the detected events.

authors.name: Paneendra G N, Vinod K R, Arul Pandian B, Abhishek R, Susan Syeda, Chandana R, Dhanushree V, Ishwarya T, Manasa K N, Shiekh Saniya, Suresh A, Yashwanth R, Supriya Nayaka M K, Prabu T

papers.title: Neckpinches in a Positively Curved Market: Ricci Flow with Surgery on the Nikkei-225
papers.summary: We study the intrinsic geometry of the Nikkei-225 through the discrete Ollivier-Ricci curvature (ORC) of its empirical correlation graph, using the graph Ricci flow and surgery methodology of arXiv:2510.15942. The 226-node correlation graph, built from daily returns between January 2020 and June 2026, is ORC-spherical: every edge has strictly positive curvature before any flow, close to the equal-weight value $\kappa\approx0.502$. Under a fixed 20-iteration Ricci flow the curvature distribution polarises into a high-curvature bulk and a low-curvature minority, and cutting the low-curvature edges splits the graph into components of 184 and 42 nodes. The recursive ARCUS procedure (Adaptive Ricci Curvature Unsupervised Surgery) stops the flow at each node once a curvature gap ratio $G$ exceeds $G_{\min}$ and the surgery set is stable. With $G_{\min}=10$ and a minimum cluster size of 15, ARCUS performs 28 surgeries over 13 levels and ends in 29 terminal clusters of 2-14 nodes. The stopping rule fires at every node, with $G$ between 10.0 and 92.4, and the top-level split reproduces the fixed-schedule 184/42 partition exactly. Eight small subgraphs stop with $G<15$, so the deeper levels are conditional on $G_{\min}$. Many terminal clusters are single industries by inspection, among them nine banks, five insurers, five general trading companies, three steelmakers and three shipping lines. Two delisted stocks without price data enter as zero-correlation placeholders; with them excluded, every terminal cluster is more strongly correlated internally than with the rest of the index.

authors.name: Siddharta Laloux, Bhargavi Srinivasan

papers.title: momipy: A time-resolved momentum microscopy data analysis workflow
papers.summary: Photoemission momentum microscopy is an emerging approach to photoelectron spectroscopy that is transforming electronic band structure mapping at both laboratory-based and large-scale facilities. Its extension to time-resolved measurements has recently enabled major advances, ranging from the femtosecond imaging of exciton wavefunctions to dark-field photoelectron microscopy of light-induced dynamics and strong light-matter interactions. However, the rapid acquisition of high-dimensional data sets (including electron in-plane momenta $k_x$ and $k_y$, kinetic energy $E_\mathrm{kin}$, time $\Delta t$, and more) poses substantial challenges for data handling and analysis. A typical workflow encompasses data acquisition, exploratory visualization, calibration and targeted feature extraction, with data management ideally guided by FAIR principles. Here, we present momipy, a Python package that streamlines the momentum microscopy data analysis workflow efficiently and at low computational cost. Among other features, momipy provides interactive 4D data visualization, energy and momentum calibration, space-charge correction, and a broad selection of multidimensional data analysis routines, including binning, momentum-map extraction and time-, energy- and momentum-resolved model fitting. momipy is accompanied by a selection of interactive example scripts, supporting adoption of momipy by both experienced researchers and users new to momentum microscopy.

authors.name: Paul Werner (I. Physikalisches Institut, Georg-August-Universit\"at G\"ottingen, Germany), Wiebke Bennecke (I. Physikalisches Institut, Georg-August-Universit\"at G\"ottingen, Germany), Jan Philipp Bange (I. Physikalisches Institut, Georg-August-Universit\"at G\"ottingen, Germany), Junde Liu (I. Physikalisches Institut, Georg-August-Universit\"at G\"ottingen, Germany), Daniel Steil (I. Physikalisches Institut, Georg-August-Universit\"at G\"ottingen, Germany), Marcel Reutzel (Fachbereich Physik, Philipps-Universit\"at Marburg, Germany, mar.quest | Marburg Center for Quantum Materials and Sustainable Technologies, Marburg, Germany), G. S. Matthijs Jansen (I. Physikalisches Institut, Georg-August-Universit\"at G\"ottingen, Germany, Leiden Institute of Physics, Leiden University, Leiden, Netherlands), Stefan Mathias (I. Physikalisches Institut, Georg-August-Universit\"at G\"ottingen, Germany, International Center for Advanced Studies of Energy Conversion)

papers.title: Material optimization of optical properties of particulate products by transition matrix method and sequential global programming
papers.summary: Material optimization of nanoparticle assemblies, such as structurally coloured photonic crystals, attracts increasing interest. We combine the transition matrix method (TMM), which avoids spatial discretization of particles and surrounding medium, with sequential global programming (SGP) to optimize optical properties of particulate products by iteratively assigning predefined catalogue materials to individual particles. We derive exact separable models, reproducing the fully coupled objective under single-particle material changes, and computationally accessible first-order correct approximations for general continuously differentiable objectives. These approximations aim to capture the nonlinear, potentially nonconvex dependence on individual material variables beyond their local first-order behaviour. Within SGP, globally minimizing the particle-wise subproblems can yield substantial improvements in few outer iterations, including steps away from unfavourable stationary points, as previously demonstrated for discrete dipole approximation-based SGP. The construction exploits the decomposition of the TMM system matrix into a material-dependent block-diagonal and a material-independent coupling matrix, while the state and adjoint problems remain fully coupled. Applications include extinction, scattering quantities, and colour objectives. In a 35-particle extinction minimization problem, the objective decreases by 31.0% in 13 iterations. A fine-grid evaluation of the fully coupled objective shows that no tested single-particle material change improves the final design. For a 627-particle photonic crystal, chroma increases by 58.4-122.1% for different particle diameters in 17-42 iterations. The optimized designs favour absorbing material in layers away from the incident light, consistent with experimental findings.

authors.name: Nico Nees, Lukas Pflug, Michael Stingl

papers.title: Time-independent equivalent matrix representation for time-domain boundary element analysis of large-scale 3D acoustic problems
papers.summary: This paper proposes a time-independent equivalent matrix representation for large-scale three-dimensional (3D) acoustic analysis with the time-domain boundary element method (TDBEM). In conventional TDBEM, pair-dependent retarded times couple spatial interactions to historical boundary data, causing substantial storage and history-convolution costs. The proposed representation decouples compressible spatial interactions from propagation history, allowing reuse of the same compressed spatial representation across propagation delays and throughout time marching without additional temporal interpolation of the kernel. For conventional space-time discretizations, blockwise low-rank compression yields the compressed equivalent matrix method in the $\mathcal{H}$-matrix format (CEM-$\mathcal{H}$), with dynamic cluster-pair tracking to skip inactive interactions during wavefront propagation. For low-frequency, long-wavelength problems with a bounded number of nonzero time-lag matrices, the framework is extended to the $\mathcal{H}^2$-matrix format (CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$) using delay-consistent partitioning, shared coupling matrices, and nested cluster bases. Under sparsity and bounded-parameter assumptions, storage and per-step cost of CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$ both scale as $O(N_s)$, excluding preprocessing. Numerical results agree well with conventional TDBEM and semi-analytical reference solutions. For CEM-$\mathcal{H}$, the storage requirement for a sphere with $N_s=20,480$ is reduced from approximately 349.0 GB to 1.6 GB, with a speedup of approximately $45.4\times$. For CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$, simulations with up to $N_s=1,310,720$ are performed in the low-frequency, long-wavelength regime. A million-degree-of-freedom underwater-vehicle model is also analyzed. These results demonstrate the capability of the proposed framework for large-scale 3D transient acoustic analysis using TDBEM.

authors.name: Weiyu Zhou, Yongqiang Chen

papers.title: The Ionospheric Cut-off as a Potential Radio Technosignature
papers.summary: Radio emission generated on a planetary surface must cross the planet's ionosphere before escaping into space: below the local plasma frequency it is reflected back towards the surface. We investigate this process for broadband radio technosignatures (BRaTs) using a Chapman-layer description of photoionised atmospheres. The plasma frequency depends only weakly on stellar XUV irradiation, scaling as $Q_{\infty}^{1/4}$, implying turnover frequencies of 5-40 MHz for most terrestrial habitable-zone planets, potentially rising towards 100 MHz in extreme environments. The basic signature is simple: the continuum of a surface-origin BRaT should be strongly suppressed below a characteristic frequency that can be estimated from the XUV output of the host star, at every orbital phase and for any viewing geometry. Oblique propagation, magnetic fields, and collisional absorption broaden the cut-off into a smooth escape function, $f_{\mathrm{esc}}(\nu,\phi)$, where $\phi$ is the orbital phase. Because the day-night ionisation pattern is anchored to the substellar point rather than to the rotating surface, disc integration adds a second, more discriminating signature: the half-escape frequency $\nu_{1/2}$ varies predictably (by about 40-50 per cent over the orbit, depending on the angular emission pattern of the leakage) and remains locked to the orbital ephemeris. Finite atmospheric response times introduce modest phase lags but preserve the modulation. A low-frequency turnover alone is not unique to technology, but one that varies periodically with the orbital period would be difficult to reproduce through known astrophysical processes. Although observationally challenging, the ionospheric cut-off is a potential technosignature diagnostic and a novel probe of exoplanet ionospheres.

authors.name: Michael A. Garrett (University of Manchester, Leiden Observatory,University of Malta)

papers.title: Three-mode chimera-like states in a minimal network of active camphor ribbons
papers.summary: Chimera states are a remarkable manifestation of symmetry breaking, wherein identical units spontaneously split into coherent and incoherent groups. The term "chimera" itself is inspired by the mythological creature having parts of different animals, reflecting the coexistence of distinct dynamical behaviors within a single system. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the existence of a three-mode chimera-like state in a system of four identical camphor-infused elliptical rotors, each pivoted at a corner of a square base. When placed on a water surface, the rotors self-propel and rotate due to Marangoni-driven flows. Chemical coupling mediated through the shared water interface gives rise to three distinct collective dynamical states, namely a synchronized one, an antisynchronized one and an incoherent one. Our results validate recent theoretical work about three-domain chimeras in reaction-diffusion models, providing new insights into nonlinear dynamics and suggesting that this new type of chimera may be observed in a broad class of physical systems.

authors.name: Ratan Sarkar, Sapna Yadav, Punit Parmananda, Charo I. del Genio, Stefano Boccaletti

papers.title: Finite-Key Analysis for Multiple-Antenna Quantum Key Distribution with Continuous Variables
papers.summary: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) techniques, known for their use in wireless communications, can also find applications in quantum communications systems. This is, for instance, relevant to satellite-based quantum communications when atmospheric turbulence and the time-varying nature of the channel can make their implementation difficult. Here, we study the application of MIMO techniques to continuous-variable (CV) quantum key distribution (QKD) in the realistic setting where a finite number of signals are exchanged. We show how data collected during the brief overpass time of low-earth-orbit satellites over ground stations can be processed to estimate MIMO channel parameters, extract a secret key, and quantify the key generation rate. For $2\times 2$ MIMO settings with Gaussian encoding and heterodyne detection, our finite-key analysis indicates that MIMO CV-QKD could outperform both multiplexed (with a nominal 3~dB improvement) and single-mode (with a nominal 6~dB nominal improvement) scenarios. Furthermore, we conjecture that the ultimate enhancement of a multiple-antenna CV-QKD system can be characterized by the product of the number of its inputs and outputs.

authors.name: Masoud Ghalaii, Ahmed Q. Lawey, Mohsen Razavi

papers.title: Transition Dynamics Matter: Hidden Markov Scoring of Epileptogenic Channels in SEEG
papers.summary: Stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) represents the most effective technique for the detection of the Epileptogenic Zone (EZ) in drug-resistant epilepsy. This procedure produces a multi-dimensional signal with hundreds of components, named channels, each associated with a different brain location. In this work, we propose a joint Hidden Markov Model (HMM), in which each SEEG channel is described by a latent Markov chain, with states shared across the network and channel-specific transition probabilities. Accordingly, we develop a detection algorithm that identifies the channels belonging to the EZ by quantifying, through the Kullback-Leibler divergence, the difference between their transition probabilities in the inter-ictal period and at seizure onset. We evaluate our framework in SEEG recordings from 30 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy and compare it with a benchmark that operates in the same observation space but does not consider a latent-state structure. Compared against medically validated EZ definitions, our study shows that modeling channel-specific temporal transitions can improve EZ localization and offer a data-driven framework to investigate the latent dynamics underlying seizures.

authors.name: Giulia Tacconi, Federico Mason, Lorenzo Ferri, Elena Pasini, Lidia Di Vito, Matteo Martinoni, Lara Alvisi, Anna Scarabello, Luca Zanuttini, Francesca Bisulli, Andrea Zanella

papers.title: The long-term divergence exponent and the temporal structure of step-to-step perturbations: a simulation study in two passive walking models
papers.summary: Purpose. Divergence exponents are used to assess the local dynamic stability of gait. Human experiments have related the long-term exponent ($\lambda_L$) to the complexity of gait fluctuations. Model studies used perturbations without controlled temporal structure. The question was whether $\lambda_L$ responds to the temporal structure of perturbations in walkers without neuromuscular control. Methods. Two passive walkers, M1 (pilot) and M2 (exploratory), received step-to-step perturbations of five amplitudes ($\sigma$) and nine temporal structures (ARFIMA parameter $d$), and human stride series of free and metronome walking. Results. At constant amplitude, $\lambda_L$ increased with $d$ in both models. It was higher with free series than with metronome series or with surrogates. It did not follow $\sigma$ in M1 and followed $\sigma$ in M2. Its double dissociation from the short-term exponent was supported in M1 only. In a descriptive analysis, the condition means of $\lambda_L$ correlated with the scaling exponent of the step durations ($r = 0.980$ in M1 and 0.906 in M2). Conclusion. In two passive walkers with fixed mechanics, $\lambda_L$ followed the temporal structure of the perturbations; its specificity depended on the model. This response supports the name attractor complexity index (ACI), proposed for $\lambda_L$ from human experiments.

authors.name: Philippe Terrier (Haute Ecole Arc Sant\'e, HES-SO University of Applied Sciences,Arts Western Switzerland, Neuch\^atel, Switzerland)

papers.title: Efficient calculation of the full Laguerre-Gaussian spectrum of entangled biphotons
papers.summary: The spatial biphoton state generated by spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) enables applications in high-dimensional quantum information processing and is often described in Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) modes. However, calculating the full LG spectrum for arbitrary radial and orbital angular momentum (OAM) indices requires computationally demanding multidimensional integrations. We present a generating-function approach that analytically performs the four-dimensional transverse spatial integral without approximating the phase-matching function. The source geometry can be completely described by a few dimensionless parameters, which reduce to two parameters for wave-vector-degenerate photons with equal waists. Our derived expressions for the full LG spectrum allow for computationally efficient and numerically stable evaluation at high mode orders, addressing a crucial obstacle in previous works. To illustrate our approach, we compare OAM spectra obtained by projection onto the lowest radial order and by radially insensitive detection, and investigate how high-dimensional maximal entanglement can be approached by tuning source parameters. Our results provide a new analytical tool for efficiently characterizing and engineering high-dimensional spatial entanglement in SPDC.

authors.name: Jiabao Peng, Richard Bernecker, Stephan Fritzsche

papers.title: Quantum Zeno Effect with a Superposed Measurement Schedule in Relational Time
papers.summary: Motivated by the Page-Wootters construction in which time is a quantum clock reading and the global system state is stationary, we propose a quantum circuit that explores the observable consequences of treating measurement timing as a quantum degree of freedom. We place two Zeno measurement schedules of a driven qubit in a coherent superposition using a schedule qubit. We show that, for a fixed drive strength, the interference visibility between the two schedules depends only on the time offset between them, not on the number of intermediate measurements taken. Then we show that, for one schedule-readout outcome, the Zeno trend reverses, predicting a result that complements the standard Zeno probability. We propose a circuit implementation with physical memory qubits and show that measuring the memory register's joint $X$-basis parity distinguishes a coherent schedule from a classical or dephased one. We give the gate count and an error budget for a superconducting-qubit implementation. The Page-Wootters picture motivates this protocol and provides an equivalent stationary representation, although the predictions follow from the standard circuit description without requiring a relational-time interpretation. This is consistent with the Page-Wootters framework recovering standard quantum dynamics through correlations between a clock and the rest of the system.

authors.name: Olivia Seidel, Chiara Marletto, Jonathan Asaadi, Sara Sussman, Sayan Biswas, Vlatko Vedral

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Statistical Mechanics: Physical Concepts & Mathematical Tools
papers.summary: As anything not in equilibrium is, by definition, nonequilibrium, there is no universally agreed-upon set of topics that can constitute an exhaustive presentation of nonequilibrium statistical mechanics. At the same time, nonequilibrium statistical mechanics has transcended traditional physics to become a powerful language for complex systems. Prompted by an enthusiastic curiosity about complex systems, these cursory lecture notes attempt to elucidate some introductory concepts and techniques used in classical nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, which find successful applications not only in foundational physics, but also across other fields such as biology, ecology, economics, and sociology. Except for the specific synthesis and presentation of the material, which assumes basic familiarity with equilibrium statistical mechanics, the author claims no originality.

authors.name: Sagar Chakraborty

papers.title: Future avenues for precision oscillation measurements with compact movable reactors
papers.summary: No planned neutrino experiment is expected to surpass Daya Bay's precision on $\thone$. Doing so requires innovative strategies to reduce statistical and systematic uncertainties. In this study, we consider a futuristic program with a movable reactor antineutrino source placed within short distances ($L\lesssim 3\,\km$) from the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) detector. Due to the large fiducial mass of JUNO, even a relatively small reactor can produce a statistically significant number of events over a few years to probe the $\lesssim 8.7\% \,\nuebar$ disappearance set by $\thone$. We consider two possibilities: a $\mathcal{O}(20\mwth)$ microreactor in alcoves of the access tunnel to the underground laboratory, and a $\mathcal{O}(400 \mwth)$ unit on the surface. In both cases the reactor is observed by a small flux monitor detector near the source, while JUNO measures the antineutrino flux at two baselines, suppressing correlated flux and detector systematics. Using the measured Daya Bay per-isotope spectra and its covariance, we model a high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) core for the microreactor and a low-enriched uranium (LEU) core for the surface unit, and discuss various potential sources of systematic uncertainties and their impact on the precision of $\thone$. The underground microreactor could improve on JUNO's reach by a factor of three to four, to $\relsth \simeq 4\%$ over a decade, while the surface reactor would reach the present global-fit precision, $\relsth=2.5\%$, in about three years, provided the emission rate is monitored across reactor relocations to the sub-percent level.

authors.name: Matheus Hostert, Stephan A. Meighen-Berger, Maxim Pospelov

papers.title: A time-domain adversarial example demonstrating the failure of $H^1$ elements in $a$-$\phi$ electromagnetic simulation
papers.summary: Frequently, $H^1$ continuous finite elements are used in computational electromagnetics despite it being widely known that such an interpolation is not guaranteed to furnish reliable approximations of solutions to general initial/boundary value problems. It is mathematically more natural to use $H(\text{Curl})$ elements (edge elements) than $H^1$ elements, since the former form part of a discrete complex that respects the differential-geometric structure of Maxwell's equations while the latter do not. However, most work discussing the failure of $H^1$ elements for electromagnetics is esoteric and concrete examples demonstrating the clear advantage of edge elements are generally restricted to quasi-static, frequency-domain, or eigenvalue problems. In this work, we summarize essential facts regarding $H^1$ and $H(\text{Curl})$ elements and present a physically feasible yet intentionally adversarial time-domain eddy-current example demonstrating the failure of gauge-penalized $H^1$ elements in an $a$-$\phi$ formulation compared to gauge-free mixed scalar/edge $H^1/H(\text{Curl})$ elements. The results indicate that edge elements can be used to furnish reasonable results for general loading conditions, whereas penalized $H^1$ elements fail (e.g., converge to an incorrect state) even with mesh refinement.

authors.name: Timothy Carlson, Sanjay Govindjee

papers.title: Nonlinearly Causal General-Relativistic Superfluid Hydrodynamics: Simulating Vortex Dynamics in Neutron-Star Interiors
papers.summary: Neutron stars provide a natural laboratory for superfluid matter under extreme conditions. Its nonlinear dynamics is central to pulsar glitches, their possible links to fast radio bursts, and tidal interactions in inspiralling binaries. We develop a general-relativistic superfluid hydrodynamics framework incorporating entrainment, vortex forces, and line energy, and derive, for the first time, necessary and sufficient conditions for nonlinear causality and strong hyperbolicity. We also show that commonly used dissipative, force-balanced formulations without line tension are generically ill-posed at short wavelengths because of the Donnelly-Glaberson instability. Exploiting the analogy between vortex arrays with tension and force-free electrodynamics, we recast vortex dynamics in terms of effective electric and magnetic fields and drift velocities. This motivates a new finite-volume scheme combining constrained transport of superfluid vorticity with implicit electric-field evolution, enabling stable numerical evolution of the full system. We validate the scheme using an exact solution to the relativistic superfluid Riemann problem and Kelvin-wave dispersion relations, among other tests. Finally, we simulate dynamical, global general-relativistic two-fluid neutron-star equilibria, validate their oscillation modes, and present the first simplified calculation of superfluid interior spin-down with prescribed vortex release and repinning. The resulting stationary state retains both a net twist in the vortex array and residual differential rotation of the superfluid. Our framework thus enables nonlinear numerical studies of general-relativistic superfluid dynamics in neutron-star interiors.

authors.name: Yuan Feng, Elias R. Most, Lorenzo Gavassino

papers.title: u3lib: An AI-Ready Computational Framework for U(3) Symmetry Algebra, Wigner Coupling, and Racah Recoupling Coefficients
papers.summary: u3lib is a C++ library for U(3)/SU(3) representation-theory calculations in nuclear structure and related applications. It evaluates Wigner coupling and Racah recoupling coefficients using the procedure proposed in 2024 by Dang et al., which avoids the binomial coefficients and alternating sums used in earlier formulations. The library also provides irreducible representations (irreps), dimensions, Casimir invariants, conjugation, and tensor-product decompositions with outer multiplicities. It supports the canonical Gelfand-Tsetlin basis and the physical SU(3) $\supset$ SO(3) basis, including inner multiplicities and the transformation between the two bases. Generator routines return matrix elements in the canonical basis and reduced matrix elements in the physical basis. Python bindings mirror the C++ API. Domain skills supplied with the repository allow an AI assistant with code-execution access to call these routines from natural-language requests.

authors.name: Daniel Langr (Department of Computer Systems, Faculty of Information Technology, Czech Technical University in Prague, Prague, Czech Republic), Phong Dang (Department of Physics and Astronomy, Louisiana State University, Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA), Tomas Dytrych (Nuclear Physics Institute, Czech Academy of Sciences, \v{R}e\v{z}, Czech Republic, Department of Physics and Astronomy, Louisiana State University, Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA), Michela Negro (Department of Physics and Astronomy, Louisiana State University, Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA)

papers.title: Activity-driven motion and deformation of a circular membrane domain
papers.summary: Lipid bilayer membranes are nanometer-thin fluid interfaces characterized by both in-plane fluidity and lateral compositional heterogeneity. Cholesterol-rich liquid domains ("lipid rafts") are thought to regulate the spatial organization of membrane proteins and numerous cellular processes. While the passive diffusion and equilibrium shape fluctuations of membrane domains are well understood, much less is known about how the activity of molecular machines, such as protein pumps and enzymes, influences their mobility and deformation. Here, we analyze the dynamics of a membrane domain driven by an embedded molecular machine within the framework of two-dimensional Stokes flow. The molecular machine is modeled as a point singularity of the two-dimensional Stokes equations, including both rotational and irrotational singularities corresponding to force and source multipoles. We show that, despite being force-free, both force and source dipoles generate active flows that propel the membrane domain. For a force dipole undergoing rotational diffusion, the domain motion is diffusive at long times but exhibits a transient superdiffusive regime at intermediate times.

authors.name: Gonzalo Ferrandez Quinto, Sho Kawakami, Petia M. Vlahovska

papers.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
papers.summary: Neural-network quantum states (NQSs) exhibit a disparity in converging to the ground state during energy minimization: while the energy converges quadratically with the error in the variational wave function, other observables converge only linearly, which limits the accuracy of physical predictions. Here we show how to close this gap by introducing a new algorithm that improves the accuracy of NQSs. Our method, termed dynamical averaging, estimates expectation values by averaging over a state (or observable) evolved in real-time. Using insights from quantum information, we prove an up-to-quadratic suppression of error in arbitrary ground state observables, thus matching the fast convergence of the energy. Importantly, this improved accuracy requires neither further energy minimization nor increased model complexity, but rather exploits the effect of randomization on quantum states. We demonstrate dynamical averaging on non-integrable spin models, where it accelerates convergence and substantially reduces errors in observables.

authors.name: John M. Martyn, Rod Rofougaran, Samuel Stein, Di Luo

papers.title: Local velocimetry for atomic superfluids: from Riemann rarefaction waves to quantized vortices
papers.summary: We demonstrate local velocimetry for atomic superfluids in two dimensions (2D). Using matter-wave interferometry based on Raman--Bragg beam splitters, we map the local gradient of the phase of the superfluid's wavefunction onto displacement of the interference fringes and reconstruct the 2D velocity field. We illustrate the capabilities of this technique by applying it to two canonical problems. First, we directly observe the self-similar evolution of the velocity field in 1D Riemann rarefaction flows. Second, we map out the full 2D velocity field around quantized vortices, explicitly demonstrating the quantization of velocity circulation.

authors.name: Yansheng Zhang, Yi Jiang, Feiyang Wang, Louis Depaepe, J. Q. Matthew Chia, Christoph Eigen, Gehrig Carlse, Zoran Hadzibabic

papers.title: Light propagation in dielectric materials: a microscopic derivation of the refractive index and of the extinction theorem
papers.summary: We present a compact, self-contained derivation of the field established inside a dielectric by an incident light wave, starting from the picture of the material as a collection of polarizable atoms (or molecules) in vacuum, each driven by the incident field and by the fields re-radiated by all the others. Following the integral-equation route of Goldberger and Watson, the same few lines of calculation yield the Lorentz local field, the Lorentz-Lorenz relation between the refractive index and the atomic polarizability, and the Ewald-Oseen extinction theorem: the incident wave is cancelled inside the medium by a field radiated by the induced dipoles and replaced by a wave travelling at $c/n$. The dilute limit is connected to the forward-scattering amplitude, the optical theorem and Rayleigh scattering. We then discuss, for a planar interface, in what sense reflection and refraction are a bulk effect for s-polarized light and a combination of bulk and surface (bound-charge) effects for p-polarized light, and why that surface term must not be confused with the local-field correction, although both stem from the same depolarization mathematics. Finally, a small coupled-dipole simulation of a random, finite collection of point dipoles checks the self-consistent local-field relation numerically. SI units are used throughout. The material is intended for an advanced undergraduate course on electromagnetism and optics.

authors.name: Giancarlo Reali, Ledo Stefanini

papers.title: First-Passage Time Fluctuation Theorem and Thermodynamic Bound in Cooperative Biomolecular Networks
papers.summary: Using a pathway analysis technique, a dynamic fluctuation relation is derived for a kinetically cooperative biomolecular machine (e.g., an enzyme or a motor protein). This new relation indicates that, in the absence of hidden current, a fluctuation theorem can be established for the first-passage time of the observable process, and we show that this dramatic reduction is a general feature applicable to a wide variety of cooperative networks. This first-passage time fluctuation theorem can be experimentally tested, with its violation serving as a signature of hidden detailed balance breaking. Importantly, we obtain a compact exact expression for the integrated correction to this fluctuation theorem, as well as the general single-loop form, revealing a thermodynamic bound on the kinetic branching ratio (a measure of directionality defined as the forward-to-backward observable process probability ratio). These results provide detailed insight into the rich connections between dynamic measurements and the underlying nonequilibrium thermodynamics for cooperative biomolecular machines.

authors.name: D. Evan Piephoff, Jianshu Cao

papers.title: Dressed Subsystems in Classical Gravity
papers.summary: This paper considers the problem of consistently defining subsystems in gravitational theories. It is argued that a subsystem is a spacetime subregion in which the observables form a closed Poisson algebra. In a generally covariant theory, the location of the subregion must be determined in relation to other degrees of freedom. It is proposed that these degrees of freedom should live within the region, so that an observer can determine its edge by only measuring fields inside of it. This turns out to be equivalent to the property that observables in the subregion generate field-dependent gauge transformations on the causal complement. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that this is \textit{exactly} what is necessary for the observables to form a Poisson algebra and thus to constitute a consistent subsystem. Observables in spacelike separated "dressed subsystems" are shown to commute. Several examples are given in the context of General Relativity. Along the way, new perspectives on the covariant phase space formalism are introduced that clarify well-known issues, such as the factorization of subregions in gauge theories and the unambiguous definition of Noether charges associated with one-sided boosts. Finally, prospects for extending these results to a perturbative quantum setting are discussed.

authors.name: Pranav Pulakkat

papers.title: Higher-Order Functional Networks from Event Time Series
papers.summary: Inferring relations among the units of a complex system from their activity is a fundamental problem across many fields. Here, we introduce a method to identify functional dependencies of arbitrary order from multivariate event time series. The method maps the data onto a symbolic sequence, and uses a Bayesian framework to extract statistically significant motifs of symbols. These motifs define the hyperedges of a hypergraph, providing a compact representation of higher-order functional dependencies in their original data and enabling their analysis with network-based tools. Applications to neural and social systems reveal nontrivial higher-order dependencies associated with collective brain activity and social behaviour. Our framework thus provides a general approach for uncovering higher-order functional organization directly from event data.

authors.name: Andrea Civilini, Fabrizio de Vico Fallani, Vito Latora

papers.title: Spacetime-Foam Correlations as the Origin of Cosmological-Constant Dark Energy: Their Effects on Cosmological Evolution and Astrophysical Systems
papers.summary: Wheeler spacetime foam at the Planck scale is characterized by quantum-gravitational fluctuations that create, oscillate, and annihilate microscopic spacetime structures. We model these structures as a Planck-scale lattice using Euclidean quantum gravity on a simplicial complex. Their long-wavelength collective excitations are described by interacting scalar fields, which we call ``foamons,'' in analogy with phonons in a crystal lattice. Through Coleman--Hawking interactions, foamons couple to quantum or classical field operators at scales much larger than the Planck length. These operators provide physical infrared scales that determine the characteristic correlation lengths of the foamon fields. We use a Wilsonian renormalisation-group framework to study their scaling-invariant behaviour near infrared and ultraviolet fixed points. Integrating out the foamon degrees of freedom generates effective actions for physical field operators, with the foamon correlation lengths setting the corresponding macroscopic scales and effective couplings. We apply this framework to cosmology and astrophysics, where the Ricci-scalar sector gives rise to an effective cosmological term $\Lambda_R\sim\xi_R^{-2}$ with equation of state $p_\Lambda\approx -\rho_\Lambda$. For a cosmological correlation length $\xi_R\sim H^{-1}$, this yields $\rho_{\Lambda_R}\sim M_{\rm pl}^2H^2$, providing a possible mechanism for the small observed dark-energy scale. The effective cosmological term $\Lambda_R$ varies in spacetime and interacts with matter through its dependence on the Ricci scalar. We investigate its effects on cosmic evolution, galactic rotation curves, and the deflection of light grazing the solar surface.

authors.name: She-Sheng Xue

papers.title: Full-field-of-view aberration correction for large arrays of focused beams
papers.summary: We propose and implement an aberration correction method for the creation of extended arrays of spots well beyond the isoplanatic region of any optical system. The method relies on an extensive calibration of aberrations in terms of Zernike polynomials over the full accessible field of an optical system. We introduce a modified Gerchberg-Saxton algorithm for generating holographic phase masks creating fully corrected arbitrary arrays of spots. By applying the method to an aspherical lens, and using a liquid-crystal spatial light modulator (SLM), we increase the aberration-free field of view from 50 to 500 $\mu$m, only limited by the largest diffraction angles accessible to the SLM. This opens new perspectives for the generation of large arrays of optical tweezers, especially for neutral atom based quantum processors and simulators.

authors.name: Yohann Machu, Gautier Creutzer, Cl\'ement Sayrin, Michel Brune

papers.title: Doubly resonant nonlinear metasurfaces enabling NIR-to-UV upconversion for reconfigurable Fourier optical processing
papers.summary: Fourier optical processing underpins optical information manipulation, yet extending such operations to short wavelengths within compact platforms remains challenging. Here, we address this challenge by embedding reconfigurable Fourier-domain processing within NIR-to-UV upconversion in a doubly resonant nonlinear metasurface. When coherently illuminated at the Fourier plane with an image-bearing signal and a spatially structured pump, the metasurface generates UV images via degenerate four-wave mixing. Crucially, the spatial-frequency content of these upconverted images is selectively shaped by the tailored spectrum of the pump. To boost the efficiency of this nonlinear process, the metasurface is designed to simultaneously support a toroidal dipole bound state in the continuum and a magnetic dipole resonance, providing spectrally aligned and independently enhanced field localization for signal and pump beams, respectively. Building on this architecture, we experimentally demonstrate directional and continuously tunable filtering at the upconverted UV wavelengths. These results establish nonlinear metasurfaces as a versatile platform for Fourier optics and reconfigurable all-optical image processing.

authors.name: Jumin Qiu, Meibao Qin, Tingting Liu, Lun Qu, Xintong Shi, Feng Wu, Tianbao Yu, Qiegen Liu, Shuyuan Xiao

papers.title: Orientation dynamics of a settling spheroid in simple shear flow: bifurcations and stochastic alignment
papers.summary: We investigate the orientation dynamics of a settling spheroid in simple shear flow, combining a deterministic dynamical-systems analysis with a stochastic Fokker-Planck treatment. The dynamics is governed by competition between the Jeffery torque from the shear and the inertial torque from settling. When gravity lies in the shear plane the equatorial great circle is invariant, and the azimuthal motion on it is overdamped motion in a tilted periodic potential controlled by a single parameter $\mathcal{R}$ combining shape anisotropy and settling strength. That reduced system undergoes a saddle-node bifurcation on an invariant circle at $\mathcal{R}=1$, with the period diverging as $(1-\mathcal{R})^{-1/2}$. For oblate spheroids the equator attracts and the bifurcation converts an attracting periodic orbit into an attracting in-plane equilibrium. For prolate spheroids the equatorial equilibria are transversely unstable and the vorticity-aligned director remains the attractor at every settling strength; rapid settling draws it onto an attracting broadside slow manifold. When gravity is parallel to the vorticity axis, a particle exhibits either log-rolling or tumbling motion, depending on its shape. Noise acts differently in the two cases. The oblate problem supports azimuthal winding, for which we obtain an exact reduced current and its Kramers limit, exponentially sensitive to the P\'{e}clet number; the prolate problem shows broadside excursions about a single nematic attractor, whose rate is set by a two-dimensional quasipotential not computed here. Asymptotics at small and large $\mathrm{Pe}$, with numerical Fokker-Planck solutions at arbitrary $\mathrm{Pe}$, quantify the orientation moments across all regimes.

authors.name: Himanshu Mishra, Anubhab Roy

papers.title: Imaging the transverse component of optical near-fields in resonant photonic structures
papers.summary: We report on imaging the optical near-fields in resonant periodic photonic structures with nanometer resolution using ultrafast 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy (U4DSTEM). In particular, U4DSTEM is applied to visualize the transverse component of the Lorentz force of a synchronous near-field mode excited by an infrared femtosecond pulse in a periodic silicon nanostructure designed for the photonic acceleration of electrons. Our results show that in addition to the accelerating/decelerating force acting on the electrons in the longitudinal direction along the electron propagation, the structures can be efficiently used for transverse electron streaking at optical frequencies when excited by light with polarization perpendicular to the electron trajectory. The measured spatial profile of the excited near-field mode intensity is consistent with the numerical simulations performed using the finite-difference time-domain technique.

authors.name: Petr Koutensk\'y, Neli La\v{s}tovi\v{c}kov\'a Streshkova, Stefanie Kraus, Peter Hommelhoff, Martin Koz\'ak

papers.title: A Volume of Fluid Immersed Boundary Method for Industrial Polymer Mixing
papers.summary: Free-surface numerical simulation of polymer mixing processes requires handling rotating solid boundaries of complex shapes as well as kinematic viscosity ratios between polymer melt and air up to $10^8$. We present a finite volume method that couples a Volume of Fluid (VOF) interface-capturing scheme with a non-conforming immersed boundary (IB) method, so that moving screws are represented on a fixed mesh without remeshing. In standard segregated VOF solvers, part of the viscous stress is treated explicitly, which can lead to instabilities and severe time-step restrictions at such viscosity ratios. To address this limitation, we integrate into the VOF-IB framework a block-coupled (BC) scheme in which the full viscous stress, including its transposed-gradient part, is treated implicitly. The method is implemented in the finite volume library OpenFOAM. On a three-dimensional injection-molding test case with a generalized Newtonian melt, segregated solvers either diverge or produce spurious air-phase velocities at the time steps allowed by the block-coupled solver, which instead yields a physical solution and reduces the computing time by a factor of about 2.7 with respect to the fastest segregated run that remains physical. On the finer grid, the IB solution agrees with the conforming-mesh solution within 2% in velocity and 0.5% in pressure drop. The BC-VOF-IB solver is then applied to single- and twin-screw extruders under fully and partially filled conditions, capturing the filling dynamics and the resulting pressure build-up along the screw, demonstrating the applicability of the method to industrial geometries. The current formulation is isothermal; its extension to non-isothermal flows, required for quantitative prediction of melt temperature and viscous heating, is the subject of ongoing work.

authors.name: Emilia Capuano, Daniele Cerroni, Holger Marschall, Giorgio Negrini, Nicola Parolini, Marco Verani

papers.title: Role of Metastable Dicationic Intermediates in the Breakup of CH$_4^{2+}$
papers.summary: We investigate the fragmentation dynamics of methane dication (CH$_4^{2+}$) produced in collisions with 50-MeV C$^{6+}$ ions using the COLTRIMS technique. The method provides complete three-dimensional momentum vectors of the charged fragments, enabling full kinematic reconstruction of the fragmentation process. The dynamics are analyzed using Dalitz plots, Newton diagrams, and the native-frame method to distinguish between concerted and sequential dissociation mechanisms. The data indicate the presence of sequential fragmentation pathways for the CH$_4^{2+}$ $\rightarrow$ CH$_2^+$ + H$^+$ + H, CH$_4^{2+}$ $\rightarrow$ CH$^+$ + H$^+$ + 2H, and CH$_4^{2+}$ $\rightarrow$ C$^+$ + H$^+$ + 3H channels, consistent with dissociation via short-lived dicationic intermediates CH$_3^{2+}$, CH$_2^{2+}$, and CH$^{2+}$, respectively. From the Newton-diagram momentum distributions, we estimate half-rotational periods of approximately 180~fs, 71~fs, and 44~fs for the $\mathrm{CH_3^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{CH_2^{2+}}$, and $\mathrm{CH^{2+}}$ intermediates, respectively, providing characteristic lower-limit timescales for their survival prior to fragmentation. The experimental observations are further supported by comparisons with calculated potential-energy curves.

authors.name: Samiksha Dehru, Evan Munaro-Langlo\"ys, Aditya Yadav, Siddhanta Barnowal, Manojit Das, Harpreet Singh, Jibak Mukherjee, Rajarshi Sinha-Roy, Victor Despr\'e, Deepankar Misra, Arnab Khan

papers.title: Optothermal Actuation of Unidirectional Thermo-osmotic Flows
papers.summary: In this paper, we experimentally demonstrate the microscale direction control of thermo-osmotic flows using a focused-laser heating. The key is the off-center laser irradiation on an immobilized light-absorbing microparticle, which generates a nonuniform, asymmetric heat source. The resulting thermo-osmotic flows are evaluated using the optically trapped particle tracking velocimetry (ot-PTV), presented in our preceding paper (T. Tsuji, et al., Physical Review Fluids 11, 034901 (2026)). It is shown that the flow characteristics can be modulated by the ionic strength of a sample solution and/or the surface molecular coating of the substrate. In particular, the significance of ionic strength on thermo-osmotic flows is discussed based on the surface potential of the substrate measured by frequency-modulated atomic force microscopy.

authors.name: Tetsuro Tsuji, Shota Suzuki, Satoshi Taguchi, Haruya Ishida, Hideaki Teshima

papers.title: Drift Behavior in a Bounded-Confidence Opinion Model with Media Influence
papers.summary: People's opinions can change both from their interactions with each other and from their interactions with media sources. Bounded-confidence models (BCMs) of opinion dynamics provide one framework to study such dynamics. In a BCM, the nodes of a network are agents with continuous-valued opinions, and these agents interact with each other via the edges of the network. In this paper, we extend the original Deffuant--Weisbuch (DW) BCM by incorporating influence from two media sources --- one with a positive value and one with a negative value --- to capture the effects of a polarized media landscape. We show both numerically and analytically that our extended DW model exhibits drifting behavior in which a large cluster of opinions shifts toward one of the media agents. We analyze how the drift trajectory and speed depend on the model parameters, and we identify conditions in which drift is promoted or suppressed. Our results provide insight into how competing media sources can influence collective opinion formation in social systems.

authors.name: Oliver Zheng, Mason A. Porter

papers.title: Towards end-to-end optimization in multimaterial 3D printing
papers.summary: Multimaterial 3D printing enables the fabrication of functionally graded components, but optimizing their spatial material distribution alongside structural topology remains a formidable challenge due to high-dimensional design spaces and complex constitutive modeling. Using neural network constitutive laws in topology optimization requires their tangents and design sensitivities, which current approaches obtain by automatic differentiation through the network or derivation by hand. This paper combines sparsification, which reduces a trained physics-augmented neural network to a compact, interpretable closed-form law, with symbolic differentiation, enabling an end-to-end workflow from a new continuously varying multimaterial system to its mechanical simulation and design. By extracting closed-form, composition-aware hyperelastic constitutive laws from sparsified neural networks trained on experimental data, this approach facilitates exact symbolic differentiation of the terms required by the adjoint state method implemented with FEniCSx, circumventing the bottlenecks of applying neural network constitutive models in analysis and optimization. This pipeline is deployed on soft robotic gripper applications, demonstrating continuous composition optimization for highly anisotropic contact responses, and the concurrent optimization of macroscopic topology and material distribution under non-failure stretch constraints. This study is a step toward replacing conventional constitutive modeling and laborious empirical prototyping, establishing interpretable machine-learning models as practical, robust design primitives for advanced multimaterial additive manufacturing.

authors.name: Xue-Ling Luo, Steven Yang, Jingye Tan, Robert F. Shepherd, Noy Cohen, Nikolaos Bouklas

papers.title: Loss of positive definiteness as constraint relaxation in high-Weissenberg-number computations
papers.summary: Loss of symmetric positive definiteness (SPD) of the conformation tensor in high-Weissenberg-number computations signals that the discrete update has relaxed a constraint preserved by the continuum model. For periodic Oldroyd-B flows with nonnegative stress diffusion, a classical solution starting from uniformly SPD data remains strictly SPD. Polynomial-closure discretizations can produce negative eigenvalues from equilibrium data. For a uniform frozen state with solvent viscosity ratio $00$. In lattice Boltzmann four-roll-mill simulations at $\beta=2/3$ and $\mathrm{Wi}=50$, time-consistent force-divergence coupling crosses the velocity stopping threshold even when the eigenvalues used to compute polymer stress stay strictly positive or above $-1$ up to that crossing. Guo force-divergence and local stress-moment schemes reach $t^*=120$ despite strongly negative eigenvalues. At $\beta=1/9$ under matched forcing, the unmodified stress-moment scheme terminates. Shifted-cone projection and a smooth softplus restoring source calibrated to $-\beta/(1-\beta)$ both sustain bounded unsteady flow to $t^*=120$ while admitting negative eigenvalues. These results link numerical breakdown to how far the local growth threshold is exceeded and how the discrete polymer stress feeds back into momentum.

authors.name: Yuan Yu, Lanjin Lian, Feiyang Chu

papers.title: Direct visualization of charge dynamics by Pockels imaging in optoelectronics
papers.summary: Understanding charge dynamics in optoelectronic devices is essential because it governs carrier transport, signal evolution, and device performance. Yet, experimental access to the spatiotemporal evolution of charge remains limited. Here, we introduce Carrier Dynamics by Pockels Imaging (CDPI), a sensitive, quantitative, and non-invasive pump-probe technique based on the linear electro-optic (Pockels) effect. CDPI images the electric-field wave associated with traveling photogenerated carriers and reveals the evolution of charge clouds in space and time. This provides direct access to fundamental transport processes, including drift, diffusion, carrier-carrier interactions, trapping, and detrapping. Furthermore, the internal conduction- and displacement-current profiles are obtained from the electric-field dynamics and shown to be consistent with the externally measured current transients. Demonstrated in CdTe radiation detectors with micrometre-scale spatial resolution and nanosecond temporal resolution, CDPI is applicable to materials exhibiting a measurable Pockels effect, including electro-optic semiconductors, oxides, halide perovskites, organic materials, and emerging low-dimensional systems, providing a platform to investigate charge transport across optoelectronics.

authors.name: Adriano Cola, Antonio Valletta, Isabella Farella, Vaclav D\v{e}di\v{c}, Lorenzo Dominici

papers.title: Transition Density Matrix in Spin-Adapted TDDFT
papers.summary: The transition density matrix between different excited states is important for calculating optical response properties and first-order nonadiabatic coupling matrix elements. Spin-adapted TDDFT (SA-TDDFT) has eliminated spin contamination, achieved minimal spin-completeness, and has been found to have important applications in conical intersections, bond dissociations, diradicals, and triradicals. In this work, we propose a unified formulation for calculating the transition density matrix of excited states from SA-TDDFT. This formulation starts from the second-quantized equation-of-motion (EOM), approximates the expansion of the translation operator, and naturally obtains the relaxed and bilinear parts of the matrix. In the closed-shell and random phase approximation (RPA) limit, this formulation is compared with formulations from quadratic response and pseudo-wavefuntion methods respectively. Computational results demonstrate the accuracy of our method and importance of the relaxed term.

authors.name: Xiaoyu Zhang

papers.title: Extremes on Rewind: Generating 1,000-Member Ensembles Initialized at a Final Condition
papers.summary: Scenario planning for rare, high-impact events often requires massive ensembles to stochastically sample relevant trajectories. Although autoregressive weather emulators can efficiently generate such ensembles, isolating trajectories of interest requires sifting through petabytes of data, a challenge that grows with lead time and rarity. In contrast, a non-autoregressive foundation model like Climate in a Bottle video (cBottle-video) can directly sample trajectories terminating in extremes, avoiding large-ensemble search. We use cBottle-video to generate 1000-member ensembles with start- and/or final-conditioning across three extreme events: the 2021 Pacific Northwest (PNW) heatwave, Superstorm Sandy, and Hurricane Ian. The antecedent 500 hPa geopotential height ($z_{500}$) spread in final-conditioned ensembles is 84--89\% as large as the forecast spread in start-conditioned runs, suggesting diverse pathways to each extreme. For the 2021 PNW heatwave, final-conditioned ensemble members begin uniformly warmer than reanalysis and stay warm, replacing the observed rapid intensification with persistent antecedent heat. For Superstorm Sandy, the leading modes of $z_{500}$ at the antecedent end of the final-conditioned ensemble explain 48\% of the variance in track latitude for ensemble members whose storm is detected at the first frame, and about 11\% of those members begin with lower central pressure than Sandy. For Hurricane Ian, variation in the first landfall location among final-conditioned trajectories underscores the potential for exploring diverse intermediate hazard exposure.

authors.name: Jerry Lin, Mu-Ting Chien, Mansi Sakarvadia, Elizabeth A. Barnes

papers.title: Measurement and Optimal Targeting of a Hidden Scatterer in a Complex Environment Utilizing Fisher Information
papers.summary: A complex, non-Hermitian scattering system with a high degree of multiple scattering and interference is often treated as a black box, described simply by the relationship between a set of incoming and outgoing waves of a given frequency or energy. The scattering matrix S that describes the system is a non-unique, generally sub-unitary matrix that reveals very little about the microscopic processes that are responsible for the observed scattering. We form the Fisher information operator $F_x$, a Hermitian matrix, utilizing a derivative of S with respect to the value of some varying parameter x of the system, associated with a localized perturbation, and experimentally demonstrate that the principal eigenvector of Fx can be used to quantitatively measure changes in the value of parameter x using only information from the scattering matrix. We propose a "discrete feedback loop" protocol enabled by the knowledge we gain from the Fisher information operator, that repeatedly determines the counter perturbation necessary to return a varying parameter to some fixed benchmark value. A further application of the Fisher information operator for energy focusing that utilizes the principal eigenvector excitation is demonstrated through compelling indirect evidence of targeting within a complex system. These methods are experimentally demonstrated to work even in the presence of time-reversal symmetry breaking due to absorption and/or loss of scattering reciprocity.

authors.name: Nadav Shaibe, Jared Erb, Steven M. Anlage

papers.title: Unified Approach to Controlling Scattering in non-Hermitian Systems
papers.summary: The ability to controllably manipulate non-Hermitian wave scattering environments has been used to discover exotic scattering phenomena such as scattering exceptional points and coherent perfect absorption, and create numerous applications including signal routing, filtering, imaging, sensing, wireless power transfer, etc. We introduce the concept that many of these applications and phenomena are fundamentally governed by singularities of the scattering matrix. With this understanding, our demonstrated ability to control the location of the scattering singularities themselves can be used to enhance current applications and develop new ones. In generic complex scattering systems, there is an abundance of topologically protected scattering singularities corresponding to complex zeros of various functions of the scattering matrix. We show that with just three tunable parameters we can create the conditions for nearly any scattering singularity at arbitrary frequencies in such systems. With five tunable parameters, we demonstrate that more complex scenarios can be accomplished, such as making disparate singularities coincident or placing singularities at different frequencies. A benefit of systems with tunable parameters is that generic complex systems can be re-purposed to exhibit many different useful properties solely by reconfiguring their tunable parameters. A particularly interesting scattering phenomenon is coherent perfect absorption, where a specific wavefront injected into the system is completely absorbed, with no energy reflected or transmitted through any channel. After creating the conditions for this singularity at an arbitrary frequency, we can find and inject the coherent perfect absorption wavefront and demonstrate output-to-input power ratios as low as 1x10^{-10}, 2x10^{-8}, and 3x10^{-8} in a quarter bowtie microwave billiard with two, three, and four ports, respectively.

authors.name: Jared Erb, Nadav Shaibe, Steven M. Anlage

papers.title: Efficient Spin-Orbit Coupling in Algebraic Diagrammatic Construction Theory: A State-Interaction Approach
papers.summary: Spin-orbit coupling and electron correlation play important roles in a broad range of chemical and physical phenomena. In this work, we systematically assess the performance of single-reference algebraic diagrammatic construction combined with state interaction (SI-ADC) for describing electronic structure in the presence of spin-orbit coupling. We find that second-order SI-ADC methods (SI-ADC(2)) achieve zero-field-splitting accuracies comparable to those of higher-level and more computationally demanding approaches, including variational four-component ADC and two-component ADC methods based on spin-orbit effective Hamiltonians. We further demonstrate the broad applicability of SI-ADC by evaluating a diverse range of spin-orbit-coupled properties, including electron affinities, ionization potentials, neutral excitation energies, core-ionization energies, and magnetic g-tensors, for systems ranging from small molecules to transition-metal complexes and f-block compounds. Across these applications, SI-ADC(2) methods provide consistently accurate results, likely benefiting in part from favorable error cancellation between electron-correlation and spin-orbit effects. In contrast, SI-ADC(3) methods are generally less accurate, particularly for systems containing transition-metal and heavy elements. Overall, these results establish SI-ADC as an efficient and broadly applicable framework for incorporating spin-orbit coupling into ADC calculations of electronic and spectroscopic properties.

authors.name: Nicholas Yiching Chiang, Rajat Majumder, Terrence L. Stahl, Ning-Yuan Chen, Alexander Yu. Sokolov

papers.title: Chiral Temporal Structures in Molecular Rotational Dynamics
papers.summary: We introduce chiral rotational wavepackets: coherent superpositions of a few low-lying rotational states of a molecule for which the expectation value of a molecular axis traces a three-dimensional chiral trajectory in the laboratory frame. The handedness is a dynamical property of the quantum state rather than of the equilibrium structure, and we show that it can be imprinted on linear rotors as well as on spherical and symmetric tops. We derive the action of space inversion, time reversal, and their product on such wavepackets in the Wigner $D^J_{MK}$ basis, and define the rotational enantiomers of a given wavepacket. To quantify their handedness we introduce two derivative-based pseudoscalar measures: a geometrical measure built from the curvature and torsion of the trajectory, which is even under time reversal, and a dynamical measure, which is odd under time reversal. The latter is shown to be proportional to the geodesic curvature of the trajectory projected onto the unit sphere, which links it, via the Gauss--Bonnet theorem, to the solid angle enclosed by the projected trajectory and to the parallel-transport holonomy of a molecule-fixed vector. Finally we show that a nonzero geometrical measure is a sufficient condition for the wavepacket to exhibit true chirality through its orientation trajectory in the sense of Barron.

authors.name: A. G. L\"ohr, O. Smirnova, M. Mirahmadi

papers.title: Multiscale Reconstruction of Weighted Networks from Coarse-Grained Data
papers.summary: Network reconstruction from partial information is usually performed at the same resolution level at which constraints are observable.
