This becomes problematic when only coarse-grained information is available, while the relevant process occurs at a finer scale. Here we employ the multiscale model of weighted networks introduced in a companion paper and turn it into a probabilistic framework for reconstructing weighted networks across arbitrary aggregation levels. The model is built to preserve its functional form under coarse-graining, so that global parameters calibrated on an observable aggregate layer can be transferred to finer layers without refitting. We test the method on two empirical systems with different aggregation mechanisms. In the International Trade Network, countries are aggregated into geographic macro-regions and the observed coarse-grained layer is used to infer the underlying country-level network. In the Dutch production network, sectoral flows are reconstructed across the hierarchical industrial classification, using coarser sectoral layers to infer finer ones. In both geographical and sectoral settings, we benchmark our genuinely multiscale reconstruction method against a state-of-the-art weighted reconstruction model calibrated directly at the target resolution, and therefore using additional information available at the same (finer) scale at which performance is evaluated. Despite this informational disadvantage, our method recovers the fine-scale binary structure with high accuracy, improving precision, specificity, accuracy and maximum degree-error diagnostics, while remaining nearly equivalent in sensitivity.

authors.name: Mattia Marzi, Frank P. Pijpers, Diego Garlaschelli

papers.title: Multiscale Renormalization of Weighted Networks
papers.summary: Recent progress in network renormalization has identified various ways to transform network representations consistently across resolution levels. In particular, the renormalization flow describing how random graph models transform under node aggregation has identified a fixed point corresponding to an aggregation-invariant model that preserves the form of the connection probability across arbitrary scales. While this probabilistic multiscale approach has successfully been used to model real-world networks, construct latent-space node embeddings, and reconstruct finer-grained versions of aggregate network data in a principled resolution-invariant way, it has so far been restricted to binary graphs. Here we reformulate multiscale network renormalization for weighted random graphs. Via a generating-function approach, we identify a weighted multiscale model whose full probability law, encoding both link creation and weight assignment, has an invariant compound-Poisson form under arbitrary node aggregation. The renormalization rules that transform parameters across aggregation levels allow the ensemble to be calibrated at one level and applied at another, enabling consistent modeling and reconstruction of weighted networks across arbitrary scales.

authors.name: Mattia Marzi, Frank P. Pijpers, Diego Garlaschelli

papers.title: Non-flat new Tsallis holographic dark energy with the Granda-Oliveros cutoff: DESI DR2 and growth tests
papers.summary: Holographic dark energy ties the dark-energy density to an infrared length. We study new Tsallis holographic dark energy (NTHDE) with the local Granda-Oliveros (GO) cutoff $L^{-2}=\alpha H^2+\gamma\dot H$ in a curved universe and test it with background and growth data. The background is an autonomous system with exact results. The dark energy splits into a matter-like part, a curvature-like part and an accelerating part. The coefficient of $(1+z)^2$ in $H^2/H_0^2$ is $R_k \Omega_{k0}$ with $R_k>1$, while distances measure $\Omega_{k0}$; the Ricci cutoff gives $R_k=1$. The nucleosynthesis bound and the future fold singularity of the flat model remain valid with curvature. With Pantheon+SH0ES supernovae, cosmic chronometers and DESI DR2 BAO, the model fits slightly better than flat $\Lambda$CDM ($\Delta\chi^2=-2.82$) and gives a flat universe, $\Omega_{k0}=-0.001^{+0.041}_{-0.043}$. Its Bayesian evidence is comparable to that of $\Lambda$CDM with Union3 supernovae ($\ln B=+0.53$), while $\Lambda$CDM is preferred with Pantheon+SH0ES ($\ln B=-2.66\pm0.24$). The model reproduces the evolution of dark energy preferred by DESI: its effective equation of state has $w_0=-0.88^{+0.11}_{-0.07}$ and $w_a=-0.48^{+0.42}_{-2.15}$ and crosses $-1$ near $z\simeq0.6$, and this comes from the Tsallis deformation. A forecast shows that standard parametrizations recover the curvature of the model without bias, although $R_k$ itself is degenerate with the dark-energy evolution. Linear growth with 18 $f\sigma_8$ data leaves these results unchanged and gives a clear test: if the matter-like part does not cluster, growth is slower, and a CMB-normalised amplitude allows only $\Omega_d^{(m)}\lesssim0.03$.

authors.name: Umesh Kumar Sharma, Pankaj, Bramha Dutta Pandey, P. Suresh Kumar

papers.title: Localization Landscapes based on the Green's Matrix of Non-Hermitian Optical Scattering Systems
papers.summary: The Filoche--Mayboroda (FM) localization landscape predicts where the spatially localized modes of a self-adjoint elliptic operator reside without diagonalizing it, but the construction fails for the complex, non-normal Green's matrix G of an open scattering array of electric dipoles. We propose three real-valued, positive landscapes built from the Feinberg--Zee hermitization of G: a regularized Gramian inverse (Gram), the diagonal Schur block that carries the Metz--Neri--Rogers spectral density (SY), and the full hermitized inverse contracted against a uniform source (TM) or an isotropic polarization pair (TE) (Herm). The three form a progression from spectrum-blind to fully hermitization-faithful, agree in the limit $z\to 0$, and diverge where it matters: at nonzero spectral shift SY resolves modes that Gram collapses, and Herm resolves modes that SY collapses. We demonstrate the progression on random and deterministic aperiodic scattering arrays with a wide range of structural correlations, extend to the vectorial case of transverse electric polarization (TE), and provide rigorous pointwise envelope bounds for the Spec and Herm landscapes, a physical argument for the spatial compactness of long-lived modes, and a complete numerical recipe in the appendices.

authors.name: Luca Dal Negro, Hari Sundar

papers.title: Persistent A-homotopy of Networks: free groups and periodic structures
papers.summary: We study how loop classes in a network change when cycles up to a prescribed length are declared contractible. The resulting sequence of quotient groups contains the fundamental group of the clique complex at length three and the graph $A$-fundamental group at length four. Its mod-two abelianisation has a barcode whose death scales are the lengths in a minimum cycle basis. This separates the choice of a network filtration from the choice of local loop relations and provides a computable connection between persistent $A$-homotopy and persistent homology. We illustrate the construction on lattices, Watts--Strogatz networks and nine benchmark networks. Filling the plaquettes of a periodic square lattice recovers the fundamental group of the torus. In the Watts--Strogatz simulations, the normalised largest death scale falls below the normalised mean path length over the sampled range, while most clique-homology classes survive the square relations at small rewiring probabilities. The power grid has fewer surviving classes but a longer tail of death scales than five degree-preserving randomisations. We also examine connectivity graphs of maximal cliques in ego networks. Explicit certificates establish non-trivial $A$-classes even though the original ego clique complexes are contractible. The group construction and its linear summary answer related but distinct questions about which loop relations a network model permit.

authors.name: Milan Rajkovic

papers.title: Entropy: the Route from the Gaussian Field to the Statistical Mechanics of the Thermal Radiation
papers.summary: Maximum Entropy or canonical typicality applied to the electromagnetic field can provide starting points for arriving at the Bose distribution of the photon numbers of thermal radiation, but they rely on statistical postulates whose experimental testability is controversial. Here we start from the experimentally verifiable assumption of Gaussianity of the electromagnetic field. We analyze the field by projecting it onto orthonormal time-frequency basis functions with unitary bandwidth duration product that represent field's orthogonal time-frequency modes. Through the Glauber-Surashdan representation, we see that the joint density operator of the modes in the photon number basis factorize into diagonal density operators with geometric coefficients of individual modes, while the mean photon occupations of the modes remains still unknown. Imposing Clausius' relation on the entropy rates and energy rates of the independent modes we get Bose's mean photon occupancy. Thus, our main claim is that for the first time Bose statistics is obtained under explicit, experimentally verifiable statistical assumptions, without any assumption that is not experimentally verifiable. From the mean occupation numbers, the Boltzmann distribution of the energy of matter particles of the material that generates/absorbes the radiation is then derived by retracing in the backward direction the Einstein-Feynman detailed balance.

authors.name: Arnaldo Spalvieri

papers.title: Buffer-Gas-Assisted Fluorescence Spectroscopy of Molecular Ions
papers.summary: Sustained fluorescence detection of generic molecules has been challenging due to the lack of cycling transitions and limited photon budgets. We demonstrate a nondestructive method for continuous fluorescence of strongly rovibronically open molecular ions, $^{232}$ThF$^+$. Effective quasi-cycling transitions are established by room-temperature buffer-gas collisions, which replenish the population back to the laser-addressed states. In situ images and rotationally resolved spectra are obtained without optical repumping or auxiliary atomic readout ions. Combined with low-background spectroscopic detection, this approach achieves a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 6 in a 1 s exposure on the P(1) line of $^{232}$ThF$^+$, despite a thermal population of only approximately 0.17% in the addressed state at room temperature. The ability to repeatedly interrogate trapped ions is particularly promising for scarce molecular samples, broadband spectroscopic searches, and in situ monitoring of molecular reactions.

authors.name: Jinyue Jiang, Kenji Shu, Huaxu Dan, Xing Fan

papers.title: Fourier-domain Crosstalk and Leakage Correction for Binary-Encoded Fourier Single-Pixel Imaging
papers.summary: Digital micromirror devices enable high-speed Fourier single-pixel imaging (Fourier-SPI), but their binary modulation introduces quantization errors that degrade the reconstructed image quality. In particular, each binarized Fourier probe contains non-target Fourier components, thereby distorting the corresponding Fourier-domain measurement. This Letter presents a Fourier domain correction framework that characterizes these errors using the Fourier-domain response matrix of the decoded binary Fourier patterns. Accordingly, a response-matrix-based Fourier-SPI measurement model is established by partitioning the matrix into components associated with the sampled and unsampled frequencies, thereby decomposing the quantization error into sampled-frequency crosstalk and unsampled-frequency leakage. This model established a generalized correction framework, termed Fourier Crosstalk and Leakage Correction (FCLC), alongside two simplified methods: Fourier Sampled-Frequency Crosstalk Correction (FSCC) and Fourier DC Crosstalk Correction (FDCC). FSCC is implemented via an inversion-free Richardson-type iteration, whereas FDCC admits a closed-form solution. Numerical simulations and experiments across multiple binary encoding strategies reveal that the proposed framework improves reconstruction fidelity without modifying the binary patterns or acquisition process.

authors.name: Chongwu Shao, Yue Cao, Wei Zhang, Xiao-Peng Jin, Yinran Shen, Shijian Li, Xu-Ri Yao

papers.title: GPROF V08: Improving Satellite Precipitation Estimates Across a Heterogeneous Constellation of Passive-Microwave Sensors
papers.summary: Precipitation estimates from the passive microwave observations (PMW) of the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) mission serve a wide range of scientific, societal, and economic applications. The Goddard Profiling Algorithm (GPROF) is the operational precipitation retrieval used to produce the level-two precipitation estimates for the GPM mission. This study presents GPROF V08 - the most recent version of GPROF and a major update aimed at improving the accuracy of precipitation estimates from the GPM constellation. GPROF V08 replaces the single-pixel Bayesian retrieval scheme used by earlier GPROF versions with a convolutional neural network (CNN). Implementing the algorithm for the full GPM constellation required addressing several challenges such as the generation of synthetic observations suitable for training CNN retrievals, which has been described in the first part of this two-part study. This second part describes the final, operational implementation of GPROF V08, which adds a finetuning stage to the training to overcome remaining uncertainties in the synthetic training data. We extensively validate the new GPROF V08 algorithm for principal GPM sensors against reference precipitation estimates from combined radar and radiometer retrievals from GPM and TRMM as well as independent ground-based reference measurements. While the magnitude of improvements varies by sensor and surface type, the retrieval accuracy for all assessed sensors is improved. Although challenges such as the persistence of climatological biases (which remain of the same order as for GPROF V07) persist, GPROF V08 constitutes a substantial advancement in spaceborne precipitation monitoring. Since the improvements are robust across all assessed GPM sensors, the update is expected to improve the full historical GPM precipitation record and thus benefit a wide range of downstream datasets and applications.

authors.name: Simon Pfreundschuh, Paula J. Brown, Christian D. Kummerow

papers.title: A Paired Monte Carlo Intensity-Ratio Method for Incorporating Detector Resolution in Amplitude Analysis
papers.summary: Finite detector resolution can bias resonance parameters and fit fractions extracted from amplitude analyses. We present the paired Monte Carlo intensity-ratio method for incorporating resolution effects into amplitude analysis. The method uses ratios of reference intensities evaluated at paired truth-level and reconstructed kinematics to reweight the Monte Carlo normalization and approximately account for detector resolution. A resampling study of simulated $D^+\to K^+\pi^+\pi^-\pi^0$ decays shows that the method substantially reduces resolution-induced shifts in fitted resonance widths. Likelihood evaluation uses intensity calculations and normalization sums, avoiding a response convolution at each data event.

authors.name: Zhenxuan Li, Liping Yang, Bai-Cian Ke, Liaoyuan Dong, Minggang Zhao

papers.title: Run it Back: Autoregression vs. Video Diffusion for Final-Conditioned Weather Trajectories
papers.summary: Low-likelihood, high-impact extremes are projected to increase in severity and frequency in a warming climate. Sampling the precursors that lead to these events traditionally requires massive ensembles that scale poorly with lead time and rarity, and typical rare-event sampling and ensemble-boosting methods do not show how a single extreme might arise from diverse synoptic precursors. Recently, Lin et al.\ (2026) showed this is possible with final-conditioned 66-hour trajectories (trajectories constrained to end at an observed state) from cBottle-video, a pre-trained, off-the-shelf video diffusion climate emulator not explicitly fine-tuned for this task (Brenowitz et al., 2025). However, its ensembles were underdispersed and geostrophically inconsistent, and it reproduces conditioned frames only approximately, hindering autoregressive rollout. Here, we train Rewind-AR, a backward-in-time probabilistic autoregressive model with a FourCastNet~3 backbone (Bonev et al., 2025), and generate final-conditioned ensembles for the same three cases: the 2021 Pacific Northwest heatwave, Hurricane Ian, and Superstorm Sandy (in the Supplementary Information). The leading modes of Rewind-AR's antecedent 500 hPa geopotential height explain far more of the across-member variance than cBottle-video's for both hurricane position and heatwave surface temperature, and Rewind-AR better reproduces the day-over-day heatwave intensification observed in ERA5. Finally, geostrophic inconsistencies close to the conditioning frame seen in cBottle-video are not reproduced by Rewind-AR. Nevertheless, up to 22\% of Rewind-AR members become numerically unstable within 66 hours, so improving rollout physical consistency and stability over long lead times is a natural next step.

authors.name: Jerry Lin, Elizabeth A. Barnes

papers.title: Projection of global daily CO2 emissions in 2026
papers.summary: Global fossil-fuel combustion and industrial-process CO2 emissions remain close to historical highs, yet the recent slowdown in growth is difficult to assess before conventional inventories become available. We project emissions for 2026 and examine daily departures during major climate and energy disruptions. We fit Prophet models to the latest five years of Carbon Monitor activity estimates for 47 region-sector series. We use these models to project daily emissions for October-December and combine them with activity estimates through September. Global emissions are estimated at 38.0 Gt CO2 in 2026, 34.1 Mt CO2 (-0.1%) below 2025. The hindcast-adjusted range for the annual change is -0.9% to +0.7%. Five September-cutoff hindcasts show lower mean daily errors and larger mean absolute annual biases for Prophet than for a seasonal-naive benchmark. Regional increases total 0.331 Gt and decreases total 0.365 Gt, so 95.1% of the 0.696 Gt gross movement cancels in the global sum. China contributes the largest reduction (-0.243 Gt), concentrated in industry and ground transport, whereas India contributes the largest increase (+0.222 Gt), led by power and industry. Heat-period power anomalies differ among countries and can be muted by summer averaging, while aviation and shipping show different disruption and recovery profiles. Resolving the near-zero global change reveals where reductions are concentrated and where continued growth offsets them, providing a timely basis for assessing the breadth of mitigation progress.

authors.name: Tao Li, Zhu Deng, Philippe Ciais, Steve J. Davis, Ling Ye, Zhu Liu

papers.title: Design and Modeling of Graded Base III-Nitride HBTs for High-Frequency Applications
papers.summary: This work analyzes the high-frequency performance constraints of AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) and proposes a novel band-engineered graded base N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBT and evaluates the RF performances. Unlike conventional p-GaN base designs, we propose a graded base in the N-polar orientation which offers polarization-induced hole accumulation with quasi-electric field-assisted minority carrier transport. The proposed design simultaneously mitigates the longstanding current crowding, Webster effect, and conventional base resistance limitations. Using well-calibrated two-dimensional TCAD simulations, the proposed compositionally graded base HBT projects peak f_T/f_{MAX} of 190/200 GHz with a power density (V_{BR}I_{MAX}/8 > 20 W/mm), offering a promising pathway toward simultaneous high-frequency and high-power GaN millimeter-wave electronics.

authors.name: Md Saklain Morshed, Chandan Joishi, Ijaas Mohamed, Siddharth Rajan

papers.title: Deciphering the role of Al$_2$O$_3$ formed during isothermal oxidation in a dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi$_{2.1}$ Eutectic High-Entropy Alloy
papers.summary: In recent times,there has been a significant volume of work on Eutectic High Entropy Alloys (EHEAs) owing to their remarkable castability combined with excellent mechanical properties,which aids in clearing obstacles for their technological applications. One of the most common EHEAs,which has been of enormous interest at present, primarily owing to its solidification and tensile behavior, is AlCoCrFeNi$_{2.1}$. However,to aim for high-temperature applications,oxidation behaviour of material is one of the major aspects that needs to be extensively investigated.To this end,the present work aims to study the phases evolved during oxidation at elevated temperatures as high as 950 and 1000$^\circ$C in AlCoCrFeNi$_{2.1}$ using XRD and also to determine the rate law followed for isothermal oxidation of this alloy at 950 and 1000$^\circ$C,in order to understand the role of Al$_2$O$_3$ phase formed during isothermal oxidation at 950 and 1000$^\circ$C.

authors.name: Mainak Saha

papers.title: Spectrally Robust Photon-Pair Generation in Topological Waveguide Arrays
papers.summary: Harnessing topological effects offers a route to protect quantum states of light from imperfections, potentially enabling more robust platforms for quantum information processing. This capability is particularly relevant for active photonic circuits that generate quantum light directly on-chip. However, the impact of topology on the spectral properties of parametric processes, crucial for scalable quantum photonic circuits, remains largely unexplored. Here, we address this question by investigating photon-pair generation via spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) in nonlinear waveguide arrays, combining experiment and theory. A systematic comparison of uniform, trivial, and topological Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) arrays reveals that only the topological configuration preserves a stable SPDC resonance spectrum under coupling disorder, with fluctuations in the resonance wavelength reduced by more than an order of magnitude. An analytical model captures the origin of this robustness in the band-structure properties of the interacting modes. Numerical analysis further shows that each SSH array can operate as a robust photon-pair source, enabling stable interference between multiple such sources and the generation of high-dimensional entangled states with high fidelity. These results establish nonlinear waveguide arrays as a promising platform for harnessing the interplay of topology and nonlinearity in quantum photonic circuits.

authors.name: A. Zecchetto, J. -R. Coudevylle, M. Morassi, A. Lema\^itre, M. I. Amanti, S. Ducci, F. Baboux

papers.title: Data-driven Reduction of Transfer Operators for Particle Clustering Dynamics
papers.summary: We develop an operator-based framework to coarse-grain interacting particle systems that exhibit clustering dynamics. Starting from the particle-based transfer operator, we first construct a sequence of reduced representations: the operator is projected onto concentrations and then further reduced by representing the concentration dynamics on a geometric low-dimensional manifold and an adapted finite-state discretization. The resulting coarse-grained transfer operator is finally estimated from dynamical simulation data by inferring the transition probabilities between the Markov states. Applied to systems with multichromatic and Morse interaction potentials, the reduced model reproduces key features of the clustering process, including transitions between cluster configurations and the emergence of metastable states. Spectral analysis and transition-path analysis of the estimated operator reveal implied time scales and dominant transition pathways, providing an interpretable and efficient description of particle-clustering dynamics.

authors.name: Nathalie Wehlitz, Grigorios A. Pavliotis, Christof Sch\"utte, Stefanie Winkelmann

papers.title: On the Coupled Cluster Doubles Truncation Variety of Four Electrons
papers.summary: We extend recent algebro-geometric results for coupled cluster theory of quantum many-body systems to the truncation varieties arising from the doubles approximation (CCD), focusing on the first genuinely nonlinear doubles regime of four electrons. Since this doubles truncation variety does not coincide with previously studied varieties, we initiate a systematic investigation of its basic algebro-geometric invariants. We show that for $4$ electrons in $n \geq 13$ orbitals, the CCD truncation variety is not a complete intersection, and we present numerical and symbolic evidence that for the remaining cases it is a complete intersection defined by $\binom{n-4}{4}$ quadrics. Using representation-theoretic arguments, we uncover a Pfaffian structure governing the quadratic relations that define the truncation variety for any $n$, and show that an exact tensor product factorization holds in the distinguished limit of disconnected doubles. We connect these structural results to the computation of the beryllium insertion into molecular hydrogen ({Be$\cdots$H$_2$ $\to$ H--Be--H}), a small but computationally challenging bond formation process where multiconfigurational effects become pronounced.

authors.name: Fabian M. Faulstich, Vincenzo Galgano, Elke Neuhaus, Irem Portakal

papers.title: Spatio-temporal air flow properties in a 3D personalised model of the human lung
papers.summary: We propose a multi-scale lung model to investigate spatio-temporal distributions of ventilation variables. Lung envelope and large airway geometries are derived from CT scans; smaller airways are generated using a physiologically consistent algorithm. Tissue mechanics is modeled using nonlinear elasticity under small deformations, coupled with local air pressure from fluid dynamics within the bronchial tree. Airflow accounts for inertia and static airway compliance. Simulations employ finite elements. Using this model, we explore spatio-temporal airflows and shear stresses distributions.

authors.name: Jonathan St\'ephano, Micha\"el Brunengo, Riccardo Di Dio, Thomas Laporte, Benjamin Mauroy

papers.title: Beads, springs and fields: particle-based vs continuum models in cell biophysics
papers.summary: Quantitative modeling has become an essential tool in modern biology, driven by advances in both experimental techniques and theoretical frameworks. Powerful high-resolution techniques now provide detailed datasets spanning molecular to tissue scales, allowing us to visualize cellular structures with unprecedented detail. In parallel, developments in soft and active matter physics have established a robust theoretical basis for describing biological systems. In this context, two main modeling paradigms have emerged: particle-based models, which explicitly represent discrete components and their interactions, and continuum models, which describe systems through spatially varying fields. We compare these approaches across biological scales, highlighting their respective strengths, limitations, and domains of applicability. To keep our discussion biologically relevant, we focus on five systems of fundamental importance: the cytoskeleton, membranes, chromatin, biomolecular condensates and tissues. With this Review, we thus aim to provide a framework for both theorists and experimentalists to select appropriate modeling strategies, and highlight future directions in biophysical modeling.

authors.name: Valerio Sorichetti, Juraj M\'ajek, Ivan Palaia, Fernanda P\'erez-Verdugo, Christian Vanhille-Campos, Edouard Hannezo, An{\dj}ela \v{S}ari\'c

papers.title: Hierarchical Reconstruction of Time-arrow from Multi-time Correlations
papers.summary: The entropy production rate (EPR), a key measure of thermodynamic irreversibility in thermodynamics of small systems, is difficult to determine directly in experiments, motivating lower-bound-based estimation from observations. However, a systematic framework for organizing increasing amounts of the irreversibility information in experimental state observables into progressively tighter bounds remains lacking. Here, we show that multi-time correlations of a class of state observations naturally encode this information to provide a hierarchy. By defining a reconstruction operation as a combination of correlations, we obtain a sequence of lower bounds on the EPR. Correlations of higher order capture the thermodynamic information at greater temporal depth, thereby capturing more irreversibility and yielding tighter bounds. Under ideal conditions, this hierarchy converges to the full EPR in the limit of infinitely dense observations over a finite time window.

authors.name: Yijia Cheng, Ruicheng Bao, Zhonghuai Hou

papers.title: Perturbations in the parametrized wormhole spacetime and their related quasinormal modes
papers.summary: We study electromagnetic perturbations and the associated quasinormal modes (QNMs) of parametrized static, spherically symmetric wormhole spacetimes, focusing on Damour-Solodukhin and braneworld geometries as well as their galactic extensions. Using the Bronnikov-Konoplya-Pappas (BKP) parametrization, we express the metric functions in terms of a compactified radial coordinate and characterize the spacetime through far-field and near-throat parameters. The far-field coefficients govern the asymptotic structure and post-Newtonian behaviour, while the near-throat continued-fraction expansion captures the strong-field geometry near the throat. We first apply the parametrization to isolated wormholes and identify its range of validity, showing that the non-analytic metric functions can limit the applicability of the BKP scheme. Moreover we have shown that such issues can indeed hamper the primary ringdown waveform. We then extend the framework to a galactic Damour-Solodukhin wormhole embedded in a Hernquist dark matter halo. Imposing observational bounds from the shadow of Sgr A$^*$, we constrain the galactic compactness and deformation parameters and obtain an observationally viable parametrized metric. Within the allowed parameter space, we compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using the transfer matrix method and analyze the corresponding time-domain ringdown signals. We find that the damping rate is more sensitive to galactic compactness, whereas the oscillation frequency remains comparatively stable. Although the spectral shifts are small within the shadow-allowed region, the framework provides a systematic link between geometric parametrization, shadow constraints, and dynamical response. Our results establish an observationally consistent parametrized description of wormhole perturbations for strong-field tests of horizonless compact objects.

authors.name: Shauvik Biswas, Sayan Chakrabarti

papers.title: Superheating field of clean superconductors near the type-I--type-II boundary: the low-temperature Meissner stability limit of niobium
papers.summary: We calculate the low-temperature superheating field $B_{\rm sh}$ of clean superconductors near the boundary between type-I and type-II superconductivity, with particular emphasis on Nb. Ginzburg--Landau theory is not applicable at low temperatures, while previous microscopic calculations have been limited to either the large-$\kappa$ regime or the dirty limit. The clean, low-$\kappa$ regime relevant to Nb has therefore remained unresolved. We solve the self-consistent nonlinear nonlocal Eilenberger problem for the Meissner state and then analyze its stability against small perturbations. For a Nb-like material with $\kappa_{\rm GL}=0.7$, we obtain $B_{\rm sh}\simeq 290\,{\rm mT}$ at $T/T_c=0.2$, using $B_{c0}\simeq 200\,{\rm mT}$. For a TESLA-shaped Nb accelerator cavity, this corresponds to an intrinsic Meissner-stability limit of about $67\,{\rm MV/m}$.

authors.name: Takayuki Kubo

papers.title: Optimal parameterization of nonequilibrium generalized master equations from discrete-time experimental data
papers.summary: Kinetic analyses of experiments often require coarse-grained descriptions, but complex systems rarely conform to the widely used modeling assumptions of Markovianity and thermodynamic equilibrium. Memory is indeed a general and often inevitable consequence of coarse-graining. Markov state models (MSMs) are a popular choice of coarse-grained description, but require microstate assignments---which are rarely experimentally tunable---to macrostates that minimize memory. Generalized master equations (GMEs) circumvent this limitation of MSMs by explicitly capturing memory. However, GMEs are difficult to parameterize and usually formally approximate in the experimentally relevant discrete-time setting. Here we introduce a maximum-likelihood-based procedure to parameterize formally exact, physically feasible, discrete-time generalized master equations from experiments and simulations in and out of equilibrium. By adapting algorithms typically used in optimal transport, we construct physical-constraint-satisfying conditional-maximum-likelihood estimators of both exact Nakajima-Zwanzig memory kernels and time-convolutionless GME propagators in discrete time. Applying these estimators to three examples---experimental recordings of F\"{o}rster resonance energy transfer in an ion channel, experimental nanoparticle tracking of a processive molecular motor, and simulated folding of a benchmark protein domain---we recover kinetic parameters including relaxation rates, irreversibilities, dwell times, and first-passage times. These results establish discrete-time GMEs as a physically and statistically principled alternative to MSMs for kinetic analyses of experimental and simulated biomolecular systems.

authors.name: Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, J\'er\'emie Klinger, Grant M. Rotskoff

papers.title: Active Learning for Calibrating Entangling Gates via Surrogate-Based Optimization
papers.summary: High-fidelity quantum gates require precise tuning of many classical control parameters, and drift in these parameters necessitates periodic recalibration that takes time and qubit resources. Physics-based calibration can be efficient, but it requires a validated and high-fidelity model of the quantum gate under the given classical control and environment. A high-fidelity model is expensive to build, especially as systems scale, and will have to be periodically re-validated as system parameters drift. Here, we present a physics-agnostic active-learning framework that identifies optimal control parameters from noisy measurement outcomes. A generic Gaussian process with a heteroskedastic noise model set by quantum projection noise is used to model the score landscape of the calibration sequence. Bayesian optimization simultaneously learns the calibration landscape and locates its optimum. We validate the technique by calibrating a two-qubit trapped-ion entangling gate. In simulation, where the ground-truth landscape is known, we find that the surrogate accurately models the three-parameter landscape and the calibrated infidelity saturates at a level set by the number of shots per evaluation. Validation on the Sandia Quantum User Testbed shows that the physics-agnostic protocol works on an experimental system with four calibrated parameters, needing an average of 44$\pm 11$ evaluation points at 100 shots per point to model the calibration landscape and find the optimal parameter set. These results show that active learning with physics-agnostic surrogate models can calibrate quantum gates.

authors.name: Caleb Walton, Patricia Garc\'ia-Caspue\~nas, Filippo Zacchei, Ana Larra\~naga, Melissa C. Revelle, Edward C. Tortorici, Brian K. McFarland, Daniel S. Lobser, Christopher G. Yale, Susan M. Clark, Steven L. Brunton, Sara Mouradian

papers.title: Physics-guided machine learning for sim-to-real calibration of NV diamond magnetometers
papers.summary: Ensemble nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond enable robust magnetometry in unshielded environments, yet deployment remains bottlenecked by complex calibration and a reliance on external references. Conventional statistical machine learning requires massive training datasets and suffers from severe simulation-to-reality mismatches. To address this, we introduce a physics-guided hybrid machine learning framework that embeds Zeeman splitting directly into the learning pipeline. In an ablation study, our model demonstrates a nearly 3-fold improvement in precision and a 372-fold reduction in mean prediction bias over a purely statistical baseline. Furthermore, anchoring scalable synthetic data generation with just 49 sparse experimental seeds circumvents physical data scarcity while incorporating real-world non-idealities. Evaluated across a hybrid dataset of over 19,000 spectra spanning a 400 G dynamic range, the framework bridges the simulation-to-reality gap and achieves robust scalar field prediction, transferring effectively to raw, uncalibrated experimental data. Operating with minimal computational overhead on standard commercial hardware, the model achieves sub-4 ms inference times per spectrum, demonstrating strong viability for real-time edge deployment.

authors.name: Jonathan Daniel, Sangwoo Lee, Jesse Hernandez, Emanuel Suarez, Jinhee Lee, Je-Hyung Kim, Martin Y. Kim

papers.title: Randomized Block Davidson Eigensolvers for Plane-Wave Density-Functional Theory
papers.summary: Iterative diagonalization is the dominant cost of plane-wave density-functional theory (DFT), with search-space orthogonalization scaling particularly quickly with problem size and the number of target states. We present a randomized block Davidson-type eigensolver that replaces Euclidean orthogonalization with randomized Gram-Schmidt in a sketched inner product, requiring only a single pass over the basis while keeping its conditioning bounded independently of the input vectors. This modification changes only the Rayleigh-Ritz step, which becomes a definite generalized Hermitian eigenproblem. Ritz extraction remains exact, preserving true Ritz pairs and the interlacing property that makes each band energy an upper bound on the true one. The method is implemented in mixed precision for CPUs and GPUs from a single Julia code, interfaces matrix-free with DFTK, and is released in the open-source RandESC library. On sparse test problems with a fixed number of eigenpairs, the sketched solver overtakes its deterministic counterpart beyond matrix dimensions of about $2\times 10^4$ and is $25\%$ faster at $5\times 10^5$. In full self-consistent field DFT calculations, the benefits of sketching depend on the application case. With standard pseudopotentials and plane-wave cutoffs, efficiency gains are limited. As the number of requested states grows with system size, orthogonalization savings are offset by the generalized eigenproblem. However, some highly accurate pseudopotentals require larger cutoffs, and in this regime, the randomized solver is measurably better by $6\%$ overall. Its relative efficiency also improves as simulated systems get larger.

authors.name: Moritz Gubler, Taejun Park, Augustin Bussy, Johannes Laute, Nicola Marzari, Iurii Timrov, Laura Grigori

papers.title: Magnetic field induced modulation of heat transport in CrPS$_4$ probed by TaIrTe$_4$ transverse Seebeck thermometry
papers.summary: Understanding and controlling heat flow in low-dimensional magnetic materials is central to thermoelectrics and spin caloritronics. One of the challenges is the absence of sensitive probes of small, field-dependent modulations in thermal transport. Here we demonstrate transverse Seebeck thermometry using exfoliated TaIrTe$_4$ as a probe of thermal conductivity modulated by an external magnetic field on a van der Waals magnet, CrPS$_4$. With a temperature gradient oriented at $45^\circ$ to its principal crystallographic axes, TaIrTe$_4$ exhibits a transverse thermopower exceeding $200~\mathrm{\mu V\,K^{-1}}$ for 900 nm wide and 30 $\mu$m long electrodes, enabling precise detection of variations in the local temperature gradients. Exploiting this with CrPS$_4$ in a nonlocal geometry, we resolve distinct field dependent thermal conductivity changes associated with both the spin-flip and spin-flop magnetic transitions which we attribute to variations in the magnon$-$phonon coupling in CrPS$_4$. At 5 K, the transverse Seebeck response is modulated by more than 8$\%$ by an external magnetic field, demonstrating strong magnetic control of heat transport in CrPS$_4$. This all van der Waals platform offers high sensitivity to modulations of thermal conductivity and a broad adaptability to a wide range of exfoliated magnetic systems.

authors.name: Krishnaraajan Sundararajan, Sergio Alvarruiz, C\'edric A. Cordero-Silis, Majid Ahmadi, Marcos H. D. Guimar\~aes, Jagoda Slawinska, Joseph Barker, Bart J. van Wees

papers.title: Impact of Surface Preparation on the Propulsion of Catalytic Janus Colloids and Implications for Reproducibility
papers.summary: Platinum-coated polystyrene (PS) Janus particles (JPs) propelled by the catalytic decomposition of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) are a widely used model system for active matter, yet reported speeds for similar particles and fuel concentrations differ by more than an order of magnitude. Broad adoption of these materials requires increasing consistency in the preparation and achieving improved repeatability in their behavior. Herein, we focused on two routine, but rarely reported, preparation steps that we found to alter the particle speed. First, we found that pre-exposing the platinum cap to H2O2 before cell assembly increased the mean speed by a factor of 2.4. The size of this effect depended on batch history, where an aged batch responded strongly, while a freshly prepared batch sped up by only 16%. Second, we found that plasma cleaning of the glass substrate decreased the speed 2.7 times. In a 120 $\mu$m cell the suppression was the same at both walls even when only one wall was treated. The suppression grew with the treated glass area per unit fluid volume, which pointed to species released into the bulk solution rather than to a change at the wall. Plasma-cleaned glass released more ions into water than untreated glass, and XPS detected an ionic metal fluoride on the plasma-cleaned surface. A model in which the released ions lower the speed through the solution conductivity reproduced the measured speeds in all four cell geometries. Of the 17 published studies compared here, pre-activation is reported in only four studies and substrate cleaning in only six studies. We propose a minimum reporting standard for the preparation and associated speed measurements of catalytic Janus particles.

authors.name: Muhammad Haroon (Case Western Reserve University), Mitchell Lau (Case Western Reserve University), Christopher L. Wirth (Case Western Reserve University)

papers.title: The two-component picture of soft hadron production: Regge exchange, duality, and resonance cascades
papers.summary: The fragmentation regions of soft hadronic collisions approach energy-independent limits. Benecke, Chou, Yang, and Yen stated this hypothesis of limiting fragmentation in 1969, and Feynman gave it a parton-model formulation the same year. Measurements from the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings (ISR) to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) show this approach. Fischer and co-workers interpret the NA49 spectra from the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) as the sum of a target and a projectile component, each the decay of an excited hadronic system. This review traces the theory behind that two-component picture. It examines the hypothesis that the hadronic tools that predate quantum chromodynamics (QCD) suffice for the soft, non-perturbative domain of QCD. Regge exchange organizes the fragmentation region in triple-Regge form and supplies the diffractive mass law of the excited systems. Finite-energy sum rules and the two-component duality of Harari and Freund equate averaged towers of resonances with that exchange. Duality therefore motivates describing the excited systems in hadronic degrees of freedom. The cascade description has five predecessors, namely the fireballs of Niu, the novas of Jacob and Slansky, the clusters of Hwa, Good-Walker diffraction, and the two-stage dissociation of Hama. A companion paper (arXiv:2611.11570) assembles these pieces into HEART (Hadronic Excitations And Resonance Transitions), an event-level cascade of two-body hadronic transitions, and fits it to the NA49 data. The review closes with the fragmentation-region measurements that would separate a resonance cascade from a string, namely the isospin of forward baryons, local strangeness balance, and forward resonance signals.

authors.name: Ondrej Chvala

papers.title: Gravitational radiation from a particle in circular orbit around a wormhole: the nonrotating case
papers.summary: In this paper, we have generalized Poisson's(1993) calculation for the case of gravitational radiation from a particle in a circular orbit around a black hole to the case of the wormhole. Considering the motion of a test particle around a Schwarzschild like wormhole and using Teukolsky formalism, we have obtained an analytical result of flux at infinity under the assumption of small velocities. Focusing on the 22-mode, we have found a novel 0.5PN order term beyond the quadrupole order, which vanishes in the black hole limit. On the other hand, all higher order terms are getting modified in such a way that they give correct correspondence in the black hole limit. We have further corroborated our results with the numerical investigations, which show that the two waveforms match well when the particle lies far from ISCO. Thus, our work provides one of the first attempts toward the study of the post-Newtonian waveforms involving wormholes (ECOs).

authors.name: Shauvik Biswas, Sayan Chakrabarti

papers.title: QCap: a physics-corrected graph neural network for the capacitance matrix of any planar superconducting device layout
papers.summary: Electromagnetic simulations of device layouts to extract capacitance are computationally intensive, a major obstacle to accurate design of circuit devices. Machine learning models can bypass these simulations, but previous approaches have been restricted to layouts using only particular components, and require thousands of simulations of those same components as training data. We present QCap, a model that accurately predicts the Maxwell capacitance matrix of an arbitrary superconducting device layout in seconds, compared to minutes to hours of Ansys Q3D simulations. We develop a novel design-embedding algorithm that converts the layout into a universal graph format, allowing the model to work with any layout created with any tool. To achieve high accuracy, we obtain a coarse physics prior from a fast method of moments simulation of capacitance, then train the model to correct this prior. On 4,009 test designs withheld from training data the model outputs agree with Q3D simulations to a median error of 0.177%, and on never-seen component families it stays below 1% error. We demonstrate the model's scaling by obtaining the capacitance matrix of a 9-superconducting-qubit device in 12 seconds on a laptop (compared to 19.9 h and 228 GB of memory in Ansys) with sub-percent error, and capacitance of a (too large to simulate) 100-qubit, 781-conductor device in 3.4 min on a laptop. We provide the open-source models and data on SQuADDS and Hugging Face. Our results provide a powerful tool for large-scale accurate circuit design and guide the development of models to bypass other physical simulations.

authors.name: Sadman Ahmed Shanto, Saikat Das, Eli M. Levenson-Falk

papers.title: Electric combined-field-only P1 Galerkin BEM for PEC scattering with scalar Helmholtz operators
papers.summary: We develop a Galerkin boundary element method for the indirect electric combined-field-only integral equation (ECFOIE) for perfectly electrically conducting obstacles with smooth surfaces. The method is free of low-frequency breakdown and of spurious resonances. It applies scalar Helmholtz operators componentwise, so that fast scalar solvers can be reused, with less memory than a Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) discretization. The iteration count of the Calder\'on-regularized ECFOIE (R-ECFOIE) is constant under mesh refinement and, with a complex-wavenumber Calder\'on regularizer, grows only mildly with frequency. The discretization uses continuous, nodal piecewise-linear basis functions on flat triangular meshes, with essentially as many unknowns as an RWG discretization, and tangential and normal projections and the mean curvature of the obstacle's surface carry the vector structure. On flat meshes the curvature is concentrated on the edges, and we average the edge measure obtained from the first variation of area over vertex patches, which gives sparse curvature matrices. At low frequency, four Lagrange-multiplier constraints on the induced charge and on the longitudinal dipole moments of the far field keep the R-ECFOIE accurate in the quasi-static regime, tested on scatterers eight orders of magnitude smaller than the wavelength. Under mesh refinement, the errors decrease at about second order. A Helmholtz resonator, a rounded Fichera cube, and a smoothed Stanford bunny are compared with electric field integral equation (EFIE) solutions, and the first two also with electrostatic references at extreme low frequency.

authors.name: Carlos P\'erez-Arancibia, Catalin Turc

papers.title: Coupling of TQFTs to QFTs and SymTFT interfaces from bordisms
papers.summary: M-theory local models may exhibit torsional cycles and other non-trivial topology which interpolate between quantum field theory sectors localized at singularities and the asymptotic regions of the local model. We show that such structures give rise, in standard decoupling limits, to additional topological sectors which can couple non-trivially to the localized QFT. From a symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) perspective, the physical boundary conditions associated to such local models are modified. We give a construction of SymTFT interfaces from geometric bordisms interpolating between the local singularity and the asymptotic boundary. We apply this construction to the circle compactification of a frozen $D_5$ singularity, identifying a topological interface between the $\mathbb{Z}_4$ SymTFT of the full theory and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ SymTFT of its local $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ gauge sector. We show that the resulting coupling between the gauge theory and an additional topological quantum field theory accounts for the apparent mismatch between electric and magnetic symmetries of the frozen theory.

authors.name: Max H\"{u}bner, Ling Lin, Daniel Robbins, Subham Roy

papers.title: Scherk-Schwarz Compactifications: From Circles to Strings
papers.summary: This review is written with a simple question in mind: what does one need to know to enter the literature on Scherk-Schwarz compactifications? It is organized as a sequence of questions that a graduate student might naturally ask, together with the concepts, calculations, and formal tools needed to work through the literature. The discussion starts at an elementary field-theory level and gradually develops toward more advanced aspects of supergravity, orbifolds, quantum effects, and string theory. Phenomenological applications are deliberately left aside.

authors.name: Karim Benakli

papers.title: Quiver-Invariant Triality between Brane Brick Models
papers.summary: We study quiver-invariant triality between 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theories described by brane brick models associated with toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds. The dual theories share the same gauge groups, field content and E-terms but have distinct J-terms. We present an explicit pair of such brane brick models and identify the sequence of triality mutations relating them. This sequence returns the quiver to its original form while transforming the J- and E-terms. We explain the relation between quiver-invariant triality and the orbifold reduction of quiver-invariant brane tilings.

authors.name: Dongwook Ghim, Juno Kwon, Rak-Kyeong Seong

papers.title: Asymmetric Orbifolds and 4-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ String Islands
papers.summary: We formulate heterotic and type II $\mathbb T^6/\mathbb Z_n$ asymmetric orbifolds preserving all 16 right-moving supersymmetries and leading to 4-dimensional islands without massless moduli other than the dilaton. We establish the consistency of the orbifold conformal field theory, including the validity of operator interpretation. In the heterotic case we classify all islands based on the $\Gamma(22,6)$ lattice constructed via the Leech lattice. In the type II case we also provide a classification of allowed $\Gamma(6,6)$ lattices and orbifold generators. In both cases we further examine whether a particular orbifold admits an archipelago of different islands arising from inequivalent realizations of the orbifold action.

authors.name: Gerardo Aldazabal, Eduardo C. Andr\'es, Anamar\'ia Font, Elisa I. Marieni, Kumar Narain, Ida G. Zadeh

papers.title: Conformal manifolds of $\mathcal{N}=1$ orbifold theories - Part I: Marginal deformations and the one-loop spectrum
papers.summary: We consider orbifolds of 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang--Mills theory that preserve minimal supersymmetry and study their conformal manifolds, focusing on two families of Abelian orbifolds in the planar limit. We compute their superconformal indices, construct their complete single-trace BPS spectra and identify the conformal manifolds. These are generically spanned by a subset of the gauge-couplings, whose number we derive from both gauge and string theory, and a universal Leigh--Strassler-type superpotential deformation. We then construct the complete, planar one-loop dilatation operator on these conformal manifolds, giving perturbative access to the full non-BPS spectrum away from the orbifold point. This lays the groundwork for studying special loci of the conformal manifold in a forthcoming Part II.

authors.name: Fabio Mantegazza, Elli Pomoni, Torben Skrzypek

papers.title: Stringy Corrections from Gravity: Predictions for BFSS and ABJM
papers.summary: Despite enormous progress in string theory, the leading stringy corrections to many holographic observables remain unknown. String/M-theory dualities nonetheless allow them to be determined from gravity alone. From the winding modes of one-loop 11d supergravity on a circle, we derive the leading tree-level stringy terms in the type IIA effective action for the metric, dilaton, and Ramond--Ramond one-form, in closed form as a finite supertrace over Lorentz generators. On the thermal D0-brane geometry, this gives the first correction to the low-temperature thermodynamics of the BFSS matrix model. Its coefficient differs from published lattice Monte Carlo estimates by $\approx 20\%$. With the four-form flux included, the same method reproduces the $\zeta(3)k^{2}$ term of the ABJM free energy on the three-sphere obtained by localization.

authors.name: Aidan Herderschee, Victor Ivo, Henry W. Lin, Yifan Wang

papers.title: Actionless Branes on Axion Wormholes
papers.summary: Can a Euclidean axion wormhole extend to infinity with every instanton still suppressed? The imaginary distance bound says it cannot: some instanton must become actionless first. Calabi-Yau compactifications appear to violate the bound: several axions share the field excursion, and the instantons charged under any one of them stay suppressed all the way. We show that the wormhole can hide from these instantons but not from their bound states: misaligned central charges make a bound state cheaper than its constituents, while the axions act on every constituent. On the type IIB wormhole supported by two axions of the Neveu-Schwarz two-form, a fivebrane carrying string charge becomes actionless at large volume within two thirds of the way to infinity, for either relative sign of the axions and however they share the excursion. In S-dual variables it is a D5-brane with magnetic flux for one sign and a D5-NS5 bound state for the other. Adding more axions does not help: the same branes become actionless on every Calabi-Yau threefold, because what counts is the degree of homogeneity of the saxion sector, not the number of axions. These bound states are what the convex-hull axion weak gravity conjecture requires.

authors.name: A. Ramesh Chandra

papers.title: Twist and Shout: defect lines on the R\'enyi torus
papers.summary: We consider what the entanglement between two regions of a critical system can reveal about its symmetries, including non-invertible ones. For two intervals in a two-dimensional conformal field theory, the second R\'enyi entropy is a partition function on a torus, and a topological defect line can be wrapped around one of the intervals. For an on-site symmetry this computes the overlap of the reduced density matrix with its image under the symmetry acting on one interval, and in general it defines an observable that depends only on the cross-ratio. As the intervals approach each other, the observable vanishes at a rate set by the lightest operator on which the line can end, and its monodromy is fixed by the spins of such operators. Since these spins are constrained by the fusion category, the observable detects 't Hooft anomalies and distinguishes categories with the same fusion rules. It can be computed in closed form for a $\mathbb{Z}_2$, a $\mathbb{Z}_3$ and a Fibonacci line of the $(E_8)_1$ theory, and for the spin-flip and Kramers-Wannier lines of the Ising model, where the spin-flip result agrees with an exact computation in the critical Ising chain. Averaged over a symmetry, the observable reduces to a known Jones-index bound on the mutual information. We also show that the associated twist-field crossing equations are a form of the modular bootstrap, and discuss whether the full fusion category can be recovered from entanglement on surfaces of higher genus.

authors.name: Naveen Balaji Umasankar

papers.title: Entanglement entropy from fundamental strings
papers.summary: In previous work, we derived the local entropy capacity from off-shell string theory and combined it with the gravitational replica construction and flow-cut duality to normalize the entropy flow carried by physical fundamental strings. In this paper, we apply this framework to interval entanglement in holographic CFT$_2$. We construct explicit on-shell F1 worldsheets in the AdS$_3$ vacuum and planar BTZ, derive their Kalb-Ramond source currents, and show that the normalized spatial currents saturate the corresponding RT surface. Their flux reproduces both the vacuum single interval entropy and the finite temperature CFT$_2$ result. We then vary the NS-NS flux fraction. Although the total maximal flux remains unchanged, the F1 equations continuously redistribute the strings among different parts of the complement. In planar BTZ, the resulting signed flux through the bifurcation line reproduces the extensive thermal entropy and can vanish in the pure NS-NS limit without changing the interval entropy. Thus the on-shell string dynamics additionally determines its physical routing and boundary contact structure.

authors.name: Houwen Wu, Shuxuan Ying

papers.title: $C_T$ and $C_J$ of general scalar--fermion conformal field theories in $d=4-\epsilon$
papers.summary: We compute $C_T$ and $C_J$, the coefficients of the stress-tensor and conserved-current two-point functions, to order $\epsilon^3$ at any fixed point of the general renormalizable theory of scalars and fermions in $d=4-\epsilon$. We give explicit results for the chiral Ising, XY and Heisenberg models and for fixed points with emergent supersymmetry in $d=3$. In theories without a four-dimensional counterpart, fermion loops with an odd number of Yukawa vertices contribute at order $\epsilon^3$ through traces whose continuation away from $d=3$ is ambiguous; we fix it with $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetry, by computing the two-point functions of the supercurrent and of the fermionic partner of a flavor current to four loops. In $d=3$, Pad\'e approximants closely reproduce the exact $C_T$ of the $\mathcal N=2$ super-Ising model. We estimate the universal conductivity at the charge-density-wave, Kekul\'e and N\'eel transitions of graphene to be $\sigma/\sigma_{\rm free}\approx0.91$, $0.79$--$0.83$ and $0.64$--$0.74$, and show that the exact conductivity at the supersymmetric transition on the surface of a topological insulator is $\sigma/\sigma_{\rm free}=\frac{9}{10}\,C_T/C_{T,\rm free}\approx0.654$, $10\%$ below the value previously reported.

authors.name: Shiroman Prakash, Shubham Kumar Sinha

papers.title: Nonzero cubic Love numbers of Schwarzschild black holes
papers.summary: Static Love numbers of Schwarzschild black holes vanish at linear and quadratic order in General Relativity, while generic nonlinear tides remain less understood. We solve a specific non-axisymmetric octupolar tide at cubic order and, building on the symmetry of static General Relativity exploited by Parra-Martinez and Podo, match the result to a worldline effective field theory (EFT) using dimensional regularization. Surprisingly, we find a Love number that neither vanishes nor runs.

authors.name: Bruno Bucciotti

papers.title: Soft Factorisation of WQFT and the Spinning 4PM Magnusian
papers.summary: We derive the soft divergences of $\hat{N}=-i\log\hat{S}$ in the Worldline Quantum Field Theory (WQFT) formalism, focusing on poles due to single massive-massive (Coulomb) and massive-massless (tail) graviton exchanges. Our derivation is inspired by the Faddeev-Kulish procedure, switching the interaction picture to one with an infrared-finite $\hat{N}$-matrix. Soft divergences emerging from the worldline are correlators of Wilson lines. As confirmation of this structure, we demonstrate explicitly how divergences of inclusive observables including the momentum impulse $\Delta p_i^\mu$ and spin kick $\Delta S_i^\mu$ cancel, and we reproduce the infrared divergence of the one-loop scattering waveform. Using the Magnus series representation of $\hat{N}$ and Murua coefficients, we then calculate the Magnusian $N=\langle0|\hat{N}|0\rangle$ at fourth post-Minkowskian (4PM) order, including linear-in-spin corrections. For aligned spins, $-\partial N/\partial L$ reproduces the full scattering angle through 3PM order; at 4PM order, $N$ develops a soft divergence as predicted by our soft factorisation. Using the Feynman $i0^+$ prescription, we also derive an infrared-finite 4PM Magnusian which compactly encodes existing results for the conservative momentum impulse and spin kick via nested iterations of Poisson brackets.

authors.name: Riccardo Gonzo, Gustav Mogull, Benjamin Sauer

papers.title: Calabi-Yau linear models with abelian bundles
papers.summary: We introduce a construction of (0,2) gauged linear sigma models whose large radius phases realize Calabi-Yau sigma models with line bundles. We study a family of such models admitting Landau-Ginzburg orbifold phases, described as asymmetric orbifolds of (2,2) Gepner models and free left-moving fermions. These orbifolds extend the Gepner construction to a broader class of (0,2) SCFTs, and reveal unexpected features, including the emergence of free fermions in twisted sectors and substantial enhancements of the left-moving current algebra. The gauged linear sigma model connects the Calabi-Yau geometry to these rational points, where the volume modulus becomes charged under the enhanced gauge symmetry and freezes at the string scale.

authors.name: Yann Proto

papers.title: From Instantons to AdS Boundaries: Tracing the Geometric Path from Quantum Anomalies to Massive Gravity
papers.summary: This thesis studies how boundary data enter two gravitational observables: the Dirac index on gravitational instantons and conserved charges in three-dimensional New Massive Gravity. In Einstein gravity coupled to ModMax electrodynamics, we compute the index of charged Dirac fermions on Taub-NUT and Eguchi-Hanson instantons using the Atiyah-Patodi-Singer theorem, which includes the spectral asymmetry of the boundary Dirac operator. The Taub-NUT index agrees with the Maxwell result. For Eguchi-Hanson, the gauge-field contribution to the axial anomaly depends explicitly on the ModMax parameter when expressed in terms of the solution parameters. For asymptotically anti-de Sitter solutions of New Massive Gravity with Brown-Henneaux boundary conditions, a term linear in the extrinsic curvature reproduces the holographic stress tensor of the auxiliary-field formulation. At the degenerate point, relaxed boundary conditions admit an additional constrained Fefferman-Graham coefficient. A quadratic extrinsic counterterm cancels the residual power divergence. We derive the boundary Ward identity and show that the holographic and Noether-Wald charges agree for the solutions studied.

authors.name: Leonardo Sanhueza

papers.title: Holographic Duals of $SL^{(q)}(2, \mathbb{R})$ Deformed CFTs
papers.summary: We study the holographic bulk dual of 2D CFTs evolved by $sl^{(q)}(2,R)$-deformed Hamiltonians. Working in the Hamiltonian-adapted frame, in which the $sl^{(q)}(2,R)$-deformed effective Floquet Hamiltonian generates time translations, we construct the dual Ba\~nados geometries for the three distinct classes of dynamics: the heating phase, the non-heating phase and the phase boundary. Specifically, we show that in the heating phase, the bulk patch dual to the region between two neighbouring fixed points has a time-dependent causal horizon and asymptotes to a static AdS Rindler geometry at late times, while the non-heating phase has no horizon. We discuss how the late-time behaviour of the entanglement entropy, particularly its linear growth in the heating phase, can be understood from the bulk in two different ways: in global AdS, from the portion of the geodesic behind the horizons, and in a quotient description, from an effective shockwave produced by a boosted conical defect. Finally, for ($q=1$), we complete the holographic analysis of Ref. [1] by reproducing the exact CFT expression of the OTOC from the bulk and explaining why it exhibits an exponential growth {\it only} when the operators lie on the side of the two fixed points.

authors.name: Somnath Porey, Baishali Roy, Rahul Roy, Bobby Ezhuthachan

papers.title: Upper Bounds on the Radion Mass in a Warped Extra Dimension
papers.summary:
We study absolute upper bounds on the mass ratio $R_{11}=m_{r_1}/m_{h_1}$ between the radion ($r_1$) and graviton ($h_1$) lightest modes in five dimensional warped models. We consider warped models with an admissible singular behavior in the infrared: i.e.~models with power-like ($\sim  ar\phi^{2n}$) and with exponential ($\sim e^{2
u ar\phi}$) bulk potentials, where $ ar\phi$ is the stabilizing bulk field. We find a correlation between $R_{11}$ and the singular behavior of the Ricci scalar, which allows to establish an absolute upper bound on the former. For the power-like models, the maximum value of $R_{11}$ increases with $n$. In the limit $n	o\infty$, the power-like model reproduces the exponential model and reaches the same upper bound as the latter. For the exponential model, we derive analytically the bound $R_{11}<1$, with the largest value approached for the case $
u	o 1^+$ (where $
u=1$ corresponds to the linear dilaton model) and consistent with unitarity sum rules. For exponential models we also obtain the absolute upper bound on the second radion mode ratio $R_{21}=m_{r_2}/m_{h_1}\lesssim 1.374$. This value is reached for $
u=2$ when the IR brane approaches the singularity. For this configuration, we verify that the scalar contribution satisfies the unitarity sum rule when the complete radion Kaluza-Klein tower is included.

authors.name: Leandro Da Rold, Eugenio Megias, Mariano Quiros, Lindber Salas

papers.title: Pairwise fermionic mode correlations in electric and magnetic backgrounds: Landau-level structure and Schwinger production
papers.summary: We investigate mutual information and logarithmic negativity in fermionic Schwinger pair production in parallel electric and magnetic fields. Using spin-dependent Bogoliubov transformations, we construct the in-vacuum and derive the particle--antiparticle correlations for selected Landau modes. We also consider an initially entangled two-particle state and evaluate the correlations for six bipartitions. The physical Landau-level structure is treated explicitly by distinguishing modes with the same oscillator index from the spin representatives of a common physical Landau level. For matched higher levels, the pairwise redistribution relations retain the electric-only form, with the magnetic-field dependence entering through the Landau-level pair-production probabilities. When the two particle groups occupy different physical levels, the cross particle--antiparticle correlations become unequal, and we derive analytic relations characterizing this asymmetry. We further obtain the local logarithmic negativity from the ordinary partial transpose in a fixed occupation-space basis. Finally, we extend the analysis to a Sauter-type electric field in a constant magnetic background and examine the dependence of the pairwise correlations on the field parameters and Landau-level structure.

authors.name: Sahil Chetan Patnekar, Sristi Sanjivanee Goswami, Sanjay Pant, Shagun Kaushal

papers.title: From Integrability to Chaos in Tensionless AdS3 String Theory
papers.summary: We study quantum-gravitational corrections to the planar integrable structure of the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N(\mathbb{T}^4)$ that is dual to tensionless string theory on AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$. We consider the deformation that switches on R-R flux in the bulk, and analyze the associated level spacing statistics. The leading non-planar corrections lift the planar degeneracies and produce signs of random-matrix behavior. Our results provide a controlled example of string interactions driving the onset of quantum chaos.

authors.name: Matthias R. Gaberdiel, Beat Nairz, Cheng Peng

papers.title: A full-color four-point form factor
papers.summary: We determine the symbol and complete functions of the full-color two-loop four-point maximally helicity violating stress-tensor form factor in $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, including $N^1$ double traces and $N^0$ single traces. Numerical unitarity and a master-integral bootstrap fix the result. A direct form-factor bootstrap reproduces the symbol. Permuting external legs in the planar 88-letter alphabet yields all 79 letters, while the $N^0$ terms contain four new nonclassical contributions. We also obtain the complete $N^0$ two-loop triple-collinear hard splitting functions.

authors.name: Song He, Xuhang Jiang

papers.title: Two Faces of Spacetime Density Matrices: Entanglement and Complexity
papers.summary: We establish a direct connection between entanglement and complexity through spacetime density matrices. For stationary pure states and complementary regions at different times, spacetime replica moments encode the return amplitude of a replica-defect quench. This representation defines an associated state spread complexity, which we call Krylov-R\'enyi complexity. It can equivalently be obtained by using a replica-defect excitation of the replicated background state as the seed and evolving it under the original replicated Hamiltonian. We further construct Krylov-von Neumann complexity as a probe limit from first-order replica data. Timelike entanglement and complexity provide complementary information at a fixed time, while the full time dependence of the timelike entropy determines the Krylov dynamics and hence the complexity. The replica construction fixes the seed and its evolution through the background state, subsystem geometry, and regulator, without an independently chosen probe operator. Like entanglement entropy, the resulting complexity is defined nonperturbatively and probes universal properties and dynamical information about the underlying theory.

authors.name: Wu-zhong Guo

papers.title: Second-order formulation of chiral fermions with a local boundary condition
papers.summary: Chiral fermions in $d$ dimensions arise naturally as boundary modes of a massive fermion in $d+1$ dimensions subject to a local boundary condition. When anomalies are absent, this construction can be used to define an intrinsically $d$-dimensional theory of chiral fermions. However, defining the path integral using the first-order Dirac operator with this boundary condition is technically inconvenient, even in the continuum. We present a formulation in terms of second-order differential operators that is completely equivalent to the original formulation in the continuum. Its natural lattice discretization generates Wilson's term and avoids fermion doubling. Our lattice formulation closely resembles the boundary-fermion construction of Shamir, and provides some insight into the case of a general Wilson parameter.

authors.name: Kazuya Yonekura

papers.title: Holographic Tessellations Tensor Networks $\{p,q\}$ from Entangled Quantum Tetrahedron in Loop Quantum Gravity
papers.summary: The relationship between spin network states in loop quantum gravity and bulk--boundary duality is further explored using the tessellated holographic tensor network. We develop a holographic tensor network construction based on quantum entanglement between tetrahedra in loop quantum gravity (LQG). This construction relates four-valent intertwiner spaces and Bell states dressed with $SU(2)$ holonomies to effective tensors on hyperbolic $\{p,q\}$ tessellations. For the $\{5,4\}$ tessellation, six tetrahedra are assembled into a single effective cell with five network legs and one logical index. Provided that the microscopic transfer map has full row rank, a right inverse and a completion on the kernel space are employed to construct an isometric embedding, yielding an effective tensor proportional to a perfect tensor. The construction is generalized to the $p=2n-1$ family, with local dimensions supporting absolutely maximally entangled states. On finite networks satisfying a radial orientation condition, an appropriate normalization produces an isometric bulk--boundary map. For cuts satisfying the isometry condition on both sides, the boundary entropy decomposes into a link contribution $\sum_{\ell}\log(2j_{\ell}+1)$ and the bulk entropy, thereby providing a discrete realization of the quantum Ryu--Takayanagi structure. Applications to the black hole interior are formulated via postselection-based non-isometric encoding. Assuming additional Haar statistics, this framework is used to analyze the preservation of overlaps on average and the competition between entropy branches underlying the Page Curve. These results establish a constructive link between the geometric degrees of freedom of LQG and holographic codes, while clarifying the conditions required to connect them to geometric area in LQG, the location of the quantum extremal surface, and evaporation of black hole.

authors.name: Deden M. Akbar, Freddy P. Zen, Jusak S. Kosasih

papers.title: Worldsheet Effective Theory of Abelian-Higgs Cosmic Strings beyond Nambu--Goto
papers.summary: Cosmic strings can support long-lived excitations confined to their cores, opening channels for energy exchange with the transverse Goldstone modes that describe the string's motion. We derive a covariant worldsheet theory of their coupled dynamics directly from the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling, with all interaction coefficients fixed by the microscopic theory. The resulting action, which we validate against numerical lattice field theory simulations, extends the Nambu--Goto description to include a massive scalar shape mode and a massive vector mode. Dualizing the vector reveals a geometric distinction: the shape scalar mode couples to intrinsic worldsheet curvature, while the pseudoscalar couples to normal bundle curvature. These interactions explain the distinct parametric instabilities observed in lattice simulations and predict how the relative polarization of colliding transverse waves controls the excitation of the two internal modes. Our results connect microscopic string structure to the nonlinear worldsheet dynamics, providing a predictive framework for cosmic strings beyond the Nambu--Goto approximation.

authors.name: Sergio Alameda-Calvo, Josu C. Aurrekoetxea, Jose J. Blanco-Pillado, Alberto Garc\'ia Mart\'in-Caro, J. M. Queiruga

papers.title: Equilibrium relativistic spin magnetohydrodynamics from chiral kinetic theory
papers.summary: We develop a microscopic and thermodynamically consistent framework for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics of massless chiral fermions, directly from first-order chiral kinetic theory. Starting from the covariant Wigner function, we recast the chiral kinetic equation as a pure streaming equation on a magnetically shifted mass shell, incorporating both the magnetic-moment energy and the Berry-curvature phase-space measure. This formulation yields a kinetic $H$-theorem and an entropy current with vanishing divergence in global equilibrium. We construct the equilibrium distribution for an arbitrary spin frame and derive the associated currents, energy--momentum tensor, spin tensor, entropy current, and frame-independent spin polarization, including the magnetic splitting between particles and antiparticles. Thermodynamic consistency further determines the second-order magnetovortical responses, revealing a relativistic Barnett magnetization, a temperature- and chemical-potential-independent anomalous charge density, and rotation-induced density corrections that reproduce exact field-theory results. Our framework provides a unified microscopic foundation for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics and establishes a direct link between quantum kinetic theory, spin polarization, magnetization, and anomalous transport.

authors.name: Gopal Mistry, Amaresh Jaiswal

papers.title: Cardinal RG=GR: Phase-Space Cardinality and the Cosmological Constant and Hierarchy Problems
papers.summary: The effective field theory approach constructs the low-energy theory by integrating out fluctuations above an ultraviolet scale which raises the cosmological constant and hierarchy problems. We investigate an alternative prescription in which the quantum theory is restricted to a finite accessible region of phase space, characterized by a dimensionless cardinality $\mathcal N$, rather than by independently prescribed spacetime and momentum scales. At fixed cardinality these scales are related. For Euclidean de Sitter space, the stationarity condition for the gravitational action can then be written as a stationarity condition with respect to the momentum scale, a relation which we call Cardinal RG=GR. We demonstrate the relation between $\mathcal N$ and the Gibbons-Hawking entropy of de Sitter space, compute the cosmological constant proportional to ${1}/{\sqrt{\mathcal N}}$, show that it is radiatively stable and apply the same prescription to demonstrate the radiative stability of the mass parameter for a simple interacting scalar field model, thereby illuminating the resolution of the hierarchy problem. We also establish a precise limit, involving gravitational data, in which the conventional results of Quantum Field Theory and the Renormalization Group are recovered.
