authors.name: Laurent Freidel, Jerzy Kowalski-Glikman, Robert G. Leigh, Djordje Minic

papers.title: Full-Color Two-loop Four-point Form Factor in N=4 SYM with Global CK-duality
papers.summary: We determine the full-color two-loop four-point MHV form factor of the stress-tensor supermultiplet in N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory. Using color-kinematics (CK) duality and unitarity cuts, we construct complete one- and two-loop integrands manifesting global off-shell CK duality without explicit $\mu^2$ dependence. Integration-by-parts reduction to uniform-transcendentality master integrals yields purely rational numbers multiplying simple kinematic prefactors, manifesting maximal transcendentality. Expressing the form factor in terms of pentagon functions, we verify full-color infrared-pole cancellation, extract the finite remainder, and obtain new non-planar results for the two-loop triple-collinear splitting function and double-soft current.

authors.name: Zhiming Cai, Yuanhong Guo, Gang Yang

papers.title: Exact Spherical Branes and Deformations: BMN, IKKT and $\mathcal{N}=2^\ast$
papers.summary: We present a unified analytic solution to the BPS equations of spherical Dp-branes for $1\leq p \leq 5$ and give the corresponding type II uplifts in closed form. These are holographically dual to maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory on $S^{p+1}$. The change of variables that makes the BPS equations integrable also allows us to analytically calculate a universal result for the holographic Wilson loop and obtain UV asymptotic behaviour previously determined numerically. The same change of variables extends naturally, with suitable modifications, to the cases $p=0$ and $p=-1$. We obtain a 1-parameter family of D0-brane solutions and show how the IR conditions lead to a singular limit of the integration constant. We also solve the D(-1)-brane BPS equations and show the resulting Euclidean uplift fails regularity conditions. Separately, we obtain an explicit representation of the one-ball electrostatic solution of polarised IKKT, which lets us express multipole moments and holographic observables using elliptic invariants. Finally, we analytically solve the BPS equations of the holographic dual of $\mathcal{N}=2^\ast$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory on $S^4$, present the corresponding type IIB uplift and calculate the holographic Wilson loop.

authors.name: Cameron Gibson

papers.title: All-Order Linearized Hydrodynamics of Charged Holographic Plasmas
papers.summary: We investigate linearized all-order transport in a finite-density holographic plasma described by five-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory. By retaining the full frequency- and momentum-dependence of the fluid/gravity equations, we determine generalized shear, diffusion, higher-gradient, and chiral-vortical transport functions together with their real-time memory kernels. The different channels exhibit a clear hierarchy of temporal response: the leading shear and diffusion sectors respond promptly, whereas the higher-gradient sectors develop only after a finite buildup time. Remarkably, the chiral-vortical response also shows a finite buildup time despite entering at first order in the hydrodynamic derivative expansion, demonstrating that derivative order does not by itself determine the temporal organization of transport. Toward the near-extremal regime, long-time memory becomes increasingly persistent across several channels. These results reveal how finite density reshapes nonlocal transport and relaxation in strongly coupled holographic plasmas.

authors.name: Karthik R., Shamant Shreedhar Dixit, K. M. Ajith, Kartheek Hegde, Shreyas Punacha, A. Naveena Kumara

papers.title: Dynamical Temperley-Lieb algebras from Quiver CFTs
papers.summary: The one-loop dilatation operator of a superconformal planar gauge theory can be written as a sum of local generators. The algebra these generators satisfy is a powerful organising principle for the spectrum. For SU(2)-like bosonic subsectors we show that this algebra can be read off directly from Feynman diagrams, which we identify as a natural graphical language for it. For N=4 super Yang-Mills this simply reproduces the Temperley-Lieb (TL) algebra of the XXX spin chain. After orbifolding and marginally deforming to N=2 superconformal quiver theories, the same recipe yields dynamical generalisations of the TL algebra. In these theories, the faces of the diagrams are coloured according to the quiver nodes, and separated by domain walls corresponding to bifundamental fields. There are two inequivalent SU(2)-like subsectors, which lead to two different TL algebras. One sector is built from the two bifundamental scalars and (in the simplest case) gives a dynamical TL algebra with a colour-dependent loop fugacity in its quadratic relation. The other sector is built from one bifundamental and one adjoint scalar, and (always) gives a novel algebra, in which the cubic TL relation becomes dynamical. In this latter case, we show that each generator of this new algebra is related to a standard XXZ TL generator by a colour-dependent twist. This twist is local and not an algebra homomorphism, and can be written as a dynamical Drinfeld twist. In both sectors, the TL structure provides a natural graphical approach to the spectral problem, as well as clarifying the structure of the irreducible representations of these chains. Finally, we give a preliminary description of the loop models associated to these algebras.

authors.name: Rob Klabbers, Elli Pomoni, Ana L. Retore, Paul Ryan, Konstantinos Zoubos

papers.title: Black holes and 2-group symmetry from blackfolds in minimal supergravity
papers.summary: We investigate the black hole phase diagram of five-dimensional minimal supergravity using the blackfold approach and the framework of generalized symmetries. Starting from supergravity coupled to probe sources, we derive the 2-group (non-)conservation laws, construct the equilibrium action for a two-dimensional 2-group fluid, and compute the associated global conserved charges. We then match the thermodynamics of the general non-extremal black string in the ungauged theory to that of this fluid, organizing the blackfold effective theory and its solutions in terms of symmetry invariants. In the non-extremal ungauged sector, we perturbatively construct new black rings, Saturns, di-rings, and bi-rings, including a black Saturn with seven independent parameters. Taking appropriate extremal limits, we identify several extremal branches, some previously unexplored and others anticipated, as well as BPS branches that approximate known supersymmetric families. Finally, we apply the same framework to construct extremal black rings in AdS$_5$, identifying three regular branches that are promising candidates for an exact completion.

authors.name: Jay Armas, Giorgos Batzios, Pedro Vicente Marto, Chiara Toldo

papers.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
papers.summary: We establish a framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms, surpassing standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. Our three conjectures are as follows: 1. For fixed field content and derivative order, effective couplings form a finite-dimensional space under stated equivalences. 2. A family of mixed RR, gauge, and scalar interactions exists at all orders, represented by a finite number of effective even forms. 3. The higher-derivative contact-term sector can be constructed from a finite set of basic tensor structures using polynomials in derivative symbols. We introduce a higher-class pullback operator \( P_{\infty} \) and mixed transgression operators \( \mathcal{T}_{\infty} \), emphasizing amplitude-derived pole residues and local contact terms as key physical data. This formalism distinguishes admissible tensor structures, presenting characteristic-form aspects as conjectures alongside their validity considerations.

authors.name: Armin Hatefi, Ehsan Hatefi

papers.title: Inhomogeneous Cutoff Regularization of Loops in Cosmological Correlators
papers.summary: We revisit the use of cutoff regularization in computing loop corrections to cosmological correlators. We argue that a cutoff corresponding to a fixed physical scale must be defined with respect to the local background geometry. In the presence of superhorizon perturbations, this is naturally implemented within the separate universe picture, where different local patches are regulated at the same physical scale. Expanding this cutoff in the long-wavelength background generates a series of regulator-induced contributions to loop amplitudes, which admit a diagrammatic interpretation as long-mode insertions on the corresponding loop contractions. Our cutoff prescription preserves residual spatial dilatations and volume-preserving anisotropic rescalings. It is therefore particularly relevant for loop correlators with soft external modes. We illustrate the mechanism by computing the contributions to the one-loop scalar and tensor power spectra on superhorizon scales. In both cases, the additional corrections induced by the inhomogeneous cutoff cancel the ultraviolet boundary terms arising in the ordinary diagrams. These calculations establish, within cutoff regularization, the late-time constancy of both power spectra and clarify its physical origin. We then investigate the squeezed one-loop scalar bispectrum and show that the additional cutoff contributions are essential for satisfying the consistency relation at finite cutoff. Finally, we discuss the role of the inhomogeneous cutoff in the late-time constancy of the one-loop bispectrum.

authors.name: Jacopo Fumagalli, Keisuke Inomata

papers.title: Twisting Spinning Particles with Superghost Backgrounds
papers.summary: We construct twists of spinning particles in the classical BV formalism by giving constant backgrounds to the bosonic ghosts of local worldline supersymmetry, in analogy with Costello and Li's twist of supergravity, which gives a nonzero background to the ghost of local spacetime supersymmetry. We represent the superghosts on polynomial states and gauge selected worldline R symmetries, imposing the shifted R constraints absolutely and the unshifted ones relatively. On flat targets, the N=2 particle, its N=4 extension on a complex target and an N=8 particle with two fermion flavors give the de Rham, Dolbeault and polynomial linear BCOV complexes. The last two are the linearized field content of the open and closed B-model target-space theories. Pairings and interactions require target-space input beyond the reduced worldline differentials.

authors.name: Erik Fink, Jingqian Gou, Niklas Holbach, Ondrej Hulik

papers.title: UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation
papers.summary: A question of fundamental interest is whether parity is violated on large scales in the Universe. This possibility has been motivated by recent analyses of the four-point matter correlation function. It has also been suggested that detectable parity violation could be generated during inflation by the dynamical Chern-Simons operator, a leading effective field theory correction to general relativity. In this work, we examine this possibility in realistic UV completions, including fermionic and string-theoretic examples. We show that existing bounds on the tensor-scalar-scalar (TSS) bispectrum strongly constrain the possibility of generating a detectable parity-odd trispectrum. For tensor-to-scalar ratios near current observational limits, detectability is incompatible with, or pushes against, the regime of validity of these UV completions. A detectable signal can remain possible for a sufficiently small tensor-to-scalar ratio, but only at the cost of an extremely large enhancement of the TSS vertex. Thus, while a future search for large scale parity violation is worth pursuing, generating a detectable signal within a consistent effective theory is highly nontrivial.

authors.name: Alexander Cassem, Mark P. Hertzberg

papers.title: Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
papers.summary: The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms. Our construction of these so-called equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for $\Gamma(2)$ and $\Gamma_0(2)$ proceeds at the level of generating series that take values in an infinite-dimensional (pro-unipotent) Lie group and closely follow Brown's analogous construction in the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ case. The required insertions of cyclotomic multiple zeta values are controlled by zeta generators for level 2 that normalise the corresponding (pro-nilpotent) Lie algebra of the generating series and whose Lie-bracket relations we determine systematically. Upon restriction to Eisenstein series of modular weight~2, we recover single-valued multiple polylogarithms on the genus 0 modular curve $\Gamma(2)\backslash \mathbb{H}$.

authors.name: Emiel Claasen, Mehregan Doroudiani, Claude Duhr, Axel Kleinschmidt, Franca Lippert, Oliver Schlotterer, Yoann Sohnle

papers.title: Entropy Products and the Extremal Limit That Never Comes
papers.summary: Two regular black hole horizons need not have an entropy product fixed by the charges and couplings. In Einstein--Maxwell--scalar theory, we construct asymptotically flat branches with products above or below the squared extremal entropy. Regularity selects their horizon scalar values, and different branches can share the charges, couplings, and asymptotic scalar. Each product stays constant as mass and asymptotic scalar vary. The horizon areas stay apart and no extremal limit is reached: the temperature vanishes only where the mass diverges. We prove local existence.

authors.name: Kevin Goldstein, Vishnu Jejjala, Suresh Nampuri

papers.title: 2-dimensional Metric-Affine Geometries and Dynamical Gravity
papers.summary: We study non-Riemannian metric-affine geometries in 2-dimensions. We explicitly show that if the connection of the space is not metric compatible (i.e. the non-metricity is non-vanishing) then the underlying 2-dimensional manifold is not an Einstein manifold, in contrast to the Riemannian case. Furthermore we prove that in general the curvature in such spaces is specified completely by the Ricci tensor which, however, is not symmetric now. An enlarged symmetry of the scalar curvature under vectorial connection shifts is also found. We then apply our results to the study of 2-dimensional Metric-Affine Gravity Theories and discuss some special cases.

authors.name: Damianos Iosifidis

papers.title: Geometric Formulation of Covariant Spin Operator
papers.summary: In relativistic quantum theory, Lorentz boosts induce momentum-dependent Wigner rotations, complicating the coupling of particle spins in arbitrary frames. We describe particle spin spaces as fibers of an associate bundle over the velocity manifold, and different particle's spins residing at distinct fibers. Analogy to general relativity, we introduce parallel transport to bring spins at different velocities into a common frame, where they can be coupled. Using spinor-helicity variables, we construct the parallel transport operator along geodesics and show how it is uniquely determined by little group covariance. This construction gives explicit form of the covariant spin and orbital operators, and yields a covariant 3-point amplitude basis with definite spin and orbital angular momentum. Higher-point amplitudes can be constructively obtained and applied to the covariant partial wave expansion for amplitudes, form factors, and correlation functions, etc.

authors.name: Yi-Ning Wang, Jiang-Hao Yu

papers.title: Accretion disks and photon rings in Palatini Kalb-Ramond gravity
papers.summary: We investigate thin accretion disks and photon rings around a static black hole in Palatini Kalb Ramond gravity, connecting thermal emission with the optical effects of the radial geometry. At fixed orbital mass and accretion rate, the local radiative flux scales as $1/\sigma$ and the effective temperature as $1/\sigma^{1/4}$, where $\sigma=\sqrt{1-q/2}$ and $q$ is the effective curvature coupling. The innermost stable circular orbit and the critical impact parameter share their Schwarzschild values, together with an emitted efficiency of approximately $5.72\%$. Moreover, photon trajectories admit an exact angular rescaling that determines the strong deflection coefficient and the exponential accumulation of successive disk images. We construct images of an opaque thermal disk and a transparent emitting sheet, taking into account gravitational frequency shifts, orbital motion, and radial emissivity. Positive $q$ increases the local thermal emission and accelerates the accumulation of successive images around the common critical curve. Under the universal coupling assumptions associated with the quoted Solar System bounds, the fractional corrections are of order $10^{-11}$ in flux and $10^{-12}$ in temperature.

authors.name: A. A. Ara\'{u}jo Filho, N. Heidari, P. H. M. Barros, Carlos F. S. Pereira

papers.title: Exact ultrastatic multi-throat wormholes: Geometry, energy conditions, and optical cavities
papers.summary: We construct an exactly solvable hierarchy of static, spherically symmetric, wormholes with arbitrary finite throat multiplicity. A factorized prescription for the derivative of the areal radius places every stationary sphere at a prescribed proper distance while retaining elementary integrability and asymptotic flatness. The order-$N$ geometry contains exactly $N+1$ throats and $N$ anti-throats, arranged as an alternating chain of necks and finite interior cavities. Independently of this particular hierarchy, the Einstein equations imply three universal ultrastatic results. Every nondegenerate throat violates the radial null energy condition, whereas every nondegenerate anti-throat satisfies the null, weak, dominant, and strong energy conditions, with the strong-energy sum condition saturated. The same local combination $\rho+p_\ell$ fixes the radial stability of the associated circular null orbit through $V_{\mathrm {null}}''=8\pi L^2(\rho+p_\ell)/\mathcal R^2$; throats are therefore unstable light rings and anti-throats are stable ones. Finally, every finite cell between consecutive stationary spheres, each exterior cell, and the complete two-ended radial null geodesic carry strictly negative integrated radial null energy. The resulting spacetimes are exact multi-cavity optical chains whose cavity centers are locally nonexotic even though no cell can eliminate averaged radial exoticity. The first nontrivial member interpolates continuously from the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole through a quartically degenerate throat to a double-throat geometry and admits closed expressions for its source, null average, branchwise Morris-Thorne form, embedding criterion, and traversability scales. Its vanishing Arnowitt-Deser-Misner mass follows from the specific radial falloff of the hierarchy, rather than from ultrastaticity alone.

authors.name: Francisco S. N. Lobo, Manuel E. Rodrigues, Gabriel I. R\'ois

papers.title: Testing the Universality of RAR Model with Constraints on Fermionic Dark Matter for M31
papers.summary: The Ruffini--Arg\"uelles--Rueda (RAR) model describes dark matter as a self-gravitating system of massive fermions in thermodynamic equilibrium within general relativity. It suggests a dual morphology in galaxies: a highly degenerate quantum core mimicking a central supermassive black hole, and a classical halo that explains galactic rotation curves. Earlier applications of the model to the Milky Way restricted the fermion mass to $mc^{2}=48\text{--}345~\text{keV}$, and the orbits of the S-stars around Sagittarius~A$^{\ast}$ (Sgr~A$^{\ast}$) favored $mc^{2}=56~\text{keV}$, whereas a recent thermodynamic stability analysis allows only $mc^{2}\approx194\text{--}387~\text{keV}$. In this work, we apply the RAR model to the Andromeda galaxy (M31), which hosts a dark compact object of approximately $1.4\times10^{8}~M_{\odot}$ within $0.19~\text{pc}$, roughly 33 times the mass of Sgr~A$^{\ast}$. We solve the relativistic equilibrium equations for $mc^{2}=6\text{--}60~\text{keV}$. For all these masses, the fermionic core lies within $0.19~\text{pc}$ and provides the central mass without a black hole. With a bulge and disk added, the total rotation curve is statistically acceptable ($\chi^{2}/N_{\text{dof}}\approx1.18$) but lies below the disk data at $3\text{--}11~\text{kpc}$, an offset attributed to the baryonic models we adopted. The Navarro--Frenk--White (NFW) and Burkert profiles fitted to the same data give a lower $\chi^{2}$ but require an additional black hole. The stability of the M31 core against gravitational collapse limits the fermion mass to $mc^{2}\lesssim60~\text{keV}$. With the earlier Milky Way range, a single fermion can therefore describe both galaxies only for $mc^{2}=48\text{--}60~\text{keV}$, which includes $56~\text{keV}$. With the thermodynamic range, no fermionic core can supply the central mass of M31, so M31 would have to host a black hole.

authors.name: Aqsa Yasmin, Ibrar Hussain, Mubasher Jamil

papers.title: The Clifford Hierarchy from Clifford Stabilizers in 2D
papers.summary: The Bravyi-K\"onig theorem limits the constant-depth logical gates of 2D topological Pauli stabilizer codes to be in the Clifford group. Known qubit codes with Clifford stabilizers exceed it by only one level of the Clifford hierarchy, and this was conjectured to hold generally. We show that this bound can be completely bypassed, and that topological codes with Clifford stabilizers in 2D can realize transversal logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy. We present two explicit constructions of codes based on copies of the quantum doubles of $D_4$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$, with $k$ logical qubits and a logical $C^{k-1}Z$ gate, which is at level $k$ of the Clifford hierarchy. The physical circuits realizing the gates consist only of physical $Z$ or $CZ$ gates. The main new ingredient comes from the logical encoding, which depends crucially on non-Abelian group multiplication.

authors.name: Alison Warman, Sakura Schafer-Nameki

papers.title: Numerical Implementation and Tests of the Quadratic Effective Action for Lorentzian Spinfoam Amplitudes
papers.summary: In the pure integral representation of Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitudes, the integration over non-geometric variables in the large-spin limit defines an effective action for Regge geometries. Expanding this effective action to quadratic order around a flat background recovers the classical Regge action $iS_{\mathrm{Regge}}$ at leading order, supplemented by a curvature correction quadratic in the bulk deficit angles $\varepsilon$. In this work, we numerically implement this effective-action framework and validate its analytic predictions using two Julia packages: LorentzianSimplexSolver, for the computation of real and complex critical-point data, and Effective-Spinfoam, for the evaluation of the effective action. We apply this workflow to the double-$\Delta_3$ complex, the $1$-$5$ Pachner move, its refinement, and a $24$-simplex hypercube triangulation. Two complementary numerical tests are performed: first, starting from the real critical point of a flat background, we verify that the leading term reproduces the quadratic Regge action and evaluate the $\varepsilon^2$ curvature correction across a range of the Barbero-Immirzi parameter $\gamma$. Power-law fits confirm that in the small-$\gamma$ regime, the $\varepsilon^2$ correction is of higher order in $\gamma$ than the Regge action. Second, for a sample of curved geometries with finite length perturbations $\delta\ell$, we numerically solve the full nonlinear critical equations at fixed perturbed edge lengths for complex critical points. By comparing the direct action evaluation at complex critical points with the quadratic effective action, we demonstrate that the latter accurately reproduces the nonlinear complex critical-point action up to remainders of cubic order in $\delta\ell$.

authors.name: Dongxue Qu, Sean Tobin, Hongguang Liu, Muxin Han

papers.title: Pure integral formula of spinfoam amplitude and curvature corrections in effective theory
papers.summary: We develop a new analytic method for the semiclassical analysis of the Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitude on a fixed triangulation. We derive a pure integral formula for the spinfoam amplitude that trades the discrete sum over internal spins for integrals over continuous variables. This reformulation is free of discrete sums and provides a well-behaved action that is well-adapted to the stationary phase approximation in the large-spin regime. Integrating out the non-geometric variables yields an effective action for the edge lengths of the Regge geometry. Applying the stationary phase approximation and expanding this effective action to second order in perturbations around a flat background, we obtain the classical Regge action at leading order, supplemented by a quadratic correction in the deficit angles $\varepsilon$. This curvature correction originates from two distinct sources: a holonomy correction resulting from the new action and the fluctuations of non-Regge areas. We show that the quadratic $\varepsilon$ correction appears at a higher order in the Barbero-Immirzi parameter $\gamma$ relative to the Regge action. Together with the large-spin expansion, this yields a two-parameter expansion for the spinfoam effective action, whose leading order is the quadratic Regge action. In the long wavelength regime, the latter approaches the action of a massless spin-2 graviton.

authors.name: Muxin Han

papers.title: Analytic and Numerical Investigation of a Proposed Non-linear Extension of Quantum Mechanics
papers.summary: In this paper, additional properties of a previously introduced non-linear extension of quantum mechanics are investigated. Analytically, we uncover a limit in which the model reduces to ordinary linear quantum mechanics. We also perform a perturbation analysis about an exact solution studied in earlier work. The equations represent a system that is subject to a periodic driver, and we use Floquet theory to help determine its properties. Numerically, we compare the exact solution to the analytic approximation, and we exhibit several examples of how the non-linear effects influence particle trajectories, with particular emphasis on trajectories near the linear limit.

authors.name: Alan Chodos, Anastasiia Purtova

papers.title: Symmetry-resolved spectroscopy of truncation-induced perturbations in loop tensor network renormalization of the six-vertex model
papers.summary: Tensor network renormalization at finite bond dimension $\chi$ introduces truncation errors that are amplified by the renormalization-group (RG) flow. For loop tensor network renormalization (LoopTNR) on the $c=1$ critical line of the six-vertex model, with Luttinger parameter $K$, we identify these errors operator by operator from symmetry-resolved transfer-matrix spectra and conformal perturbation theory. With $O(2)$ symmetry imposed, the dominant error is the dimerization operator, which is allowed because LoopTNR breaks one-site translation. With less symmetry it is the $U(1)$ current or a charge-two vertex operator. The growth of the dimerization per RG step and a parameter-free ratio of its amplitudes agree with conformal perturbation theory to within a few percent. The parameter $K$ drifts slowly, owing to a weak marginal error and to the running induced by the dimerization. A larger $\chi$ lowers the initial amplitude of the error for $0.75\le K\le 1.5$ but changes neither the operator nor its growth rate.

authors.name: Akira Otsuki, Yuta Yamamoto, Kokin Cho, Rikuto Fushio, Masahito Yamazaki

papers.title: Critical droplets and metastability in long-range chains
papers.summary: Metastable decay in first-order phase transitions proceeds through the nucleation of critical droplets. In the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising chain, the cost of the two walls bounding a droplet is independent of its size. For interactions decaying as $1/r^{1+\sigma}$, this surface cost instead depends on the droplet size and competes with the bulk free-energy gain. The critical radius scales as $R_c\propto h^{-1/\sigma}$ at small $h$, where $h>0$ is the bias field. The value $\sigma=1$ separates two regimes: for $\sigma1$, it remains finite, as in the nearest-neighbor chain. A nonlocal $\phi^4$ field theory yields critical droplets with algebraic tails and confirms the predicted radius and barrier scalings, while stochastic long-range dynamics independently reproduces the critical-radius scaling.

authors.name: Laura Batini, Valerio Pagni, Nicol\`o Defenu

papers.title: Majorana dark matter from a thick-to-thin brane junction: Modal stability, real-mediator coannihilation, and a dark-radiation imprint
papers.summary: We show that the localized spectrum of a $D=7$ thick-to-thin brane junction can host a thermal Majorana dark-matter candidate. The anisotropy of the wall widths isolates a light junction fermion, which a four-dimensional Majorana mass splits into two nearby states. The factorized transverse profiles impose a modal selection rule on all cubic couplings, and together with the relaxation of the softly deformed background this makes the lighter state stable without an imposed dark parity. Because the localized mediator is a real scalar, identical Majorana particles annihilate in the $s$ wave, and the relic coupling becomes nearly independent of the Majorana mass. The junction sector is a Standard-Model singlet whose light chiral mode is a source of dark radiation. Current CMB data restrict its decoupling temperature and imply $0.05\lesssim\dNeff\lesssim0.076$ for dark-matter masses between $10\GeV$ and $1.5\TeV$, a range accessible to next-generation CMB surveys.

authors.name: F. A. Brito

papers.title: Equation of state of hot and dense QCD at the physical point via the complex Langevin equation
papers.summary: This study presents the first results for the equation of state of 2+1+1-flavor QCD at the physical point, obtained using the complex Langevin equation. We calculate continuum-extrapolated thermodynamic quantities, such as the baryon density, pressure, the speed of sound and the adiabatic compressibility. The simulations are performed in the isospin-symmetric, strangeness- and charm-neutral setting above the crossover temperature and at unprecedentedly large baryon chemical potentials.

authors.name: Michael Mandl, D\'enes Sexty, Daniel Unterhuber

papers.title: Galaxy Bias and Soft Limits from Inflation
papers.summary: Primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG) leaves an imprint on large-scale structure through a scale-dependent galaxy bias, and properly incorporating the effects of higher order PNG into the bias expansion requires a consistent renormalization framework that extends beyond the squeezed limit of the bispectrum. We develop the multi-loop renormalization of bias operators in the presence of non-vanishing primordial n-point functions of arbitrary order, including stochastic contributions. We show that galaxy bias renormalization is determined by the multi-soft limits of primordial correlators and bias kernels. We provide explicit computations for one- and two-loop renormalization of deterministic operators up to fifth order in the bias expansion. Finally, we derive the renormalization group equations for the bias parameters at one and two loops.

authors.name: Charalampos Nikolis, Henrique Rubira

papers.title: Notes on non-equilibrium thermodynamics of Robinson-Trautman spacetimes
papers.summary: Robinson-Trautman spacetimes are determined by a parabolic heat-type evolution equation of fourth order for a scalar field on future null infinity. This equation may be re-written as an energy balance for an asymptotically time-like observer. In turn, it becomes a first law in the context of non-equilibrium thermodynamics if the non-linear memory is interpreted as heat. This leads to a local version of temperature and a manifestly increasing entropy density from the viewpoint of the environment.

authors.name: Glenn Barnich

papers.title: Fast extraction of universal data from temporal spectrum: Applications to Haagerup CFT and monopole scattering
papers.summary: Extracting precise universal data on conformal field theory (CFT) on the lattice traditionally requires large-scale simulations of the ground states and excitations of critical systems. Here, we propose an alternative accurate and fast algorithm, where we read off the CFT spectrum from the transfer matrix spectrum of an infinite matrix product state after a short imaginary-time evolution. We apply this method to extract the charge-resolved spectrum of a Haagerup CFT to higher levels and obtain a central charge $c = 2.137(27)$. Moreover, we show that the Maldacena--Ludwig monopole boundary can be realized as the ground state of the Fidkowski--Kitaev Hamiltonian after space-time rotation.

authors.name: Tokiro Numasawa, Boris De Vos, Masataka Watanabe, Atsushi Ueda

papers.title: Weyl-induced ultrasoft renormalization of the static QCD potential
papers.summary:
We derive the leading curvature-dependent ultrasoft anomalous dimension of the static color-singlet potential in potential nonrelativistic QCD. In a Ricci-flat background the electric Weyl tensor introduces a $t^{-2}$ term in the short-time chromoelectric correlator. The resulting dipole self-energy is ultraviolet divergent at order $\alpha_s^2$ in the curvature sector, two orders earlier than the flat-space contribution. For $W=C_{\mu\alpha
u eta}r^\mu u^\alpha r^
u u^ eta$ and $V_s^{(W)}=c_W W/r$, we obtain $
u\,\partial_
u c_W=C_F C_A\alpha_s^2/(3\pi)$. We calculate the compensating soft infrared pole and the finite one-loop matching coefficient in an optical dimensional subtraction scheme. A direct physical-metric fermion calculation reproduces the finite light-flavor term. We also exhibit the cancellation of the leading regulated infrared overlap and the compensating transformation of soft and ultrasoft constants under an evanescent curvature rescaling. In the perturbative adiabatic regime the anomalous dimension fixes the coefficient of a curvature-dependent $\alpha_s^2\ln\alpha_s$ term in the static energy.

authors.name: Michael Wilson

papers.title: Half-strings across the deconfinement transition of a $U(1)$ quantum link model
papers.summary: The phenomenon of confinement is arguably the key feature of gauge theories regularly studied in high-energy and condensed matter physics. This causes hadrons to exist as stable particles in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) as bound states of quarks (and gluons), and strings in pure gauge theories. The promise of realizing such strings in quantum simulator setups have fueled extensive studies of a plethora of simpler lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Quantum link models (QLMs) generalize Wilsonian LGTs and yield richer scenarios of confinement. For example, the string joining two static charges in the spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ $U(1)$ QLM fractionalize, giving rise to confining phases that break the point group and internal symmetries spontaneously. It was further shown in PRL 130, 071901 (2023) that adding annealed $Q = \pm 2$ charges to this model qualitatively changes the confinement-deconfinement transition. In this paper, we examine the finite temperature phase transition both in the presence and the absence of annealed charges through detailed extraction of critical temperature, $T_c$ , and exponents. The (effective) string tension $\sigma$ at zero and finite- temperatures are compared between the theory with and without annealed charges. The quantity $T_c/\sqrt{\sigma}$ for the QLM with annealed charges is similar to the usual $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory, while the theory without the charges provides a new universal value.

authors.name: Indrajit Sau, Arnab Sen, Debasish Banerjee

papers.title: Thermal Resummation Effects on Electroweak Phase Transitions and Gravitational Waves in Conformal and Non-Conformal 2HDMs
papers.summary: We quantify how thermal resummation affects electroweak phase transitions and gravitational-wave predictions in classically conformal and non-conformal two-Higgs-doublet models. We compare multi-field partial dressing (PD), which retains the full thermal functions and determines scalar masses and mixing from gap equations, with the Parwani and Arnold-Espinosa (AE) prescriptions at identical zero-temperature inputs. Completed first-order transitions dominate the conformal scan under all three prescriptions. PD typically gives the strongest and most supercooled transitions, reaching $T_p/T_c \simeq 0.5$ versus $T_p/T_c \gtrsim 0.8$ for Parwani and AE. At every conformal point where all three predict completion, PD gives the largest gravitational-wave peak amplitude, followed by Parwani and AE. The non-conformal model has no universal ordering, and the prescription changes the type of thermal history across extended regions of parameter space. For representative benchmarks, PD and AE differ by up to about nine orders of magnitude in peak amplitude and a factor of about fifty in peak frequency. In multi-field PD, the dressed tadpole is not a gradient, so the reconstructed potential depends on the integration path. In benchmark tests, changing the path shifts the transition temperatures by at most about 7% and the peak amplitude by up to a factor of about three. This intrinsic ambiguity is smaller than the largest differences between prescriptions. Thermal resummation is a major source of uncertainty in these phase-transition and gravitational-wave predictions.

authors.name: Yu-Bo Zhao, Ji-Wei Li, Zhi-Wei Wang

papers.title: Bianchi cosmologies with four-dimensional groups of motion in New General Relativity
papers.summary: We study the dynamics of the most general metric teleparallel spacetimes of Bianchi types II, III and IX, which admit a four-dimensional symmetry group, in the 1-parameter family of New General Relativity. We first show that in each of these classes the most general metric teleparallel geometry is described by four free functions of time, while another four functions of time describe the most general energy-momentum tensor compatible with the same symmetries. We then derive the field equations of New General Relativity for this class of geometries. Finally, we present some solutions to these field equations. Our results show that both solutions resembling features of the standard Friedmann-Lema\^itre-Robertson-Walker cosmology of General Relativity and deviations thereof exist.

authors.name: Manuel Hohmann, Paul Martin Kull, Margus Saal

papers.title: Relativistic Kinetic Theory of Collisionless Particles with Variable Mass and Frame Transformations
papers.summary: In this work, we present the relativistic kinetic theory of a gas of collisionless point particles with non-constant mass, which can also be understood as being subject to a scalar force. Our results hold in an arbitrary conformal frame, and we explicitly derive how they transform between frames. The mathematical construction relies on a tilted Sasaki metric, whose associated phase-space geometry is adapted to particles of variable mass, as well as on the one-particle distribution function, from which macroscopic observables are derived. Finally, we show that the one-particle distribution function can always be taken to be gauge- and frame-invariant, and the corresponding generalisation of the Liouville (or collisionless Boltzmann) equation is satisfied in each frame.

authors.name: Adri\'an Casado-Turri\'on, Paulo B. Ferraz, Mindaugas Kar\v{c}iauskas, Jos\'e Jaime Terente D\'iaz

papers.title: Which black hole modes ring freely? Horizon regularity, the forced ringdown transient, and GW250114
papers.summary: The quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a black hole are defined by keeping only ingoing waves at the horizon. We ask what horizon regularity requires of the outgoing waves this condition discards. For a scalar-like perturbation, bounded first derivatives in a frame regular at the future horizon rule out outgoing waves that decay more slowly than the surface gravity $\kappa$, and smoothness singles out a ladder of frequencies, $\omega=m\Omega_{\rm H}-ij\kappa$ with $j=1,2,\dots$ and $\Omega_{\rm H}$ the horizon angular velocity. We call these the horizon modes. For Schwarzschild black holes and the dominant $\ell=m=2$ Kerr modes, only the fundamental QNM decays more slowly than $\kappa$. These local statements leave the QNM spectrum unchanged but matter for merger ringdowns, because a source falling through the horizon drives the exterior at the horizon frequencies. Each QNM then has a driven and a free part, and the free part takes over only once the driving decays faster than the mode. The fundamental mode separates from the driving early. The overtones stay driven until the source is hidden behind the potential barrier, so overtone amplitudes fitted near the signal peak are in general not those of free oscillations. In GW250114, a ringdown model of the fundamental mode plus the first horizon mode, $\omega=2\Omega_{\rm H}-i\kappa$, is preferred over the fundamental mode plus its first overtone, with Bayes factors between 2 and 30, for start times from $2M_f$ before to $8M_f$ after coalescence. The horizon-mode fit returns a remnant that is heavier and spins faster than the inspiral predicts, as expected from nonlinear backreaction: the horizon that emits the mode has not yet settled to its final mass and spin. Zero-noise injections of numerical-relativity-calibrated waveforms reproduce both the preference and the shift, which are therefore features of general relativity.

authors.name: Jahed Abedi, Niayesh Afshordi

papers.title: Field theory and the biquadratic spin-1 chain
papers.summary: The antiferromagnetic biquadratic spin-1 chain is gapped, $SU(3)$ symmetric, and integrable. Standard arguments suggest that its low-energy physics is described by the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ nonlinear sigma model at $\theta=\pi$. Using the Bethe ansatz, we show that its low-energy excitations can be interpreted as deconfined domain walls, just as in the sigma model. However, the lattice model is integrable, whereas the field theory is generally believed not to be. We propose a solution to this mystery by finding an integrable field theory with the same low-energy limit but which is not Lorentz invariant. The integrability-preserving scaling limit is obtained by adding a higher conserved charge and tuning the chain to criticality. The gap closes quadratically, so that the limit must be described by some nonrelativistic field theory rather than the relativistic sigma model. We describe the two-particle scattering matrix of this field theory.

authors.name: Luisa Eck, Paul Fendley

papers.title: Nonabelian mirrors and Gromov-Witten invariants
papers.summary: We propose quantum differential equations (QDEs) for periods of nonabelian mirror theories and develop an algorithm for constructing them directly from the mirrors. We verify the proposal by recovering known quantum differential equations of Grassmannians and Picard-Fuchs equations of Calabi-Yau complete intersections in Grassmannians. Our algorithm applies to a broad class of nonabelian GLSMs and yields new examples of quantum differential equations for several Fano varieties. The associated cohomology-valued generating functions can be extracted directly from these equations. Using them, we compute instanton numbers of both complete-intersection and non-complete-intersection Calabi-Yau manifolds, including the Pfaffian and Gulliksen--Neg{\aa}rd Calabi-Yau threefolds. The resulting instanton numbers agree with all previously known computations, while the generating functions obtained for the non-complete-intersection examples are new.

authors.name: Wei Gu, Jirui Guo, Yaoxiong Wen

papers.title: On co-dimension 2 defect anomalies in N=4 SYM and (2,0) theory via brane probes in AdS/CFT
papers.summary: We consider a half-BPS solution for a D3 brane probe in AdS$_5 \times S^5$ that has world-volume geometry of AdS$_3 \times S^1$. It intersects the boundary over a surface that represents a dimension 2 defect in the boundary ${\cal N}=4$ SYM theory. The effective action of the probe brane is proportional to the logarithmically divergent volume of AdS$_3$ and may thus be interpreted as computing conformal anomaly of supersymmetric $S^2$ defect. The classical action scales as $N$. We compute the 1-loop correction to it due to quantum fluctuations of the D3 brane world-volume fields and compare the result to an earlier suggested expression for the defect anomaly. With the boundary condition for the zero mode of the world-volume vector required by supersymmetry the sum over the modes gives the 1-loop coefficient $-3$ instead of the expected $-6$. We suggest that the remaining part is due to the classical response of the background to the probe. We also perform a similar analysis of a half-BPS supersymmetric M5 brane probe solution in AdS$_7 \times S^4$ with the world-volume geometry of AdS$_5 \times S^1$ that represents a dimension 4 defect in the boundary (2,0) 6d theory. Here the classical M5 brane action computes the leading order $N^2$ term in $a$-anomaly of the supersymmetric $S^4$ defect. The fluctuations form a tower of chiral multiplets and a flavour current multiplet of the 4d ${\cal N}=2$ superconformal symmetry. We perform a detailed computation of the 1-loop correction to the M5 brane effective action and discuss prescription dependence of the prediction for the contribution to the $S^4$ defect $a$-anomaly coefficient.

authors.name: Hongliang Jiang, Arkady A. Tseytlin

papers.title: Relationship between a $\Phi^4$ matrix model and harmonic oscillator systems
papers.summary: A Hermitian $\Phi^4$ matrix model with a Kontsevich-type kinetic term is studied. It was recently discovered that the partition function of this matrix model satisfies the Schr\"odinger equation of the $N$-body harmonic oscillator, and that eigenstates of the Virasoro operators can be derived from this partition function. We extend these results and obtain an explicit formula for such eigenstates in terms of the free energy. Furthermore, the Schr\"odinger equation for the $N$-body harmonic oscillator can also be reformulated in terms of connected correlation functions. The $U(1)^N$-symmetry allows us to derive loop equations.

authors.name: Harald Grosse, Naoyuki Kanomata, Akifumi Sako, Raimar Wulkenhaar

papers.title: A measure on the space of CFTs and pure 3D gravity
papers.summary: We define a normalizable measure on subspaces of two-dimensional conformal field theories, which we interpret as a maximum ignorance ensemble. These subspaces are specified by a range of allowed central charges and a minimum gap on the scaling dimension of operators. We test whether pure quantum gravity in AdS3 is dual to the average over this ensemble. We find a negative answer, which implies that CFTs with a primary gap of order the central charge are highly atypical in our ensemble. We provide evidence that more generally, holographic CFTs are atypical in the space of all CFTs by finding similar results for permutation orbifolds: subgroups of SN with a good large N limit are very sparse in the space of all subgroups. Along the way, we derive several new results on the space of CFTs. Notably we derive an upper bound on the spacing in central charge between CFTs, which is doubly exponentially small in the large central charge limit.

authors.name: Alexandre Belin, Alexander Maloney, Florian Seefeld

papers.title: Noncommutative Gauge Theories: Yang-Mills extensions and beyond - An overview
papers.summary: The status of several representative gauge theories on various quantum space-times, mainly focusing on Yang-Mills type extensions together with a few matrix model formulations is overviewed. The common building blocks are derivation based differential calculus possibly twisted and noncommutative analog of the Koszul connection. The star-products related to the quantum space-times are obtained from a combination of harmonic analysis of group algebras combined with Weyl quantization. The remaining problems inherent to gauge theories on Moyal spaces in their two different formulations are outlined. A family of gauge invariant matrix models on $\mathbb{R}^3_\lambda$, a deformation of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is presented among which a solvable model. The characterization of 11 new quantum Minkowski space-times through their $*$-algebras is given. A gauge theory of Yang-Mills type is constructed on one recently explored of these space-times and compared to its counterpart built on the popular $\kappa$-Minkowski.

authors.name: Jean-Christophe Wallet

papers.title: Cosmological Correlators Using Tensor Networks
papers.summary: We develop tensor-network methods for computing cosmological correlators nonperturbatively in de Sitter space and use them to test the proposal that suitably defined in-in correlators can be obtained from an in-out formalism by gluing the expanding and contracting Poincar\'e patches. Focusing on interacting $1+1$-dimensional $\phi^4$ theory, we formulate finite-time lattice observables using Matrix Product State (MPS) techniques and analyze the regulator subtleties associated with the singular behavior near the patching surface. We consider two different contour prescriptions: a finite-time real-contour and a complex contour which properly accounts for the regulator. In the regulated light-field theory, exact-diagonalization and MPS checks support recovery of the full complex in--in/in--out equality at the tested finite cutoffs, suggesting a non-perturbative resolution of light field singularities in perturbation theory. We briefly discuss how these methods extend to low-angular-momentum sectors in $3+1$ dimensions, and why regimes of rapid entanglement growth may eventually motivate quantum-computing implementations.

authors.name: Ujjwal Basumatary, Aninda Sinha, Xinan Zhou

papers.title: Non-planar corrections in the symmetric orbifold
papers.summary: We calculate the non-planar corrections to the anomalous dimensions of certain quarter BPS states in the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N\big({\mathbb{T}^4}\big)$. We find that some of the degeneracies in the spectrum for large twist $w$ and large $N$ are lifted by these contributions. This suggests that integrability in the symmetric orbifold is broken by the non-planar (i.e. $\frac{1}{N}$) corrections.

authors.name: Matthias R. Gaberdiel, Beat Nairz, Cheng Peng

papers.title: Stochastic Survival near Swampland Boundaries
papers.summary: Swampland and compactification data tell us where a chosen EFT description can lose parametric control; stochastic cosmology asks which histories survive near that edge. We turn this question into a survival problem for fluctuating moduli over cosmological time scales. Given a valid stochastic generator, hard loss surfaces, soft degradation profiles, and finite horizons define a survival probability, whose negative logarithm is the survival action. The Doob transform then converts this logarithmic survival cost into the drift of the ensemble conditioned to remain on the controlled side. Near a regular hard boundary with nonzero normal diffusion, the inward normal component of the conditioned response is universal: it is fixed at leading order by the proper distance to the wall and the normal diffusion coefficient. The same finite-horizon construction also determines loss probabilities, first-exit statistics, survival hazards, and the control margin required to retain a prescribed fraction of histories. In this way, tower/species cutoffs, weak-coupling limits, string and Kaluza-Klein thresholds, and carefully qualified potential-based diagnostics acquire stochastic boundary layers without becoming microscopic forces. The inverse map tests when a conditioned drift is compatible with a scalar operational loss surface and reconstructs its boundary-normal Doob class. The construction therefore gives a stochastic survival interface between quantum-gravity control data and the cosmological histories that remain inside the prescribed EFT domain.

authors.name: Omer Guleryuz

papers.title: Near-horizon modifications in finite $N$ holography
papers.summary: If one extends the AdS/CFT extrapolate dictionary to large but finite $N$, we are expected to obtain non-perturbative violations of bulk semi-classicality and micro-causality. Previously this was achieved by implementing a late boundary time cut-off, while smearing the boundary operator via the HKLL kernel. By performing explicit bulk reconstructions in the backgrounds of near-horizon modified AdS$_2$ and BTZ black holes, we recover similar deviations from semi-classicality as above. For these black hole mimickers, the near-horizon modification is controlled by a throat parameter which sets the scale of this deviation. In three bulk dimensions, probe dynamics, for a fixed radial band, also exhibits a dip-ramp-plateau structure in their spectral form factor when averaged over the throat parameter. Such structure has also been found recently in the background with a stretched horizon or a brick wall.

authors.name: Rishkrith Bairy, Mrityunjay Nath, Debajyoti Sarkar

papers.title: Higher-Spin dS/CFT beyond minimal type-A, and the doubled nature of de Sitter space
papers.summary: We study the holographic duality between free vector models and Higher-Spin Gravity in 4-dimensional de Sitter space. On both the bulk and boundary sides, we introduce new reality conditions, which allow us to include odd spins in the bulk, and to extend the duality from type-A to type-B (i.e. from boundary scalars to spinors). The new reality conditions are closely related to a higher-spin-symmetric Hilbert-space norm for the single-particle (super)multiplet in de Sitter space. We construct two alternative viewpoints on the type-A and type-B theories. In one view, the two co-exist in "parallel universes", specifically in even vs. odd antipodal identifications of de Sitter space. In the other view, type-A and type-B are Legendre-transformed descriptions of the same twistor-space theory in Euclidean AdS (this involves the observation that the higher-spin partition function is Legendre-dual to itself). In this way, higher-spin holography reconciles the two-boundary nature of de Sitter space with the one-boundary nature of Euclidean AdS. The supersymmetric theory that unifies type-A and type-B with bulk fermions fails to be consistent under the appropriate reality conditions.

authors.name: Julian Lang, Yasha Neiman

papers.title: Divergences in Nonpolynomial Quantum Field Theories
papers.summary: The structure of divergences in several nonpolynomial scalar quantum field theories are investigated. Various $n$-point Green functions for nonpolynomial theories are calculated and their renormalization is analyzed, with special regard for the nonpolynomial $\left|\phi\right|^{3}$ theory in $4$ spacetime dimensions.

authors.name: Galib Hoq, Thomas Curtright

papers.title: Millicharged particles and the degree-3 Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem
papers.summary: We use geometry to solve a problem in arithmetic relevant for physics. Namely, for any $m$ we find all integer solutions to the equations $\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^k = \sum_{i=1}^m y_i^k$, where $k \in \{1,2,3\}$; this seems to be new for $m \geq 5$. In physics, these are the anomaly cancellation conditions for models with $m$ fermions which can be naturally light and carry small electric charges (a.k.a. millicharged or minicharged particles). The small charges arise by kinetic mixing of the Standard Model $U(1)$ gauge symmetry with an unbroken non-chiral (a.k.a. vector-like) $U(1)$ and the masses are suppressed by a spontaneously-broken chiral $U(1)$.

authors.name: Ben Gripaios

papers.title: Inverse KLT kernel of AdS string integrals from the intersection matrix
papers.summary: We develop a topological and combinatorial interpretation of the Kawai--Lewellen--Tye (KLT) relations for $n$-point AdS string-amplitude building blocks, which are disk integrals with multivariable multiple polylogarithm insertions and sphere integrals with their single-valued counterparts. Building on the framework of twisted de Rham theory over a noncommutative ring, we reformulate the problem in terms of associahedral chambers of the moduli space loaded with solutions of the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equation. We construct regularized twisted cycles and express their intersection pairings through local monodromies and Drinfeld associators, which control transport between fusion-tree normalizations. Organizing the intersection contributions by common boundary faces yields the intersection matrix, which is identified with the inverse KLT kernel by the twisted period relation. The field-theory limit of the inverse KLT kernel is also given.

authors.name: Yi-Xiao Tao, Shijie Zhang

papers.title: Type IIB Forms and Scalars from an $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Topological Field Theory with Boundary
papers.summary: We formulate the scalar and form-field sector of type IIB supergravity as an eleven-dimensional topological field theory with boundary. Unlike the pseudo-action, it is a genuine action principle with manifest global $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ symmetry. The IIB fields arise as edge modes: a boundary term breaks the $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ gauge symmetry to $\mathrm{SO}(2)$, so the axion-dilaton parametrizes $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SO}(2)$, and the boundary field equations give the duality relations, including $F_5$ self-duality. As the action never refers to the axion-dilaton directly, S-duality monodromies become holonomies of a flat connection.

authors.name: Euihun Joung, J. A. Rosabal

papers.title: Towards a recursive construction of string scattering amplitudes
papers.summary: We construct open superstring scattering amplitudes from three-point data using the Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten (BCFW) recursion and four-dimensional spinor helicity variables. We compute the contributions of selected leading and subleading Regge families to the color-ordered four-gluon amplitude by sewing their cubic couplings and summing over intermediate polarizations. The four-dimensional description makes helicity selection rules explicit and reduces the massive polarization sums to SU(2) little group contractions. The resulting residues are expressed in terms of Jacobi and Legendre polynomials, yielding explicit sums over mass levels. We construct a differential operator relating the two polynomial kernels, including their level-dependent normalizations. These results provide a concrete starting point for organizing the infinite intermediate-state sum and investigating whether relations among Regge families can support a recursive reconstruction of the full string amplitude.

authors.name: Arkajyoti Manna

papers.title: Holographic warped CFTs on AdS$_3$, parity violation and unitarity
papers.summary: We consider recently introduced boundary conditions for General Relativity on AdS$_3$, whose canonical generators span the warped conformal algebra, in the case of the Einstein-Hilbert action supplemented by parity-odd terms that do not modify the field equations in vacuum. The canonical generators are shown to acquire nonlinear contributions, and their algebra remains being the semidirect sum of Virasoro and $u(1)$ Kac-Moody, but with shifted central extensions. Thus, for suitable values of the parity-odd coupling, the Kac-Moody level can be nonnegative ($k_\text{KM}\geq 0$), admitting unitary representations. Nevertheless, requiring the black hole entropy to be nonnegative, implies $k_\text{KM}\leq 0$, in agreement with the established understanding of holographic warped CFTs. Compatibility of both requirements (entropy and unitarity) then singles out the case $k_\text{KM}=0$. However, the field equations degenerate in this case, which can be amended by imposing vanishing torsion as a constraint. The theory then precisely becomes Topologically Massive Gravity (TMG) at the chiral point, suggesting the extension of our boundary conditions to accommodate nontrivial logarithmic branches.

authors.name: Kristiansen Lara, Ricardo Troncoso

papers.title: Tripartite nonlocal magic from reflected and negativity spectra
papers.summary: A tripartite pure state is local-unitary equivalent to a stabilizer state if and only if its marginal, reflected, and negativity spectra (up to signs) are flat. These conditions are quantified using anti-flatness, giving a diagnostic of tripartite nonlocal magic that is computable and experimentally measurable using randomized measurements. In non-abelian quantum doubles, it appears only when the triple points of the tripartition lie on plaquettes. In random tensor networks, it appears exactly when the entanglement wedge of two boundary regions connects.

authors.name: Sriram Akella

papers.title: Effective scalar-fluid description of thermal first-order phase transitions and their spinodal instabilities
papers.summary: We formulate an improved scalar-fluid effective description of first-order phase transitions in relativistic theories, and test it against a microscopic calculation in a holographic model. The effective theory shows that the nature of the spinodal instability is linked to thermodynamic stability, determined by the sign of the specific heat. When the specific heat is positive, the sound modes are stable and there is a non-hydrodynamic instability. When it is negative, a sound mode becomes unstable instead. The holographic calculation confirms the validity of the effective description at long wavelengths, improving on the purely hydrodynamic description. We also identify a friction coefficient that governs the bubble wall velocity and can be extracted from a holographic correlator.

authors.name: Alessio Caddeo, Oscar Henriksson, Carlos Hoyos, Mikel Sanchez-Garitaonandia, Pedro Taranc\'on-\'Alvarez

papers.title: Echoes and light rings of regular black holes and their singular counterparts
papers.summary: Recent work [Phys. Rev. D 111, 104040] showed that the Bardeen and Hayward solutions arise as fine-tuned regular members of broader families that also contain singular black holes. We study massless scalar and auxiliary Maxwell perturbations of these solutions using time-domain evolution and a sixth-order WKB approximation. For part of the singular branch, the time-domain profiles exhibit late-time echoes and the effective potentials develop a double-barrier structure. We also examine null geodesics of the background metric. The same singular branch can have two exterior maxima of the null effective potential separated by a minimum, whereas the type-I regular black holes have a single exterior maximum. The Bardeen and Hayward families display the same qualitative behavior.

authors.name: Xiao-Pin Rao, Xiao Qian Wang, Hyat Huang

papers.title: Interplay between the chiral and deconfinement transitions from a Curci-Ferrari-based Polyakov loop potential
papers.summary: We couple the two-flavor Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model to a gluonic background corresponding to the gauge-field expectation value in the center-symmetric Landau gauge. Low-energy features in this gauge are captured by a center-symmetric extension of the Curci-Ferrari model and provide a good grasp on key aspects of the confinement/deconfinement transition. Within this framework, we can investigate the interplay between the chiral and deconfinement transitions. Compared to other approaches based on multi-parameter Ans\"atze of the Polyakov loop potential fixed from comparison to finite-temperature lattice data, the modeling of the glue sector in the present set-up depends on only one phenomenological parameter that can be fixed by comparison to lattice data in the vacuum. We detail the structure of the phase diagram, with special emphasis on the finite density axis, and compute thermodynamical observables relevant for applications. We also highlight the properties of the recently introduced net quark number response of the medium as a sensible probe of the phases of QCD, in particular as a tool to disambiguate the nature of certain regions of the phase diagram where the use of the Polyakov loops could lead to misinterpretations. Finally, we critically assess the sensitivity of our results to the various parameters, both in the glue sector and in the chiral sector.

authors.name: V. Tomas Mari Surkau, Urko Reinosa

papers.title: A strongly hyperbolic viscous relativistic hydrodynamics theory with first-order charge current
papers.summary: We extend the first order dissipative relativistic hydrodynamics model of Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha- Kovtun (BDNK) in order to include the charge number current in full first order expansion with out-of-equilibrium contribution proportional to the evolution equation of the ideal fluid. We obtain a fully second order system of partial differential equation (PDE) that can be casted in a fully conservative way. We analyze the hyperbolicity of this model coupled to Einstein field equations using a newly developed technique that allows for hyperbolicity studies without explicit first order reduction. Furthermore, we identify a frame choice where our formulation is causal, stable and with positive entropy generation for a wide range of equations of state (EoS). Our analysis shows that the inclusion of an out-of-equilibrium correction to the charge current, plays an important role in guaranteeing the strong hyperbolicity and, therefore, the well-posedness of the system.

authors.name: Federico Schianchi, Fernando Abalos

papers.title: Quantum gravitodiamagnetic interaction
papers.summary: In the framework of linearized quantum gravity, we investigate the quantum gravitational interaction induced by the gravitodiamagnetic coupling of two massive objects to vacuum fluctuations of the gravitational field. Starting from the Lagrangian of a particle in a gravitational field and employing the formalism of Weyl gravitoelectromagnetism, we derive the interaction Hamiltonian associated with gravitodiamagnetic coupling. Unlike the linear couplings that arise in gravitoelectric and gravitomagnetic interactions, the gravitodiamagnetic coupling depends quadratically on the gravitomagnetic field. Based on this Hamiltonian, we show that, for a spherically symmetric gravitational hydrogen-like system in its ground state, the induced quadrupole moment has the opposite sign to the applied gravitomagnetic field, which is the defining signature of gravitodiamagnetism. Using leading-order perturbation theory, we derive an explicit expression for the gravitodiamagnetic interaction potential, valid for $r\gg a$, where $r$ is the separation and $a$ the characteristic size of the objects. Unlike previously studied quantum gravitational interactions, which exhibit distinct power laws in the near and far regions defined relative to the characteristic transition wavelength of the gravitational hydrogen-like systems, the gravitodiamagnetic interaction is attractive and scales as $r^{-11}$ throughout its regime of validity.

authors.name: Di Hao, Jiawei Hu, Hongwei Yu

papers.title: Probing the dynamical inverse seesaw mechanism with low-frequency gravitational waves
papers.summary: We study the possibility of probing the dynamical inverse seesaw mechanism for the origin of light neutrino masses via the detection of stochastic gravitational waves (GW) in the low-frequency regime currently being probed by pulsar timing arrays. As the lepton number-violating term in inverse seesaw typically remains in the sub-MeV ballpark, its dynamical origin naturally brings the possibility of a low-scale first-order phase transition, which can be probed at low-frequency GW experiments. We also find interesting complementarity with heavy neutral lepton searches, as GW experiments remain sensitive to parameter space with small active-sterile mixing, which is out of reach for most particle physics experiments.

authors.name: Debasish Borah, Sounak Dutta, Partha Kumar Paul, Indrajit Saha, Narendra Sahu

papers.title: Hidden Conformal Boundary Data in Finite-Temperature Stabilizer Entropy
papers.summary: We study the finite-temperature stabilizer R\'enyi entropy of the open critical transverse-field Ising chain. At R\'enyi index one half, this observable probes the distribution of thermal Pauli-string expectation values and can be written as a sum over absolute values of all square minors of a finite-temperature correlation matrix. We show that this exponentially large sum is exactly reducible to a single Pfaffian. The Pfaffian representation reveals a block Toeplitz--Hankel structure and allows us to extract the large-size scaling in several thermal regimes. In the crossover window where the inverse temperature is proportional to the system size, the stabilizer numerator factorizes into a saturated extensive contribution and a universal finite-size scaling function. We find that this scaling function is a level-eight eta quotient, rather than the ordinary free-boundary Majorana thermal factor. We identify it with the normalized midpoint disorder-field one-point function of the free-boundary Ising CFT. The deviation is exponentially hidden at low temperature but becomes manifest in the small-\(\tau\) modular limit, where it gives a Cardy-like asymptotic for the Pauli-string expectation-weight spectrum. These results show that finite-temperature stabilizer entropy probes a universal Ising disorder-field amplitude that is invisible to ordinary thermodynamic probes.

authors.name: Reyhaneh Khasseh, M. A. Rajabpour

papers.title: Mass Varying Neutrino Oscillation in Teleparallel Gravity
papers.summary: In the Cartan teleparallel formulation of gravity, a scalar field coupled to the torsion tensor can acquire an environment-dependent effective mass. This gives rise to a screening effect: inside dense bodies such as the Sun, the scalar field is suppressed, causing the neutrino mass to vary with local density. We investigate the impact of this torsion-induced screening on solar neutrino oscillations. The mechanism modifies the standard MSW resonance condition distinctly, leading to detectable shifts in the flavor conversion probability. Using data from solar neutrino experiments (Super-Kamiokande, Borexino, SNO), we place constraints on the torsion scalar coupling parameters. Our work provides a concrete test of teleparallel gravity through mass-varying neutrino oscillations.

authors.name: H. Mohseni Sadjadi, H. Yazdani Ahmadabadi

papers.title: Spherical-DAHA predictions for boundary monopole bubbling of non-minuscule 't Hooft lines in $\mathcal N=4$ SYM
papers.summary: We study non-minuscule boundary 't Hooft lines in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ $U(N)$ super Yang-Mills theory with the regular Nahm-pole boundary condition. For one-row charges we construct the spherical-DAHA operator $\mathbf{e}_+h_r(Y)\mathbf{e}_+$ and determine its finite shift expansion and discrete Macdonald spectrum. For the first non-minuscule $U(2)$ coefficient, a local two-minuscule convolution model with Higgs branch $T^*\mathbb{P}^1$ has two Jeffrey-Kirwan residues, while subtracting the determinant intersection-cohomology summand supplies the additional $-\mathfrak{t}$ term. The same transverse $A_1$ calculation, dressed by the spectator-root factor, reproduces the first lower $U(3)$ coefficient. The two residues are the cross terms of the square of the first Macdonald-Ruijsenaars operator and the subtraction realizes $h_2=e_1^2-e_2$, so that this calculation is a geometric realization of the algebraic coefficient, while its boundary-localization interpretation remains conjectural. We then let the operators act on the evaluation functionals at the points $q^\lambda\mathfrak{t}^\rho$ with $\rho=(N-1,\ldots,0)$, which for minuscule $\lambda$ coincide, up to a common factor and the order of the entries, with the fugacities of the Higgsing computation of Hatsuda and Okazaki. The zero-shift coefficient at $\mathfrak{t}^\rho$ of the product of the two oppositely oriented operators equals the normalized Neumann Wilson two-point function for every one-row charge, and for $U(2)$ and $r=2$ this equality requires the $-\mathfrak{t}$ term.

authors.name: Ruiliang Li

papers.title: Minkowskian open/closed conformal field theory possibly without vacuum: the Cardy case
papers.summary: For any conformal net, not necessarily rational, we construct the associated Cardy-type conformal field theory on the Minkowski spacetimes $(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)\times\mathbb R$ for closed strings and $[0,\pi]\times\mathbb R$ for open strings within the framework of algebraic quantum field theory. In addition to verifying some of their basic properties, we prove three forms of Haag duality for multi-double-cones and boundary intervals, interpreted respectively as the Minkowskian versions of modular invariance, the Cardy consistency condition, and the Morita equivalence of boundary field algebras.

authors.name: Bin Gui

papers.title: Preheating and oscillon formation in Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
papers.summary: Non-perturbative processes in the early universe may create overdense structures in scalar fields like the inflaton, called oscillons. In this work, we explore whether the leading order higher derivative contributions to the scalar-tensor theory change the formation and growth of these structures, and investigate the limits in which the effective field theory (EFT) description breaks down. We find that whilst the properties of the oscillons are not significantly modified, and black holes do not generically form, for large couplings the period of formation can result in the evolution leaving the regime of validity of the EFT, at which point predictivity is lost and the next order terms in the EFT should become relevant. If the oscillons survive their formation, they tend to be stable and the EFT corrections remain bounded. The EFT breakdown is triggered by large curvature terms in the metric in the densest regions of the oscillon, meaning that approximations of such modified theories that neglect the local backreaction and non-linear dynamics of the fields may miss important effects.

authors.name: Areef Waeming, Josu C. Aurrekoetxea, Katy Clough, Pau Figueras, \'Aron D. Kov\'acs

papers.title: False vacuum decay in long-range interacting quantum systems
papers.summary: We formulate false-vacuum decay in a mixed-field Ising chain with $r^{-(1+\sigma)}$ interactions as a spatially nonlocal Euclidean $\phi^4$ theory featuring a fractional spatial kinetic term $\sim |q|^\sigma$. The nonlocal bounce is anisotropic in space-time and develops algebraic spatial tails. Combining thin-wall arguments with numerical solutions of the full nonlocal saddle, we find two nucleation regimes separated by $\sigma = 1$. For $0<\sigma<1$, the lifetime exponent scales with the energy bias $h$ of the metastable state as $B\sim h^{-1/\sigma}$; for $1<\sigma<2$, the leading Coleman scaling $B\sim h^{-1}$ is recovered, while long-range effects are retained in the subleading correction $\sim h^{\sigma-2}$. The same exponents are recovered directly within a two-kink description of the Ising chain on the lattice. Our results show that tunable long-range interactions fundamentally reshape bubble nucleation and alter false-vacuum decay in quantum simulators.

authors.name: Valerio Pagni, Laura Batini, Nicol\`o Defenu

papers.title: Neutron stars in $f(Q) = Q +\xi Q^2$ gravity
papers.summary: Modified theories of gravity based on the symmetric teleparallel framework have recently attracted considerable attention as viable alternatives to General Relativity. In this context, f(Q) gravity, in which the gravitational interaction is encoded in the nonmetricity scalar Q, provides a consistent geometrical formulation that differs from the standard curvature-based description. In this work, we investigate the structure of neutron stars within a family of f(Q) gravity models by employing realistic equations of state, namely FPS, SLy, ENG and MPA1. Using the covariant formulation of f(Q) gravity, we derive the corresponding Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations and apply them to model compact stellar configurations. Numerical integration of the field equations provides the mass-radius relations and the maximum masses supported by each equation of state, enabling a direct comparison with current observational constraints. Furthermore, we analyze the behavior of the nonmetricity scalar both inside and outside the stellar object, providing additional insight into the gravitational structure of compact stars in this framework.

authors.name: J. C. N. de Araujo, H. G. M. Fortes

papers.title: Neural-Spectral Discovery of Rotating Black Holes Beyond General Relativity
papers.summary: Finding rotating black hole solutions in higher-curvature theories of gravity is a problem of fundamental importance. Virtually every approach to reconcile gravity with quantum mechanics predicts corrections to the Einstein-Hilbert action, yet no systematic solution-generating method exists for the stationary sector. We close this gap with Akribeia, a novel hybrid framework that pairs physics-informed neural networks with a pseudo-spectral refinement step, yielding certified neural-field rotating black hole solutions ---continuous, globally defined functions, parametric in the coupling constants--- whose residuals against the field equations are verified to extreme precision. We apply the method to theories quadratic and cubic in the curvature and construct, for the first time, families of rotating black holes featuring multiple non-vanishing angular momenta, parametric in the new coupling constants. After validating against previously known five-dimensional spacetimes, we present new solutions in scenarios leading to a highly non-linear/non-perturbative coupled system of ordinary differential equations. Our method can be systematically adapted to other setups involving partial differential equations as well.

authors.name: Felipe Agurto-Sep\'ulveda, Marcelo Oyarzo, Anxo Biasi, Devansh Agarwal, Ethan Tregidga, James F. Steiner, Jose D. Edelstein, Gaston Giribet, Cecilia Garraffo

papers.title: The Goldstone Awakens: Unimodular dark energy in scale-invariant $R^2$ gravity
papers.summary: We construct an $R^2$ cosmology based on scale invariance and unimodular gravity in which the Goldstone boson of dilatations establishes a predictive connection between inflation and dark energy.
