The conservation of the corresponding Noether current confines the inflationary trajectory to a one-dimensional orbit in field space, freezing the Goldstone direction and rendering the inflationary dynamics effectively single field. After inflation, the system settles on a Minkowski vacuum manifold. The unimodular integration constant, already present in the full theory but negligible during inflation, lifts the flat Goldstone direction, generating an exponential potential for the canonically normalised field. Unlike in phenomenological quintessence models, its slope is not a free DE parameter, but is instead fixed by the field-space geometry inherited from the inflationary attractor. This geometry excludes matter-era tracking and, throughout the inflationary viability region, places the field in the thawing regime compatible with accelerated expansion. For a representative inflationary benchmark, the now pseudo-Goldstone field remains frozen until close to the present epoch, yielding DE equation-of-state parameters $(w_0,w_a)\simeq(-0.992,-0.011)$ in the CPL parametrisation $w(a)=w_0+w_a(1-a)$. More generally, the same parameter controlling the inflationary spectral tilt also fixes the slope of the DE potential, leading to a tight correlation between early- and late-Universe observables: increasing the thawing signal lowers $n_s$, while values of $n_s$ closer to unity drive the model towards $\Lambda$CDM.

authors.name: Mariaveronica De Angelis, Javier Rubio

papers.title: Monopoles, Strings, Walls and Gravitational waves
papers.summary: The gauge symmetry breaking $SU(2) \to U(1) \to Z_2 \to 1$ successively produces monopoles, strings and domain walls bounded by strings (WBS), with the elementary monopole carrying a $U(1)$ magnetic flux twice as large as the elementary string. The elementary strings and subsequently WBS emit gravitational waves, and during their decay, the WBS yield a network of composite strings that carry the same $U(1)$ flux as the monopoles. Depending on the cosmological evolution, we provide the gravitational wave spectra generated by the elementary strings and WBS, in combination with the composite strings which are either effectively stable, quasistable, or metastable. These three scenarios are also realized in the symmetry breaking chain $SU(3) \to SO(3) \to Z_2 \to 1$. Both $SU(2)$ and $SU(3)$ have appeared in the literature as flavor gauge symmetries.

authors.name: Rinku Maji, Qaisar Shafi

papers.title: A major origin of quantumness
papers.summary: A system property is considered to be elementary, when any further refined specification is impossible. Any two elementary properties of a classical system mutually exclude each other. However, this does not hold anymore for a quantum system, where mutual exclusivity becomes a special relation. This orthogonality relation becomes our first axiom. It is sufficient to define states in an abstract setting and we then introduce two simple, but far-reaching further basic axioms for the states, which mimic the quantum mechanical correspondence between the pure states and the rank-one projections. All examples that we can identify origin from operator algebras or certain Jordan algebras and require the Gleason theorem. The identification of further cases is an unresolved challenge. If some exist, they might result in promising new mathematical models for an extended quantum theory. The non-existence would mean that our extremely basic postulates bring us unexpectedly close to common quantum theory. In any case, the distinction between inequality and mutual exclusivity of elementary system properties appears to be a major origin of quantumness. Our basic approach does not encompass the non-atomic von Neumann algebras of type II and III, which play a crucial role in quantum field theory, and we present a modification of the axioms to include them.

authors.name: Gerd Niestegge

papers.title: Gravitational Waves from Superconducting Cosmic Strings
papers.summary: We study the evolution of superconducting cosmic-string networks in a $U(1)_{\rm local}\times U(1)_{\rm global}$ field-theoretic model using three-dimensional lattice field simulations in an expanding universe. The scalar field charged under $U(1)_{\rm local}$ forms cosmic strings, while the scalar field associated with $U(1)_{\rm global}$ acts as a current carrier and condenses in their vicinity. We investigate the evolution of the string network for several values of the coupling constant between the string-forming and current-carrier fields and estimate the gravitational-wave power spectrum sourced by the resulting superconducting cosmic-string network. We find that the spectral shape depends on the coupling constant: as the interaction strength increases, the spectrum is suppressed on small scales. This feature may be probed by future high-frequency gravitational-wave observations.

authors.name: Jinyoung Jhun, Takashi Hiramatsu

papers.title: Kerr-Newman and genuine Kerr black holes in the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field
papers.summary: We present a spacetime that describes a rotating and charged black hole immersed in an external magnetic (or electric) field which is oriented along the rotational axis. This solution is characterized by four physical parameters, namely the black hole mass $m$, its charge $e$, Kerr-like rotation $a$, and the value of the external field $B$. Such exact solution to the Einstein-Maxwell equations has a surprisingly simple form. Moreover, for $B=0$ it reduces to standard Kerr-Newman metric, while for $m=0$ and $e=0$ we recover the Bertotti-Robinson universe with a uniform (electro-)magnetic field. We also show that the Kerr-BR solution presented in [Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 181401 (2025)] has a special charge, and we identify a genuine uncharged Kerr black hole immersed in the magnetic field. In the weak-field limit, it gives the Wald solution. We analyze the main physical properties of the new family, namely singularities, horizons, regularity of axes, charges, entropy, and temperature.

authors.name: Hryhorii Ovcharenko, Jiri Podolsky

papers.title: Four-Point String Monodromy from Six-Point Supersymmetric Consistency
papers.summary: Can finite-particle consistency determine an infinite string amplitude? For four-dimensional planar tree-level $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills effective theories with a specified scalar parity condition, we derive all-order constraints directly from physical six-point Ward identities and local factorization. An overlapping-channel limit forces a scalar cocycle, while an explicit differential Ward functional eliminates all relevant five- and six-point contact freedom and fixes the four-point kernel by $q''=-6c_{00}q$. Its normalized branches are linear, trigonometric, and hyperbolic, and the target amplitude obeys the associated four-point monodromy. If its entire pole-subtracted axis sequence additionally admits one common nonzero positive moment measure, the trigonometric branch is selected and the complete Veneziano low-energy germ is unique up to scale. The result separates a formal low-energy necessity theorem from its conditional analytic-germ uniqueness corollary; no worldsheet or auxiliary KLT-module membership is assumed for the physical theorem.

authors.name: Jianqi Sheng

papers.title: Gauge-parameter cancellation and finite form factors in one-loop quark scattering in the refined Gribov-Zwanziger framework
papers.summary: We calculate the one-loop amplitude for distinct-flavor massless quark scattering in a local BRST-invariant refined Gribov-Zwanziger theory with minimally coupled quarks. The constraint determinant and two dynamical quark flavors are included in the action and loop sum. Retaining the RGZ masses in the free field matrix, we combine the mixed self-energy insertion, complete vertex and box corrections, and external-leg residues. The difference between a general linear covariant gauge and a reference gauge vanishes symbolically after removal of the Stueckelberg regulator in the specified dimensional prescription. We separate ultraviolet and infrared poles, including contributions hidden by scaleless integrals and the order of mass and dimensional limits. Local modified-minimal-subtraction counterterms cancel the ultraviolet poles, and the remaining infrared poles cancel in the stated nonzero-mass domain. The finite result is supplied as eight color-spin form factors over a thirty-entry scalar integral inventory, with all 144 finite-function coefficients provided electronically. Physical-region benchmarks evaluate the scalar functions on a common analytic sheet. Along a specified common-mass scaling path, the four physical color-helicity coefficients approach the QCD finite hard amplitudes numerically at three scattering angles after an explicit infrared conversion. Infrared helicity differences isolate color-dependent mass corrections beyond a universal rescaling of the Born exchange. A low-momentum expansion identifies an effective contact-interaction scale and clarifies the suppression relative to massless exchange. The result defines a partonic amplitude on a specified analytic branch; it does not establish a unitary colored-state S matrix or an inclusive next-to-leading-order cross section.

authors.name: Wan Wu

papers.title: Hadron masses and pseudoscalar meson form factors in a Poincar\'e-invariant constituent quark model
papers.summary: We study a Poincar\'e-invariant constituent quark model with pair, fine-structure, and finite-range three-quark interactions treated in the diagonalization. A fit of 20 parameters to 36 meson and 27 baryon masses gives an rms deviation of $6.85\,\mathrm{MeV}$, with the common offset fixed by a spectral condition. The same mass-fit wave functions give the elastic form factors of ten pseudoscalar mesons in the light-front impulse approximation with the Melosh rotation. The pion and charged-kaon radii are $0.407$ and $0.411\,\mathrm{fm}$, below the measured values. Unlike experiment, the kaon radius slightly exceeds the pion radius. Replacing the pion radial function by the normalized $S$-wave component of the $\rho$ raises its radius to $0.604\,\mathrm{fm}$, showing that hyperfine compression accounts for most of the deficit in the mean-square charge radius. With the light-quark size fixed by the pion, the $K^+$ and $K^0$ radii require strange-quark sizes that differ by $2.2$ standard deviations.

authors.name: Jongheon Baek

papers.title: Nucleon light-front transverse densities from three-body and quark + diquark Faddeev equations
papers.summary: Nucleon elastic electromagnetic form factors obtained from two complementary continuum Schwinger function approaches -- a Poincar\'e-covariant three-body Faddeev equation formulated in rainbow-ladder truncation and a quark + fully-interacting-diquark, $q(qq)$, Faddeev equation -- are used to chart light-front transverse charge and magnetisation densities of the proton, the neutron, and their dressed valence quarks. Going beyond a comparison of observables, the bound-state amplitudes that underlie them are also compared. Both amplitudes are dominated by $s$-wave structures; and in the three-body solution, the mixed-antisymmetric (mixed-symmetric) flavour component is dominated by structures with the Dirac character of scalar (axialvector) diquark correlations, so that the association between these flavour components and diquark correlations is realised explicitly. The $q(qq)$ amplitude falls more slowly with the quark-diquark relative momentum than the three-body amplitude does with the corresponding Jacobi momentum. The two descriptions deliver mutually compatible densities, which match expectations based on modern parametrisations of data. Transverse-plane valence $u$- and $d$-quark Dirac radii are practically indistinguishable, whereas the $d$-quark Pauli radius is roughly 10% larger; and the valence $d$ quark is magnetically far more active than the valence $u$ quark, a feature tied to the mixed-symmetric (axialvector-diquark) components of the nucleon amplitude. For a $+\hat{x}$ polarised nucleon, positive charge is displaced in the $+\hat{y}$ direction, with the opposite effect for negative charge.

authors.name: Zhen-Ni Xu, Zhao-Qian Yao, Peng Cheng

papers.title: Theory of Particle Scattering on Superconducting Qubits: From Single Devices to Quantum Arrays
papers.summary: Superconducting qubits provide microwave-scale transitions and thus offer quantum targets for direct particle scattering with extremely small energy transfer. We develop a general framework for inelastic scattering in which an incident particle exchanges an off-shell photon with a superconducting quantum circuit, inducing a transition from a lower-energy internal state of the circuit to a higher-energy one. The target dependence is encoded in a finite-momentum electromagnetic transition current and, for charge-dominated response, in a qubit transition form factor. A key feature of particle scattering is that a microwave-scale excitation does not necessarily correspond to a long-wavelength interaction, since nonrelativistic particles can transfer spatial momenta much larger than the deposited energy. The full finite-momentum device response is therefore essential. We specialize the formalism to transmon qubits, construct a realistic electrostatic response for a planar Xmon-style transmon, and apply it to photon-mediated scattering of eV-scale bosonic dark matter, including final-state Bose stimulation. We find that the resulting enhancement substantially improves the projected sensitivity at the lowest masses. Owing to the exceptionally low transition threshold of superconducting qubits, this approach opens sensitivity to dark matter in the eV-to-keV mass range, which remains largely unexplored by existing direct-detection experiments. We further show that $N$ independently operated qubits give the expected rate proportional to $N$, while suitably prepared Dicke states can in principle achieve a collective enhancement approaching $N^2$ when spatial coherence is maintained across the array. These results establish superconducting qubits as quantum targets for direct particle scattering and provide a framework for optimizing low-threshold dark-matter searches.

authors.name: Doojin Kim, Kyoungchul Kong, Myeonghun Park

papers.title: Automate the geometric SMEFT at dimension eight
papers.summary: We present the first complete dimension-eight implementation of the geometric Standard Model Effective Field Theory (geoSMEFT) as UFO models for event generators such as MadGraph. The models contain all 674 baryon-number-conserving operators, with minimal flavour violation for the fermionic operators, and are also provided in the Murphy basis. We include dimension-six contributions and electroweak input-parameter corrections consistently through order $1/\Lambda^4$, and provide dimension-eight squared contributions as a diagnostic of EFT truncation. We validate the implementation against independent calculations and Ward identities. To make these models practical for collider studies, we develop a standalone tool that identifies all operators contributing to a given process at tree level, including those entering through input-parameter shifts. It reports their expected energy scaling and generates a restriction card to reduce the computational cost of event generation. The same geometric construction allows us to calculate two- and three-point functions beyond dimension eight, to arbitrary order in $1/\Lambda^2$. The models and the tool are publicly available.

authors.name: Beno\^it Assi, Adam Martin

papers.title: Dirac leptogenesis with charged leptons
papers.summary: Popular frameworks that explain the baryon asymmetry of the Universe (BAU) are electroweak baryogenesis, requiring a first-order phase transition, and Majorana leptogenesis, which relies on lepton number violation in the neutrino sector. Dirac leptogenesis offers an alternative mechanism that avoids both requirements, instead allowing the BAU to follow from previously generated chiral asymmetries that remain out of equilibrium in the early Universe. Conventional realizations of this scenario typically invoke ultra-light Dirac neutrinos. In this work, we generalize the mechanism to include Standard Model charged leptons by assuming that their mass-generating interactions have a UV origin and arise from higher-dimensional operators. For concreteness, the analysis is performed within a Froggatt-Nielsen setup, which allows us to naturally address fermionic mass hierarchies, too, now linked to the BAU, and we show that the proposed mechanism is viable by supercooling the flavon phase transition. The framework predicts a flavon with a (1.7-50) GeV mass, bounded by the non-observation of lepton flavor violation and the requirement for the Universe to not reheat above sphaleron temperatures, which could be indirectly probed by future lepton flavor violation experiments.

authors.name: Juan P. Garc\'es, Florian Goertz, Maya Hager

papers.title: Resonance-aware NLOPS matching for off-shell $t\bar t+tW$ production in association with a Higgs boson
papers.summary: We present a new NLO QCD Monte Carlo generator for the complete off-shell final state encompassing $t\bar tH$ and $tWH$ production with dileptonic decays, matched to parton showers in the resonance-aware POWHEG-RES framework. At Born level the calculation corresponds to the process $pp\to b\bar b\,e^+\nu_e\,\mu^-\bar\nu_\mu\,H$ in the four-flavour scheme with massive $b$ quarks. The complete matrix elements include all double-resonant, single-resonant and non-resonant topologies, all interferences and spin correlations, with both top quarks and $W$ bosons treated in the complex-mass scheme. This approach provides a unified and consistent treatment of $t\bar{t} H$ and $tWH$ production modes without the need for a diagram-removal or diagram-subtraction prescription. The generator, dubbed $\texttt{bb4lH}$, is implemented in the POWHEG-RES framework with OpenLoops amplitudes, and takes advantage of the multiple-radiation scheme ($\texttt{allrad}$) and of matrix-element-based resonance projectors. Semileptonic events are also supported and can be obtained from dileptonic ones, including QCD radiation in the hadronic $W$-boson decay. In addition, we present two new on-shell POWHEG generators for $t\bar{t} H$ and $tWH$ production, the latter being the first of its kind. We validate all generators against known fixed-order results and in the narrow-width limit, and present NLO and NLOPS predictions for the LHC in the dileptonic and semileptonic channels. Tuned comparisons with the corresponding on-shell descriptions show good agreement for inclusive observables, while sizeable differences arise in observables sensitive to the reconstructed top-quark line shape and in $tWH$-enriched regions. These findings are of direct relevance for the LHC analysis of $t\bar{t} H$ events and for the separation of $t\bar{t} H$ and $tWH$ production.

authors.name: Patrick E. Hurley, Tom\'a\v{s} Je\v{z}o, Jonas M. Lindert

papers.title: Naturalness scale inference in chiral perturbation theory and chiral logarithms
papers.summary: We infer naturalness scales of chiral perturbation theory in the mesonic sector using Bayesian techniques that are extended to explicitly take into account chiral logarithms. To demonstrate our approach, we consider the chiral expansion of the pion decay constant $F_\pi$ and the threshold and subthreshold parameters of $\pi\pi$ scattering. We find a strong observable dependence of the inferred naturalness scales, and show that they need not coincide with the pion mass at which the order-by-order hierarchy of the chiral expansion breaks down. As an application, we discuss the requirements for lattice-QCD constraints on the two combinations of $O(p^6)$ low-energy constants that in the current matching of Roy-equation analyses to chiral perturbation theory need to be estimated from resonance saturation, but could be extracted from the pion-mass dependence of $\pi\pi$ scattering parameters.

authors.name: Tara Hassanzadeh, Martin Hoferichter, Lucas Platter, Jacobo Ruiz de Elvira, Matthias R. Schindler

papers.title: Radiative-recoil corrections at order $\alpha^2 (Z \alpha)^5$ to energy levels of muonium and positronium
papers.summary: We have calculated radiative-recoil corrections at order $\alpha^2 (Z \alpha)^5$ to the energy levels of spin-1/2--spin-1/2 Coulombic bound systems. The corrections we consider involve two exchange photons with two-loop radiative corrections on the electron line. We obtain precise results for all values of the mass ratio. Our results are relevant for upcoming improved measurements of the muonium ground-state hyperfine splitting and 1S-2S interval.

authors.name: Gregory S. Adkins, Addison Kovats-Bernat, Elias Mitchell, A. Volkan Turan

papers.title: Small-$x$ helicity evolution with gluon saturation
papers.summary: We include gluon saturation in the revised small-$x$ helicity evolution at large $N_c$. Keeping the unpolarized dipole $S$-matrices, set to one in the double-logarithmic approximation, we derive the evolution equations for the polarized dipole amplitudes $G$, $G_2$ and their neighbor amplitudes. The equations reduce exactly to the known ones for $S=1$ and contain new terms proportional to $1-S$, including one in the equation for $G_2$ arising because the real and virtual contributions that cancel for $S=1$ are weighted differently by the $S$-matrix of the small daughter dipole; this term is ultraviolet finite and acts only for a saturated daughter dipole. Inside the saturation region the growth rate of $G$ drops from $3.66$ to $2\sqrt{1-\lambda}$, in units of $\sqrt{\alpha_sN_c/2\pi}$, with $\lambda$ the growth exponent of the saturation scale, while $G_2$ oscillates without growing. In the asymptotic regime, the gluon helicity $\Delta G$ reaches a maximum and decreases, while the quark helicity $\Delta\Sigma$ and $g_1$ keep growing with an exponent set by the dipoles at the edge of the saturation region, obtained in closed form; saturation raises the critical $\alpha_s$ below which the integral of $\Delta\Sigma$ converges from $0.156$ to $0.21$ for $\lambda=0.25$. For $10^{-2}\ge x\ge10^{-6}$ we solve the equations numerically with a target described by the running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov equation, with a saturation scale close to the one extracted from HERA data. At the reach of the Electron-Ion Collider, $x\sim10^{-4}$, and $Q^2=10$ GeV$^2$, saturation reduces $\Delta G$ by a factor of about three and $\Delta\Sigma$ by about two; both still grow, more slowly. Comparing three choices of the starting point, $x_0=0.1$ and $0.01$, we find that this dependence is lost toward $x=10^{-6}$.

authors.name: Michael Roa

papers.title: Helicity amplitudes and angular distributions in $D\to b_1(1235)(\to\omega\pi)\ell^+\nu_\ell$
papers.summary:
Using the helicity amplitude technique, we derive the decay intensity for the charmed meson semileptonic decays $D	o b_1(1235)\ell^+
u_\ell, b_1(1235)	o\omega\pi$ with $\ell=e,\mu$. Based on the theoretically predicted hadronic transition form factors, the branching fractions for $D^0	o b_1(1235)^-\ell^+
u_\ell$ and their lepton flavor universality ratios are calculated. The predicted branching fractions of the positronic channel span $(2.6$--$8.8)	imes10^{-5}$, with most theoretical predictions being consistent with the previous BESIII measurement $(7.2\pm1.8^{+0.6}_{-0.8})	imes10^{-5}$ by assuming $\mathcal{B}(b_1(1235)	o\omega\pi)=1$. We further explore the partial decay widths and angular distributions of $D	o b_1(1235)\ell^+
u_\ell, b_1(1235)	o\omega\pi$ and find distinct behavior among various hadronic transition form factors. Further amplitude analysis with larger statistics is thus desired to test these theoretical predictions.

authors.name: Yijia Zeng, Hailong Ma

papers.title: A New Gravitational Wave Power Law from Dissipative Sound Waves in Cosmological Phase Transitions
papers.summary: Power-law behavior in cosmological gravitational wave (GW) spectra reveals the physical nature of their sources. For sound waves generated by cosmological first-order phase transitions, we identify a new high-frequency power law arising from the dissipative evolution of the acoustic source. In a dissipative plasma, the GW spectrum acquires an additional $q^{-2}$ suppression relative to the perfect-fluid result in the late-time, strong-damping limit. The exponent is largely insensitive to the source profile, while the turnover and suppression strength probe plasma transport and the source lifetime. In particular, the turnover frequency in weakly coupled hidden sector plasmas is sensitive to the underlying gauge coupling and can lie in the millihertz band targeted by space-based interferometers, opening a way to probe microscopic plasma dynamics through the detailed GW spectrum.

authors.name: Huai-Ke Guo, Sihao Xiao, Yang Xiao, Jin Min Yang, Yang Zhang

papers.title: Parity restoration in a sterile-neutrino scenario: bounds from atomic parity violation to the LHC
papers.summary: In a four-fermion-interaction scenario beyond the Standard Model (SM), in which right-handed (sterile) neutrinos take part in TeV-scale composite dynamics, the $Z$ boson acquires an energy-dependent right-handed coupling $\GR(q^2)$ that is expected to vanish at low energies and to restore parity symmetry at high energies. We derive the contribution of $\GR$ to neutral-current parity-violating observables. At first order in $\GR$, every low-energy parity-violating coupling is obtained from its SM value by the replacement $\sin^2\theta_W\to\sin^2\theta_W(1-\GR)$; in particular the nuclear weak charge is shifted by $\Delta Q_W=4\sin^2\theta_W\,Z\,\GR$, while the $Z$-pole effective mixing angle is shifted by $-\tfrac12(1-2\sin^2\theta_W)\GR$. Using atomic parity violation in cesium, parity-violating electron scattering and $Z$-pole determinations of $\sin^2\theta_{\rm eff}$, we extract $\GR$ at each momentum transfer. All data are consistent with $\GR=0$; at the $Z$ pole we find $\GR(m_Z)3.8$, $2.1$ and $1.7$~TeV for $n=1,2,3$. Future MOLLER, P2 and HL-LHC data will improve these bounds.

authors.name: Iman Motie, She-Sheng Xue, Alain Blanchard

papers.title: Direct simulation Monte Carlo for dark matter production and phase-space evolution
papers.summary: To study the early-universe production of dark matter particles beyond thermal equilibrium often requires solving several coupled Boltzmann equations at the phase-space level. We present a new method to address this challenge using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) based on stochastic interactions of an ensemble of particles. We implement and validate efficient algorithms to describe freeze-out, decays, elastic scattering and number-changing processes within the dark sector. These algorithms do not require a discretisation of momentum space on a pre-defined grid and do not rely on approximations such as thermally averaged cross sections. As illustrative example, we consider a scenario with two-step dark matter production, leading to a bimodal phase-space distribution, and consider the subsequent evolution under elastic and number-changing processes. We show that DSMC is a flexible approach to explore out-of-equilibrium processes and solve Boltzmann equations at the phase-space level in order to predict the abundance of dark matter particles and their effect on structure formation.

authors.name: Felix Kahlhoefer, Ann Cathrin Wesener

papers.title: Resonant Cavity Searches for Millicharged Dark Matter
papers.summary: A plethora of resonant cavity experiments have been designed to search for ultralight dark matter (DM) candidates, such as axion or dark-photon DM. In this work, we show that these same apparatuses can be sensitive to ultralight millicharged dark matter (mDM) with masses $m_\phi\sim1-100\,\mu\mathrm{eV}$. Similar to axion DM, in the presence of a background magnetic field, mDM acts as an effective current which can excite the modes of a resonant cavity. Importantly, for a cylindrical cavity, axion DM dominantly couples to the transverse magnetic (TM) modes, whereas mDM dominantly couples to the transverse electric (TE) modes. We project the sensitivity to mDM that resonant cavity experiments can achieve if they are able to tune and readout their TE modes. We find that fractional millicharges as small as $\epsilon_m=e_m/e\sim10^{-19}$ can be probed. If mDM constitutes only a subfraction $f_\mDM \lesssim0.2\%$ of the total DM density, competing astrophysical bounds do not apply. In this case, resonant cavities can be the most sensitive probes of mDM in this mass range.

authors.name: Miguel Gonz\'alez Albert, Ariel Arza, Saarik Kalia

papers.title: New unintegrated gluon density in proton and nuclei tested with small $x$ processes at modern colliders
papers.summary: We present a new unintegrated, or transverse momentum dependent (TMD) gluon density in proton and nuclei. Parameters of the new function have been obtained from a fit on inclusive soft charged hadron production and structure functions at low scales, and from comparison with data on a number of processes at higher scales results taken at LHC and HERA, such as heavy quarks production, prompt photon photoproduction and Higgs boson production. A modification employing the geometric scaling approach has been made to extend the obtained parton density to the case of light and heavy nuclei. As a test of the nuclear TMD distribution we perform a calculation of the charged hadrons multiplicity spectra in pPb collisions at the LHC energies.

authors.name: Maxim Malyshev, Artem Lipatov, Gennady Lykasov

papers.title: Interpretation of the LZ Event via Inelastic ALP-Dark Photon Transition with Photon Exchange
papers.summary: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has reported a nuclear recoil event at $248\pm23$~keV with a global significance of about $2.6\sigma$. We for the first time explain it via the inelastic process with photon mediator. We consider a dark matter (DM) axion-like particle (ALP) $a$ converts into a heavier dark photon $\gamma'$ via the nuclear electromagnetic current, and study the photon-mediated endothermic transition $aA\rightarrow\gamma'A$. We derive the kinematics and cross sections for non-relativistic halo and boosted ALPs. A three-bin Poisson fit to the LZ data includes the xenon isotopes, charge form factors, detector efficiency, and energy resolution. Halo DM, which has mass $m\simeq1.2$~TeV, mass splitting $\delta\simeq346$~keV, and near the upper coupling bound, reproduces the event with about $61\%$ in the middle bin. Boosted DM with $v_{0}=0.05\,c$ and $\Phi_{0}=10^{5}~\mathrm{cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ requires only $m\simeq5.74$~GeV and $\delta\simeq6.66$~MeV to give about $62\%$. We find that a broader Gaussian spread in the incident energy has a significant effect on the fitted masses.

authors.name: Quanyu Wang, Xiangwei Yin, Tianjun Li

papers.title: Inclusive and diffractive D meson photoproduction in $pPb$ collisions at the LHC using Pythia8 framework
papers.summary: We present a systematic analysis of inclusive and diffractive $D$-meson photoproduction in $ep$ and ultraperipheral $pPb$ collisions within the Pythia8 framework. Predictions obtained with different proton and Pomeron PDFs are compared with H1 measurements of inclusive and diffractive $D^*$ photoproduction at HERA. We also present predictions for the rapidity and transverse-momentum distributions of inclusive and diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction at the LHC. Our analysis indicates that the diffractive contribution exceeds 15\% at low $p_T$ and forward rapidities, suggesting that diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction could be accessible in future LHC runs. In addition, measurements of inclusive and diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction in ultraperipheral $pPb$ collisions can help constrain the proton and Pomeron PDFs.

authors.name: Victor P. Goncalves, Luana Santana, Wolfgang Sch\"afer

papers.title: Concerning Factorization at Lepton Colliders
papers.summary: We uncover super-leading logarithms in non-global observables at lepton colliders. They arise from Glauber interactions involving colored partons produced by electromagnetic splittings of the incoming leptons. A three-loop analysis establishes the resulting factorization breaking, which we reconcile with the use of lepton PDFs below the soft veto scale. We conjecture that soft--collinear factorization fails for exclusive observables even in pure QED by identifying a genuine Glauber region in massless QED. This reveals a far richer infrared structure than naively expected.

authors.name: Patrick Hager, Dominik Schwienbacher

papers.title: NNLO QCD corrections to radiative and hadronic $\Upsilon(1S)$ decays
papers.summary: We present the complete next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) QCD corrections to radiative and inclusive hadronic $\Upsilon(1S)$ decays in the color-singlet framework at leading order in the heavy-quark velocity expansion. For radiative decay, the NNLO correction reshapes the photon energy spectrum and lowers the partial width in the fiducial window $0.65\leq 2E_\gamma/M_\Upsilon\leq0.92$, bringing the central prediction into good agreement with reconstructed CLEO data. For inclusive hadronic decay, the NNLO correction provides a large negative shift that lowers the predicted width from its inflated NLO value to a level fully consistent with the experimental determination. Although both individual decay widths exhibit larger renormalization-scale uncertainties at NNLO, their ratio demonstrates a significantly reduced scale dependence due to the cancellation of common short-distance dynamics and the nonperturbative matrix element. Using the window ratio inferred from CLEO measurements, we extract the strong coupling constant $\alpha_s^{(5)}(M_Z) = 0.12135^{+0.0039}_{-0.0036}$, compatible with the world average, and evaluate the sensitivity to uncalculated higher orders via the unexpanded quotient.

authors.name: Xiangyu Chang, Chao Zeng, Ruichang Niu, Bin Gong, Jian-Xiong Wang

papers.title: Photon-Mediated Axino-Bino Scattering Process for the LZ High-Energy Recoil Event
papers.summary: We for the first time investigate the photon-mediated endothermic axino-bino scattering process to explain the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) high-energy recoil event. We calculate the signals from non-relativistic halo and boosted dark matter (DM), including natural xenon isotopes, detector efficiency, and energy resolution. For a fixed Standard Halo Model (SHM) distribution, a simplified three-bin Poisson analysis yields a best-fit benchmark with mass $m\simeq506\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and mass splitting $\delta\simeq326\,\mathrm{keV}$ at the adopted upper coupling bound $g_\gamma=10^{-3}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. It predicts approximately one accepted event, with $70\%$ in the middle bin. A boosted benchmark with $m\simeq82.87\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and $\delta\simeq0.626\,\mathrm{MeV}$ provides a comparable fit. Broader Gaussian incident energy distributions allow fitted masses down to a few GeV. Thus, both the halo and boosted DM scenarios can fit the LZ signal at different DM mass scales.

authors.name: Xiangwei Yin, Quanyu Wang, Tianjun Li

papers.title: Predictions for Inclusive Production Cross Sections of the Higgs Boson at the LHC and HL-LHC
papers.summary: We present updated recommendations of the LHC Higgs Working Group (LHCHWG) for the inclusive production cross sections of a Standard Model Higgs boson in proton--proton collisions at centre-of-mass energies between $7$ and $14$ TeV, including the Run-3 energy of $13.6$ TeV, and for Higgs-boson masses between $120$ and $130$ GeV. All the major production modes are covered. The central values remain consistent with those of Yellow Report 4 (YR4) [arXiv:1610.07922] within the uncertainties quoted there, while the theoretical uncertainties are reduced for most production modes. The improvements rest on specific calculations rather than on a uniform advance: the complete N$^3$LO result in the heavy-top limit together with exact NNLO top-quark mass effects for gluon fusion; the N$^3$LO structure-function calculation supplemented by non-factorisable corrections for vector-boson fusion; the completion of the NLO QCD corrections to the loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ channel for $VH$; NNLO QCD matched to NNLL soft-gluon resummation and combined with NLO electroweak corrections for $t\bar{t}H$, and updated predictions for $tH$; and the matched four- and five-flavour-scheme prediction, with its explicit resummation-scale uncertainty, for $b\bar{b}H$. Since no PDF4LHC recommendation exists beyond NNLO, the mismatch between an N$^3$LO matrix element and NNLO distributions has to be carried as an uncertainty, estimated process by process: it is well determined for vector-boson fusion, whereas for gluon fusion it is doubled relative to YR4. PDFs are now the leading source of uncertainty for the most precisely predicted modes, while residual perturbative uncertainties dominate for the remainder. These results supersede the inclusive cross sections of YR4 and the ad interim recommendations of Ref. [arXiv:2402.09955], and form part of Report 5 of the LHCHWG.

authors.name: Robin Hayes, Alexander Karlberg, Bernhard Mistlberger, Dermot Moran, Hannah Arnold, Gaetano Barone, Christian Biello, Johannes Bl\"umlein, Valeria Botta, Christian Br{\o}nnum-Hansen, Alessandro Calandri, Benjamin Campillo, Alessandra Cappati, Andrea Cardini, Suman Chatterjee, Jiayi Chen, Michal Czakon, Valerio Dao, Goutam Das, Felix Eschment, Silvia Ferrario Ravasio, Giancarlo Ferrera, Alessandro Gavardi, Yanping Huang, Alexander Huss, Stephen Jones, Judith Katzy, Sven Yannick Klein, Matthew Lim, Stefano Manzoni, Josh McFayden, Sven-Olaf Moch, Alexander M\"uck, Marco Niggetiedt, Mathieu Pellen, Christian T. Preuss, Tom Schellenberger, Lukas Simon, Michael Spira, Lourdes Urda G\'omez, Davide Valsecchi, Marco Vitti, Marius Wiesemann, Malgorzata Worek, Sebastian Wuchterl, Silvia Zanoli, Marco Zaro, Licheng Zhang

papers.title: Towards Consistent Thermal Resummation: Improved Partial Dressing for Precise Electroweak Phase Transition Predictions
papers.summary: Reliable predictions for the electroweak phase transition depend critically on a consistent resummation of thermal fluctuations. However, existing prescriptions often entail sizable uncertainties, motivating the development of a robust and systematically controlled resummation scheme. In this work, we develop an improved partial dressing (IPD) scheme that resolves intrinsic inconsistencies in the original partial dressing prescription, including the overlapping momentum problem and the associated divergences in the gap equations. By consistently incorporating momentum-dependent self-energies and reorganizing the daisy resummation, the IPD scheme provides a more systematic framework for thermal resummation. We perform a comprehensive comparison of 5 different resummation prescriptions in the well-motivated inert doublet model and demonstrate that the choice of resummation scheme can substantially affect the predicted phase transition parameters and the resulting gravitational wave spectra. Notably, the IPD prescription yields a reliable potential and comparatively robust phenomenological predictions, highlighting the importance of a self-consistent treatment of thermal corrections. Our results establish the theoretical consistency of IPD and demonstrate that controlling resummation uncertainties is essential for reliable predictions of cosmological phase transitions and their gravitational wave signatures.

authors.name: Dayun Qiu, Fa Peng Huang

papers.title: $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings at the Large Hadron Collider
papers.summary: Constraining the $Z$-boson couplings of the $b$ quark, or even ruling out the possibility of an opposite-sign coupling, is considered very challenging at the LHC. Utilizing signatures of new physics resulting from contact operators accompanying the modification of $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings from Standard Model predictions, we show that the ATLAS measurement of $pp\to Zh$ already ruled out the opposite-sign couplings by more than 9.5 standard deviations. We also argue that $pp\to Zhb$, which receives a contribution from the same contact term, would lead to even better sensitivity. Furthermore, we show that with future data this indirect method can provide the strongest constraints on $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings, and can even probe the anomaly in these couplings left over from the LEP era.

authors.name: Radovan Dermisek, Keith Hermanek, Marcos A. Hernandez Ojeda, Taegyu Lee, Navin McGinnis

papers.title: Quantum Autoencoder on Real Hardware for New Physics Searches at Muon Colliders
papers.summary: We apply a quantum autoencoder to search for new physics (NP) in the tri-photon process $\mu^+\mu^-\to\gamma\gamma\gamma$ at muon colliders. Using a six-qubit circuit on the Tianyan176 quantum computer, we measure the reconstruction losses for Standard Model (SM) events and anomalous quartic gauge couplings (aQGCs) events. The results demonstrate that the hardware-implemented quantum autoencoder effectively discriminates NP signals from the SM background. Concurrently, we derive the expected constraints on the aQGCs coefficients and compare them with those obtained from conventional methods.

authors.name: Shuai Zhang, Ji-Chong Yang

papers.title: Constraint on anomalous $W^-W^+\gamma$ coupling in $\ell^\pm \gamma\slashed{E}$ final state at NLO QCD
papers.summary: We study the anomalous $W^-W^+\gamma$ triple gauge couplings in the $pp\to \ell^\pm\gamma\slashed{E}$ channel at $\sqrt{s}=13$~TeV with next-to-leading order QCD corrections. Eight polarization asymmetries of the reconstructed $W$ boson, measured in four disjoint regions of $\Delta\eta_{\ell\gamma}$ and combined with the $m_{W\gamma} \ge 1$ TeV distribution, are used to constrain the two CP-even and two CP-odd couplings. The bounds improve only marginally with increasing luminosity, far below the statistical expectation, while they degrade substantially when the systematic uncertainties are relaxed, showing that the sensitivity is systematically limited. A simultaneous four-parameter MCMC fit is performed to obtain marginalized limits. Relative to the CMS $WW+WZ$ combination, our bounds are significantly tighter for the CP-odd coupling $\widetilde{\lambda}_\gamma$ and competitive for $\lambda_\gamma$. The CP-odd results are also compared with the electron EDM limit, which constrains both couplings by roughly $2.5$ orders of magnitude beyond the collider reach.

authors.name: Amir Subba, Yu Shi, Athul P, Ritesh K Singh

papers.title: $Z\gamma$ production in gluon fusion at NLO+NLL
papers.summary: We study the production of $Z\gamma$ in gluon fusion at hadron colliders at the next-to-leading-order (NLO) in QCD. At the $13.6$ TeV LHC, we find that these NLO corrections are found to enhance the leading-order (LO) cross section by about $83$\% and reduce the conventional seven-point scale uncertainty from $22.3$\% at LO to $15.2$\% at NLO. We further perform the threshold resummation at next-to-leading-logarithmic (NLL) accuracy and match to the fixed order NLO results. We have presented the production cross section for various center of mass energies at the LHC. We find that this NLL resummation enhances the NLO production cross section by about $23$\%. We also give the invariant mass distribution up to $Q=1000$ GeV for $13.6$ TeV LHC. In this case, the resummation reduces the seven-point scale uncertainty from $25\%$ at NLO to about $16$\% at NLO+NLL for $Q=1000$ GeV. We also present the uncertainties due to the strong coupling constant and the parton distribution functions in our results. We further estimate the contribution of the top quark in our predictions, using the Born Improved Theory (BIT).

authors.name: Chinmoy Dey, Niraj Koirala, M. C. Kumar, Vaibhav Pandey

papers.title: Self-gravity depletes superradiant clouds
papers.summary: Superradiant clouds of ultralight scalars around black holes are often modeled as free fields, whose levels grow independently and decay slowly through gravitational-wave emission. We show that this limit is never realized. The cloud's self-gravity redistributes particles between levels, just as in the case of axion self-interactions, and dominates over self-interactions for decay constants $f_a\gtrsim6\times10^{16}\,{\rm GeV}\,(\alpha/0.1)$, with $\alpha$ the gravitational fine-structure constant. Self-gravity depletes the cloud by orders of magnitude and feeds more extended levels, weakening all signals that rely on the existence of a large cloud mass. A binary companion, however, can partly offset the depletion. Any assessment of superradiant signals must therefore account for both self-gravity and the cloud's environment.

authors.name: Mateja Bo\v{s}kovi\'c, Lucas Gathercole, Thomas F. M. Spieksma, Samuel J. Witte

papers.title: Refractive Neutrino Mass: Effects of Fluctuations of the Dark Matter Field
papers.summary: Observed neutrino oscillations can be reproduced by a refractive neutrino mass-squared arising from interactions with ultralight scalar dark matter (ULDM). The wave behaviour of the scalar field gives rise to a fluctuating interference pattern, inducing spatial and temporal variations in the refractive mass that can distort neutrino oscillation probabilities. We simulate the interference patterns of the scalar field in the presence of self-interactions. Using results of these simulations, the oscillation probabilities for JUNO and T2K experiments are computed. We find that the refractive mass scenario remains viable for the complex scalar field without self-coupling for $m_\phi \lesssim 10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$. For $m_\phi\gtrsim10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$, repulsive self-interactions narrow the density distribution, reducing the deviation of the survival probability at the first minimum to $\Delta P \approx 0.07$ for an appropriate self-interaction coupling. In contrast, for a real scalar field, rapid oscillations with the Compton frequency distort the probabilities for scalar masses $ 10^{-22}~\mathrm{eV} \lesssim m_\phi \lesssim 10^{-10} ~\mathrm{eV}$, and self-interactions do not remove this distortion. This distortion becomes negligible only for $m_\phi\gtrsim10^{-9}~\mathrm{eV}$. We explore additional effects which could modify the interference pattern and relax the constraints on the required values of $m_\phi$. These include scenarios with multiple scalar fields (the axiverse), the gravitational effects of the Sun and Earth on the granule structure, and interactions with the relic neutrino background.

authors.name: Soham Sahasrabuddhe, Manibrata Sen, Alexei Y. Smirnov

papers.title: Simulation-based inference for gravitational-wave cosmology: parameter reconstruction of a first-order electroweak phase transition
papers.summary: The detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) from a cosmological first- order phase transition would be unambiguous evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model, with a strong electroweak phase transition (EWPT) at LISA as a prime example. Reconstructing the underlying model from such a signal is challenging, since the map from the model parameters to the spectrum is degenerate and strong transitions occupy only small and sparse regions of parameter space. We show that simulation-based inference (SBI), a likelihood-free approach applicable to generic SGWB sources, provides a reliable parameter reconstruction despite these difficulties. We first apply SBI to the thermodynamic parameters characterizing the transition, namely its strength, inverse duration, temperature and bubble wall velocity. As a concrete application, we then consider a strong EWPT in a singlet extension of the Standard Model and reconstruct the model parameters from the resulting SGWB. We find that the SBI posteriors agree with those of a likelihood-based Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis, at negligible cost per data set once the network has been trained. Using the network posterior as the proposal for importance sampling with the exact likelihood further corrects its remaining deviations, at a sampling efficiency several orders of magnitude higher than sampling from the prior. SBI thus offers a fast and flexible framework for the cosmological science case of LISA

authors.name: Thomas Biek\"otter, Andrii Dashko, Kateryna Radchenko

papers.title: Dark Matter Model Implications of a Candidate Sub-halo Near the Sun, and the Data Needed to Discriminate Among Them
papers.summary: Pulsar-timing accelerations point to a localized mass concentration near the Sun, consistent with a dark matter sub-halo. We work out what such an object implies for the nature of dark matter, organizing the implications by their observable effect: suppression or enhancement of structure formation, internal structure and survival after formation, and emission or scattering by the constituents. We discuss ultralight wave dark matter, thermal and nonthermal warm dark matter, dark acoustic oscillations and dark matter-baryon scattering, elastic and inelastic self-interactions, invisible decays with recoil, primordial black holes, indirect detection, and a possible connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN high-energy recoil candidate. We then ask what new data would discriminate among these models. The existing accelerations are measured outside the tidal radius, where they are blind to the interior mass distribution, to the object's velocity, and to the sub-halo population. We identify four routes that lift these degeneracies: accelerations measured inside the halo, which separate point-mass, cuspy, and cored profiles; lensing and accretion, which test whether the mass is compact; the morphology of annihilation or decay emission, which probes the inner profile; and a search for a comoving stellar population, which tests whether the object is dark and measures its velocity. We also contrast this program with pulsar-timing-array searches for transiting dark matter substructure, which probe vastly lighter objects through a different observable.

authors.name: Stefano Profumo, Sukanya Chakrabarti

papers.title: Gamma-Ray Bursts from Primordial Black Hole-Induced Neutron Star Collapse
papers.summary: We show that the capture and subsequent endoparasitic consumption of a neutron star (NS) by a primordial black hole (PBH) can produce a short gamma-ray burst (GRB) without forming an accretion disk. During PBH-induced NS consumption, the NS spin is amplified through angular-momentum conservation and transfer from infalling matter, while flux freezing and a differential-rotation-driven dynamo amplify the magnetic field. We find that, for rapidly rotating millisecond pulsars (MSPs), these mechanisms can power short GRBs through magnetic dipole radiation and magnetic energy release. If asteroid-mass PBHs in the range $10^{-14}M_\odot$--$10^{-11}M_\odot$ constitute the dark matter, we estimate that searches of the Fermi-GBM archive and a future MeV gamma-ray mission such as COSI could detect these bursts. We also discuss possible multimessenger counterparts, including fast radio bursts powered by magnetic energy release, kilonovae and $511\,{\rm keV}$ line emission associated with centrifugally ejected neutron-rich matter, and gravitational waves from the rapid collapse and subsequent black-hole ringdown. Together, these signals probe complementary stages of PBH-induced NS consumption.

authors.name: Yu Watanabe, Koichiro Yasuda, Alexander Kusenko

papers.title: Nucleon Short-Range Correlations and Supersoft Nuclear Symmetry Energy: Compatibility with Massive Neutron Stars and GW170817
papers.summary: Massive neutron stars (NSs) require a sufficiently stiff core equation of state (EOS), while the relatively small tidal deformability inferred from GW170817 favors softer nuclear matter at intermediate densities. Given the importance of the nuclear symmetry energy in neutron-rich matter, an intriguing question arises: Can the symmetry energy become supersoft at high densities while remaining compatible with these seemingly competing constraints? Within the nonlinear Walecka framework, we demonstrate that nucleon short-range correlations (SRCs), manifested as a high-momentum tail (HMT) in the nucleon momentum distribution, can accommodate such behavior without introducing additional interaction parameters. We derive for the first time analytical expressions for the symmetry energy curvature $K_{\rm{sym}}$ for both free Fermi gas (FFG) and HMT momentum distributions. Using model parameter sets that reproduce empirical nuclear matter properties around saturation density, we find that SRC-HMT yields substantially more negative $K_{\rm{sym}}$ than the FFG case, allowing the symmetry energy to reach a maximum at low supra-saturation densities and subsequently decrease while the total pressure remains sufficient to support massive NSs. The resulting EOSs also predict smaller NS radii and tidal deformabilities consistent with GW170817. These results connect the microscopic nucleon momentum distribution with the density dependence of the symmetry energy and macroscopic NS properties.

authors.name: Hai-Xiang Zhu, Bao-Jun Cai, Yu-Gang Ma

papers.title: Sourcing vector perturbations in warm inflation through shear viscous effects
papers.summary: Vector modes are generally believed not to play a significant role in standard cosmological perturbation theory because they decay rapidly. Non-equilibrium dynamics in the radiation bath present during warm inflation can lead to shear viscous effects, requiring a description beyond the perfect-fluid approximation. We adopt the fluctuating hydrodynamic approach to account for stochastic anisotropic stress related to shear viscosity. We show that the vector mode obeys a constrained Langevin equation in an inflationary background. The resulting power spectrum, considered in the weak-viscosity regime, is proportional to the shear viscosity and it also depends on the Hubble slow-roll parameter $\epsilon$, decaying approximately as $a^{-(1-\epsilon)}$. This behaviour is significantly slower than the unsourced, non-viscous power spectrum, which decays as $a^{-4}$. The continuously sourced vector modes, nevertheless, decay on superhorizon scales, and the illustrative benchmark parameter choices adopted in our numerical examples give a negligible late-time vector-to-scalar ratio. Despite the absence of direct large-scale observable vector signatures, the main results establish a source of vector perturbations during warm inflation and provide a framework for studying possible secondary effects along with large-scale white noises in the vector channel.

authors.name: Arjun Berera, Suddhasattwa Brahma, Zizang Qiu, Rudnei O. Ramos

papers.title: The antibaryon-baryon interaction based on chiral EFT with a focus on $\bar pp$ and $\bar\Lambda\Lambda$ reactions
papers.summary: The antibaryon-baryon ($\bar BB$) interaction is reviewed in the context of the hyperon(Y)-production reactions $\bar NN\to\bar YY$ with special emphasis on the $\bar \Lambda\Lambda$ system. The experimental situation for $\bar BB\to\bar YY$ from threshold up to antiproton lab momenta of $2$ GeV/c is discussed and likewise past theoretical approaches and results. The formalism for a description of the $\bar BB$ interaction in terms of potentials derived within SU(3) chiral effective field theory (EFT) is outlined. Constraints from SU(3) flavor symmetry on the $\bar BB$ interaction in the various reaction channels are discussed. As concrete application a new analysis of the reaction $\bar pp\to\bar \Lambda\Lambda$ is performed utilizing potentials for the $\bar NN$ and $\bar \Lambda\Lambda$ channels, and for the $\bar NN\to\bar\Lambda\Lambda$ transition, up to next-to-leading order in the chiral expansion, supplemented by a phenomenological part to account for annihilation processes. An excellent reproduction of data from the PS185 experiment at CERN up to momenta of $1.55$ GeV/c is achieved. When including higher-order contact terms in the analysis the range of agreement can be extended up to momenta around $1.65$ GeV/c, where a complete set of scattering observables is available. Predictions for $\bar\Lambda\Lambda$ scattering are provided and compared to results from the literature.

authors.name: Qin-He Yang, Johann Haidenbauer, Ulf-G. Mei{\ss}ner

papers.title: Review of Pion and Nucleon Gluon Parton Distribution Functions from Lattice QCD
papers.summary: Gluons play an essential role in the strong interaction that binds quarks into hadrons, as described by quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Understanding how the fundamental dynamics of QCD give rise to hadron structure remains one of the outstanding challenges in nuclear and particle physics. Parton distribution functions (PDFs) provide a successful framework for describing high-energy scattering processes involving hadrons. However, our knowledge of gluon PDFs remains comparatively limited because of the experimental challenges associated with directly constraining the gluon structure of hadrons. In recent years, a major breakthrough has enabled the calculation of the Bjorken-$x$ dependence of PDFs directly from lattice QCD. Among the available approaches, the large-momentum effective theory (LaMET) and pseudo-PDF frameworks have emerged as the most widely used methods and have produced the majority of lattice determinations of parton distributions. These developments have sparked rapid progress in first-principles studies of the $x$-dependent structure of hadrons, including gluon PDFs of the nucleon and pseudoscalar mesons. In this review, we summarize recent advances in lattice QCD calculations of gluon PDFs {using the LaMET and pseudo-PDF methods}, discuss the current status and impacts of these developments, and highlight the remaining challenges and future opportunities.

authors.name: William Good, Huey-Wen Lin

papers.title: Little Red Dots from Primordial Vacuum Bubbles
papers.summary: Quantum tunneling transverse to the inflaton trajectory can produce $10^6$--$10^8M_\odot$ primordial black holes at the abundance of JWST's little red dots, without the enhanced curvature perturbations excluded by limits on CMB spectral distortions. Rare vacuum bubbles nucleate during a brief interval of inflation and later form black holes, with adjustable mass and abundance and a narrow mass spectrum of percent-level width. The leading constraint, from accretion, is satisfied for a population matching the bright little red dots even if all the emitted radiation escapes as hard X-rays.

authors.name: Miguel Barroso Varela, Katherine Freese, Matthew Kleban, Cameron Norton, Evangelos I. Sfakianakis

papers.title: Charged pion production in the annihilation reactions $e^+ + e^- \to p + \bar{n} +\pi^-$ and $e^+ + e^- \to n + \bar{p} +\pi^+.$ Contribution of the nonresonant mechanism
papers.summary: The nonresonant mechanism in the reactions $e^+\,e^-\to \pi^-\,p\,\bar{n}$ and $e^+\,e^-\to \pi^+\,n\,\bar{p}$ is investigated in frame of the one-photon exchange approximation. The description of the hadronic phase space and the invariant amplitude formalism, earlier developed for the neutral pion channel, are applied here. Some modification is required to fulfill the conservation of the hadron electromagnetic current and to account for an additional contribution due to diagram with the pion pole. The double and single distributions over the invariant variables as well the total cross section, are obtained. The results are plotted for $s=$5,\,10,\,16\, GeV$^2$. The calculations are performed for the $\pi^-\,p\,\bar{n}$ channel and the rules to proceed to the $\pi^+\,n\,\bar{p}$ channel are formulated for every distribution.

authors.name: M. I. Konchatnij, N. P. Merenkov

papers.title: Mono-Higgs signature in a singlet fermionic dark matter model
papers.summary: We investigate mono-Higgs production as a probe of singlet fermionic dark matter (SFDM) at the LHC. In this framework, a Standard Model (SM) gauge-singlet Dirac fermion serves as the dark matter candidate, interacting with the visible sector through a real scalar mediator that mixes with the SM Higgs boson. Focusing on light dark matter with $M_\psi \in [0.1,10]$ GeV, we analyze the viable parameter space under constraints from relic density, Higgs decay properties, invisible decay bounds, rare $B$-meson decays, and direct detection experiments. We compute the mono-Higgs production cross sections at $\sqrt{s}=13~\mathrm{TeV}$ and compare approximate detector-level yields with the ATLAS $b\bar b$ search, supplemented by an inclusive upper bound for the CMS four-lepton channel. For the two benchmarks, the signal is dominated by non-resonant Higgs-pair production followed by an invisible Higgs decay. The resulting signal rate depends on both the production cross sections and the physical invisible branching fractions. The inclusive rates of $3.33$ and $1.43$~fb at loop-induced leading order provide quantitative signal targets before the visible Higgs decay and analysis cuts. For representative benchmark points satisfying the constraints considered, these comparisons indicate limited sensitivity in the analyzed channels. Nevertheless, the mono-Higgs channel provides a complementary probe of Higgs-portal dark matter scenarios, particularly in the low-mass mediator regime.

authors.name: Yeong Gyun Kim, Kang Young Lee, Soo-hyeon Nam

papers.title: Probing the nonstrange quark star equation of state with compact stars and gravitational waves
papers.summary: A recent study shows that incorporating a new term into the thermodynamic potential density, as required by the thermodynamic consistency criterion, can effectively resolve the thermodynamic inconsistency problems of the conventional perturbative QCD model. This additional term plays a crucial role in resolving inconsistencies at relatively low densities and becomes negligible at extremely high densities. Within this revised perturbative QCD model, we find that if we require only that the energy per baryon of up-down ($ud$) quark matter exceeds 930 MeV so as not to contradict the standard nuclear physics, the maximum mass of an $ud$ quark star allowed by the revised perturbative QCD model can reach up to 2.17 $M_{\odot}$. From this perspective, the observed 2.14 $M_{\odot}$ pulsar PSR J0740+6620 may be an $ud$ quark star. However, if we further impose the constraint that the tidal deformability of a 1.4 $M_{\odot}$ $ud$ quark star must be consistent with the GW170817 event, the maximum mass allowed by the revised perturbative QCD model would decrease to no more than 2.08 $M_{\odot}$. Consequently, our results suggest that the compact object with a mass of 2.50-2.67 $M_{\odot}$, as observed in the GW190814 event, cannot be an $ud$ quark star, according to the revised perturbative QCD model.

authors.name: Shu-Peng Wang, Zhen-Yan Lu, Zhi-Jun Ma, Rong-Yao Yang, Jian-Feng Xu, Xiangyun Fu

papers.title: From Lead to Helium: Potential for a Measurement of Jet Quenching in the Smallest Collision Systems
papers.summary: We present perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD) predictions for the modification to the yield of high-momentum particles in very light ion collisions - ${}^{10}\mathrm{B} + {}^{10}\mathrm{B}$, ${}^{6}\mathrm{Li} + {}^{6}\mathrm{Li}$, ${}^{4}\mathrm{He} + {}^{4}\mathrm{He}$, and ${}^{3}\mathrm{He} + {}^{3}\mathrm{He}$ - both with and without medium-induced energy loss. We show that there is non-trivial suppression expected from our partonic energy loss model in symmetric systems from ${}^{208}\mathrm{Pb} + {}^{208}\mathrm{Pb}$ to ${}^{3}\mathrm{He} + {}^{3}\mathrm{He}$ and in asymmetric systems $A + B$, and that the energy loss scales approximately with $(\sqrt{A B})^{1 / 3}$. Further, we find that deep inelastic scattering measurements in ${}^{3}\mathrm{He}$ and ${}^{6}\mathrm{Li}$ tightly constrain the nPDF baseline, making these isotopes a particularly clean environment for searching for final-state partonic energy loss induced by the formation of a quark-gluon plasma in these very small systems.

authors.name: Coleridge Faraday, Ben Bert, Jack Brand, Werner Vogelsang, W. A. Horowitz

papers.title: Kaon T-even transverse-momentum-dependent distributions and form factors in a self-consistent light-front quark model
papers.summary: We present a self-consistent light-front quark model (LFQM) for the kaon based on the Bakamjian--Thomas (BT) construction and apply it to the electromagnetic and scalar form factors, as well as the full set of unpolarized T-even transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (TMDs) and their collinear parton distribution functions (PDFs). A uniform implementation of the invariant mass $M_0$ in both the hadronic matrix elements and the associated Lorentz structures enforces four-momentum conservation at the meson--quark vertex and yields current-component--independent observables by consistently incorporating the light-front zero-mode structure required by covariance. The electromagnetic form factor $F_{K^+}(Q^2)$ is demonstrated to be unique by explicit computation from all available current components ($\gamma^+$, $\gamma^\perp$, and $\gamma^-$). In the scalar channel, we compare the direct $f_S(Q^2)$ and mass-factored $F_S(Q^2)$ definitions and show that they are not interchangeable within the BT-based LFQM, since the replacement $M\!\to\!M_0(x,\bm{k}_\perp)$ must be implemented at the integrand level. Using a Gaussian light-front wave function, the twist-2 TMD $f_1^q$ exhibits an exact Gaussian dependence in $\bm{k}_\perp$, while higher-twist TMDs ($f^{\perp q}$, $e^q$, $f_4^q$) display systematic twist and flavor hierarchies. We further analyze the perturbative QCD evolution of the valence PDFs for the pion and kaon and report their Mellin moments at representative scales, enabling direct comparison with phenomenology.

authors.name: Yongwoo Choi, Ahmad Jafar Arifi, Ho-Meoyng Choi, Chueng-Ryong Ji

papers.title: Resurrecting Kaluza-Klein Dark Matter with Low-Temperature Reheating
papers.summary: In Universal Extra Dimension (UED) scenarios, the lightest Kaluza-Klein (KK) particle is naturally stable due to a remnant discrete symmetry, KK parity, arising from extra-dimensional compactification. This stability requires no ad hoc symmetry and renders Kaluza-Klein dark matter a well-motivated candidate, provided it reproduces the observed relic abundance. The minimal UED (mUED) framework being highly predictive is strongly constrained by the combined requirements of relic density and collider searches under standard cosmological assumptions. We revisit the dark matter phenomenology of mUED in the presence of a nonstandard cosmological history featuring a low reheating temperature driven by prolonged inflaton decay. Solving the coupled Boltzmann equations for dark matter, radiation, and inflaton energy densities, we show that entropy injection during reheating can dilute the relic abundance by orders of magnitude, reopening large regions of parameter space previously ruled out. We further demonstrate that the revived parameter space is consistent with current collider, direct-detection, and indirect-detection constraints, while remaining testable by upcoming experiments.

authors.name: Kirtiman Ghosh, Abhishek Roy, Rameswar Sahu

papers.title: Aspects of a Five-Dimensional $U(1)_{L_\mu - L_\tau}$ Model at Future Muon-Based Colliders
papers.summary: We study a five-dimensional (5D) framework based on the $U(1)_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ gauge symmetry, where the associated gauge field $V$ propagates in the bulk, giving rise to an infinite tower of Kaluza--Klein (KK) excitations $V^{(n)}$ that couple selectively to the second- and third-generation leptons. Originally motivated by its potential to address the muon $g-2$ anomaly, this framework remains of interest as a minimal, anomaly-free, phenomenologically well-motivated extension of the Standard Model (SM) of particle physics. We focus on high-energy muon-based colliders, which could directly probe the gauge structure without relying on the kinetic mixing between the SM hypercharge gauge boson and the 5D gauge boson $V$. We explore a set of complementary processes: the elastic $\mu^+\mu^+ \to \mu^+\mu^+$ scattering via off-shell exchange of KK (gauge) excitations $V^{(n)}$; the bremsstrahlung production of $V^{(n)}$ followed by their decays into neutrinos and into $\mu^-\mu^+$ at a future $\mu$TRISTAN collider. Further, we study the $\mu^-\mu^+ \to \mu^-\mu^+$ scattering via resonant KK excitation(s) at a future muon collider. Our results show that these future muon-based colliders could offer sensitive and complementary probes into regions in the parameter space of the scenario that are beyond the reach of low-energy experiments. In particular, such experiments would be able to probe both heavier such KK gauge bosons with TeV-scale masses for relatively large gauge couplings, as well as the much lighter ones with masses in the MeV-scale for couplings as weak as $g_D \sim \mathcal{O}(10^{-5})$, thereby offering a promising $2\sigma$ exclusion reach for such KK excitations, over an extensive range of masses, at these facilities.

authors.name: Dibyendu Chakraborty, Arindam Chatterjee, AseshKrishna Datta, Ayushi Kaushik, Kenji Nishiwaki

papers.title: Gravitational waves from CP domain wall collapse and electron EDM in a complex singlet model with dimension-five Yukawa interactions
papers.summary: We study the interplay between gravitational waves (GWs) from domain wall collapse and the electron electric dipole moment (EDM) in a complex singlet extension of the standard model with dimension-five Yukawa interactions. In this framework, the scalar potential admits CP-related degenerate vacua, leading to the formation of CP domain walls. While the resulting GW signal provides a probe of the vacuum structure of the singlet scalar sector, it does not by itself constitute a CP-violating observable. Once the singlet scalar is coupled to standard model fermions, CP-violating phases become observable through EDMs. We analyze whether current and future EDM experiments can probe the parameter region where the GW signal is detectable by SKA and THEIA. We find that the current electron EDM bound already constrains part of the parameter space, while future sensitivities at the level of $10^{-31}$--$10^{-32}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ can probe regions overlapping with the GW-detectable domain. Our results highlight the complementarity between GW and EDM observables in probing the singlet scalar sector, providing a coherent picture of its vacuum structure and CP properties.

authors.name: Hieu The Pham, Eibun Senaha

papers.title: $b\to c \bar u q$ decay and $CP$ violating observables in the presence of new physics contributions
papers.summary: In this work, a comprehensive analysis for processes related to $b\to c\bar{u}q~(q=d, s)$ transitions is carried out, including new physics contributions. In light of a recent tension between branching fractions for $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}^{(*)}M$ ($M=\pi, K$) decays in the QCD factorization approach and relevant experimental results, phenomenological constraints on complex-valued Wilson coefficients are discussed. Analyzed observables contain direct $CP$ asymmetry ($A_{\text{CP}}$) in $B^-\to D^0\pi^-$ decays and $\gamma/\phi_3$, one of the angles in the unitarity triangle, combined with others from $\tau_{B^+}/\tau_{B_d}$, $\Delta\Gamma_{q}/\Gamma_q$, and $A_{\rm SL}^{q}~(q=d, s)$. We constrain the complex Wilson coefficients at $1\sigma$ and $2\sigma$ levels under color-singlet and color-rearranged scenarios. These constraints yield correlated predictions for $\Delta\Gamma_d/\Gamma_d$, $A_{\rm SL}^d$ and $A_{\text{CP}}$.

authors.name: Xuanning Guo, Albertus Hariwangsa Panuluh, Hiroyuki Umeeda, Jinglong Zhu

papers.title: Role of the $\Sigma(1430)(1/2^-)$ in the $J/\psi \to \Lambda \bar{\Lambda} \pi^0$ reaction
papers.summary: We study the $J/\psi \to \bar{\Lambda} \Lambda \pi^0$ reaction, an \xiu{isospin-violating} reaction, by looking at the trios of \xiu{a} baryon-antibaryon-pseudoscalar meson that conform to a singlet of $\text{SU}(3)$ in the $u, d, s$ quarks. These terms conserve isospin; however, once the final-state interactions of meson-baryon and meson-antibaryon are taken into account, \xiu{the} isospin is violated due to the different masses of particles within the same isospin multiplets. Since the reaction is tied to the interaction of particles, only resonances that are dynamically generated by these interactions show up in the reaction. In this sense, our approach produces the $\Sigma(1430)(1/2^-)$ state \xiu{ but not the $\Sigma(1385)(3/2^+)$ state}. Comparing with the BESIII data we observe that, within the limited statistics of the experiment, the data show a structure {around $M_{\pi\Lambda} = 1430$ MeV} that is reproduced by the theory, and no signal is seen for the $\Sigma(1385)(3/2^+)$ as the theory predicts. We call for a future update of the experiment once better statistics become available.

authors.name: Yu-Shan Ren, Wen-Tao Lyu, Eulogio Oset

papers.title: Non-Markovian heavy-quark equilibration and equilibrium correlation function in a thermal medium
papers.summary: We compute the charm-quark current-current correlation function within the Langevin framework and extract the heavy-quark diffusion coefficient using the Green--Kubo formula. The formalism is further extended to evaluate the correlation function using a generalized Langevin equation that incorporates memory effects via an exponentially decaying memory kernel. We find that while memory effects qualitatively modify the transient structure of the current correlations, the value of the transport coefficient remains unchanged. In addition, we investigate heavy-quark thermalization in the presence of memory and compare the nonequilibrium solution of a generalized Fokker--Planck equation with the one obtained from the generalized Langevin equation in the non-relativistic limit. We also consider the relativistic case with correlated noise and observe that memory effects can give rise to a damped, oscillatory equilibration of the heavy quark momentum distribution in a non-Markovian bath.

authors.name: Monisha Nair, Juan Torres-Rincon, Santosh K. Das

papers.title: Photon Fragmentation Functions in LHAPDF: Existing Sets and a Pythia-Based Extraction
papers.summary: Prompt-photon predictions with experimentally relevant isolation criteria retain a residual dependence on parton-to-photon fragmentation functions, whose phenomenological uncertainties remain only weakly constrained. We present a pragmatic study of photon fragmentation functions extracted from Pythia parton-shower events and stored in LHAPDF grids. We briefly review the role of photon fragmentation in perturbative QCD and then construct shower-level estimates of the flavour-dependent functions $D^{\mathrm{PS}}_{\gamma/i}(z,\mu_D)$ as functions of the photon momentum fraction $z$ and fragmentation scale $\mu_D$. The extracted distributions show the expected qualitative hierarchy between quark and gluon channels and an increasing fragmentation contribution with scale. In parallel, we convert the commonly used BFG, GRV, and GDRG parameterizations into LHAPDF grids and study their interpolation. We find that the default logcubic interpolation in LHAPDF reproduces the non-trivial $z$- and scale-dependence of the tabulated fragmentation functions more faithfully than the linear interpolation commonly used in legacy implementations. We also define a simple collider-oriented envelope set, based on the BFG and GRV families. These results provide a portable baseline for future phenomenological studies and for more systematic extractions of photon fragmentation functions.

authors.name: Alexander Puck Neuwirth

papers.title: Probing the Inert Scalar Sector of the Inert Doublet Model via Vector-Boson Fusion at a Muon Collider
papers.summary:
We investigate how a future high-energy muon collider (MuC) probe the inert scalar sector of the Inert Doublet Model (IDM) through a comprehensive set of $2	o4$ electroweak gauge-boson fusion processes. The scalar spectrum consists of two $CP$-even neutral scalars, $h$ and $H$, one $CP$-odd neutral scalar $A$, and a pair of charged scalars $H^\pm$. We assume the neutral scalar $H$ is the lightest inert state and the dark matter (DM) candidate, while we identify the observed $125$~GeV Higgs boson with the scalar from the Standard-Model-like doublet. We consider charged Higgs pair production, $\mu^+\mu^-	o H^+H^-
u ar{
u}$, induced by $WW$ fusion, as well as the associated channels $\mu^+\mu^-	o HH^\pm\mu^\mp
u$ and $\mu^+\mu^-	o AH^\pm\mu^\mp
u$, induced by $WZ$ and $W\gamma$ fusion. Owing to their Vector Boson Fusion (VBF) origin, the corresponding cross sections increase significantly with collider energy, making them particularly well suited for exploration at a high-energy MuC. We first study the $2	o 2$ subprocesses $WW	o H^+ H^-$ and $WV	o H^+ S_i$, with $V=Z, \gamma$ and $S_i=H,A$, and establish the presence of destructive interference among the contributing diagrams. After imposing theoretical consistency requirements and current experimental constraints, including those from DM and collider searches, we evaluate the corresponding signal rates at $\sqrt{s}=3$, $10$, and $20$~TeV. We further perform a detector-level Monte Carlo analysis combined with a cut-based signal-background selection. Our results demonstrate that the sensitivity to inert scalar production grows significantly with collision energy, establishing the $10$ and $20$~TeV stages of a MuC as powerful probes of the IDM scalar sector.

authors.name: Abdesslam Arhrib, Es-said Ghourmin, Ayoub Hmissou, Larbi Rahili, Bassim Taki

papers.title: Bakamjian--Thomas construction and light-front zero modes in pseudoscalar transitions: A comparison with the covariant Bethe--Salpeter model
papers.summary: We examine the role of light-front zero modes in the extraction of the semileptonic form factor $f_-(q^2)$ between pseudoscalar mesons. In an exactly solvable covariant Bethe--Salpeter (BS) model, we calculate the transverse-current zero-mode contribution directly from the shrinking nonvalence region and reproduce it with an effective operator in the valence convolution. In the valence-only light-front quark model (LFQM) based on the Bakamjian--Thomas (BT) construction, the one-body current is built from on-shell constituent spinors, and the interaction enters through the mass operator and wave functions. The $(+,\perp)$ extraction of $f_-$ is zero-mode free and is saturated by the on-shell overlap. Using the free constituent invariant masses in the internal minus-current projection gives the same $f_-$ from $(+,-)$ after integration. For spacelike momentum transfer, we prove this equality for rotationally invariant radial wave functions with the light-front Jacobian and the adopted pseudoscalar spin coupling, provided the reduced overlaps converge. Subtracting the minus-current result obtained with physical meson masses from the common transverse result gives the BT completion. Current-component independence indirectly identifies this completion as the effective zero-mode contribution missing from the physical-mass minus-current extraction. When the BS valence current and the effective zero-mode operator for the nonvalence endpoint contribution are transferred unchanged to the Gaussian BT-based LFQM, the resulting expression fails to reproduce the component-independent BT result for $f_-$.
