papers.summary: This study presents an analytical investigation of entanglement quantification in three-qubit pure states using the Acin canonical representation. A global concurrence measure is constructed from the one-qubit-versus-rest bipartite concurrences of the three-qubit system. A closed-form expression for this measure is derived in terms of the canonical parameters of a general three-qubit pure state. Its behavior is then examined for representative product, biseparable, GHZ-type, and W-type states. The measure is further compared with the three-tangle and tripartite negativity to examine their respective sensitivities to different forms of multipartite entanglement. The results show that the global concurrence remains sensitive to bipartite entanglement in biseparable states, whereas tripartite negativity and the three-tangle vanish when genuine tripartite entanglement is absent. These results demonstrate the complementary information provided by the different measures in characterizing entanglement in three-qubit pure states.

authors.name: Zikra Aram

papers.title: A Non-Nested Quantum Search for TSP: Explicit Oracle Construction Beyond the $2^n$ Barrier
papers.summary: The traveling salesman problem (TSP) is a classic NP-hard problem. Held--Karp dynamic programming~\cite{held1962dynamic, bellman1962dynamic} solves it exactly in $O(n^2 2^n)$ time. Ambainis et al.~\cite{ambainis2019quantum}\ (SODA~2019) proposed a hybrid classical-quantum dynamic programming that improved the query complexity to $O^*(1.727^n)$. However, their algorithm uses nested quantum minimum finding, which complicates coherent circuit implementation, particularly the handling of threshold updates within nested subroutines. To address this difficulty, we design a quantum divide-and-conquer framework without any recursive process. We overcome the oracle-construction bottleneck by preparing a set partition state, requiring $O(n^2)$ gates and $O(n)$ depth. Under assumed QRAM model, the structured state preparation enables polynomial-depth oracle evaluation, yielding an overall running time of $O^*(1.866^n)$ for TSP. Qiskit simulations for $n=6$ and 7, using QFT-based data loading in place of QRAM, yield empirical optimal-solution probabilities of $98.9\%$ and $100\%$, respectively, in fixed-threshold amplitude-amplification tests.

authors.name: Xujun Bai, Yun Shang, Honghong Lin

papers.title: Robust self-testing of a maximally entangled qubit pair with arbitrary binary measurements
papers.summary: Robust self-testing certifies quantum states and measurements from Bell correlations in the presence of experimental noise. Many analytic proofs assume projective measurements; extending their guarantees to arbitrary measurements requires additional control over the action of the original measurement operators. We provide a direct treatment of this problem in the CHSH scenario, establishing a robust self-test of a maximally entangled qubit pair and Pauli observables for arbitrary, possibly mixed, bipartite states and binary positive operator-valued measurements on both sides. By bounding the change in measurement action under regularization, we derive explicit analytic $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\epsilon})$ vector-norm bounds for the state and the joint action of the original observables, where $\epsilon$ is the deficit from the maximal CHSH value. The same local isometries and normalized auxiliary vector apply to all settings, and the isometries leave an external purifying system untouched. We compare these guarantees with projective self-tests and general lifting results in a common error metric, and discuss the limitations imposed by the prefactor in a photonic Bell scheme.

authors.name: Alexandre C. Orthey Jr., Magdalena Stobi\'nska-Moretto

papers.title: Formal Verification of Continuous-Variable Quantum Programs
papers.summary: Continuous-variable quantum computing (CQC) is a promising paradigm already accessible through public cloud services. Yet, unlike discrete-variable quantum computing (DQC), CQC lacks a formal program logic. Extending existing quantum Hoare logics to CQC poses fundamental challenges: continuous-variable quantum programs act on {\em infinite-dimensional} Hilbert spaces; their measurement outcomes are often {\em unbounded}, so expectation values may {\em diverge}. We overcome these challenges to give a formal semantics to a universal programming language for CQC and, to our knowledge, provide the first Hoare logic for CQC. We introduce an assertion language based on polynomials over canonical observables and establish soundness and relative completeness of the resulting logic. We also implement a symbolic weakest-precondition calculator for CQC. Our tool has successfully verified CQC algorithms from textbooks and calculated their approximation errors for physically realizable implementations, proved the correctness (i.e., equivalence) of gate decompositions for CQC hardware, and computed the resource requirements (i.e., number of photon-number states) for achieving a desired accuracy in the classical simulation of continuous-variable quantum programs.

authors.name: Stefanie Muroya, Thomas A. Henzinger

papers.title: Unitary designs from perturbed time evolutions of a chaotic Hamiltonian
papers.summary: Unitary designs provide efficient substitutes for Haar-random unitaries in quantum information processing, randomized measurements, and many-body quantum dynamics. We propose a protocol based on time evolutions of a single chaotic Hamiltonian interleaved with unitary perturbations to generate unitary designs. We derive the frame potential of the resulting ensemble in terms of those of the intermediate ensemble. The intermediate ensemble need not itself be Haar random or exhibit Haar-level frame potentials, provided that its trace moments and frame-potential growth are sufficiently suppressed. The nontrivial Pauli set and the Clifford ensemble are simple examples, whereas ensembles whose cardinality does not grow with the Hilbert-space dimension generally fail. We further establish a frame-potential correspondence between multi-Hamiltonian temporal protocols and one-Hamiltonian protocols interleaved with repeated fixed trace-suppressed perturbations, showing that two perturbations suffice to recover Haar-level frame potentials. For local Hamiltonians, we derive a lower bound on the space--depth control resource, while more generally we establish a universal finite-window bound that constrains the required temporal sampling range. Together, these results identify complementary spatial and temporal resource requirements for perturbation-assisted randomness generation.

authors.name: Zhongyi Yang, Biao Wu

papers.title: Bosonic quantum communication beyond the thermal threshold
papers.summary: The thermal threshold has long been the highest level of thermal-loss noise below which bosonic quantum communication was known to be possible. Here, we show that this threshold can be surpassed. Simple single-mode non-Gaussian states yield positive quantum capacity beyond it at every nonzero bath temperature, even when all multimode Gaussian states yield zero rates. Even a two-mode Gaussian state suffices at low bath temperature, establishing a phenomenon of Gaussian superadditivity. In the weak-loss regime, we also determine the asymptotic expansion of the full quantum capacity up to and including the term linear in the loss.

authors.name: Francesco Anna Mele, Giuseppe Catalano, Marco Fanizza, Vittorio Giovannetti, Ludovico Lami

papers.title: Forward gain tracks the mean-response share of the Fisher information in non-Hermitian bosonic ladders
papers.summary:
Non-Hermitian lattices are proposed as sensors because non-normal amplification turns a small frequency shift into a large output, yet whether this increases precision at fixed photon number remains contested. We evaluate the classical Gaussian-state Fisher information of the intracavity field, split into mean-response and covariance-response terms, for a single bosonic chain and a two-chain opposing-skin ladder across 
um{34560} points under a Hurwitz stability margin. Over the 
um{15432} configurations passing both the margin and an independent covariance check, the mean-response share of the clean-cavity benchmark tracks forward gain along one curve in both architectures ($R^2=
um{0.978}$; architecture increment $\Delta R^2=
um{0.0012}$), falling from 
um{0.97} below zero gain to below 
um{2e-3} above \qty{60}{\dB}. Inter-chain coupling shifts the accessible gain range without raising the share at matched gain. Amplification thus relocates information into an ill-conditioned noise covariance, making the mean--covariance split and covariance conditioning the decisive metrics.

authors.name: Juste Deuyekbe, Philippe Djorw\'e, Nsangou Mama, Serge Guy Nana Engo

papers.title: Solving wave propagation problems via geometric quantum state preparation on dispersion manifolds
papers.summary: We present a quantum algorithm for solving partial differential equations through a linear-system formulation, focusing on wave propagation problems described by the discretized Helmholtz equation in frequency domain. Although quantum linear-system solvers offer exponential compression of the system degrees of freedom, their runtime complexity is generally governed by the condition number of the discretized operator. Exploiting the analytic structure of the differential operator can provide an alternative to explicit matrix inversion, as illustrated for the screened Poisson equation through an explicit quantum circuit. For the Helmholtz equation, however, the inverse operator becomes singular on the dispersion surface $k^2=\omega^2/c^2$, rendering direct Fourier-space state-preparation methods exponentially inefficient. We address this challenge by directly preparing quantum states supported on the resonant manifold and encoding source locations through Fourier phases. The resulting algorithm eliminates the exponentially large overhead associated with post-selection on the resonant manifold, yielding a success probability that depends linearly on the number of sources and is independent of the computational domain size. More generally, our approach applies to hyperbolic differential equations whose Fourier-space solutions possess singular support on dispersion manifolds, recasting their solution as a problem of geometric quantum state preparation.

authors.name: Yakov Solomons, Lee Peleg, Netanel Barel, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Amit Ben-Kish, Yotam Shapira

papers.title: Improved Separations between Quantum and Classical Communication Complexity of Total Functions
papers.summary: We refine Gavinsky's framework (arXiv:2608.18784) for exponential separations between quantum and randomized communication complexity of total functions and obtain larger separations: polylogarithmic quantum communication versus $\tilde\Omega(\sqrt n)$ randomized communication with two quantum messages, and versus $\Omega(n^{1-\varepsilon})$ for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1$ with more quantum messages. Our main technical contribution is a general conversion from quantum versus randomized communication separations for partial functions to separations for total functions. Our construction combines the communication lookup construction of Anshu, Belovs, Ben-David, G\"o\"os, Jain, Kothari, Lee, and Santha (FOCS 2016), the fully linear PCPs of Boneh, Boyle, Corrigan-Gibbs, Gilboa, and Ishai (CRYPTO 2019), and a linear seeded extractor with a short seed based on the construction of Raz, Reingold, and Vadhan (JCSS 2002). The key idea is to use the extractor to compress the lookup table into a single cell, thereby reducing the input length.

authors.name: Fran\c{c}ois Le Gall

papers.title: Collective Shortcuts for Preparing Identical Qubits
papers.summary: Allowing two qubits to interact during preparation can reduce the total cost relative to preparing them independently. We characterize this advantage for two copies of any pure qubit state, starting with each qubit in $|0\rangle$ and measuring the cost by the sum of the absolute Pauli rotation angles. Independent preparation is optimal precisely for targets on the four meridian arcs joining the north pole of the Bloch sphere to the eigenstates of $X$ or $Y$. Every other pure qubit state admits a collective shortcut. For example, the equatorial states $|+\rangle$ and $|T\rangle$ differ only in their relative phase, by $\pi/4$. The cost is additive for $|+\rangle$, whereas a four-pulse preparation of two $T$ states costs $13.4\%$ less than the optimal independent preparation. Collective control can also reduce the cost while keeping the qubits unentangled throughout a continuous preparation.

authors.name: Lin Zhu, Ranyiliu Chen, Xin Wang, Shenggen Zheng

papers.title: Percolation of Data Constraints and Reorganization of Boolean Function States in Parity Learning
papers.summary: We study how a neural network reorganizes its learned function as training proceeds and as previously unseen parity data accumulate. The trained model is itself a Boolean function on binary strings of finite length. We then evaluate it on all data, inside and outside the training set, and read off its complete sign table. Its $\pm1$ entries are the amplitudes of a normalized state, dubbed the function-state, whose inverse subsystem purity $K_f=1/\textrm{Tr}(\rho_A^2)$ is an effective Schmidt rank. We find that small data additions broaden the Schmidt spectrum, whereas larger additions reconcentrate it in the target mode. The former is called differentiation because the model distinguishes inputs more sharply. The latter is called target-selective recoherence, where the model settles on the single rule shared by the added data. As the dataset grows, the connectivity of the constraint graph defined by the training set increases monotonically, whereas the learned inverse purity changes nonmonotonically. On a fixed connected dataset, as learning proceeds, the Schmidt spectrum begins to reorganize, followed by gains in target alignment and later by improvement in predictive accuracy. This ordering distinguishes three aspects of learning: constraint identifiability, function-state organization, and predictive accuracy. At fixed data size, a function that has already been learned can re-differentiate, an event we call retreat, without changing graph connectivity. Recovery reconcentrates the Schmidt spectrum in a similar target-selective pattern, without exact recurrence of the Boolean state. Thus the percolation of data constraints fixes the identifiable support, while the reduced state produced by training continues to reorganize even after that support stops changing.

authors.name: Han Ma

papers.title: QuasiStim: Scalable Accurate Non-Pauli Noise Simulation for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
papers.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computer design relies on simulating noisy quantum error correction (QEC) circuits with hundreds to thousands of physical qubits and large circuit depths. High-throughput stabilizer simulators, such as Stim, are the de facto tools for this regime. However, these simulators typically support only Clifford gates and stochastic Pauli noise. As a result, more realistic device noise models, such as coherent control errors and thermal relaxation, are often approximated using Pauli twirling. This replacement offers speed but can introduce substantial inaccuracies. To address this, we propose QuasiStim for scalable, accurate QEC simulation of realistic noise, with QuasiFold as a compiler frontend and DeltaFrame as a sampling backend. QuasiFold lowers sampling overhead by opportunistically merging non-Pauli noise sites in the quantum circuit without changing the circuit output. DeltaFrame samples the resulting stabilizer trajectories by reusing precomputed predicted references instead of resimulating the full tableau for each shot. In our evaluation, QuasiFold can reduce the number of shots by over $1000\times$ on bivariate-bicycle (BB) codes under coherent $R_{ZZ}$ noise. Compared to a per-shot tableau simulator, DeltaFrame is $190\times$ to $1479\times$ faster on rotated surface-code memory as $d$ grows from 5 to 35. QuasiStim also makes the PTA bias measurable: the gap is non-trivial and varies with noise strength, decoder, and circuit schedule.

authors.name: Yuewen Hou, Gokul Subramanian Ravi

papers.title: The Pre-Optimization Structure of QAOA: Polynomial Equivalence of Average and Optimal Probabilities
papers.summary: We develop a theoretical framework connecting problem structure and variational parameter optimization in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). We derive a general bound on how much variational optimization can improve the probability of measuring configurations in arbitrary subsets of computational basis states, relating the maximum probability to its average over variational parameters. For NPO-PB problems at constant depth and with polynomially many distinct mixer eigenvalues, optimization improves the average probability by at most a polynomial factor. This raises the question: to what extent is variational optimization necessary for sampling desirable solutions? Under suitable efficiency assumptions, randomly parameterized QAOA can achieve cumulative success probabilities comparable to variationally trained QAOA, with only polynomial overhead in circuit executions. In particular, under these conditions, efficient sampling of desirable solutions can be achieved without variational training whenever variationally optimized QAOA achieves inverse-polynomial success probability. Beyond its algorithmic implications, the mean--max bound reveals that, under polynomial mean--max proximity, a pre-optimization structural layer determines the asymptotic scaling of optimal measurement probabilities up to polynomial factors. For single-layer QAOA initialized in a uniform superposition, we explicitly characterize this layer for the measurement probability of a reference state using an exact expression for the average probability that captures the interplay between problem structure and mixer dynamics through the overlap of a problem structure matrix and a mixer-dependent matrix. We derive a mixer-dependent capacity bound and identify cancellations between constructive and destructive contributions as a mechanism for additional superpolynomial suppression relative to this capacity.

authors.name: Guilherme Adamatti Bridi, Franklin de Lima Marquezino, Andris Ambainis

papers.title: Electron-photon entanglement in real space from quantum electrodynamics
papers.summary: We study the entanglement between an electron and the photon it scatters, resolved in real space and time. Starting from nonrelativistic QED in Fermi's oscillator representation, we write Fock's coupled equations for components with fixed photon number in the photon configuration space, in the length gauge, where the photon is created around the atom through a nonlocal kernel. Truncated at one photon, the equations are solved numerically without the rotating-wave approximation for a one-dimensional model atom in a waveguide with a single transverse mode and enhanced coupling. The atom is driven by a short, off-resonant laser pulse, with the electron and photon represented on real-space grids. The global electron-photon entanglement is largely transient. It peaks during the pulse and decreases as the polarized electron cloud returns to the core, leaving a state close to a product of the electron state and a superposition of the field vacuum with a single scattered photon. Local entanglement, obtained from walkers sampled across both photon-number components, exhibits opposite spatial patterns for the two particles. The electron entropy is smallest at the nucleus and maps the local strength of the dipole coupling, whereas the photon entropy is largest near the atom, where photons are created and absorbed, and smaller in the outgoing wave packets.

authors.name: Ivan P. Christov

papers.title: Shor's algorithm compiled on cat qubits: 22 593 qubits for RSA-2048 in 3.14 days
papers.summary: We present an end-to-end resource estimation of Shor's algorithm on superconducting cat qubits, from its mathematical description to the allocation and scheduling of physical qubits on a chip layout. We review modern versions of Shor's algorithm for RSA, ECDLP and FFDLP, and make their logical circuits and trade-offs explicit. We compile the dominant subroutines down to physical-qubit operations on two architectures: one based on repetition cat codes and one on LDPC cat codes. We design a parity-Cnot gate for cat qubits, extend a multi-target Cnot gate to the LDPC-cat architecture, and adapt an active injection procedure to cat qubits. Building on these primitives, we adapt to cat qubits the adder from Gidney's 2025 resource estimate for factoring RSA-2048. We combine our adder compilation and a coarser estimate for the phaseup with the factory designs and lookup compilation from the FeMoco resource estimation of Kroell et al. Together, these lead to chip layouts and schedules for factoring RSA-2048. Assuming a 1$\mu$s error-correction cycle time, a 10$\mu$s reaction time, circuit-level phase-flip noise with probability $p_Z = 5 \times 10^{-4}$ and no bit-flips, factoring RSA-2048, the configuration we compile in full, requires about 23 000 cat qubits and 3.14 days. Reusing the compiled operations, solving ECDLP on secp256k1 requires at most 30 000 cat qubits and 1 hour, and FFDLP-512, which we propose as an intermediate benchmark, about 6 700 cat qubits and 21 minutes. Trading space for time, RSA-2048 runs in 1.25 hours on about 611 000 cat qubits. The no-bit-flip requirement (a bit-flip time of about 100 years) can be relaxed to a bit-flip time of about one hour by adding a concatenation layer with a distance-3 bit-flip code, in which case RSA-2048 needs about 45 000 cat qubits.

authors.name: Axel Pappalardo, Dahmun Goudarzi, Victor Hertz, Hugo Jacinto, Larissa Kroell, Andr\'e Schrottenloher, Peter Shanahan, \'Elie Gouzien, R\'emi de la Vieuville, Vivien Londe

papers.title: Beyond Robustness of Magic: Quantifying Quantum State Convertibility
papers.summary: In fault-tolerant quantum computing, magic states provide essential resources for implementing non-Clifford operations. The robustness of magic (RoM) quantifies the magic contained in a quantum state and is closely related to the cost of classical simulation. However, knowing how much magic two states contain is not sufficient to determine whether one can be converted into the other using free operations. In this work, we develop a geometric framework in which RoM is represented as half the distance to the set of free states, and extend this framework to state conversion. We introduce a directed conversion deficiency that measures how far a target state lies from the states freely reachable from a given input. This quantity vanishes exactly when free conversion is possible and, beyond being a mathematically well-defined measure, has an operational interpretation in terms of stabilizer quasiprobability. Furthermore, our framework provides lower bounds on the additional magic states required for conversion that can be strictly stronger than conventional RoM-based bounds. We demonstrate this distinction analytically by constructing a continuous family of mixed single-qubit states with identical RoM for which free conversion is possible in one direction but impossible in the reverse. Our results reveal that the usefulness of magic for quantum state conversion depends not only on its amount but also on the specific transformation being performed.

authors.name: Satoshi Kanno, Yoshi-aki Shimada

papers.title: Reference-Assisted Qutrit Control and Conditional One-Round Distillation in a Charge-4e Superconductor Model
papers.summary: We formulate a charge-$4e$ parafermionic-vortex route to qutrit processing as a conditional theory with explicit operational assumptions. Sector preservation and same-label charge-conjugation covariance imply closure for every adaptive visible record. For charge-conjugation-invariant inputs, record probabilities are independent of the supported reference state; for arbitrary inputs, discarding the reference gives a population-weighted mixture of conjugate sector maps. We give a finite-depth stability bound for complete labelled instruments, including postselection and initial zero-sector contamination. A self-contained calculation reproduces the known dense single-qutrit closure of the registered Clifford-plus-Flip gate set. We also specify an abstract ternary CSS $[[11,1,5]]_3$ syndrome/recovery decoder: 243 classical representatives per CSS component correct all 3,609 Pauli errors of support weight at most two, and an exact integer dynamic program yields the full independent-Pauli logical enumerator. Its all-syndrome acceptance is distinct from the known $1/1728$ ideal acceptance of one-round strange-state Golay distillation. An accepted-run target-infidelity budget and a synthetic parameter protocol expose the remaining noise assumptions. Native charge-$4e$ syndrome extraction, material feasibility, a device threshold, and unconditional fault tolerance are not established.

authors.name: Junhao (Eigen), Wang

papers.title: Efficient $XX$ Placement Strategies for Energy-Gap Enhancement in Quantum Annealing
papers.summary: Quantum annealing offers the prospect of a computational advantage over classical methods for certain classes of combinatorial optimisation problems. Its performance, however, is fundamentally constrained by the minimum spectral gap between the ground state and the first excited state encountered during the annealing process. When this gap closes exponentially with problem size, the runtime required to maintain adiabatic evolution can likewise grow exponentially, severely limiting the practical efficiency of the annealer. For problems including the maximum weight independent set (MWIS), previous work has shown that introducing $XX$ interactions along problem-graph edges can substantially enlarge the minimum energy-gap and thereby improve annealing performance. In practice, however, current quantum annealing hardware does not support these interactions natively and methods for implementing effective $XX$ couplings come with hardware overhead and connectivity constraints. These limitations motivate the use of only a limited number of $XX$ interactions. In this paper, we investigate $XX$ placement strategies for MWIS instances under both resource and topological constraints, and demonstrate that careful selection of the placements can substantially increase the minimum energy-gap. We evaluate these strategies through a detailed statistical analysis of both deliberately constructed hard MWIS instances and random Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs. Notably, these strategies are particularly effective for hard MWIS instances with initially small minimum gaps, where targeted placement yields the largest relative improvements.

authors.name: Jennivine Chen, Natasha Feinstein, P A Warburton

papers.title: Proven optimality for LABS with quantum-classical branch and bound
papers.summary: Low autocorrelation binary sequences (LABS) are the phase codes of pulse compression radar and the synchronization words of digital communication, and finding the sequence of a given length whose aperiodic autocorrelations have the smallest sum of squares is a hard binary optimization problem. The quantum optimization methods tested on LABS so far return good sequences, but they cannot show that a sequence is optimal or bound how far from optimal it may be. We show that a quantum optimization algorithm can deliver proven optimality. In our quantum-classical branch and bound, fixed-angle QAOA samples the Hamiltonians of the nodes of the search tree, its samples supply candidate sequences and the branching choice, and classical bounds prune the tree, so that the algorithm returns either a proof of optimality or, if it is stopped early, the best sequence found with a certified lower bound and gap. It works on the native quartic Hamiltonian without penalty terms, and its correctness does not depend on the sampler. With QAOA at depth p= 12 and at p= 1 and 1,000 shots per node, it proved the optima of all lengths from 2 to 30, where from length 27 on the root node is split without being sampled. Every run records both bounds against time, and its primal-dual integral measures its convergence. We claim no speedup.

authors.name: Andr\'as Cz\'egel

papers.title: Fe$^{2+}$:forsterite Qubit System
papers.summary: Quantum Computing uses quantum mechanical phenomena, such as superposition and entanglement of quantum bits (qubits), to represent and manipulate information in multidimensional state spaces. This approach allows complex mathematical functions to be executed simultaneously rather than sequentially, making them much more efficient than classical computers. However, current quantum computers suffer from quantum decoherence, where small changes to their environment, such as thermal fluctuations and vibrations, affect the systems' fragile states. The goal of this study is to discuss the functionality of a proposed Fe$^{2+}$:forsterite qubit system by solving the unitary time-evolution of a quantum state vector for the system's Hamiltonian, using known axial and traverse anisotropy terms at temperatures up to 10 K. The system can effectively transfer population between its two lowest states at rates predicted by the Rabi half-period, with 99.9% fidelity. Additionally, it can hold the population at a desired state without docohering. The results remained consistent for temperatures up to 10 K, meaning, unlike many common qubit systems, the proposed qubit system could function without a dilution fridge and is not fragile to thermal noise.

authors.name: Dishaanth S. Pillai, G. M. Wysin

papers.title: Stationary Quantum Time Series: Spectral Theory of Process Memory and Measurement Records
papers.summary: Classical time series analysis converts temporal dependence into structure that can be learned from a single observed trajectory, through stationarity, ergodicity, spectral representation, and finite-memory models. Quantum experiments are naturally time series: every run is a sequence of interventions and outcomes, and the memory of an open system is written in its temporal statistics. However, the classical foundation cannot be translated directly: measuring a process and forgetting the outcome differs from not measuring at all, so no single family of joint probability distributions describes a quantum process. We develop a process-tensor framework for stationary quantum time series and establish its first structural theorems. For stationary combs of finite quantum Markov order l relative to a fixed informationally complete causal break, we construct a finite-dimensional causal transfer map of dimension at most d^{4l}, where d bounds the system Hilbert-space dimension at each step. ... These results supply the stationary foundation on which quantum spectral analysis, model identification, and single-trajectory inference can be built.

authors.name: Hai Wang

papers.title: QuFrame: Pauli Frame Tracking for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Control
papers.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires continuous quantum error correction (QEC) to suppress physical noise. While Clifford-only workloads can defer corrections to software post-processing, universal computation breaks this paradigm: executing non-Clifford gates via magic-state gadgets introduces hard, real-time control-flow dependencies on error-corrected measurements. Consequently, the controller must extract syndromes, decode them, and update the Pauli frame in real time, closing the entire QEC loop within a strict $1\,\mu\text{s}$ cycle. However, prior proposals on Pauli frame tracking remain largely theoretical, leaving the microarchitectural bottlenecks of tracking, resolving, and synchronizing frame updates across distributed control pipelines unaddressed. To this end, we present QuFrame, a control microarchitecture for real-time Pauli frame tracking that closes the QEC loop within $1\,\mu\text{s}$ while sustaining QPU-rate throughput. By introducing QuFrameISA, we cleanly decouple instruction execution from continuous Pauli frame management. Execution is distributed across per-qubit Instruction Resolution Engines (IREs) that resolve instructions against the frame via a single table lookup, while a Pauli Frame Management Unit enables independent, lock-free concurrent commits. To strictly guarantee the $1\,\mu\text{s}$ deadline, QuFrame pairs an asynchronous primary decoder with an on-chip fallback decoder that resolves in $144\,\text{ns}$, natively reconciling divergent updates in hardware without degrading logical error rates.

authors.name: Aleksandra \'Swierkowska, Ilgaz Er, Emmanouil Giortamis, Pramod Bhatotia

papers.title: Influence of dark matter on quantum entanglement and coherence in curved spacetime
papers.summary: Dark matter (DM) has not yet been directly detected, and phenomenological models such as perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) provide analytically tractable settings for investigating its possible gravitational effects. Here PFDM denotes the conventional name of an anisotropic effective source, rather than a perfect fluid in the usual isotropic sense. In this work, we study the entanglement and coherence of bosonic and fermionic test fields near a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by PFDM. These quantum fields probe the background geometry and are not assumed to be microscopic constituents of PFDM. Under our sign convention, only the $\alpha0$ branch is retained solely as a formal extension of the same metric family. Within the positive-density PFDM sector, entanglement and coherence vary monotonically with the PFDM parameter, while the complete extended parameter range exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence arising from the corresponding variation of the Hawking temperature. Bosonic entanglement is more susceptible to this geometric effect than fermionic entanglement, whereas fermionic coherence shows a stronger response than its bosonic counterpart. These results characterize how particle statistics and the choice of quantum resource govern the sensitivity of test fields to PFDM-induced modifications of the spacetime geometry.

authors.name: Shu-Min Wu, Yu-Xuan Wang, Si-Han Shang, Wentao Liu

papers.title: On the Spectral Statistics of Multiparametric Random Real Asymmetric Matrices: a hidden universality
papers.summary: Theoretical analysis of a wide range of complex system e.g. those in contact with environment necessitate consideration of the generic real-asymmetric matrix ensembles, those with varying order of matrix elements e.g. a sparse structure or a banded structure. We pursue the complexity parameter approach to analyze the spectral statistics of the multiparametric Gaussian ensembles of normal real asymmetric matrices and derive the theoretical formulations for the ensemble averaged spectral densities of the real as well as complex eigenvalues. Considerations of the matrix elements with arbitrary choice of mean and variances render us the freedom to model the desired sparsity in the ensemble. Our formulation provides a common mathematical formulation of the spectral statistics for a wide range of sparse real-asymmetric ensembles and also reveals, thereby, a deep rooted universality among them.

authors.name: Ratul Dutta, Pragya Shukla

papers.title: Non-chiral edge states and cascading of exceptional points in the non-reciprocal Haldane model
papers.summary: Robust boundary-localised modes and band geometry arise in a variety of condensed matter lattice systems, of which the Haldane honeycomb model is a paradigmatic example. We study a non-Hermitian variant of the Haldane model, which exhibits two key features: distinctive exceptional-point (EP) structures in the periodic and open boundary spectra and non-chiral edge modes. In a fully periodic system, there are exceptional rings (ERs) that mark the boundary between the $\mathcal{PT}$-unbroken and $\mathcal{PT}$-broken regions, revealing Berry-curvature confinement across the $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry transition. The system on a cylinder with zigzag boundaries exhibits a bifurcation transition of edge-to-bulk delocalisation. We also observe a ``Russian-doll-like'' cascading of exceptional points as the non-Hermiticity is increased and we demonstrate how this is inherited from the bulk ER structure. The non-chiral edge modes remain robust against disorder in the non-Hermitian hopping parameter. The dynamical evolution shows a tunable range of weak non-Hermiticity and wave packet widths for which the edge-to-bulk delocalization time is extended. These results establish this model as a natural platform to explore Berry-curvature confinement, exceptional-point cascading and non-chiral edge physics.

authors.name: Aditi A. Prabhudesai, H. S. Chhabra, Suraj S. Hegde

papers.title: Emergent Kinetic Constraints and Subspace Fragmentation in Rydberg Arrays
papers.summary: In a strongly interacting Rydberg atom array, the dynamics are often constrained to the decoupled and fragmented Hilbert subspaces, representing an intriguing paradigm for nonergodicity. Here we investigate the Hilbert-space fragmentation in the degenerate subspaces arising from the interplay between tunable detuning and arbitrary long-range interactions in a one-dimensional Rydberg-atom array with lattice-translation symmetry. We analytically establish the conditions for the emergence of subspaces and their subsidiary fragmentations in the thermodynamic limit, enumerate the emergent kinetic constraints at the discrete dynamical points where dynamics are possible at all, and demonstrate the conditions for strong fragmentation and the rich scaling behaviors of the fragments. Our results provide systematic and analytical understandings of Hilbert-space fragmentation in Rydberg arrays, and shed light on engineering nonergodic many-body dynamics beyond the PXP model.

authors.name: Wen-Jie Geng, Zhenming Zhang, Wei Yi

papers.title: Multidimensional Reconciliation in Continuous-Variable QKD: Review, Coding Schemes, and Open-Source Simulation
papers.summary: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) requires highly efficient reconciliation techniques to operate at low signal-to-noise ratios and long distances. Multidimensional reconciliation addresses this challenge by transforming the physical Gaussian quantum channel into a virtual binary-input additive white Gaussian noise (BIAWGN) channel, enabling the use of modern errorcorrecting codes. In this work, we review the principles of multidimensional reconciliation, with a particular focus on high-dimensional constructions beyond the algebraic dimensions 1, 2, 4, 8. We describe the construction of the virtual channel, discuss practical coding schemes for reverse reconciliation, and analyse their integration with linear error-correcting codes. We also present an opensource simulation framework, HDirac, implementing multidimensional reconciliation for arbitrary dimensions, and use it to evaluate state-of-the-art LDPC codes. The results highlight key trade-offs between dimension, reconciliation efficiency, and frame error rate, providing practical guidance for CV-QKD system design.

authors.name: Lucien Martial, Alexis Rosio, Eleni Diamanti, Adrien Cassagne, Baptiste Gouraud

papers.title: Asymmetric quantum steering harvested near a Lorentz-violating BTZ black hole
papers.summary: We investigate the harvesting of quantum steering and its directional asymmetry between two Unruh-DeWitt detectors in a Lorentz-violating BTZ black hole spacetime. Since the detectors are located at different radial positions outside the black hole, they experience inequivalent local environments induced by gravitational redshift, causing Alice to undergo stronger effective thermal noise than Bob. Remarkably, we uncover a counterintuitive phenomenon in which the detector subjected to a higher effective temperature exhibits stronger steerability than the other one, revealing a nontrivial inversion of thermal intuition in curved spacetime. Furthermore, quantum steering survives only within a finite window of detector energy gaps and reaches its maximum within an optimal regime. We find that Lorentz violation suppresses steering most strongly near this optimal energy gap, indicating an enhanced sensitivity of maximal correlation extraction to symmetry breaking effects. Our results demonstrate that Lorentz violation acts as a geometric constraint on the quantum information capacity of spacetime, simultaneously restricting both the strength and the directionality of quantum correlations.

authors.name: Si-Yu Liu, Xin-Ze Song, Xiang-Yue Yu, Wentao Liu, Xiao-Li Huang, Shu-Min Wu

papers.title: Phonon Scharnhorst effect: Acoustic analogue of the vacuum-fluctuation-boosted speed of light
papers.summary: The Scharnhorst effect in quantum electrodynamics predicts a superluminal velocity shift $\delta c>0$ at low photon frequencies due to vacuum fluctuations between two mirrors. Although theoretically robust (no causality violation), the effect is extraordinarily small ($\delta c/c\approx 10^{-32}$ for mirrors $1\,\mu{\rm m}$ apart) and outside current experimental reach. Here we propose a condensed matter analogue, replacing the photons in the electromagnetic vacuum by phonon excitations of a Bose-Einstein condensate. In an idealized geometry, the two-dimensional surface of a cylinder (circumference $L$) at zero temperature, the axial speed of sound is increased due to zero-point fluctuations of the condensate by $\delta c/c\simeq 5\times 10^{-3}\,\tilde{g}$ at $L\simeq 2\,\xi$, to first order in the dimensionless interaction constant $\tilde{g}\simeq 10^{-1}$ of the Bose gas of healing length $\xi\simeq 1\,\mu{\rm m}$. This is 28 orders of magnitude larger than the photonic effect at a comparable confinement length, basically because phonons have a self-interaction while photons only interact via massive electrons. When $L$ drops below $1.19\,\xi$ the velocity shift changes sign, signaling the crossover to a one-dimensional Bose gas. We discuss the prospects for observation of the acoustic Scharnhorst effect. The main obstacles are the nK temperature requirement and the need to separate the vacuum-fluctuation shift from a mean-field geometric correction.

authors.name: C. W. J. Beenakker

papers.title: The often overlooked role of sound in liquid thermal transport
papers.summary: Formulated a hundred years ago, the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of liquids postulates a proportionality between sound velocity and thermal conductivity. This designates phonons as heat carriers in a liquid. Its empirical success has been under-appreciated and its conceptual implications overlooked. Here, we review its origin, its links to hydrodynamic Euler equations and to the fundamental paradox surrounding the parabolic heat equation and its fate across the quantum-classical crossover.

authors.name: Kamran Behnia

papers.title: Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
papers.summary: In classical statistics, local asymptotic normality provides a general framework for characterizing optimal testing power and constructing asymptotically efficient procedures. Extending this framework to quantum statistical models introduces additional challenges arising from the noncommutativity of observables and the need to optimize over quantum measurements. In this paper, we develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency for quantum hypothesis testing using quantum local asymptotic normality and the asymptotic representation theorem. We establish sharp nuisance-maximin power bounds for one-sided tests and two-sided tests within the unbiased class by reducing the corresponding classical--quantum Gaussian shift experiments to classical testing problems. This reduction is justified through a quantum Hunt--Stein argument that accommodates both commuting and noncommuting Gaussian coordinates. Under suitable asymptotic invariance conditions, the resulting bounds transfer to the original quantum experiments and are attained by scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests. We further develop a two-stage adaptive construction that achieves the same local asymptotic power without knowledge of the reference parameter. As an application, we study testing of smooth spectral functionals of quantum states. We compare scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests with the weak Schur sampling plug-in test and with optimally weighted linear statistics of its fluctuations. This comparison distinguishes loss from the plug-in weighting from a gap between the best such spectral statistic and the scalar score procedure. We characterize equality of the corresponding variances and illustrate the two gaps through explicit examples.

authors.name: Rathindra Nath Karmakar, Samriddha Lahiry, Koichi Yamagata

papers.title: Exact Fractional Chern Insulators from Hubbard Interactions
papers.summary: Laughlin's wavefunction and its parent interaction, Haldane's pseudopotential, underpin our analytic understanding of fractional quantum Hall effect. They are an exact pair in the sense that the wavefunction is the unique, zero-energy ground state of its frustration-free parent Hamiltonian. In this work, we propose exact pairs of many-body wavefunctions for fractional Chern insulators in tight binding models with onsite Hubbard interactions as their parents. The key to our construction is introduction of a Landau-dual Chern band, a multi-orbital Chern band obtained from directly sampling the spin-$s$ Dirac Landau level on a Bravais lattice. The exact many-body wavefunctions are given, analytically, in terms of the matrix coordinate $X+iY+J$, where $(X,Y)$ are the lattice coordinates and $J$ is a nilpotent matrix in spin space. The constructed exact pairs cover the fractional Chern states of the Laughlin, the Read-Rezayi, and the Halperin series. Our results prove that FCI ground states exist beyond ideal bands.

authors.name: Jonah Herzog-Arbeitman, Rui-Heng Liu, Jiangping Hu, Chen Fang

papers.title: Umklapp-enhanced high-$T_c$ topological superconductivity mediated by magnons in $p$-wave magnets
papers.summary: We show that magnon exchange can induce nodal topological superconductivity in a microscopic model of a $p$-wave magnet. Solving the weak-coupling multiband gap equation for itinerant electrons exchange-coupled to localized spins, we find a nodal $p$-wave gap and a critical temperature that rises sharply as the Fermi surface approaches the magnetic Brillouin-zone boundary. In this regime, small-reduced-momentum magnons can scatter electrons between Fermi-surface segments on opposite sides of the zone. These Umklapp processes enhance pairing because the contributions from different sites in the magnetic unit cell cancel less in their electron-magnon vertices than in those for ordinary scattering at comparable reduced momenta. Momentum-resolved winding numbers predict zero-energy Majorana flat bands at symmetry-preserving edges where the bulk nodes project to distinct momenta.

authors.name: Kristoffer Leraand, Asle Sudb{\o}

papers.title: First order vortex-unbinding transition in 2D topological superconductors
papers.summary: We study the fate of the Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) transition in a two-dimensional topological superconductor whose vortex cores each host an isolated Majorana zero mode, energetically well separated from the bulk gap and other bound states of the vortex. When the Majorana localization length $\xi_F$ exceeds the vortex core size $\xi$, nearby vortices acquire an additional short-range attractive channel from Majorana hybridization, modifying the vortex-antivortex interaction at short distances and generating a metastable minimum in the two-vortex free energy above the nominal $T_{BKT}$. We construct an effective field theory for the resulting dilute vortex gas, coupling the ordinary BKT phase field to an additional field encoding the Majorana-mediated interaction, and show, using renormalization-group and instanton methods, that this hybridization can drive the transition first order, with the metastable phase decaying at an exponentially small rate. We propose an array of Josephson-coupled $p+ip$ superconducting islands as a microscopic platform realizing the required hierarchy of scales. Finally, we discuss experimental signatures of this first-order transition, in particular a hysteresis loop whose width is set by the coexistence window.

authors.name: Vera Mikheeva, Elio J. K\"onig

papers.title: Chern Numbers from Symmetry-Enforced Zeros and Dispersion Shifts
papers.summary: Wave-function zeros and their local vorticities provide a complementary characterization of Chern topology to more commonly used Berry-curvature formulations. Using wave-function overlaps between a Chern band and freely chosen reference states, we show that crystalline symmetry can enforce their zeros and fix their vorticities modulo the rotation order from the angular momenta of the band and reference state. We further show that weak local perturbations produce band-dispersion shifts proportional to the absolute square of the overlap, allowing its zeros and local structure to be read off directly from the dispersion. Combined with crystalline symmetry, this can identify Chern topology without measuring wave-function phases. Our construction applies to multicomponent and multiband wave functions and allows reference states whose momentum-space representation may vanish at some momenta. This permits compact localized states to be used directly as reference states and makes use of their known real- and momentum-space properties in flat-band systems. The dispersion shift near an overlap zero further provides a lower bound on the quantum metric at the zero.

authors.name: Yoonseok Hwang, Henry Davenport, Frank Schindler

papers.title: Anyon Coherent States in Fractional Chern Insulators
papers.summary: In fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems, coherent anyonic excitations are the natural entities for describing anyon dynamics, their interactions, and braiding, yet no general expression for their wavefunctions is known beyond Laughlin's quasiholes. We introduce a systematic, operator-based construction of maximally-localized wavefunctions of anyons of either charge in FQH states and fractional Chern insulators, including those in non-ideal, non-vortexable bands. We find that these wavefunctions describe coherent quasiparticles: zero modes of local annihilation operators that saturate projected-density uncertainty bounds. These coherent states owe their existence to a nontrivial topology of the anyon band, with the winding of their Bloch coefficients encoding an anyon band's Chern number. As such, their guiding centers exist anywhere within the lattice, and their mutual overlaps decay as Gaussians determined by the effective magnetic length of the anyon band.

authors.name: Pedro Fittipaldi de Castro, Haylen Gerhard, Wladimir A. Benalcazar

papers.title: Topological (in)equivalence encoded in zeros of wavefunction overlaps
papers.summary: Topological equivalence between two gapped band structures is determined by whether their occupied states can be continuously deformed into one another without closing the energy gap or breaking the protecting symmetries. We show that this relative topology can be read directly from the overlap matrix between the two occupied subspaces, in a way that treats Chern and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariants within a single framework. The determinant of the overlap matrix defines a global section of a line bundle over the Brillouin zone, which vanishes at the momenta where the map between the subspaces fails to be invertible. A singular connection, whose curvature is concentrated at these zeros, assigns each zero an integer charge given by its phase winding. In two-dimensional class A, the total charge equals the difference between the Chern numbers of the two systems. In class AII, time reversal pairs zeros of opposite charge, and the relative $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant is the parity of the total charge in half the Brillouin zone; the Kane-Mele Pfaffian is recovered as a special case. The zeros coincide with the gap closings of an interpolation between the two systems, and crystalline symmetries constrain their positions and charges. We illustrate the construction in the Haldane, Kane-Mele, and Qi-Wu-Zhang models, including cases where rotation symmetry alone enforces the zeros.

authors.name: Carolina Paiva, Bruno Mera, Roni Ilan, Raquel Queiroz

papers.title: Mixtures of a fluid with competing interactions and a simple solvent near a hard wall
papers.summary: We study a binary mixture of soft particles near a planar surface. The main component interacts through a competing short-range attraction and long-range repulsion (SALR) potential, modelled by a sum of three Yukawa terms, while the solvent and the cross interactions are described by two Yukawa terms. Using a field-theoretical mean-field approach we derive the coupled equations for the density profiles of both species, formulate the contact theorem for the two-component system, and obtain closed-form profiles in the mesoscopically homogeneous region by linearizing the theory and solving the associated eigenvalue problem. Their amplitudes are fixed by exact boundary conditions following from the continuity of the Yukawa potentials at the wall, which supply as many relations as there are unknowns. Although these conditions are implicit in the derivation of the contact theorem, they have not previously been used to fix the amplitudes of the linearized profiles, and they bring those profiles into quantitative agreement with the nonlinear solution. The equations are solved numerically for a fluid confined by hard walls. The theory predicts mixing of the two species far from the surface at high temperatures, and their microphase separation into alternating layers upon cooling or upon increasing the density. The mean-field profiles agree well with molecular dynamics data once the mean-field overestimate of the onset temperature of microsegregation is taken into account, and the analytical ones reproduce them closely except in the immediate vicinity of the wall.

authors.name: Ivan Kravtsiv, Oksana Patsahan, Taras Patsahan

papers.title: Where electrons conduct and where to change it: gauge-invariant sensitivities and the networks of sensitive bonds
papers.summary: Where is the electrical current carried in a disordered solid, and where would a local change alter it? The two questions differ. We answer the second exactly: the derivative of the Kubo-Greenwood conductivity with respect to the Hamiltonian is gauge invariant and gives the response to any local change. The construction applies to any Hamiltonian. We try it on amorphous silicon, with tight-binding cells of up to 10000 atoms and density-functional cells of up to 512 atoms, and compare it with three ways of allocating the conductivity: the space-projected conductivity (SPC), KuboMap, and the local density of states (LDOS). KuboMap follows the LDOS closely (median Spearman correlation 0.97). The sensitivity does not. It ranks the response to an on-site shift accurately and the response to removing an atom poorly, and it transfers between Hamiltonians less well than the other maps. The most sensitive bonds form connected clusters. In three large networks they are tree-like filaments of 24 to 38 atoms in the valence tail and looped networks deeper in the gap; the excess over an LDOS-weighted random selection reaches 48 standard deviations and appears only when the broadening spans about five level spacings. The filament overlaps the tail eigenstate with the most weight on it, and one of the leading conduction channels, far more than a random cluster does, but no single state or channel explains it. The networks are largely lost in thermal snapshots at 300 K. Where the conductivity is carried and where it responds are different problems: local transport maps are useful for the first and limited for the second.

authors.name: D A Drabold, C Ugwumadu

papers.title: Machine Learning-Driven High-Throughput Screening of Equimolar and Non-Equimolar High-Entropy Carbides
papers.summary: Search for optimal compositions among high-entropy ceramics are challenging due to large composition space, which are unable to test either experimentally or by \textit{ab initio} calculations. Here we present a high-throughput screening for equimolar and non-equimolar high-entropy carbides (HEC) among group IVB and VB transition metals (Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb and Ta). Large Atomistic Model MACE, and deep learning based interatomic potential DeePMD trained on \textit{ab initio}-based dataset of structures are used to effectively screen over the thousands of potential non-equimolar compositions among high-entropy carbides of Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb and Ta transition metals. A set of both equimolar and non-equimolar HECs are predicted to be stable in order to further synthesize those compositions based on the predictions.

authors.name: Arina A. Svinukhova, Faisal Baber, Michel M. Lukanov, Viktor S. Baidyshev, Daria Terentieva, Alexander Ya. Pak, Alexander G. Kvashnin

papers.title: The phase diagram of fluid hydrogen near melting from machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on quantum Monte Carlo
papers.summary: Dissociation of molecular hydrogen increasing temperature or pressure may either occur gradually or abruptly, via a phase transition. Despite considerable experimental and theoretical efforts, the phase diagram of dense hydrogen at temperatures above solid melting is not precisely known. Here, we perform classical and quantum Path Integral molecular dynamics simulations of dense hydrogen using two machine-learned interatomic potentials both trained on quantum Monte Carlo energies and forces. The resulting phase diagram is constructed using state-of-the-art techniques. Both models show a first-order phase transition from the molecular to the atomic liquid terminating in critical points whose locations were determined using finite-size scaling techniques. Triple points, located at the highest temperature of the melting curve, are found at the intersection of the liquid-liquid lines with the melting curve and should lead to clear signatures in ramp compression experiments.

authors.name: Shubhang Goswami, Hongwei Niu, Ilnur Saitov, Mathieu Istas, Yubo Yang, Scott Jensen, Markus Holzmann, Carlo Pierleoni, David Ceperley

papers.title: Single-Crystal Growth, Structure, and Physical Properties of Yb2MoO6
papers.summary: Rare-earth molybdates are functional oxides of considerable interest because their structural and chemical flexibility enables diverse magnetic, electronic, and optical behavior. Here, millimeter-sized single crystals of $Yb_2MoO_6$ are synthesized, their crystal structure determined and physical properties investigated. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirms the formation of $Yb_2MoO_6$ and yielded lattice parameters of $a = 16.228(2)$ $\mathring{A}$, $b = 10.901(3)$ $\mathring{A}$, and $c = 5.286(2)$ $\mathring{A}$, in good agreement with previously reported neutron powder diffraction data. Scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive spectroscopy show a Yb:Mo ratio close to the expected 2:1 stoichiometry. Optical measurements based on diffuse-reflectance spectra and Tauc analysis yield an estimated optical gap of $\sim 3.28$ eV under the direct-allowed transition assumption. Magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal Curie-Weiss-like paramagnetic behavior, with an effective magnetic moment of $\mu_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 4.2\mu_B$ per Yb and an apparent Weiss temperature of $\theta \approx -65.7$ K, consistent with possible antiferromagnetic interactions or correlations, with no clear magnetic-ordering transition observed down to 10 K. These results establish the growth of $Yb_2MoO_6$ single crystals and provide initial insight into their structural, optical, and magnetic properties.

authors.name: Ali Sarikhani, Santhoshkumar Sundaramoorthy, Sadracd Gamez, Mathew Pollard, Deepak Singh, Jeremy Watts, Steven Kelley, Amitava Choudhury, Yew San Hor

papers.title: Molecular engineering for crack-free transfer of single-crystalline oxide membranes onto silicon
papers.summary: Heterogeneous integration of single-crystalline complex oxides with silicon offers a route to incorporating their functionalities into next-generation microelectronics. Released from their growth substrates, freestanding oxide membranes enable this integration. However, cracks, wrinkles, and fragmentation during release and transfer limit membrane size and quality. Here, we present an interfacial energy-controlled release strategy that enables crack-free, single-crystalline freestanding oxide membranes with centimeter-scale lateral dimensions. Using SrTiO3 as a model system, time-resolved release studies identify water-induced blistering at the membrane-support interface during prolonged water exposure as the origin of membrane cracking. Lowering the molecular weight of the poly(propylene carbonate) support through polymer deconstruction increases its polarity and surface energy, suppresses interfacial blistering, and reduces organic residue after support removal. The resulting SrTiO3 membranes exhibit optical properties comparable to those of bulk single crystals. We extend this approach to the metallic ferromagnet La0.7Sr0.3MnO3, obtaining crack-free membranes on Si that preserve ferromagnetism and metallicity.

authors.name: Jeongkeun Song, Jihye Choi, Benjamin Doughty, Young-Hoon Kim, Keun-Yeol Park, Uvinduni I. Premadasa, Miaofang Chi, Seung Sae Hong, Celesta S. Chang, Zheng Gai, Ambrose Seo, Tomonori Saito, Ho Nyung Lee

papers.title: Altermagnetic magnon splitting in hematite: from bulk g-wave to planar i-wave
papers.summary: Hematite is an insulating iron oxide with both a collinear antiferromagnetic and a weakly ferromagnetic phase with intriguing properties, such as long-range spin transport distances, that make it promising for spintronics applications. It has also been identified as a candidate for g-wave altermagnetism. Here, we present the results of fully relativistic ab initio calculations of the magnon properties of hematite, with a focus on altermagnetic effects. We quantitatively evaluate both the anisotropic and altermagnetic magnon band splitting as well as the magnon lifetimes. We show that dipolar interactions lead to a sizeable non-altermagnetic splitting and a hybridisation between opposite-chirality magnons resulting in a strong reduction of the spin expectation value of magnons close to the {\Gamma} point and around nodal planes, even in the collinear out-of-plane phase. Both the frequencies and the lifetimes have a large altermagnetic splitting in the $k_z = 0$ plane, which is characteristic of hematite and not generally expected for g-wave altermagnets. We compare our results to the prototypical, hexagonal g-wave altermagnet manganese telluride, which has four symmetry-protected nodal planes, whereas the fourth nodal surface in hematite is not completely fixed by symmetry. We derive implicit analytical expressions for this surface and discuss how it arises from a combination of rotational and translational symmetry, which leads to a transition to i-wave symmetry at the Brillouin zone boundary. The example of hematite reveals the trigonal altermagnets as a special case where the splitting function exhibits both bulk (g-wave) and planar (i-wave) components, and shows that the point symmetries alone are not sufficient to capture the full symmetry-determined behaviour of the splitting function.

authors.name: Tobias Dannegger, Julian A. Beisch, Levente R\'ozsa, L\'aszl\'o Szunyogh, Ulrich Nowak

papers.title: Canted antiferromagnetism and spin-flop transition in honeycomb $\alpha$-Na$_2$PrO$_3$ revealed by angle-dependent torque magnetometry up to 35 T
papers.summary: We report angle-dependent piezocantilever torque measurements on single crystals of the honeycomb magnet $\alpha$-Na$_2$PrO$_3$, proposed to display unconventional magnetism stabilized by anisotropic exchange interactions between spin-orbit entangled, pseudospin 1/2 Pr$^{4+}$ magnetic moments. Previous powder susceptibility observed signatures of a transition at low temperatures to antiferromagnetic order with a weak ferromagnetic moment. From the torque angular dependence in three orthogonal crystallographic planes, we infer a zero-field canted antiferromagnetic structure, with moments almost normal to the honeycomb layers, but weakly canted such as to give rise to a spontaneous magnetization along the in-plane monoclinic $a$-axis, with two magnetic domains related by time reversal. Sharp jumps in the torque angular dependence when the field projection along $a$ changes sign are interpreted as field-induced switching between the two degenerate domains with oppositely aligned ferromagnetic moments. We propose a minimal spin Hamiltonian including easy-axis exchange anisotropy and symmetry-allowed Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) couplings, for which mean-field calculations reproduce the main features of the observed angle-dependent torque. Torque measurements up to 35 T applied almost normal to the layers observe a strong anomaly attributed to proximity to the field-induced spin-flop transition predicted for the above Hamiltonian. We contrast the predicted magnetic phase diagrams for magnetic fields in different orthogonal crystallographic planes normal to the honeycomb layers and discuss how DM interactions convert some transitions into smooth crossovers and stabilize a phase boundary line connecting the spin-flop transition in field normal to the layers to magnetization saturation for in-plane field normal to $a$; such a phase boundary line does not exist in the absence of DM interactions.

authors.name: Kylie MacFarquharson, Ryutaro Okuma, Matthew Pearce, Amalia I. Coldea, Alix McCollam, Roos Leenen, Uli Zeitler, Yurii Skourski, Radu Coldea

papers.title: Learning Spin Hamiltonians from Interacting Magnon Spectra
papers.summary: A neural network that learns an inverse map inherits the approximations of the forward solver used to generate its training data. We demonstrate this in the inference of spin Hamiltonians from synthetic neutron-scattering spectra and show how a fast many-body solver can overcome the limitation of linear spin-wave theory (LSWT). We consider a family of anisotropic triangular-lattice spin Hamiltonians at fields just above saturation, where magnon interactions shift and broaden the spectrum in ways that LSWT cannot capture. Using the truncated Hilbert-space ladder (THL) method, we compute the dynamical spin structure factor (DSSF) nonperturbatively within the one- and two-magnon space. THL is fast enough to generate large training sets of DSSF spectra, enabling us to train neural networks that accurately predict Hamiltonian parameters. By empirically benchmarking several neural-network architectures, we find that a one-dimensional convolutional network performs best. A learned forward decoder then reconstructs the DSSF from the predicted parameters, providing a rapid self-consistency check and a visualization of the predicted response. When interactions are strong, networks trained on LSWT and THL spectra infer markedly different parameters. Analysis of the Fisher information matrix shows that the measurement protocol, including which spin-correlation components are resolved and the momentum cut, determines which couplings can be identified. Combining machine learning with fast many- body theory is therefore essential for quantitative Hamiltonian inference from scattering data.

authors.name: Ang-Kun Wu, David A. Dahlbom, Kipton Barros, Cristian D. Batista, Hao Zhang

papers.title: Circuit model for gate-induced excitation of quantum Hall edges tuned by DC gate bias
papers.summary: Edge excitations, which propagate along the edge of a quantum Hall system, are of great interest in the study of low-dimensional electron systems and mesoscopic transport phenomena. In this study, we investigate the relationship between the input voltage and the excitation waveform for gate-induced excitations. By varying the offset voltage applied to the gate, we observe that the excitation waveform changes from a first-derivative-like response to a response proportional to the input waveform in the time domain. In the frequency domain, we observe that the frequency dependence of the gate excitation changes significantly as the offset voltage crosses the pinch-off voltage. We show that these changes can be described by a single equivalent circuit model with different effective gate-2DEG capacitances on either side of the pinch-off voltage. In addition, we confirm that the effective capacitance obtained from the fitting of the model with the experimental data is consistent with the capacitance calculated from the device structure.

authors.name: Kodai Sugizaki, Takaaki Mano, Go Yusa

papers.title: Magnetic order in Tb and Dy substituted La3Ni2O7 and effects of high-pressure high-temperature O2 annealing
papers.summary: To study the influence of magnetic lanthanide (Ln) substituents on La3Ni2O7, polycrystalline samples of La3-xLnxNi2O7 (Ln = Pr, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm, and Yb) were synthesized and characterized by electrical transport, magnetization, and x-ray and neutron powder diffraction before and after high-pressure high-temperature oxygen annealing. The annealing process led to the formation of La3Ni2O7 polymorphs and more metallic-like temperature dependence of the electrical resistance while changing the density-wave transition temperature only slightly. For unannealed La2.7Tb0.3Ni2O7 and La2.7Dy0.3Ni2O7, distinct features in the magnetic susceptibility and additional magnetic peaks in neutron diffraction patterns indicate that both samples develop long-range magnetic order below ~13 and 11 K, respectively. The magnetic signatures were strongly suppressed following oxygen annealing, suggesting a possible association with the accompanying structural modifications. These behaviors distinguish Tb and Dy from Pr, Nd, and Sm substituents which do not introduce magnetic ordering in the system, establishing La3-xTbxNi2O7 and La3-xDyxNi2O7 as promising platforms for exploring the interplay between magnetic order and pressure-induced superconductivity in La3Ni2O7.

authors.name: Yuhang Deng, Farhad Taraporevala, Jui-Chia Lee, Zhekai Yang, Gabriel Mee, Swadhin Rout, Richard Erber, F\'abio Abud, Renato F. Jardim, Maxim Avdeev, Jeffrey W. Lynn, M. Brian Maple

papers.title: Weakly coordinating anions and solvents break the conductivity-transference-solvation tradeoff
papers.summary: Lithium-metal batteries promise high energy density, but common electrolytes trade ionic conductivity against the share of current carried by lithium ions and against how strongly solvent binds those ions. We show that simultaneously weakening both interactions of the lithium ion, with solvent and with anion, relaxes this trade-off. Thus, a weakly coordinating perfluorinated alkoxyaluminate salt in liquefied fluoromethane conducts 39.2 mS cm$^{-1}$ at 25 $^\circ$C while maintaining a lithium-ion transference number of 0.71. Molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that the anion prevents persistent ion aggregation and lowers the salt's dissociation penalty. Consistent with these properties, nickel-rich cathode/lithium-metal anode full cells charge at 10C at room temperature and at 2C at $-40$ $^\circ$C. We advance coordination strength as a design axis for future energy storage devices.

authors.name: Alex Liu, Ganesh Raghavendran, Eric S. Yang, Kevin J. Anderton, Vibhu Vardhan Singh, Aiden Larson, Kun Ryu, Kent J. Griffith, Joshua S. Figueroa, Ying Shirley Meng, Tod A. Pascal

papers.title: Generalized Critical-State Analysis of Local Field Screening in High-Pressure Yttrium Polyhydride
papers.summary: We resolve the long-standing controversy over the interpretation of magnetic-flux expulsion in high-pressure superhydrides by measuring the local magnetic field adjacent to yttrium polyhydride at 171 GPa and 4.1 K with a $^{57}$Fe M\"ossbauer sensor. Nuclear forward scattering tracks the local induction $B_{\rm sensor}(B_a)$, which nearly merges with the normal-state line near 1.5 T. Rather than assuming a constant-current Bean state, we solve the critical-state problem for the actual thin-disk geometry using the Shantsev--Clem--Sanchez method and compare generalized field-dependent critical-state models. Both the Kim and exponential laws reproduce the measured virgin branch, whereas the constant-$J_c$ Bean model fails. The corresponding zero-field critical-current densities, $(4.38\pm1.48)\times10^{11}$ and $(2.45\pm0.22)\times10^{11}$ A/m$^2$, respectively, are consistent in order of magnitude with transport estimates for granular YH$_6$. These results establish that the observed flux expulsion is a pinned critical state, not the equilibrium Meissner effect, and demonstrate a general methodology for probing local superconductivity under extreme conditions.

authors.name: A. G. Gavriliuk, I. A. Troyan, A. A. Mironovich, A. G. Ivanova, H. -K. Mao, V. V. Struzhkin

papers.title: Origin and hole-density dependence of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites
papers.summary: Metal halide perovskites have spin-orbit coupling among the strongest in semiconductors, yet whether their centrosymmetric bulk phases can convert charge current into spin current, and what controls the response, is unknown. Here we identify, from first-principles calculations on the four all-inorganic compounds CsBX3 (B = Pb, Sn; X = Br, I), the factors that govern their intrinsic spin Hall conductivity. The conductivity arises from the spin Berry curvature of the spin-orbit-split halide-p bands, 1.1-2.6 eV below the valence band maximum, and exceeds that of III-V and group-IV semiconductors when the Fermi level lies inside them. Because the valence band maximum is an s-p singlet, shifted only in second order, these contributions cancel in the undoped compounds, which respond like conventional semiconductors. With hole doping the response recovers, and at densities reachable by electric double-layer gating CsPbI3 attains the spin Hall conductivity of p-GaAs. The response is therefore determined by the position of the halide-p bands relative to the valence band maximum, not by the atomic spin-orbit constant, a criterion that applies to any semiconductor with an orbital-singlet band edge. These results point to CsPbI3 as a candidate gate-controlled source of spin current for perovskite spin-orbit torque devices.

authors.name: Thanh Tung Huynh, Yuefeng Yin, Weiyao Zhao, Junlin Yan, Qurat Ul Ain, Jacek J. Jasieniak, Julie Karel, Nikhil V. Medhekar

papers.title: Topological Bound States in the Continuum
papers.summary: We uncover topological bound states in the continuum in AB-stacked bilayer graphene mass-wall junctions. Valley topology supports interface states propagating along the wall, while a distinct winding of the confinement conditions governs exact decoupling from conducting leads. Tuning the junction length or interlayer bias can merge oppositely charged bound states and remove confinement without changing the valley topology. At generic critical points, the state remains bound and nearby resonance widths open quartically with momentum. These results connect complementary roles of topology in interface propagation and confinement within a conducting continuum.

authors.name: Dan-Na Liu, J. Villavicencio, Pierre A. Pantaleon

papers.title: Scattering Circular Dichroism from Spatially Modulated Anisotropic Magnetic Dipoles in BiFeO$_3$
papers.summary: Antiferromagnets with broken time-reversal symmetry, including altermagnets, have attracted growing interest because they can exhibit ferromagnet-like responses, such as the anomalous Hall effect and magneto-optical effects, despite their compensated spin structures. Such time-reversal symmetry breaking is characterized by ferroic time-reversal-odd multipoles, distinct from the conventional spin and orbital moments. Among them, the anisotropic magnetic dipole (AMD), which reflects the local orbital anisotropy, shares the symmetry of magnetization and can have a ferroic component even when the spin moments cancel. AMD responses have thus far been identified primarily in antiferromagnets with unit-cell magnetic periodicity, whereas spatially modulated AMDs in long-wavelength magnetic textures remain unexplored. Here, we report resonant soft x-ray small-angle scattering measurements on the antiferromagnetic spin cycloid of the multiferroic BiFeO$_3$. We observe pronounced circular dichroism in the resonant scattering intensity, i.e., scattering circular dichroism, which is not expected from the established cycloidal and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya-interaction-induced sinusoidal spin structures. We show that the staggered rotation of the FeO$_6$ octahedra gives rise to ferroic AMD components despite the antiparallel spin alignment. As the local magnetic symmetry varies with the cycloidal phase, these AMDs are spatially modulated and produce the dichroism through interference with the sinusoidal spin component. Our findings demonstrate that long-wavelength antiferromagnetic textures can host spatially modulated AMDs, opening new avenues for exploring hidden multipole textures in magnetic and multiferroic materials.

authors.name: Y. Ishii, N. Sasabe, T. Honda, S. Kawachi, T. Ito, A. Sumiyoshiya, H. Nomura, T. Nakamura, T. Arima, Y. Yamasaki

papers.title: Comparative First-Principles Study of the Physical Properties, Phonon-Mediated Superconductivity and Functional Potential of Technetium-Based Binary Borides TcB2, Tc2B and Tc3B
papers.summary: Phonon-mediated superconductivity in binary transition-metal borides reflects a balance between the metal d-states, metal-boron bonding, and the lattice vibrations that couple to them. Here, we compare P6/mmm TcB2 at 20 GPa with I4/mcm Tc2B and P4/mmm Tc3B at 0 GPa within a first-principles framework. Their mechanical responses differ appreciably: TcB2 is the most rigid under its compressed condition, Tc2B shows the strongest tendency toward ductility, and Tc3B falls between the two. Despite these differences, all three phases remain metallic. The states at the Fermi level are dominated by Tc-4d character, although the extent of Tc-d/B-p mixing varies from one compound to another. Charge redistribution is more directional and B-centered in TcB2, but more delocalized around the Tc network in Tc2B and Tc3B. Inclusion of spin-orbit coupling leaves all three compounds metallic. The optical response remains metallic and electric field polarization dependent, with substantial visible reflectivity and strong ultraviolet absorption. Low-frequency Tc rich vibrations dominate the electron-phonon coupling (EPC). With {\mu}* = 0.10, the Tc values of TcB2, Tc2B, and Tc3B are 24.92, 11.07, and 15.12 K, respectively. Although Tc3B exhibits a higher electronic density of states at the Fermi level, N(EF), TcB2 couples most strongly to EPC-active low-frequency modes, showing that the superconducting hierarchy depends on electronic-phonon matching rather than DOS magnitude alone.

authors.name: M. Rabi Us Sani Shapon, Jubair Hossan Abir, Md. Asif Afzal, Raihana Shams Islam, Saleh Hasan Naqib
