papers.title: Valley enhanced Rabi frequency in n-type planar Silicon-MOS quantum dot
papers.summary: Electron spin resonance spectroscopy (ESR) of a single electron in planar Si-MOS quantum dot is reported in the vicinity of a valley level anti-crossing. A number of one and two-photon resonances are observed due to mixing of magnetic spin-flip and electric valley-flip transitions. This allows the reconstruction of the energy-level diagram of a four state system with two valley and two spin states. Near the anti-crossing, an enhancement of the Rabi frequency is observed. This is attributed to an electric-dipole transition activated by admixing of the upper energy level due to inter-valley spin coupling. The electric-dipole transition may be driven via capacitive coupling between the ESR antenna, and the confinement gate. To characterize spin-valley coupling responsible for the enhancement, we measure the anisotropy of the g-factor difference between the two valley states, the mean g-factor and the inter-valley spin coupling for both in and out-of-plane magnetic fields. The inter-valley spin coupling is strongly modulated by the direction of the B-field, and is strongest for out-of-plane B-field, consistent with an in-plane spin-valley field. In principle, this strong Electric dipole spin resonance (EDSR) effect could be utilized for fast all-electrical spin control in small-scale devices.

authors.name: Xunyao Luo, Xander Peetroons, Tsung-Yeh Yang, Ruben M. Otxoa, Normann Mertig, Sofie Beyne, Julien Jussot, Yosuke Shimura, Clement Godfrin, Bart Raes, Roy Li, Roger Loo, Sylvain Baudot, Stefan Kubicek, Shuchi Kaushik, Danny Wan, Kristiaan De Greve, Takuma Kuno, Takeru Utsugi, Noriyuki Lee, Itaru Yanagi, Toshiyuki Mine, Satoshi Muraoka, Hideo Arimoto, Shinichi Saito, Digh Hisamoto, Ryuta Tsuchiya, Hiroyuki Mizuno, Charles Smith, Andrew Ramsay

papers.title: Symmetry-Protected Topological Phases in the Triangular Majorana-Hubbard Ladder
papers.summary: We uncover a family of symmetry-protected topological phases in a model of interacting Majorana fermions on triangular-lattice ladders. Included among these phases is one in which symmetry-protected topological order coexists with spontaneous symmetry breaking. Our results indicate a mechanism through which interactions among Majorana modes generate nontrivial symmetry-fractionalized orders. These phases may be realized in arrays of vortex-bound Majorana zero modes on the surface of topological superconductors.

authors.name: Will Holdhusen, Alberto Nocera, Jian-Xin Zhu, Armin Rahmani

papers.title: Unusual critical currents in quasi-one-dimensional superconducting aluminum two-width structures in a magnetic field
papers.summary: We measured critical switching and retrapping currents as functions of temperature in the zero field and as functions of a magnetic field perpendicular to the substrate surface at a temperature close to the critical temperature in thin-film long quasi-one-dimensional superconducting aluminum two-width structures consisting of narrow and wide wires with different critical temperatures. It is found that the switching current as a function of the field is nonlocal (dependent on electron transport in the area containing the junction line between the narrow and wide wires). The unusual behavior of the switching current lies in the fact that it is poorly described by the classical Ginzburg-Landau theory. In low and intermediate fields, the switching current is determined mainly by the densities of critical currents in the narrow and wide wires, respectively, near the wire junction line. In high fields, the switching current is due to equilibrium fluctuations of the order parameter.

authors.name: V. I. Kuznetsov, O. V. Trofimov

papers.title: Nonuniform superconducting states from Majorana flat bands
papers.summary: Zero-energy flat bands within the superconducting gap can give rise to competing ordered phases. We investigate such phases in topological superconductors based on the magnetic adatom platform hosting a flat band of Majorana edge states. Our self-consistent calculations of the superconducting order parameter show the emergence of both a pair density wave with edge-localized amplitude modulations, often a bond wave order, and a phase crystal characterized by longer-wavelength edge-localized phase modulations. Both these states lower the free energy by gapping out the Majorana flat band, but use different mechanisms tied to the underlying topology. In fact, at zero temperature the uniform superconducting solution with Majorana flat band never survives. Instead, a pair density wave appears when sufficient Majorana modes exist with oppositely signed topological winding numbers, while a phase crystal appears in regions of the phase diagram where one non-trivial winding number is heavily dominating. A crossover region connects these two states with modulations in both amplitude and phase. At finite temperatures, the pair density wave survives up to around 80% of the bulk superconducting transition temperature, while the phase crystal only appears at lower temperatures and the crossover region is also strongly suppressed. Our findings establish the ubiquity of emergent nonuniform superconducting phases and their temperature-dependent behavior in topological superconductors.

authors.name: Sushanth Varada, Aksel Kobia{\l}ka, Ankita Bhattacharya, Patric Holmvall, Annica M. Black-Schaffer

papers.title: First-principles finite-size correction schemes for point defects of Cu$_3$N
papers.summary: Point defects play a key role in determining semiconductor properties, such as electrical conductivity and photoluminescence, and often enable functional behavior. Accurate first-principles supercell simulations of point defects require reliable finite-size corrections. In this study, we combine PBE+U structural relaxations with HSE hybrid-functional calculations to determine defect formation energies and thermodynamic transition levels of Cu$_3$N. Finite-size trends are quantified using $\Gamma$-point calculations in supercells containing 256, 864, and 2048 atoms. We assess and extend the Makov-Payne and Lany-Zunger correction schemes by introducing additional $1/L^n$ terms, together with core-level potential alignment and defect-specific scaling models. Using Cu$_3$N as a case study, we show that charged vacancies are accurately described by the Makov-Payne-type scaling ($1/L + 1/L^{3}$), whereas interstitial defects with shallow or weakly localized electronic character are better captured by a hydrogenic impurity model that accounts for defect-band dispersion. Residual trends for neutral or weakly localized defects are described by higher-order polynomial fits in $1/L^{3}$ and $1/L^{4}$. Hybrid-functional energetics corrected using PBE+U-based finite-size trends confirm the intrinsic $p-n$ doping character of Cu$_3$N under the conditions considered and demonstrate that no single finite-size correction can be transferred across all defect types.

authors.name: Abdul M. Reyes, Sebastian E. Reyes-Lillo, Eduardo Men\'endez-Proupin

papers.title: Universal critical behavior in ideal Bose-Einstein condensation
papers.summary: The experimental realization of photonic Bose-Einstein condensates has renewed the interest in the critical behavior of the ideal Bose gas, a paradigmatic system generally considered to be well understood. Here we establish a universal thermodynamic classification of ideal Bose-Einstein condensation in terms of experimentally measurable critical observables. We identify three universality classes with distinct critical exponents and singular thermodynamic behavior, arising from the low-energy scaling of the single-particle density of states. Depending on the low-energy scaling exponent of the density of states, which is controlled by dimensionality and confinement, the transition displays either the usual algebraic divergences of thermodynamic susceptibilities, divergent behavior with marginal logarithmic corrections, or a more subtle form of criticality, where only the correlation length diverges. Our work provides a unified framework for equilibrium criticality in noninteracting bosonic systems. This classification applies broadly to atomic, photonic, polaritonic, and magnonic condensates, where dimensionality, confinement, and spectral engineering can strongly reshape the density of states. We connect our thermodynamic classification with previously identified universality classes based on condensate fluctuations and order parameters.

authors.name: Arturo Camacho-Guardian, Leon Kleebank, Frank Vewinger, Martin Weitz, Julian Schmitt, Rosario Paredes, Victor Romero-Roch\'in

papers.title: Domain wall drift in a ferrimagnet induced by a linearly oscillating in-plane magnetic field
papers.summary: We investigate ferrimagnetic domain-wall dynamics under linearly oscillating in-plane magnetic fields. Starting from a ferrimagnetic Lagrangian that retains the field-dependent contribution to the kinetic energy, we derive collective-coordinate equations for the domain-wall position and azimuthal angle. This formulation makes explicit the field-induced inertial terms, including Coriolis-, Euler-, and centrifugal-like contributions, and clarifies how they couple translational and azimuthal dynamics. For an oscillating in-plane field supplemented by a weak static out-of-plane bias field, we show that periodic switching of the wall angle can be rectified into a finite average domain-wall velocity. At low drive frequencies, where the wall angle follows the oscillating field, the induced drift is proportional to the drive frequency rather than the field amplitude, and reversing the static field reverses it. Above a cutoff frequency, which we derive analytically, the wall angle can no longer follow the drive and the drift is suppressed. Micromagnetic simulations confirm the analytical predictions and demonstrate that the magnitude and direction of the drift can be tuned by the net spin density. These results identify linearly oscillating fields as a mechanism for frequency-controlled domain-wall motion in ferrimagnets and highlight the role of inertial spin dynamics near magnetic compensation.

authors.name: Murod Mirzhalilov, Jacob Freyermuth

papers.title: Automatic-differentiation-enabled dynamic parameter retrieval with sub-pulse-width resolution
papers.summary: Time-resolved terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) is a phase-sensitive tool in condensed matter physics for tracking photoinduced non-equilibrium dynamics of low-energy elementary excitations. However, the measured response function, optical conductivity $\sigma(\omega,t_{pp})$, becomes unreliable in reporting the state of matter when material properties drastically change on a timescale comparable to or less than the probe pulse duration, obscuring the sub-pulse-width dynamics. To resolve this issue, we present a full-waveform inversion framework inspired by the multi-dimensional retrieval philosophy of frequency-resolved optical gating (FROG). By leveraging the automatic differentiation (AD) technique and the two-dimensional time-domain signal $E(t_{g},t_{pp})$, we show one can uniquely solve the inverse problem, at the sub-pulse-width resolution, of retrieving physical observables that are still well-defined, i.e., time-dependent scattering rate $\gamma(t)$, plasma frequency $\omega_\mathrm{p}(t)$ and resonance frequency $\omega_0(t)$, while the response functions are not. Further optimization by gradient-based routines (Adam + L-BFGS) via JAX makes the method exceptionally robust against experimental noise and probe pulse distortions. The validity of the AD-enabled methodology is benchmarked both by a self-consistent numerical approach and by experimental data from real ultrafast THz spectroscopy measurements.

authors.name: Huaiyue Peng, Yuchen Lin, Fu Deng, Xiaoyue Zhou, Jingdi Zhang

papers.title: Encoding Orbital-Projected Densities of States in Graph Neural Networks for Materials Property Prediction
papers.summary: Graph neural networks have become the dominant machine-learning architecture for predicting materials properties from crystal structures. Yet the initialization of atomic node features has received comparatively little attention, and conventional approaches rely on static elemental descriptors that carry no information about the quantum-mechanical electronic environment of each atom in its crystalline host. Here we show that augmenting atomic node representations with site-projected orbital density of states (pDOS) fingerprints, computed directly from density functional theory calculations, yields systematic and substantial improvements in predictive performance.These representations are fused with Pettifor elemental embeddings at each atomic site before message passing. For the superconducting critical temperature $T_c$ and the optical dielectric constant $\epsilon_{\infty}$,the pDOS augmentation reduces prediction errors by 22.9% and 27.9%, respectively, relative to the elemental-descriptor baseline. These improvements are comparable to those achieved by doubling the training-set size. The gains are, however, contingent on training-set size. For the magnetic exchange energies of Heusler compounds, a substantially smaller dataset, the improvement is reduced,indicating that pDOS augmentation is most effective when the training data exceeds the length of the pDOS feature vector. We introduce an interpretable spectral attention-gating mechanism that reveals that the model autonomously learns to prioritize the orbital channels and energy windows most physically relevant to each target property. These results establish pDOS-augmented graph nodes as a broadly applicable strategy for infusing first-principles electronic-structure knowledge into graph networks, opening a practical route to high-accuracy property prediction in data-scarce regimes.

authors.name: Paulo Pires, Pierre-Paul De Breuck, Mauro Fava, Hai-Chen Wang, Miguel A. L. Marques

papers.title: Emergent $\mathrm{SU}(2)_2$ Wess-Zumino-Witten criticality in an anisotropic spin-1 Kitaev-$\Gamma$ chain
papers.summary: Bond-directional interactions underpin unconventional quantum phenomena, yet their interplay with single-ion anisotropy remains elusive. Here we combine large-scale density-matrix renormalization group calculations and bosonization to investigate the spin-1 Kitaev-$\Gamma$ chain. Positive anisotropy drives a smooth crossover from the Kitaev regime to the trivial large-$D$ limit, contrasting with the topological Haldane-to-large-$D$ transition in the spin-1 Heisenberg chain. This adiabatic evolution reshapes the excitation spectrum, nonlocal correlations, and thermodynamic signatures. Conversely, negative anisotropy induces a changeover from a first-order to a continuous dimer-Haldane transition. The continuous transition exhibits $\mathrm(2)_2$ Wess-Zumino-Witten criticality with central charge of $3/2$, despite the absence of microscopic continuous symmetry. Bosonization predicts a spin-correlation exponent $\eta = 3/4$, consistent with our numerical estimate of $0.77(3)$. Our findings reveal how bond-directional interactions shape distinctive gapped regimes and emergent conformal criticality.

authors.name: Qiang Luo, Shijie Hu, Wang Yang, Yuhai Liu, Jinbin Li, Jize Zhao, Xiaoqun Wang

papers.title: First-principles carrier mobility and optical absorption of strained ZnO with self-consistent Hubbard interactions
papers.summary: Carrier mobility and optical absorption are key performance parameters of oxide semiconductors in transparent and flexible displays. We use a newly developed density-functional perturbation theory with a self-consistent Hubbard correction (DFPT+U) to study phonon-limited electron transport and phonon-assisted optical absorption in strained zinc oxide (ZnO). This parameter-free approach accounts for electron-phonon interactions and on-site correlation effects simultaneously. Electronic structures and phonon dispersions are computed under three distinct uniaxial strain directions. Uniaxial tensile strain up to 4.8% along [\bar110] is found to increase the room-temperature electron mobility by 19% while leaving visible-range optical absorption essentially unchanged. These results demonstrate that moderate strain can selectively enhance carrier transport without degrading optical transparency, and establish DFPT+U as an effective framework for predicting strain-dependent transport and optical properties in wide-band-gap oxides with implications for strain-engineered display and optoelectronic applications.

authors.name: Hong-Guk Min, Wooil Yang, Sabyasachi Tiwari, Feliciano Giustino, Young-Woo Son

papers.title: Dual-Mode Exciton Coupling in Epitaxially Registered Organic-Inorganic 2D Heterocrystals
papers.summary: Two-dimensional (2D) heterocrystals comprising molecules and semiconductors can serve as an ideal platform for studying interfacial excitons and for future optoelectronic applications, yet the energy and charge flow across these atomically sharp interfaces remain unclear. In this work, we investigated PTCDA-MoS2 as a prototypical 2D organic-inorganic heterostructure and revealed dual-mode exciton coupling between the constituent crystals. Monolayer-resolved PTCDA molecular crystals were grown on monolayer MoS2 via physical vapor assembly, and their crystallographic details, including the stacking angle, were determined by electron diffraction. Upon the formation of the heterostructures, PTCDA's photoluminescence was completely quenched because of organic-to-inorganic hole transfer, whereas that of MoS2 increased markedly with PTCDA thickness. Using differential reflectance and photoluminescence excitation spectroscopy, we found that the enhancement arises from two distinct mechanisms. Ground-state charge transfer injects holes into MoS2, which suppresses negative trion formation and enhances the radiative recombination of neutral excitons. In addition, resonant energy transfer, enabled by spectral overlap between PTCDA and MoS2, diverts excitation energy from PTCDA to MoS2. Our findings reconcile previously proposed mechanisms and establish a unified framework in which charge and energy transfer cooperate to govern exciton coupling at organic-inorganic interfaces.

authors.name: Eunbeen Jeon, Kihyun Lee, Jieun Yeon, Juseung Oh, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kwanpyo Kim, Sunmin Ryu

papers.title: Emergence and Detection of Surface altermagnetism in KV$_2$Se$_2$O
papers.summary: We demonstrate the recent concept of emergent surface altermagnetism through its unique signatures in KV$_2$Se$_2$O. We show that for bulk antiferromagnetically ordered KV$_2$Se$_2$O, the (001) surface exhibits $d$-wave altermagnetism. Our results fully explain the recent seemingly contradicgting experimental evidence, independently showing both an antiferromagnetically ordered bulk from neutron diffraction, and $d$-wave spin splitting from photoemission spectroscopy. To fully verify this conecept, we predict, as a key experimental signature, a large nonlinear Edelstein response, which is localized at the surface, and follows the $d$-wave altermagnetic symmetry. These results are not only relevant for the metallic and room-temperature magnet KV$_2$Se$_2$O, but also for several other Lieb lattice systems. Our work expands the pool of techniques that can be used to detect altermagnetism emerging at the surfaces of antiferromagnets.

authors.name: Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Colin Lange, Sergio Rodr\'iguez Fern\'andez, Atasi Chakraborty, Alexander Mook, Jairo Sinova

papers.title: Boundary-layer analysis of the partial engulfment of a small particle by a lipid membrane
papers.summary: We study the axisymmetric partial engulfment of a small rigid sphere by a fluid Helfrich membrane. The neck that joins the wrapped cap to the membrane is an elastic boundary layer, which we analyse by matched asymptotic expansions. Its leading surface is a catenoid, which stores no bending energy and is obtained from the equilibrium equations for a regular inner expansion. Beyond the term linear in the size ratio, known from the literature, the energy contains a term proportional to the logarithm of the size ratio. Its coefficient is the effective lateral tension acting on the logarithmic excess area of the catenoid, and it depends on how the membrane is closed far from the particle. For a membrane in contact with a tension reservoir we obtain the wrapping energy to second order in the size ratio, in closed form at every wrapping angle. The resulting landscape contains as limits the low-tension regime and the local landscape of the wrapping problem previously derived in the literature, and describes the crossover between them. The landscape recovers the known binding threshold of a flat membrane, independent of tension and spontaneous curvature, and the bistability of the partially and fully wrapped states is controlled mainly by the spontaneous curvature. The order of the remainder is estimated, and the neck energy is checked against numerical solutions of the full nonlinear shape equations.

authors.name: Gaetano Napoli

papers.title: Quetzalcoatlite as a Disorder-Free Platform for Chiral Magnetism and Frustration
papers.summary: The natural mineral quetzalcoatlite Zn$_6$Cu$_3$(TeO$_6$)$_2$(OH)$_6$ $\cdot$ (Ag$_x$Pb$_y$Cl$_{x+2y}$) is a structurally ideal kagome magnet, providing a platform for exploring the interplay of geometric frustration, chirality, and tunability in a disorder-free framework. Here, we present the (first) comprehensive ab initio study of its electronic and magnetic properties. The electronic structure is dominated by localized half-filled Cu $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals that become insulating through electronic correlations. Mapping the low-energy physics onto a Heisenberg model reveals that the magnetism is governed primarily by two exchange interactions: a nearest-neighbor intralayer kagome coupling and a next-nearest-neighbor interlayer coupling. Their competition stabilizes an unconventional three-dimensional chiral magnetic state. Each kagome layer hosts a $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order, while adjacent layers are rotated by $60^\circ$, producing a right-handed spiral along the crystallographic $c$-axis. This intrinsic chiral order emerges naturally from the crystal structure and magnetic interactions, establishing quetzalcoatlite as a distinctive realization of chiral magnetism on a perfect kagome lattice. At the same time, the small energy scale of the exchange interactions places the material close to competing magnetic regimes, suggesting that moderate pressure, chemical substitution, or structural modifications may strongly enhance frustration, suppress long-range order, and potentially drive the system toward a quantum spin-liquid state.

authors.name: Aleksandar Razpopov, P. Peter Stavropoulos, Felix Flicker, Michael R. Norman, Roser Valent\'i

papers.title: Electrically Switchable Spintronics in a Multiferroic Altermagnet
papers.summary: We introduce a minimal model of a two-dimensional lattice that, upon spontaneous symmetry breaking, simultaneously develops altermagnetic order, a finite electric polarization, and a spin-polarized transport response, all of which are controlled by an external electric field. By coupling a dimerized altermagnet to an external electric field, we show that the three order parameters are not merely compatible but dynamically entangled, so that switching one (for instance, reversing the polarization with an electric field) necessarily reconfigures the other two. We show that this model offers a clear physical blueprint for designing next-generation spintronic logic and pure spin current memdevices that merge the ultrafast, stray-field-free advantages of compensated magnets with the low-power switching architectures of ferroelectrics.

authors.name: Martin Latorre (Departamento de F\'isica, CEDENNA, FCFM, Universidad de Chile, Santiago, Chile), Sebastian Allende (Departamento de F\'isica, CEDENNA, Universidad de Santiago de Chile, Santiago, Chile), Alvaro S. Nunez (Departamento de F\'isica, CEDENNA, FCFM, Universidad de Chile, Santiago, Chile)

papers.title: Josephson effect in bipolar magnetic semiconductors
papers.summary: We theoretically investigate equilibrium currents in a one-dimensional Josephson junction incorporating a bipolar magnetic semiconductor (BMS). We show that the intrinsic exchange splitting of the spin-resolved bands enables purely electrical control of the $0$--$\pi$ transition through gate-tunable modulation of the BMS chemical potential, eliminating the need for an external magnetic field. This provides a viable route toward electrically tunable $\pi$-junction behavior and highlights the potential of BMS-based Josephson devices for phase-controllable superconducting electronics. Furthermore, in the presence of Rashba spin--orbit coupling, we find an anomalous Josephson effect characterized by a finite equilibrium supercurrent at zero phase difference. This behavior originates from the intrinsic breaking of time-reversal symmetry associated with the spin-polarized electronic structure of the BMS. Interestingly, despite the simultaneous breaking of time-reversal and inversion symmetries---conditions often associated with nonreciprocal superconducting transport---we do not observe a Josephson diode effect. Our results therefore highlight an important distinction between anomalous Josephson transport and superconducting nonreciprocity: the former does not necessarily imply a finite critical-current asymmetry between opposite current directions.

authors.name: Polireddi Naveen, Abhiram Soori

papers.title: Gauge invariance, collective modes, and the justification of normal-state subtraction in Dirac superconductors
papers.summary: In Dirac superconductors, the unbounded spectrum of low-energy Dirac models is known to give rise to unphysical interband contributions from deep-lying states to the electromagnetic response. To eliminate these contributions, normal-state subtraction (NSS), in which the normal-state response is subtracted from the superconducting-state response, has been widely employed. However, the relation between NSS and a gauge-invariant electromagnetic response, particularly the role of the vertex correction required by the Ward identity, has remained unclear. In this work, we consider a massive-Dirac model with $s$-wave pairing and analytically investigate the electromagnetic response at zero temperature by solving the Bethe--Salpeter equation and incorporating the collective-mode contribution to the electromagnetic vertex. We show that, in the static long-wavelength limit, the vertex correction exactly cancels the bare longitudinal response with NSS, yielding the vanishing longitudinal response required by gauge invariance. In contrast, the transverse component of the vertex correction vanishes in the long-wavelength limit, so that the gauge-invariant Meissner weight coincides with that obtained from the bare transverse response with NSS. Moreover, within the class of isotropic and analytic UV regularization terms, we show that gauge invariance uniquely fixes the regularization term in the static long-wavelength limit to the value prescribed by NSS. Our results thus provide a microscopic justification for NSS.

authors.name: Hiroshi Hayasaka

papers.title: Heterogeneous planar diffusion with axisymmetric power-law decaying diffusion coefficient under stochastic resetting
papers.summary: We analyse two-dimensional isotropic heterogeneous diffusion with a radially decaying diffusion coefficient $D(\rho)=D_0/\rho^2$, subject to Poissonian stochastic resetting to the origin. Since multiplicative noise makes the process interpretation-dependent, we treat the It\^o, Stratonovich, and H\"anggi--Klimontovich prescriptions within a single approach. For each, we obtain the exact probability density function, the non-equilibrium stationary state induced by resetting, the mean squared displacement, and the first-passage properties. The non-equilibrium stationary state is governed by modified Bessel functions and departs from the Laplace form found for homogeneous diffusion under resetting, while the mean squared displacement saturates at long times as $\langle\rho^2\rangle\sim\bar{r}^{-1/2}$, $\bar{r}$ being the resetting rate. The mean first-passage time to an absorbing boundary exhibits an optimal resetting rate at which it is minimised. In addition, we incorporate memory effects through a subordination (continuous-time random walk) approach with a power-law kernel, deriving the fractional Fokker--Planck equation together with the non-equilibrium stationary state, the mean squared displacement expressed via the three-parameter Mittag-Leffler function, and the first-passage statistics; the optimal resetting rate increases as the memory exponent decreases.

authors.name: Trifce Sandev, Sebastien Fumeron, Malte Henkel, Ervin K. Lenzif

papers.title: Assessing the Transferability of General-Purpose MachineLearning Interatomic Potentials for Heterogeneous Catalysis with HetCat26
papers.summary: Foundation machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) promise near-density functional theory (DFT) accuracy across broad areas of chemistry and materials science. However, their performance in describing systems and processes relevant to heterogeneous catalysis remains underexplored. Here, we introduce HetCat26, a collection of benchmark tests designed to assess pre-trained MLIPs across key aspects of catalytic modeling, including surface energetics, metal-metal oxide interactions, adsorption, and catalytic reaction networks. Evaluating eighteen foundation models, we find that performance on existing general materials benchmarks is only weakly predictive of performance on HetCat26; transferability to heterogeneous catalysis cannot be inferred from these general benchmarks. Across the benchmark tests, current models describe surface energetics and, perhaps surprisingly, reaction barriers well, whereas larger errors are observed for adsorption, and DFT site preferences are often not reproduced. Three models, eSEN-30M-OAM, SevenNet-Omni-i12 and MACE-MH-1-OMAT, nevertheless achieve high accuracy across the properties evaluated. Beyond model benchmarking, HetCat26 highlights the importance of training data consistency: PBE and PBE+U calculations should not be mixed within a training set. Overall, we identify challenges limiting the transferability of current foundation MLIPs to heterogeneous catalysis and, more broadly, to chemical reactions at interfaces, providing guidance for the development of the next generation of foundation models.

authors.name: Alexandre Peuch, Angus Whiteside, Giaan Kler-Young, Kaifeng Niu, Jinwoo Hwang, Manos Mavrikakis, Angelos Michaelides, Fabian Berger

papers.title: Spontaneous breaking of continuous scale invariance and Efimovian-like dynamics in a driven-dissipative system
papers.summary: The Efimov effect manifests discrete scale invariance through a geometric series of three-body bound states. Analogous discrete scale symmetry has been observed in the Efimovian expansion of scale-invariant strongly interacting Fermi gases. However, it is unclear whether strong correlation is necessary. Here we investigate the spontaneous breaking of continuous scale invariance in a driven-dissipative two-level system whose driving and dissipation parameters scale as \(1/t\). By transforming to logarithmic time, we show that the evolution is governed by a non-Hermitian superoperator whose spectral decomposition reveals the emergence of a pair of eigenmodes with opposite real parts and equal imaginary parts. This signals the spontaneous breaking of continuous scale invariance and gives rise to Efimovian-like oscillations: log-periodic decay oscillations obeying discrete scaling laws. The onset of oscillations coincides with a PT-like-symmetry breaking transition in logarithmic time. Our work implies that the spontaneous breaking of continuous temporal scale symmetry and the emergence of Efimovian-like dynamics can be observed in a minimal driven-dissipative system without requiring strong correlations.

authors.name: Zehui Wu, Jian Yu, Jian-Song Pan

papers.title: Replica Fragmentation and Glassy Dynamics in Parity Learning
papers.summary: We study how independently trained Transformer neural networks reconstruct a binary string from its local domain walls. Runs sharing the data and training protocol can realize different functions. We treat them as replicas and measure truth alignment $m$, prediction confidence $q_{\mathrm{self}}$, and cross-replica agreement $q_{\mathrm{cross}}$. Confident disagreement defines the finite-size replica fragmentation that we call glass-like. With small training sets, replicas predict all training examples correctly but remain confident in incorrect predictions for unseen inputs, a regime we call memorization. With larger sets, runs can generalize and then retreat. Retreat occurs when outputs start to deviate from truth while confidence remains high. The frontier between learned and unlearned outputs recedes toward shorter strings. Many later recover as the frontier advances again. The self--cross gap $q_{\mathrm{self}}-q_{\mathrm{cross}}$ clearly distinguishes the three learning regimes of memorization, retreat, and recovery. With overall and position-dependent truth alignment subtracted, their residual correlations also differ: memorizing replicas have weakly and uniformly correlated residuals, while retreat has the largest fraction of replica pairs whose residuals are anti-correlated. That is, on the inputs where one replica of such a pair does better than its average, the other tends to do worse. These finite-size observations distinguish persistent memorization from ongoing retreat--recovery dynamics. The thermodynamic and long-time limits, and extensions to other learning tasks, remain open.

authors.name: Han Ma

papers.title: Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations
papers.summary: Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs. Unlike approaches based primarily on phenomenological leakage models, our first-principles, multi-terminal quantum-transport framework treats the source, drain, and gate as current-carrying quantum-mechanical contacts and resolves the local current density throughout the device. The spatially resolved current density shows that gate-injected carriers tunnel through the high-$k$ dielectric preferentially near the drain side of the gate, where the dielectric barrier is most strongly lowered by the drain bias, and are collected by the drain. This provides a direct real-space picture of the DIDBL-driven gate-drain leakage mechanism.

authors.name: Denis Mamaluy, Juan P. Mendez, Coleman Cariker, Michael Titze, Alex A. Belianinov

papers.title: Foresight-dependent entropy production in stochastic two-agent dynamics
papers.summary: Nonreciprocal interactions can break detailed balance by sustaining stationary probability currents. We ask whether such currents can also emerge when agents' immediate coordination preferences are reciprocal but their adjustment rules result from forward-looking optimization. We study a minimal stochastic linear--quadratic game in which two agents control noisy scalar states and minimize individual discounted costs in a full-information feedback Nash equilibrium. The optimized controls yield an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process whose stationary current, entropy production, and inter-agent information flow follow exactly from the Nash feedback. For reciprocal coordination with unequal self-anchoring, the drift asymmetry first appears at order $\tau^5$, where $\tau$ is the planning timescale, and the normalized entropy production scales as $\tau^8$. We trace this delay to one mechanism: the asymmetry is set by the mismatch between the agents' value-function curvatures along the coordinate each does not control. At leading order this equals the mismatch of the corresponding cost curvatures, which instantaneous incentives cannot see and which the coordination cost fixes to zero; unequal persistence of the partners' fluctuations generates a value-function mismatch at order $\tau^3$, postponing the asymmetry to fifth order, while a direct stake in the partner's state restores a cubic law. The normalized information flow, of order $\tau^4$, identifies the weakly anchored agent as the one that tracks its partner. For conformist--contrarian coupling, normalized entropy production starts from a nonzero limit and initially decreases as $\tau^2$; for equal anchoring, we prove that its long-foresight limit lies below the short-foresight value and that the stationary mutual-information flow vanishes. Numerical solutions of the full Nash equations confirm these laws.

authors.name: Arpan Dey

papers.title: Dopant depth determination from momentum-resolved core-loss 4D-STEM data
papers.summary: Moving beyond specimen-projected micrographs in scanning transmission electron microscopy to determine a three-dimensional distribution of dopants is of vital importance for materials characterization and development. Within the Born approximation, Fourier transformation over probe position of a momentum-resolved core-loss 4D-STEM dataset reveals fringes whose frequency encodes the dopant's distance from the focal plane. We address two principal challenges which arise under experimental circumstances. First, fringe contrast is degraded by dynamical scattering, but can be partially recovered by acquiring off major zone axes. Second, the excessive doses typical of core-loss scattering can be alleviated using a Bayesian framework which, on a simulated Fe-doped strontium titanate, achieves nanometre to sub-nanometre depth precision from 100 to 1000 core-loss counts, depending on the signal-to-background.

authors.name: Michael Deimetry

papers.title: Wegner model in high dimension: singular continuous spectrum from U(1) symmetry breaking and AAT self-consistency
papers.summary: We analyze the energy-spectral decomposition of the Wegner one-orbital model in high lattice dimension using ideas from field theory and statistical mechanics. Most notably, we identify a local spectral measure of singular continuous type for the disordered model at the Anderson transition. The key mechanism that leads to a singular continuous spectrum is a novel scenario of spontaneous symmetry breaking, intimately connected to the non-compactness of the global symmetry group of the field theory. While that symmetry breaks down to a compact subgroup in the metallic phase, it spontaneously breaks down to a nilpotent subgroup at criticality. We describe the symmetry-breaking extremal states approximately, by applying the self-consistent theory of localization due to Abou-Chacra, Anderson, and Thouless. The thrust of our work is to provide a field-theoretical foundation for disorder phenomena associated with singular continuous spectra.

authors.name: Julian Arenz, Martin R. Zirnbauer

papers.title: Euler Topological Metals in 1D
papers.summary: We give a rigorous one-dimensional formulation of Kane's transport proposal for probing the Euler characteristic of a Fermi sea. For a clean, translation-invariant continuum Hamiltonian with real-analytic dispersion, a Fermi sea confined to a finite momentum range, and nonzero Fermi velocity at every Fermi point, we analyze a particular regularized transport response (obtained by tracing over the Fermi sea) and prove that its large-time limit equals the Euler characteristic. We derive an explicit finite-time formula, show that quantization requires the large-time limit, and obtain a convergence rate under additional nonstationarity assumptions. We also prove the lattice analog, where the commutator of the spatial switch with its time evolution is trace-class and a completely filled band contributes zero. Finite-volume calculations illustrate the prescribed order of the thermodynamic and large-time limits.

authors.name: Yichen Hu, Jacob Shapiro

papers.title: Adaptive Filtering With Reduced Computational Complexity Using SOPOT Arithmetic
papers.summary: Implementing finite impulse response (FIR) adaptive filters by employing the sums of signed-powers-of-two (SOPOT) arithmetic may lead to simpler hardware and consequently reduced power consumption. In this paper, one evaluates the effects of SOPOT arithmetic on the adaptive filter's recursion algorithms. The filters' coefficients and algorithms' underlying variables are fully operated using SOPOT arithmetic in the whole iterative process. More specifically, one evaluates convergence rate, numerical stability, and accuracy since using few signed-powers-of-two (SPT) terms propagates numerical errors during the adaptive cycle that may impair the algorithm behavior. The SOPOT approximations are obtained through the technique known as Matching Pursuits with Generalized Bit-Plane (MPGBP) algorithm, with notable cost-performance trade-off and low computational complexity. Results are provided for the Least-Mean-Squares (LMS), the Normalized Least-Mean-Squares (NLMS) and the Recursive-Least-Squares (RLS) algorithms, considering adaptive filters employed for system identification and change detection.

authors.name: Luiz F. da S. Coelho, Lisandro Lovisolo, Michel P. Tcheou

papers.title: Asymmetric Transistor Aging Under Thermal Gradients
papers.summary: Advanced technology nodes improve performance but increase susceptibility to BTI-induced aging. Using aging- aware circuit simulations, we show that realistic on-chip thermal gradients can cause significant asymmetric transistor degradation in 16 nm FinFET circuits, leading to setup and hold time violations. These results highlight the necessity of incorporating thermal-gradient-aware aging analysis into timing signoff to ensure chip reliability.

authors.name: Alex Grinshpun, Firas Ramadan, Freddy Gabbay

papers.title: An {\alpha}-potential linear approximation for LQ differential games
papers.summary: Feedback Nash equilibria of infinite-horizon linear-quadratic (LQ) differential games are characterized by coupled algebraic Riccati equations (cAREs), whose numerical solution generally relies on iterative algorithms and can be highly sensitive to their initialization. Motivated by the $\alpha$-potential-game framework, this letter proposes an $\alpha$-potential linear approximation for constructing a systematic, game-dependent initialization. For an N-player LQ game, a reference potential game is constructed. Its equilibrium requires solving only one standard algebraic Riccati equation. The original cAREs are subsequently linearized around this reference solution, yielding a coupled linear system whose solution provides player-specific corrections and hence an approximate feedback Nash equilibrium. The resulting approximation is used to initialize three standard cARE solvers. Numerical experiments on $10^4$ randomly generated two-player games show that the proposed initialization reduces the mean number of iterations. Further experiments for $N=2,\ldots,13$ show that the reduction in iteration count persists as the number of players increases.

authors.name: Balint Varga, Gergely Lorant Kiss, Andreas Schwung

papers.title: Reliability-based Sizing of Energy Storage for Large Load Integration
papers.summary: The number of large loads connected to the bulk power system has been increasing rapidly worldwide. Emerging high-demand facilities, particularly AI data centers, are introducing new challenges for power system planners. In absence of appropriate planning mechanisms, the addition of high volumes of data center loads will lead to an increase in outages, thus degrading reliability of the system. Energy storage systems (ESS) offer a promising solution to mitigate the reliability impacts of these large loads, due to their flexibility and fast-ramping characteristics. However, ESS should be judiciously sized and sited to maximize the reliability benefits to the grid. This paper presents a framework for the optimal sizing and siting of ESS to minimize the adverse reliability impacts of large load additions. First, a stochastic semi-Markov model is developed to model the load of AI data centers and generate profiles for several such facilities. These profiles are then incorporated into a Markov-chain Monte Carlo simulation-based composite system reliability assessment framework. A detailed nodal network model is used to quantify the reliability impacts of adding data centers and to identify buses most affected by large loads. Resource adequacy metrics are used to evaluate the overall system reliability impacts. ESS are then strategically sized and sited based on this analysis to mitigate the negative impacts of large loads on overall system reliability. The proposed framework is demonstrated using the RTS-GMLC 72-bus test system. The results show how ESS can effectively enhance system reliability in the presence of rapidly growing large-load demand. This framework provides system planners, utilities, and regulators with a practical tool for maintaining reliable power system operation using energy storage as more large loads are integrated into the grid.

authors.name: Atri Bera, Chandan Chaudhary, Dilip Pandit, Cody J. Newlun, Tu A. Nguyen, Raymond H. Byrne, Joydeep Mitra

papers.title: Stochastic Crew Placement for Winter Storm Restoration of Rural Distribution Feeders Considering Building Cooling Deadlines
papers.summary: Winter storm outages on rural distribution feeders may leave electrically heated houses cooling below acceptable indoor temperatures. This paper proposes a two-stage stochastic mixed-integer linear program for pre-storm crew placement that considers the building cooling deadline. Crews are placed before the storm, and repairs and reconnection are scheduled in each damage scenario to minimize the expected cost. Specifically, outage house-hours beyond the deadline are penalized, and feeder voltage and loading constraints account for cold load pickup at each reconnection. A case study on a synthetic rural feeder shows that the penalty shifts one of two crews toward a remote village, reducing expected house-hours beyond the deadline by 39 percent for 5.3 percent more outage house-hours. With three crews, the penalty does not change crew placement. Immediate reconnection would violate the voltage limit in four of six scenarios.

authors.name: Rajkumar Silwal, Shambhu Marasini, Bo Tu

papers.title: AE-DISC: Automorphism Ensemble Direct-Invocation Successive Cancellation for Low-Latency Decoding
papers.summary: Emerging applications in hyper-reliable low-latency communication (HRLLC) demand channel decoders that deliver deterministic performance under stringent latency and reliability constraints. While Polar codes are well suited for this scenario due to their strong error-correction capability, conventional successive cancellation (SC) decoding exhibits inherent serial dependencies that lead to high decoding latency. This paper presents the automorphism ensemble direct-invocation successive cancellation (AE-DISC) decoder, a low-latency framework that enables the concurrent computation of the left and right decoding subtrees in the SC process, yielding substantial speed-ups. By exploiting permutation automorphisms, AE-DISC decoding further improves error-correction performance. Simulation results demonstrate that AE-DISC attains up to 1.4 dB gain over the 5G SC baseline and surpasses layered min-sum (LMS) low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoders at a frame error rate (FER) of $10^{-6}$, while maintaining fixed algorithmic complexity. Both theoretical analysis and application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) synthesis results further show up to 2 times decoding speed-up relative to fast simplified successive cancellation (FSSC).

authors.name: Sihui Shen, Ryan Seah, Marvin R\"ubenacke, Warren J. Gross

papers.title: Conditional-Hierarchical Open-Set Deep Learning for Robust Radio Signals Intelligence
papers.summary: This paper proposes an open-set radio-frequency (RF) deep learning (DL) framework that jointly performs conditionally hierarchical multi-level radio signal classification and out-of-distribution (OOD) detection. To exploit image-based classification models, the raw radio samples are transformed into time-frequency representations using the short time Fourier transform (STFT) to pre-process the radio signals. A lightweight novel architecture using neural network (CNN), that applies con- ditional hierarchical multi-task classification heads, is introduced, and compared to two baselines including: (1) The conventional convolutional neural network (CNN) and (2) Swin-T model with multitask classification heads, where the model accuracy and complexity perspectives are considered for the comparison. Moreover, to address open-set scenarios, we introduce the fusion of two OOD detectors each of which is fitted to a Gaussian mixture model by using the learned feature space (e.g. the feature embeddings and logits) from the multi-head classifica- tion network. The overall training process is achieved on two stages following a post-hoc design: the in-set classification neural network is trained first, then the learnable parameters are frozen in the evaluation mode to process the training dataset again to aggregate the embeddings and logits used to fit the GMMs for OOD detection. Moreover, a proof of concept using experimental setup is implemented to validate the operation of the introduced models and algorithms in practical scenarios. The simulation- based trained model is fine-tuned using experimentally measured radio signals. For the experimental setup, a USRP-B210 acting as a transmitter, and an edge Deepwave Air-T software-defined radio, which is equipped with the fine-tuned neural networks is used as a detector or receiver.

authors.name: Mohammad Aljarrah, Emad Alsusa

papers.title: Data-driven Linearization of Operational Dynamics of Soft Open Points in Power Distribution Networks
papers.summary: This paper proposes a novel data-driven linearization of operational power losses in a Soft Open Point (SOP). The proposed learning-based representation, combined with the standard segmentation of the quadratic device capacity inequalities, linearizes the operational dynamics of SOPs in unbalanced power distribution network applications without a significant drop in power loss estimation accuracy. The technique was tested in three applications using a three-phase extension of the IEEE 33-bus network. The case studies include a sizing application for a multi-terminal phase-changing soft open point (PCSOP), an operational optimization application for an active distribution network featuring a PCSOP, and a system simulation engine built for a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) application that trains an agent to optimally dispatch a PCSOP in an unbalanced distribution network. The results of the three case studies were validated against the standard nonlinear AC load-flow representations and point to the efficacy of the proposed solution.

authors.name: Shoaib Hussain, Mostafa Farrokhabadi, Hamidreza Zareipour

papers.title: The Prediction-to-Decision Gap: First-Action Informativity in Data-Driven Predictive Control
papers.summary: Model predictive control (MPC) applies only the first input of an optimized sequence before replanning. Do the available data determine this input? We define first-action informativity as agreement across data-compatible models at a fixed history and reference, with common MPC settings. For autoregressive models with exogenous inputs (ARX) and unconstrained quadratic MPC, we show that first-action agreement and prediction agreement under a fixed input sequence do not imply one another. We give structural conditions for action agreement without requiring unique model identification. When actions disagree, we quantify their mean-squared deviation from the fitted model's input under a specific parameter distribution. We approximate this measure using local sensitivities and parameter covariance. Analytical and numerical examples illustrate how model uncertainty affects predictions and actions differently. The framework evaluates model uncertainty through its effect on the first action MPC is about to apply.

authors.name: Aihui Liu, Magnus Jansson

papers.title: Data-Driven Hamiltonian Under Parametric Uncertainty
papers.summary: Hamilton--Jacobi (HJ) reachability computes the states from which a system can be kept out of an unsafe region, but it requires knowledge of dynamics. The data-driven Hamiltonian (DDH), under a black-box dynamics setting, lower bounds the Hamiltonian directly from trajectory data, which produces a guaranteed conservative safe set. However, it needs a Lipschitz constant of the dynamics, and its bound loosens with the distance from the data. We consider dynamics that are linear in unknown parameters through a known feature vector, with a Gaussian prior on the parameters, and use this structure to construct a parametric DDH. From a few short trajectories with noisy velocity measurements, the parametric DDH lower-bounds the Hamiltonian at all states and costates with a probability of at least $1-\delta$. The safe set obtained by replacing the Hamiltonian with this bound is then contained in the true safe set with the same probability. For control-affine systems, evaluating the bound amounts to a second-order cone program, so it can be solved efficiently within existing grid-based and neural PDE solvers. We demonstrate the approach on a two-state system and a six-state lunar lander.

authors.name: Zach Liu, Namhoon Cho, Jason J. Choi

papers.title: WiFo-D: Wireless Foundation Model Based on Discrete Representations
papers.summary: Wireless foundation models have shown strong generalization capabilities across heterogeneous wireless tasks and configurations. However, most existing models rely on continuous representations, limiting ultra-low-overhead channel state information (CSI) feedback, few-shot generalization, and robustness to noise. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a wireless foundation model based on discrete representations (WiFo-D), which learns multi-granularity discrete CSI representations. It comprises a CSI encoder, multi-codebook vector quantization, and a modulation-based decoder, with the learned token maps and quantized features supporting multi-rate CSI feedback, CSI reconstruction, and diverse CSI-related downstream tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate strong CSI feedback performance at an ultra-low latent compression ratio of 1/32 with 3 bits per token, reducing normalized mean square error (NMSE) by more than 4.7 dB compared with the strongest baseline. Furthermore, for frequency-domain prediction with limited training samples, WiFo-D improves generalization and noise robustness over continuous-representation-based methods. The results also demonstrate its superiority across downstream tasks, including beam prediction, wireless localization, and line-of-sight/non-line-of-sight identification.

authors.name: Xinyu Pan, Boxun Liu, Chen Chen, Xiang Cheng

papers.title: 20 ghz longitudinal surface acoustic wave resonators in 100-nm x-cut lithium niobate on silicon carbide
papers.summary: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators above 15~GHz require a fast acoustic mode that retains strong electromechanical coupling ($k^2$). This work reports longitudinal SAW (L-SAW) resonators designed for high $k^2$ in 100-nm X-cut lithium niobate (LN) on 4H silicon carbide (SiC), operating up to 21.7~GHz and reaching a $k^2$ of 8.1\%, a maximum Bode $Q$ of 70, and a figure of merit (FoM) of 5.7 at 20.24~GHz. In this thin-film waveguide, shrinking the wavelength ($\lambda$) keeps the normalized LN thickness ($h_\mathrm{LN}/\lambda$) large, sustaining both $k^2$ and acoustic confinement. Conversely, increasing $\lambda$ from 292 to 471~nm lowers $h_\mathrm{LN}/\lambda$ from 0.34 to 0.21 and raises the L-SAW phase velocity from 6.32 to 7.05~km/s, within 1.1\% of the 7126-m/s shear-wave velocity of 4H-SiC. As the velocity approaches this limit, more of the acoustic energy spreads into the non-piezoelectric SiC, and $k^2$ falls from its 8.1\% peak at $\lambda = 322$~nm to 1.7\% at $\lambda = 471$~nm. No L-SAW resonance is observed for $\lambda \geq 518$~nm ($h_\mathrm{LN}/\lambda \leq 0.19$), where the mode becomes leaky. Overall, the FoM stays within 5\% of its maximum for $h_\mathrm{LN}/\lambda$ between 0.26 to 0.31, defining a design window for L-SAW resonators in thin LN on SiC at K-band and beyond.

authors.name: Jiajun Huang, Ziqian Yao, Tzu-Hsuan Hsu, Ian Anderson, Joshua Campbell, Ruochen Lu

papers.title: Cone-Constrained Safe Policy Learning With Finite-Step Improvement Guarantees
papers.summary: One central challenge in safe reinforcement learning is improving task performance while reducing infeasibility risk, especially when long-term constraint consequences are difficult to represent and optimize. We propose the Constraint Aggregation Function (CAF), a learnable feasibility-oriented representation of long-horizon risk that satisfies a discounted Bellman recursion and admits a unique fixed point. The proposed CAF induces a risk advantage that measures the reduction in predicted unsafety relative to the current policy. Building on this representation, we develop Cone-Constrained Policy Optimization (CCPO), which uses the CAF-induced risk advantage to define a risk descent direction. The proposed CCPO resolves conflicts between task ascent and risk descent through gradient projection, selecting the final update from the relative interior of a constructed safety cone. Under standard smoothness assumptions and a step-size bound, this update guarantees simultaneous task improvement and risk reduction. Numerically, CCPO stays feasible with a 1.05% mean optimality gap in emergency braking and attains low constraint violations on safety-critical benchmarks.

authors.name: Liangliang Hao, Wei Liu, Yunjian Xu

papers.title: DeoPC: Data-Enabled Output-Feedback Predictive Control for State Regulation
papers.summary: Constrained regulation of the internal state of an unknown linear system is challenging when only input-output measurements are available online. In this work, we develop a data-enabled output-feedback predictive control (DeoPC) framework for constrained state regulation using input-output data. Specifically, a data-driven state estimate is constructed from past input-output data via a subspace-based singular value decomposition. Based on this state representation, we formulate a predictive controller that directly penalizes the state and control effort while enforcing the system constraints. Under persistent excitation and initialization conditions, we establish recursive feasibility and closed-loop stability of DeoPC in both noise-free and bounded-noise settings. In addition, we show that DeoPC can be calibrated to the physical state coordinates using a few offline state measurements, or treated as a model predictive control tuning problem when no state measurements are available. The effectiveness of DeoPC is demonstrated through simulations on an unstable batch reactor system.

authors.name: Jingyuan Li, Dawei Shi, Ling Shi

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Deep Learning for Prediction of Radiation-Induced Xerostomia in Head and Neck Cancer
papers.summary: To develop and evaluate an uncertainty-aware multimodal learning framework for predicting radiation-induced xerostomia in patients receiving head-and-neck cancer radiotherapy. We developed a Bidirectional Attention-enhanced Diffusion Transformer (BA-DiT) that combines self-supervised multimodal representation learning with supervised Bayesian fine-tuning. The model integrates pretreatment CT images and three-dimensional dose distributions, focusing on bilateral parotid glands while incorporating surrounding anatomical and dosimetric information. During pretraining, bidirectional cross-attention integrates anatomical and dosimetric features, while a latent Diffusion Transformer learns joint representations through diffusion-based learning, feature reconstruction, and contrastive alignment. Supervised fine-tuning employs a Bayesian classifier to predict individualized xerostomia risk and quantify predictive uncertainty, with a learnable label-transition model accounting for potential toxicity label uncertainty. BA-DiT was developed using four independent cohorts (Moffitt, Emory, MSHS, and TCIA) and evaluated against baseline and ablation models. Evaluation included predictive performance, calibration, uncertainty quantification, decision curve analysis, and patient-level case studies. In independent MSHS and Emory cohorts, BA-DiT achieved AUCs of 0.83 and 0.80, respectively, outperforming baseline models. Predictive uncertainty peaked near the decision boundary, with aleatoric uncertainty being the predominant component. Uncertainty-based selective prediction generally improved net benefit among retained patients, with greater gains at lower prediction coverage. BA-DiT enables individualized xerostomia risk prediction while providing complementary uncertainty estimates, potentially supporting informed clinical decision-making and personalized toxicity management.

authors.name: Jin Yang, Tian Liu, Jose Penagaricano, Jing Wang, Erin L. Moshier, Jerry Liu, Richard Bakst, Ming Chao

papers.title: Motion-Sickness-Aware Vehicle Control via DKUC-Based Inverse Design and Iterative Feedback Tuning
papers.summary: Tuning existing vehicle controllers for motion-sickness reduction requires a desired vehicle response that reflects physiological comfort. The six-degree-of-freedom subjective vertical conflict (6DoF-SVC) model can evaluate sensory conflict induced by vehicle motion, but it does not directly provide a target motion for controller design. This paper proposes a 2-step framework to construct such a reference. First, a target SVC trajectory is generated from the baseline response by limiting conflict peaks while imposing a minimum activity level. Second, a lifted linear model identified using Deep KoopmanU with Control (DKUC) is inverted to map the target SVC trajectory to a regularized reference expressed in vehicle-acceleration and angular-velocity coordinates. The resulting motion reference is then used in an Iterative Feedback Tuning (IFT)-style procedure for fixed-structure PI and LQR controllers. In the considered simulation scenario, the selected SVC target reduces the sequence norm by 6.95\% relative to the baseline. Controller tuning with reduced response models decreases the regularized PI and LQR objectives by 49.5\% and 32.3\%, respectively. These results show that a nonlinear physiological comfort objective can be converted into a practical motion reference for tuning fixed-structure vehicle controllers.

authors.name: Uta Kawakami, Kenji Sawada

papers.title: Distributed Regenerative Resource Allocation with Exact Centralized Optimality
papers.summary: This letter presents a Distributed Regenerative Resource Allocation (or DRRA) framework for multi-agent networks with utility-driven resource regeneration, in which the resource available for the next allocation round depends endogenously on the utility generated by the agents in the previous allocation. We develop fully distributed, two-stage inner--outer dynamics that perform primal--dual allocation and resource regeneration. Under sufficient distributed algorithmic gain conditions, the inner dynamics exhibit local exponential convergence to a Lyapunov-stable equilibrium. After inner convergence, the DRRA allocation exactly recovers the centralized optimum, and the local resource-reference updates exactly reproduce the centralized resource-regeneration dynamics.

authors.name: Rajul Kumar, Goutam Das, Ningshi Yao

papers.title: Koopman Lifting for Linear Encrypted Control of Nonlinear Systems: Applications to LQR and MPC
papers.summary: Homomorphic encryption enables control computations to be outsourced to a third-party cloud server without disclosing measurements or controller parameters. Applying existing encrypted linear controllers to nonlinear plants requires a compatible representation of the plant dynamics. This paper presents Homomorphically Encrypted Koopman-Based Control (HEK-Control), which connects nonlinear plants to encrypted linear computations through Koopman lifting. A trusted plant-side client evaluates nonlinear functions of the measured state, and a linear predictor identified in these coordinates supports conventional controller design. The resulting control laws retain the server's encrypted linear operations. We demonstrate the framework using state feedback based on linear quadratic regulation and input-constrained model predictive control. Closed-loop simulations with the Cheon--Kim--Kim--Song encryption scheme show close agreement with unencrypted computations. Additional unencrypted simulations compare regulation under input constraints across a common set of controller designs. For a continuous stirred-tank reactor, Koopman lifting supports regulation at input bounds not handled by the tested controllers designed directly in the original state coordinates. Tests of encrypted computations also show that packing multiple values into each ciphertext reduces computation time and communication volume. These results clarify how existing encrypted linear computations can serve nonlinear plants.

authors.name: Uta Kawakami, Kenji Sawada

papers.title: Physics-Guided Multi-Output Surrogate Modeling of a Centralized-UPS Data Center
papers.summary: Data centers supplied through centralized uninterruptible power supplies (UPSs) are converter-dominated loads whose grid response reflects IT demand, power-conversion controls, energy storage, cooling, and site-support dynamics. This paper develops and electrically realizes a causal multi-output surrogate for a nominal 1-MW, 0.48-kV simulated data center. Four physics-informed terminal features-normalized IT demand, positive-sequence voltage deviation, voltage-unbalance ratio, and frequency deviation-are used to predict active and reactive power at both the point of common coupling (PCC) and UPS output. Six causal surrogate families are evaluated using separate training, validation, and held-out trajectories. A ridge-regularized low-order nonlinear autoregressive model with exogenous inputs (NARX) achieves the lowest validation and test errors, with mean four-output errors of 0.1959\% and 0.1441\% on a 1-MVA base, respectively. The selected surrogate is then coupled to a three-phase electrical interface in MATLAB/Simulink, where predicted PCC active power controls a variable resistive load and predicted reactive power is realized through controlled current sources synchronized to the PCC voltage. Across two 41-s AI workload profiles, including an additional pipeline parallelism trajectory, the electrical realization tracks the NARX commands with active- and reactive-power RMSEs of 0.604 kW and 0.353 kVAR for Evaluation Profile A and 1.539 kW and 0.442 kVAR for Evaluation Profile B, respectively. The results demonstrate a compact terminal surrogate that can reproduce both predicted power trajectories and their corresponding three-phase electrical behavior under measured PCC excitation.

authors.name: Jesus D. Vasquez-Plaza, Sunil Subedi, Jin Dong, Joao Pereira Pinto

papers.title: LBW-NPS: A Local Band-Weighted Noise Power Spectrum Loss for Texture-Preserving Low-Dose CT Denoising
papers.summary: Low-dose CT denoising should suppress noise while retaining the local texture of the reference image. Matching a pooled spectrum can overlook regional discrepancies, whereas pixel losses alone can favor overly smooth outputs. We propose a local band-weighted noise power spectrum loss (LBW-NPS) that compares spectral energies within overlapping Hann-tapered patches, without tissue-specific loss conditioning. Each valid patch contributes a weighted squared log-energy difference across three frequency bands, alongside an $L_1$ reconstruction term. We compare LBW-NPS against $L_1$-only training and five auxiliary-loss baselines using the same U-Net and three seeds on DeepLesion slices with simulated low-dose acquisitions, including patch-scale ablations and lung, soft-tissue, and bone evaluations. On 220 test slices from 31 patients, LBW-NPS reduces a local spectral gap related to the loss, on $64\times64$-pixel evaluation windows, by 31.9% relative to pooled band-weighted NPS, without a statistically significant PSNR change. This improvement is supported by lower errors relative to the reference in average NPS frequency and gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) measures not used in the loss, evaluated in homogeneous soft tissue. Local band-power matching therefore improves regional texture agreement without changing the denoising architecture.

authors.name: Fatma Elif Yal\c{c}{\i}nda\u{g}, Mehmet Ozan \"Unal, Metin Erta\c{s}, \.Isa Y{\i}ld{\i}r{\i}m

papers.title: An LLM-Orchestrated Agent Framework for CKM-Assisted Network Deployment Optimization
papers.summary: Channel knowledge maps (CKMs) offer reusable, site-specific radio priors to facilitate environment-aware network planning. However, deploying heterogeneous network nodes to meet diverse performance requirements in complex environments is challenging and requires executable workflows that coordinate scene preparation, candidate-site specification, CKM construction, optimization, and validation. This paper presents a large language model (LLM)-orchestrated agent framework for CKM-assisted network deployment optimization, where an LLM translates high-level requirements into modular, typed, and reproducible planning workflows. In this framework, an LLM layer interprets intent, selects modules, and populates normalized configurations; physics-grounded modules generate scene, CKM, optimization, and validation artifacts; and a deterministic guarded controller performs validation-guided refinement. A common target-candidate-CKM-optimizer interface supports the registration and composition of compatible planning modules, with CKM backends, samplers, and solvers remaining replaceable. We instantiate the proposed framework for base station (BS) deployment, intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) deployment, and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) trajectory planning. An urban-block case study demonstrates automatic scene consistency checks, bounded BS/IRS deployment refinement, and collision- and radio-feasible UAV planning.

authors.name: Yilong Chen, Yuan Guo, Jie Xu

papers.title: UMelCodec: An Ultra-Low-Bitrate and Lightweight Mel-Domain Neural Speech Codec
papers.summary: Ultra-low-bitrate speech coding is crucial for bandwidth-constrained communication and compact storage, but preserving intelligibility, naturalness, and fine-grained acoustic details at bitrates of only a few hundred bps remains challenging. Existing purely acoustic codecs generally operate at relatively high bitrates, whereas incorporating semantic representations can reduce the bitrate, but at the cost of increased complexity. Therefore, we propose UMelCodec, a purely acoustic neural speech codec operating in the mel domain at an ultra-low bitrate of 325 bps with a lightweight architecture. UMelCodec consists of two stages. In the first mel-domain coding stage, alias-free Snake-ConvNeXt (AF-SC) encoder-decoder backbones model temporal and harmonic structures, a factorized single-codebook vector quantizer (VQ) enables ultra-low-bitrate quantization, and a multi-scale mel-spectrogram discriminator (MSMD) improves mel-spectrogram reconstruction. In the second waveform synthesis stage, a lightweight modified discrete cosine transform (MDCT)-based neural vocoder predicts the MDCT spectrum from the reconstructed mel spectrogram and recovers the waveform through inverse MDCT. Experiments on LibriTTS dataset demonstrate that UMelCodec outperforms strong baselines across most objective reconstruction metrics while maintaining competitive subjective naturalness. In terms of model complexity and inference efficiency, UMelCodec has only 19.67 M parameters, requires 1.93 G MACs, and supports real-time inference on both GPU and CPU platforms.

authors.name: Hui-Peng Du, Yang Ai, Zhen-Hua Ling

papers.title: A closed-loop agentic research environment for MRI development within Siemens IDEA platform
papers.summary: Motivation: Testing new ideas in MRI can require substantial effort to learn sequence programming and reconstruction tools and to debug implementations before the scientific question can be addressed. Goals: Reduce the implementation and debugging burden of testing MRI ideas while retaining researcher control of scientific decisions. Approach: We developed an environment where LLM agents develop sequences in the native Siemens IDEA platform, evaluate them through Bloch simulation and reconstruction, and further iteratively refine them using scanner feedback. Results: As test cases, the agentic environment was used to implement and validate a GIRF-based gradient-calibration sequence and reconstruction in approximately 4 hours, and to develop and optimize a rapid 3-second multichannel calibration scan in approximately 12 hours of researcher-guided iteration.

authors.name: Zimu Huo, Zachary Shah, Adam B Kerr, Kawin Setsompop

papers.title: Signed Powers-of-Two Greedy Vector Approximation of Zadoff-Chu Sequences
papers.summary: This paper explores the use of sums of signed powers-of-two (SOPOT) for a representation suitable for multiplierless applications of ZC sequences, where multiplications are reduced to a prescribed number of shift-and-add operations. The SOPOT representation is achieved using a greedy algorithm that outperforms other approaches for multiplierless approximations, such as CORDIC and CSD. The proposed algorithm is based on the matching pursuits using generalized bit planes (MPGBP), and the proposed modification enables robustness to hyperparameter tuning. The resulting sequences retain, to some extent, the good autocorrelation properties of ZC, as shown in a matched-filter detection simulation. This corroborates to their use in various practical applications across mainstream cellular systems and devices requiring moderate computational cost.

authors.name: Luiz Coelho (CEDRIC - LAETITIA, PEE/COPPE-UFRJ), Paulo Diniz (PEE/COPPE-UFRJ), Didier Le Ruyet (CEDRIC - LAETITIA)

papers.title: Personalized Privacy-Aware MARL Offloading in the Edge-Cloud Continuum
papers.summary: Task offloading in End-Edge-Cloud computing enables resource-constrained User Devices (UDs) to execute computation-intensive applications with reduced latency and energy consumption. However, existing task offloading schemes generally overlook the heterogeneous privacy requirements of users, leading to inefficient privacy-aware offloading decisions. In this paper, we propose a personalized privacy-aware task offloading framework, where the privacy requirement of each task is quantified through a User-Centric Privacy (UCP) model that considers task sensitivity, user privacy preferences, and task urgency. The task offloading problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) to jointly optimize the offloading ratio and the target computing server while minimizing the long-term system cost under latency, energy, and privacy constraints. To efficiently solve the resulting high-dimensional continuous optimization problem, we develop an Advantage-Weighted Actor-Critic (AWAC)-enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) algorithm under the Centralized Training and Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves lower average system cost, lower energy consumption, and higher task success rate than representative baselines under diverse privacy requirements.

authors.name: Muhammad Rafid, Golshan Famitafreshi, Kostas Ramantas, Luis Alonso, Christos Verikoukis

papers.title: DISC: A Deterministic Instantaneous-SINR Combiner for Uplink Massive MIMO Systems
papers.summary: Future Massive MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) systems will fit more antennas into compact arrays, making minimum mean-square-error (MMSE) combining computationally demanding. Maximum-ratio (MR) combining serves as a cheaper alternative but performs poorly in multi-user scenarios. Existing solutions to this either mimic the MMSE combiner using second-order statistics or, as in the optimal bilinear equalizer (OBE), rely on the loose use-and-then-forget (UaTF) bound. In this paper, we propose DISC, a novel receive combiner that instead maximizes a deterministic approximation of the instantaneous signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), obtained by replacing the random terms in the SINR with deterministic equivalents. This approximation becomes increasingly accurate as the number of antennas grows, and it exploits useful information discarded by the UaTF bound. The computational complexity of DISC matches that of OBE, with the low-complexity variant DISC-D being even cheaper than conventional MR combining. We further prove that the SINR achieved by DISC grows unbounded with the number of antennas, even under pilot contamination, similarly to MMSE combining. Finally, we numerically demonstrate that DISC achieves a sum spectral efficiency close to that of MMSE combining under full pilot sharing, while outperforming other combiners across signal-to-noise ratio, pilot length, and spatial correlation models.

authors.name: Emanuel Wennemo, Ki Won Sung, Emil Bj\"ornson

papers.title: Coordinated Offloading: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for the Edge-Cloud Continuum
papers.summary: The increasing demand for intelligent, low-latency services in edge-cloud continuum systems poses new challenges for dynamic and efficient task offloading. We propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for distributed task offloading under partial observability, where each device offloads only a portion of its computation to a target edge server while executing the remaining portion locally (partial offloading). The problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), where each device independently learns an optimal policy under partially observable system states. To address the non-convexity, high-dimensional state space, and continuous action space, we develop a multi-agent Advantage-Weighted Actor-Critic (AWAC)-enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based computation offloading algorithm. The proposed method combines the stable policy updates of PPO with an advantage-weighting mechanism inspired by AWAC to emphasize higher-quality actions during training.
